items.statement: Management expects around 10% volume growth next financial year with CNG and industrial/commercial as main contributors
items.quote: Now maybe next year, we will not be able to have that much number, but we are comfortable that around 10% numbers we will be able to clock next financial year also and which will be definitely -- CNG will be a main contributor in that growth along with industrial and commercial segment.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated volume growth of 12-13% for FY25 and double-digit growth for FY26
items.quote: If you add on UEPL because it has a small volume, but the growth is much higher there, maybe more plus 20%. So collectively on a consolidated basis, we are around 12% growth as of now, 12% to 12.5%. So in the year-end we expect it to be around 13% or 13.5%. Next year also we definitely should be in -- at least in the double digit, yes.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA per SCM to remain in INR9-12 range depending on LNG prices and contracts
items.quote: So it is not very off the mark of the guidance which we have given about INR10 to INR12. So we expect similar range to continue and depending on the price of LNG, Henry Hub and other contracts. We may be very comfortable in this range, INR9 to INR11 or INR10 to INR12 range.

items.statement: MGL spent INR650+ crores in 9M FY25 and expects INR200-250 crores more in Q4; UEPL to spend INR125-150 crores in FY25 and INR150-200 crores in FY26
items.quote: As far as MGL is concerned, already INR650 crores plus capex has been done in this 9 months period and we expect anywhere between INR200 to INR250 additional capex in Q4 as well. Out of these, major will be on steel and low-pressure pipelines. And roughly INR200 crores or plus, minus 10% on CNG. And balance is on steel grid and LMC, last mile connectivity.

items.statement: UEPL standalone capex guidance: INR125-150 crores for FY25, INR150-200 crores for FY26
items.quote: See, UEPL standalone should spend in the range of around this year, at least INR125 crores to INR150 crores. And it will be further up maybe next year because we have now have the ground and the groundwork is done. So we'll be able to do more capex on CNG stations et cetera. And it could go from INR150 crores to INR200 crores next financial year.

items.statement: Battery JV with IBC: Phase 1 (1 GW) to start revenue in 1.5 years, targeting INR900-1000 crores revenue per GW at 18% IRR
items.quote: is INR1,000 crores revenue will be there, it is around that number or 1 gigawatt factory. Probal Sen: Sorry, sir, INR1,000 crores per gigawatt? Management: Yes, around that number INR900 crores to INR1,000

items.statement: Mumbai High Court order on phasing out diesel/petrol vehicles could drive CNG growth to 15-20% if implemented favorably
items.quote: We can see a growth of around 15% to 20% in case everything goes in favor of CNG.

items.statement: APM gas allocation cut by 7% per annum from April 2025, to be replaced by NWG at NWG prices on pro-rata basis
items.quote: Earlier was the r e-allocation, means two cuts were there. Now in our information, as far as we understand the next r e-allocation or re -adjustments will happen somewhere from 1st of April because around 7% per annum is recommended to be reduced from APM and put into NWG.

items.statement: Forex impact: INR0.22-0.25 per SCM cost increase per rupee depreciation; partially naturally hedged via industrial/commercial pricing linked to alternate fuels
items.quote: Roughly, my estimate is -- yes, you are right in that sense. It adds around INR 0.22 to INR0.25 per rupee increase on our overall company basis, a rough ballpark number.

items.statement: UEPL merger approved by Board Oct 2024, submitted to NCLT Dec 2024, interim order reserved Jan 17 2025
items.quote: A scheme of amalgamation or merger of UEPL with MGL was approved by the Board in October '24 last year and the scheme was submitted to NCLT Mumbai on 6 December, 2024. And the matter was heard by the Mumbai bench on January 17, 2025 and they've reserved the pronouncement of its interim order.

items.statement: Interim dividend of 120% (INR12 per equity share) approved for FY25
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that Board has approved an interim dividend at the rate of 120% that is INR12 per equity share for the current financial year.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle penetration at 9.5-10% (38,000 of 4 lakh vehicles); potential volume churner if court order implemented
items.quote: Within that, if I take number of commercial vehicles which are mostly on diesel are going to get impacte d initially. And that number is around 4 lakh in our geographies. And currently, we have around 38,000 such commercial vehicles already on CNG which is about 9.5%, 10% penetration.

items.statement: Gas sourcing mix: 2+ MMSCMD APM, 1.45 MMSCMD Henry Hub, 0.5 MMSCMD HPHT, 0.1 MMSCMD Brent-linked, small NWG spot
items.quote: As of today, that means in January, we have already tied up Henry Hub contracts, all contracts -- put together around 1.45 mmscmd. HPHT is around 0.5 million, okay? And rest is spot and whatever NWG have.

items.statement: Industrial margins under pressure due to LDO/FO price declines and 10% committed discount to new customers; commercial margins better linked to LPG prices
items.quote: If you look at current industrial margins compared to the last quarter because of the LSHS and LDO prices going down, has gone down slightly. Whereas in case of commercial, where most of the customers are linked to commercial LPG 19 kgs where prices have s lightly gone up, the margin is better.

items.statement: EV battery JV risk mitigated by government protection (like solar), strong Korean partner, local manufacturing edge in lifecycle management
items.quote: We have seen with solar PV cells to promote indigenous PV manufacturing, the government has supported the industry quite a lot. Having said that, we are very much confident that we will be able to source very competitive raw material, lithium-ion and other products, which are required for battery cell manufacturing. We have a very strong partner-- South Korean partner.

items.statement: Guides 20-25% AuM growth long-term; confident of ~20% in FY25 with Jan at 15-20% trajectory
items.quote: We continue to guide on a 20 – 25% of an AuM growth on a long-term basis. I think the traction which we got in the Q3 and the numbers in Jan really give us confidence on delivering the guided AuM growth of ~20.

items.statement: Targets opex-to-assets below 3% with ~20 bps annual reduction; achieved 42 bps YoY improvement to 3.21% in 9MFY25
items.quote: At the beginning of the financial year we have guided that we will bring down opex to assets ratio by ~20 bps every year to reach below 3%. I am happy to report a remarkable improvement in the Opex to Assets ratio by 42 bps Y -o-Y to 3.21% in 9MFY25 as a result of our cost optimisation strategy.

items.statement: Guides credit cost below 25 bps on sustainable basis; 9MFY25 at 15 bps vs 19 bps in 9MFY24
items.quote: We continue to guide credit cost of below 25 bps on sustainable basis.

items.statement: Incremental business yield up 25+ bps across products; disbursement yield improving QoQ; 25 bps BPLR hike in Oct fully accounted
items.quote: Our focus continues to underwrite quality business with risk adjusted return as a result our incremental business yield has gone up by 25 bps+ across products.

items.statement: Demand uptick post-elections in PMAY affordable supply and self-construction; Tier 3-5 markets strong; Jan showing green shoots
items.quote: Yes. Demand has to see an uptick and specifically in certain segments and verticals as I speak of the PMAY -led affordable supply, which is there.

items.statement: ~60% of AuM <Rs15L ticket; targeting 45% <Rs10L (currently 30-35%); <Rs10L yields ~200 bps higher; home loan yield 11.5-12%, non-home 250 bps higher
items.quote: Our aim presently is to get to the 45%. Currently, we are hovering between 30% to 35% of the loans which are less than Rs. 10 lakhs in ticket size.

items.statement: Asset quality pristine: 1+ DPD 3.85% (<4% guided), GNPA 1.14%, NNPA 0.81%; BT-out at 5.4%; ECL model upgraded to Deloitte Bolt-on with Vasicek macro factors
items.quote: Our asset quality remains within the guided range with 1 day past due below 4% at 3.85% in Q3 FY25 and Gross Stage 3 & Net Stage 3 under 1.25% stood at 1.14% and 0.81% respectively.

items.statement: Opened 6 branches in 9MFY25; adding 20+ in Q4 FY25 mainly Karnataka & UP; accelerating branch expansion in calendar year
items.quote: We have opened 6 new branches during 9MFY25 and opening another 20+ branches in this quarter predominantly in the states of Karnataka and UP.

items.statement: Raised Rs 6.3 bn NCDs from IFC in Q3 (largest ever); total borrowings Rs 172 bn at 8.41% for 9MFY25; 51% bank borrowings EBLR/short-MCLR linked for fast repricing
items.quote: I am happy to share that we have successfully raised NCDs amounting to Rs 6.3 bn from the IFC in Q3. This is largest NCD raised by company till date.

items.statement: Aspires to reach Rs 500 bn AUM in next 4-5 years and become Pan-India player while continuing cost optimization
items.quote: We aspire to reach a milestone of Rs. 500 bn in assets under management in the next 4 to 5 years and broaden our horizons as a Pan-India player and continue our cost optimization strategy.

items.statement: Room AC industry expected to grow at 19% CAGR over next five years to reach higher penetration levels
items.quote: So, the CAGR projected by various studies are at 19% over the next five years in order to reach a penetration level that India should have. So, 19% CAGR is the guidance.

items.statement: Segment-I margin guidance 7% to 7.5%, Segment-II margin guidance 8% to 8.5%
items.quote: The margin guideline was 7% to 7.5% in Segment-I, 8% to 8.5% Segment-II. Unless and until something dramatically changes, let us say commodity prices crash, the margin can go up.

items.statement: Target to achieve 15% market share in Room AC within a couple of years while maintaining 8.5% operating margin
items.quote: Our immediate goal is 15% market share. Our goal is to keep that operating margin intact of 8.5%.

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 750 cr to Rs. 800 cr over around three years for manufacturing, product development and digitalization
items.quote: The CAPEX amount over a period of around three years will be in the region of around Rs. 750 cr to Rs. 800 cr, and that will be moving towards both manufacturing as well as product development, and certain amount of digitalization.

items.statement: Carried forward order book at record high of Rs. 6,801.99 cr as of December 31, 2024, up 12.8% year-on-year
items.quote: Carried forward order book as of December 31, 2024, is at a record high of Rs. 6,801.99 cr as compared to Rs. 6,038.53 cr as on December 31, 2023. This was a growth of 12.8%.

items.statement: Segment-II margins improved 100 bps to 8.1% in Q3 FY25 driven by Room AC scale benefits
items.quote: Overall margins in this segment registered a strong 100 bps improvement in the current quarter, which, as you have seen, was 8.1% in the current quarter as compared to 7.1% in the last corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Energy label change due January 1, 2026; products already developed, no pre-buying in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The energy label change is from 1st January 2026, and 1st January, 2025, no change has happened. What can happen potentially is somewhere in festival season it can be pre-launched that the future-ready or like that, that can happen.

items.statement: Room AC demand strong in Q3 FY25 due to festive season; industry likely to close above 15 million units, Blue Star above 1.5 million units in FY25
items.value: above 15 million units industry, above 1.5 million units Blue Star
items.quote: All that we know is that it is very likely the industry closes above 15 million, and we will close much higher than 1.5 million this year. And that we are aware and more or less this guidance can be given.

items.statement: Affluent customers moving up value chain to heavy duty and Wi-Fi enabled ACs, improving SKU margins
items.quote: The second one is connected with the affluent customers moving up the value chain. So, we are very clearly seeing year-after-year heavy duty air conditioner or Wi-Fi enabled air conditioner, these going up.

items.statement: Headwinds from rupee depreciation, commodity price escalation, supply chain disruptions, and liquidity issues in certain market segments
items.quote: However, there are headwinds owing to depreciation of Indian rupee, escalations in commodity prices, and possible supply chain disruptions due to huge demand. We have strong mitigation action in place to tackle these challenges.

items.statement: Segment-III Professional Electronics and Industrial Systems expected to revive in FY26 as CAPEX cycle picks up
items.quote: The challenges in this segment continues to impact revenue growth and profitability, and we expect to revive in FY26. Therefore, we are focused on controlling cost and managing working capital.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity modular; HP plant at ~600,000 units, Sri City scaling from 300,000 to 600,000, can scale up to 1.8-2.4 million units as demand grows
items.quote: the capacity at HP plant was already in the region of around 600,000, and at Sri City we were investing, we started with 300,000, we will now reach up to 600,000 and as and when we want, we can scale it up. So, in the current year also the capital investments have happened and this will keep happening as we see the demand. We can go up to around 1.8 million to 2.4 million as the demand scales up.

items.statement: Confident of closing Q4 FY25 on a high note, delivering good results for third consecutive year
items.quote: We are confident that we will close the forthcoming quarter also on a high note, which means for the third year in succession, we will deliver good results for the whole financial year.

items.statement: PLI benefits eligible for ~Rs. 75-80 cr over four years for ~Rs. 155 cr investment; on track to fully avail Phase-1 benefits
items.quote: we have indicated earlier that we are eligible for somewhere close to over a four-year period Rs. 78 cr of PLI benefits for eligible investment of somewhere around Rs. 155 cr or something, I do not remember the exact figure, but it is in the order of around between Rs. 75 cr to Rs. 80 cr, and we are on track on that.

items.statement: Expect sequential improvement in demand over next few months on back of infrastructure investments, good harvest and government initiatives in upcoming budget
items.quote: We expect sequential improvement in demand over the next few months on the back of increase in infrastructure investments, good harvest and government init iatives to spur growth in the upcoming budget

items.statement: Expect mid-single digit value growth in Q4 with margin maintenance
items.quote: for quarter 4, o ur intent is at a mid-single digit top- line growth, we will try to maintain our margins for quarter 4

items.statement: Invested in aseptic PET line for coconut water under Activ portfolio
items.quote: As far as Coconut Water is concerned under Activ, there also w e have invested in an aseptic pet line and coming out in a pet bottle besides tetra pack which wi ll give us huge growth in the beverage

items.statement: Operating profit increased 2.1% and PAT grew 1.8% YoY in Q3 FY25 despite inflationary pressures
items.quote: Operating profit increased by 2.1% and PAT grew by 1.8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect 5% inflation going forward, will take calibrated price increases to maintain margins
items.quote: We expect a 5% inflation to actually hit us. So, whether it is SLEs, SLAs, Oral Care, so inflation will hit us and fruit concentrates also that we are purchasing because Indian currency will depreciate.

items.statement: Targeting 20-21% margin levels in FY26 through premium mix, premiumization, cost savings and price increases
items.quote: our attempt will be to go to around 20-21% lev els. That's what we were aiming at. I think the levers to achieve that would be changing the mi x of the product portfolio that we sell

items.statement: Took judicious price increases in portfolio to mitigate inflationary pressures in Q3
items.quote: We faced inflationary pressures this quarter and took judicious price increases in our portfolio.

items.statement: Plan consumer offer to reduce nectar prices from Rs 130 to around Rs 100 and launch economical range with RPI of 2 vs colas
items.quote: We are proposing, or we have already designed to do a consumer offer to reduce the prices from Rs. 130 to around Rs. 100, but this will happen by way of consumer offer, not by reducing prices.

items.statement: Rural outperformed urban for fourth consecutive quarter; rural grew 2% vs urban 0.6% in Q3
items.quote: If the overall India business is grown by 1.7%, urban business has grown by 0.6% and rural business has grown by 2%. So, the difference between the two is 140 bps for us.

items.statement: Oral Care grew 9.1% with Red franchise and Meswak driving double-digit growth; Gels grew 50% YoY
items.quote: The Oral Care portfolio recorded a growth of 9.1% driven by str ong double-digit growth in the Red franchise and Meswak. The Gels toothpaste portfolio has rec eived a good response in the market, recording a 50% year-on-year growth in this quarter

items.statement: Hair Oil grew 3.1% with coconut and perfumed oils gaining 125 and 236 bps market share respectively; overall share at 18% highest ever
items.quote: Within Hair Oils, both coconut and perfumed oils grew ahead of the category, gaining market share of 125 an d 236 bps respectively, taking our overall Hair Oil shares to around 18%, the highest ever

items.statement: Foods business strong with Culinary and Badshah domestic growing 30% and 15% respectively
items.quote: The Foods business demonstrated strong performance with the Culinary and Badshah domestic portfolio growing at 30% and 15% respectively.

items.statement: Revised strategic vision cycle from 4 years to 3 years due to volatile geopolitical landscape and uncertain macro indicators; partnered with McKinsey
items.quote: In light of the volatile geopolitical landscape and uncertain macroeconomic indicators, we have revised our strategic vision cycle from 4 years to 3 years. We have partnered with leading consultancy firm McKinsey & Company to refine and align our strategy for the next three years.

items.statement: Beverage nectar portfolio under pressure from Cola wars with RPI worsening from 2 to 2.7; category declined 16% in Nielsen terms
items.quote: the category is declined by around 16% and our decline is around 8 to 9% in the Nielsen ter ms. We have gained market shares of around 320 basis points in Juices and Nectar category

items.statement: Cement demand expected to grow 4-5% in FY25 with H2 much better than H1
items.quote: This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25, meaning H2 should be much better than H1, further supported by pro infra and housing budget in the 2025.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex target around INR9,000 crores with INR6,200 crores spent in 9 months
items.quote: For the full year, it is closer to INR9,000 crores. And so, another INR2,200 crores will go for this quarter.

items.statement: Capacity expansion on track to reach 140 million tons by FY28 with 118 million tons by FY26
items.quote: As we plan to expand our cement capacity to 140 million tons by FY '28, we are pacing well to achieve the stated target.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 18.4% in Q3 FY25 at INR1,712 crores with EBITDA per ton of INR1,038
items.quote: With improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR1,712 crores at a margin of 18.4% and EBITDA per ton of INR1,038.

items.statement: Operational cost reduced to INR4,618 per ton in Q3 FY25 driven by 7% energy cost decline and 6% freight reduction
items.quote: Operational costs for the quarter is at INR 4,618 per ton. This is driven by a 7% decline in energy cost owing to better fuel management and strong focus on green power.

items.statement: Target to reduce total cost to INR3,650-3,700 per ton by FY28 from current INR4,600 level
items.quote: Our end-state target is to drop down the total cost to about INR3,700-3,800 over the next couple of years, that's the target.

items.statement: Industry demand growth was tepid at 1.5-2% in H1 FY25 but expected to rebound to 4-5% for full year
items.quote: The improved consumption demand in housing and infrastructure segments and increased government spendings are poised to reverse the tepid 1.5% to 2% cement demand growth during H1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Blended cement at 82% and premium products increased 400 bps to 26% of trade sales volume
items.quote: blended cements at 82%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales volume by 400 bps to 26 percentage.

items.statement: Sanghi and Penna assets currently at sub-40% and sub-50% utilization, expected to reach 70%+ in FY26
items.quote: My estimate is in the next financial year, both the assets should go up, I think Sanghi earlier and Penna because it's also in the market where it takes time to ramp up. But both of them should hit 70% plus utilization levels in the next financial year.

items.statement: Net worth increased to INR63,000 crores from INR51,000 crores with nil debt and AAA rating
items.quote: I'm glad to share that we have achieved a net worth of almost INR63,000 crores, which was in April INR51,000 crores, so almost up by INR12,000 crores. And we remain nil debt and with the highest rating of AAA.

items.statement: 200 MW solar plant at Khavda commissioned in Q3 FY25, targeting 218 MW WHRS by March 2025
items.quote: 200-megawatt solar power, the project in Gujarat, Khavda, has been commissioned in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition at advanced stage, expected to add capacity to 104 million tons by Q4 FY25
items.quote: With Orient acquisition at advanced stage, the total capacity by Q4 FY '25 to hit 104 million tons.

items.statement: Incentive income expected to rise from INR400-500 crores annually to INR600-650 crores with new capacities
items.quote: Historically, say, it was around, say, INR100-odd crores of incentive per quarter, almost INR400 crores for a year. But this will actually now start moving up to INR600 crores, INR650-odd crores prospectively with new capacities coming in.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents at INR8,755 crores as of December 31, Orient acquisition outflow ~INR4,000 crores in Q4
items.quote: In terms of the expected outgo for Orient, that is ballpark around INR4,000-odd crores, which will be there.

items.statement: Green power share increased to 21.5% from 15.8%, targeting 60% of power needs from green sources by FY28
items.quote: The share of green power in power mix has increased to 21.5% from 15.8%.

items.statement: India realisations QoQ expected flat unless budget or safeguards provide upside; coking coal costs expected $10/t lower in 4Q vs 3Q
items.quote: On realisations, we are seeing India realisations QoQ being flat, unless there's something significant in the budget or safeguards which come, then there should be an upside. Otherwise, at minimum, we see it flat. In terms of costs, as far as India is concerned, coking coal costs are expected to be about $10 per ton lower in 4Q vs. 3Q.

items.statement: TSUK breakeven targeted in first two quarters of FY2026, focusing on June 2025; cost takeout and redundancies ongoing
items.quote: Nonetheless, breakeven is the target for the next few quarters, and we should be in that zone in the first two quarters of FY 2026. We're certainly focusing on getting it by June 2025.

items.statement: Kalinganagar Phase 2 completion by September 2026 with ~Rs. 3,000 crore spend in FY2026; Ludhiana EAF 0.85 MTPA bulk spend in FY2026; UK EAF ~3 MTPA civil construction from July 2025; Netherlands decarbonisation FID in 4-5 months pending go
items.quote: By September of 2026, we would have completed Kalinganagar and then the full benefit will start coming in. These capital expenditures, whether it is UK or Netherlands, do have their own timeframe, especially Netherlands, I think it's clearly about 1.5 years behind because the permitting time will also be building before any capex is spent.

items.statement: India capex FY2026 includes ~Rs. 3,000 crore for Kalinganagar completion, blast furnace relining at Jamshedpur, Ludhiana EAF, UK EAF spend starting; Neelachal expansion proposal to Board in few months; Kalinganagar 8 to 13 MTPA and Meramand
items.quote: for next year is concerned, the elements that will be there is certainly some part of the Kalinganagar expansion, which will be about Rs. 3,000 crores along with ancillary spend on that expansion. There is the blast furnace reline that is currently going on. You will see that in both 4QFY25 and 1QFY26. There's another relining that will happen towards the end of 4Q and then there are more on impro

items.statement: NINL EBITDA margin improved from 13% in 2Q to 20% in 3Q on 17% volume growth QoQ and conversion cost reduction ~Rs. 3,000/t QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved from 13% in 2Q to 20% in 3Q on account of rise in volumes by about 17% QoQ and as an outcome of cost efficiency through reduction in conversion costs, which reduced by about Rs. 3,000 per ton QoQ.

items.statement: Netherlands transformation program targeting cost takeouts of a couple hundred million euros over multi-year, focusing on productivity, fixed/variable efficiency, mill availability, product mix; impact visible from 1Q FY26
items.quote: The transformation program is focused on productivity, cost takeouts, both fixed and variable efficiency, including availability of the mills in terms of benchmarks and optimi sing the product mix. [inaudible] I think it is also not a one-year cost takeout program. It will be multiyear, but we will want to take as much advantage of that in the next year, and it will run into a couple of hundred mi

items.statement: India steel demand growing but momentum eased; domestic prices under pressure from cheap imports; DGTR safeguard investigation initiated; China exports 111 Mt in 2024
items.quote: India steel demand continued to grow but momentum eased, and domestic prices remained under pressure due to cheap imports. The DGTR (Director General of Trade Remedies), has initiated investigation to consider safeguard duty. In 2024, several nations relied on trade measures such as antidumping duty to combat the impact of steel imports, particularly from China.

items.statement: Sukinda mine surrender process underway with state permissions received; will remove MDPA pressures and improve FAMD business stability; further optimisation planned
items.quote: Work is going on in surrender of the mine. We have got some of the permissions that we needed from the state government, but we are still going through the procedures. Once we surrender the mines, we won't have the MDPA pressures, and there will be a better balance between our ability to produce, grow more, and ability to convert them. That brings business to a better level of stability than we've

items.statement: UCP segment margin guidance: aim to retain high single digit in Q4 and by year-end
items.quote: Generally, we will remain around this high-single digit, our endeavor would be by the end of the year as a Company. And on the segment also, we will try and retain a high single digit in the last quarter as well.

items.statement: Chennai AC plant: ~Rs 400 cr spent; additional Rs 400-450 cr earmarked for compressor manufacturing and ramping capacity to 1.5-2 mn units over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: Besides this, we have also earmarked additional roughly around Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 450 crores which is for compressor manufacturing as well as ramping up our production in Chennai factory from 1 million to take it to 1.5 million and then 2 million.

items.statement: Compressor capex ~Rs 250 cr, pending technological partnership; other Chennai ramp-up investments to complete in 10-12 months
items.quote: Compressor capex is about Rs. 250-odd crores, which will take a while. As we are looking for some technological partnership, etc. Unless it is done, we will not be able to commence production of compressors.

items.statement: UCP segment margin dipped to 5.9% in Q3 due to higher ad/ISD spend to gain market share; nine-month segment PBT up 30% to Rs 548 cr
items.quote: Firstly, when you are asking why there is pressure on UCP margin. So, we were trying to gain market share, and therefore, we were spending money on ISDs, BTL advertisement, ATL advertisement.

items.statement: No price hike taken in Q3; will evaluate passing on commodity/forex pressure via value engineering and selective price increases later
items.quote: No, we have not taken any price hike in the last quarter, Quarter 3. Because as it is, it's a leaner quarter for especially the air conditioners. And as I told you that our endeavor is to increase the scale of the numbers.

items.statement: Expect robust demand for all product categories in upcoming summer; optimistic on volume growth and market share gains
items.quote: With the summers around the corner, we remain optimistic and expect robust demand for all our product categories. And we hope that the demand will remain strong and positive consumer sentiments will further support the volume.

items.statement: UCP Q3 mix: RAC ~60%, Commercial Refrigeration ~15%, Air Coolers ~5%, Commercial AC balance
items.quote: So, the current quarter, as a part of Segment A: UCP, RAC has been around 60%-odd, commercial refrigeration has been around 15%, air cooler has been around 5%, and commercial air condition has been balance.

items.statement: Voltbek JV: volume growth 59% in Q3, 56% in 9M; market share >10% in washing machines (semi-auto 16.7%), 5.1% in refrigerators; targeting EBITDA breakeven by March 2025
items.quote: We had anticipated that by the end of this year, in the last quarter probably, we will be reaching the EBITDA breakeven, which our endeavor is still there, probably by the month of March, we should be able to hit that number.

items.statement: Peak annual depreciation after full capitalization of CR and Chennai plants estimated at Rs 70-75 cr company-wide
items.quote: It should be roughly about Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 75 crores for the full year, company wide.

items.statement: PLI benefits for Chennai plant expected from next fiscal year (FY26); some residual Pantnagar benefit may accrue in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, I think for Chennai plant, if you are asking in particular, next year onwards, the benefits will start accruing. So, in the next quarter, I do not think anything is coming in from Chennai. But yes, some leftover for Pantnagar, which we have already spent, could get in, in Quarter 4.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA run rate achieved in Q3 FY25 should be taken as base for next 4-5 quarters; additional developments will only add to earnings
items.quote: But EBITDA -- stand-alone EBITDA run rate, which we have achieved in December '24 quarter should be taken as a base for the next 4, 5 quarters, because all additional developments that will happen will only add further to the earnings of Jindal Drilling.

items.statement: Order book of INR1,636 crores given rig-wise with day rates and contract duration; year-wise breakup provided
items.quote: Thereafter, our order book of INR1,636 crores is given rig-wise with day rates and contract duration.

items.statement: Acquisition of Jindal Pioneer rig for $75 million purchase price expected to conclude within Q4 FY25; no debt on the rig
items.quote: $75 million is the purchase price.

items.statement: Operating margins at 34% in Q3 FY25 expected to normalize at this rate and increase further after Pioneer acquisition
items.quote: Yes, definitely. And margins will increase further once the acquisition of Jindal Pioneer goes through.

items.statement: ONGC press release hiring BP Exploration as technical services provider indicates increased exploration activity and expected higher capex in oil & gas sector
items.quote: This is a clear indication that ONGC wants to increase exploration activities. And the fact that they have issued a press release means that further capital expenditure in the oil and gas sector is expected.

items.statement: All five rigs deployed in Bombay High; Jindal Supreme deployed 75 days in Q3, full 90 days in Q4; Jindal Explorer contract ends May or Sep 2025
items.quote: Bombay High. All five rigs are deployed in Bombay High.

items.statement: Only risk is securing contracts from ONGC; once awarded, contracts are firm, not renegotiated or canceled
items.quote: The only risk in this industry is securing a contract from ONGC. There is no other risk which cannot be addressed apart from the ability to secure a contract from ONGC.

items.statement: Net cash position doubled to INR101 crores in 9 months; gross debt INR156 crores, cash INR257 crores as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: Our net cash position has doubled in last 9 months from INR51 crores to INR101 crores.

items.statement: No share buyback program under consideration; natural hedge covers 100% of USD payables on rented rigs; FX gain ~INR9 crores in Q3
items.quote: We are not considering any such corporate action right now.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer rig manufactured March 2015, currently in Mexico; plan to bring to India for deployment unless $180k/day rate available internationally
items.quote: Jindal Pioneer, March 2015.

items.statement: No new rig building economics viable currently ($250-300M capex, 10-15 year payback at $100k/day); no distressed rig acquisition opportunities in upcycle
items.quote: Therefore, people are still reluctant to build new rigs due to the long gestation period.

items.statement: Upcycle started Feb 2022 post Russia-Ukraine war; expected to be longer due to US political change favoring drilling; not at peak as crude not at all-time high
items.quote: The up cycle in the oil and gas industry started after the Russia -Ukraine war, in February 2022.

items.statement: Only capex planned is Jindal Pioneer acquisition; reassessment after transaction concludes; consolidation of rented rigs preferred growth path
items.quote: The only capex which we are doing is acquisition of Jindal Pioneer, which is expected in this quarter.

items.statement: Day rates function of international market and Indian competition; last purchase price not confirmed indicator; cannot comment on Explorer renewal rate
items.quote: We cannot say that, because usually day rates are a function of the international market and the competition available in the Indian market.

items.statement: Directional drilling and mud logging services are small high-margin divisions but not scalable; no diversification planned beyond rig operations
items.quote: In addition to operating jack -up rigs, offshore jack -up Jindal Drilling & Industries Limited 29 January 2025 rigs with ONGC, we also have directional drilling and mud logging services, which are small divisions and give good margin, but it is not possible to scale those businesses up

items.statement: Aim to grow overall volumes by at least 12% in FY26 on a FY25 base of ~190,000 tons
items.quote: We do aim to grow by at least 12% overall.

items.statement: Expect FY25 total volume to reach around 190,000 tons by March
items.quote: Yes, we should be able to do that.

items.statement: Management sees Q3 as margin bottom; expects improvement from One Usha Martin initiatives by September 2025
items.quote: To be straight to you, I think this is the bottom of the margin. And with the various initiatives of One Usha Martin where we are looking at rationalizing our cost across all our subsidiaries.

items.statement: Galfan (Gal Star) zinc-aluminum line commissioned, under trial production; full benefits expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: I am happy to say that we have commissioned our plant, and it is under trial production, and we hope to stabilize the operations in this quarter, and we should start getting the full benefits of this from Q1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Zero capex planned for regular LRPC; focus only on plasticated and galvanized LRPC conversion
items.quote: No CAPEX at all. Zero CAPEX.

items.statement: Value-added products 71% of wire rope revenue in 9MFY25; international markets 55% of total revenue
items.quote: Within the wire rope division, value-added products accounted for 71% of revenue in 9MFY25, with encouraging contributions from the elevator sector. International markets formed 55% of total revenue in 9MFY25.

items.statement: Replacement demand is 80-85% of total; slowdown due to equipment idling (e.g., 50 rigs removed in Saudi) and general economic weakness
items.quote: The replacement market is almost 80% to 85% of the demand. It is not 50%-55%, in most products, 80%-85% of the market is replacement.

items.statement: European demand slowdown in oil & offshore, fishing; competitors cutting prices to keep plants running, forcing margin compression
items.quote: The area where we see a lot of competition as well as demand challenges coming is the oil and offshore. This is because of the competition and because of the lower demand; the competition is being aggressive to trying to get i.e everybody's trying to get a pie of the same market.

items.statement: One Usha Martin integration to complete by September 2025: centralizing procurement, logistics, back-office shift to India, and Brunton Shaw UK model shift to direct finished rope supply from India
items.quote: The implementation has already started, and we aim to complete this transition by September, 2025.

items.statement: Saudi rigging and distribution facility operational; expect significant volume increase in FY26
items.quote: We have been supplying there through our Brunton wire plant but now by having this facility, I think, there is a fairly good demand, and we expect good orders to flow in. And next year we should be having a significant increase in volume from that market.

items.statement: CE certification obtained for ropeway/Parvat Mala projects; only Indian company with manufacturing capability and certification; demand medium to long term
items.quote: As of today, we are the only Company with the manufacturing capability to produce these ropes. To the best of our knowledge, we are also the only Company in India with CE Certification for this.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 168 crore (28% of annualized EBITDA) as of Dec 2024; manageable despite ongoing capex
items.quote: As at 31st December 2024, our net debt stood at Rs. 168 crore which is 28% of our annualized operating EBITDA. Despite ongoing capital expenditure initiatives including expansions in Ranchi and Thailand and upgrades at the UK facility, our debt level remains well within manageable limits.

items.statement: Aiming for EBITDA margins between 13% and 14% for FY26
items.quote: FY '26, we are aiming for EBITDA margins between 13% and 14%, which highlights our commitment to maintaining financial health and enhancing operational efficiency

items.statement: Revenue target of roughly INR 4,000 crores on consolidated basis achievable in 3 years
items.quote: the revenue guidance, what we had given, obviously, we revised it down in last quarter because of the fallen prices to say, roughly around INR 4,000 crores of revenue on a consol basis is still achievable in 3 years' time

items.statement: Expect to inch towards 15% EBITDA margins in 2 years if current situation remains
items.quote: we should definitely start inching towards 15% EBITDA margins, frankly speaking

items.statement: Incurred INR 136 crores capex in 9 months FY25, anticipate total INR 200 crores for full year
items.quote: During 9 months FY '25, the company incurred cap ex of INR136 crores, mainly towards capacity expansion, backward integration and new product launches. We anticipate a total capex of around INR 200 crores for the full year

items.statement: Sayakha greenfield project to commence trial production in February, operating leverage expected from subsequent quarter
items.quote: the greenfield project at Sayakha, Gujarat for Specialty Chemicals, which is also related to the backward integration, will commence trial production in this quarter, most probably in the month of February itself. With this, the operating leverage is expected to kick in from the subsequent quarter with improved capacity utilization.

items.statement: Tarapur greenfield project ramp up to 500+ tons per month by end of March 2025, total sequential ramp-up of 1,600 metric tons per month by end of FY26
items.quote: There had been certain teething issues in Tarapur greenfield project, which are sorted now, and we expect to ramp up the production to 500- plus tons per month by end of March '25. In total, we will have a sequential ramp -up of capacity of 1,600 metric tons per month by end of FY '26.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement expected sequentially as raw material and selling prices have stabilized after 90-100 days inventory FIFO impact
items.quote: So now that it has stabilized, I think, the margin -- gross margin should in fact improve on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 15% to 20% for FY26 with help of salicylic acid capacity
items.quote: Yes. So volume growth, we will definitely try for 15% to 20%, no doubt about that. We'll try to -- with the help of salicylic acid, I hope we'll get to those numbers.

items.statement: Formulation segment expects flattish growth next quarter but strong order book for next 2 quarters with export-driven growth, 30% capacity added via brownfield expansion
items.quote: in the very short term in the next coming quarter, we are expecting a flattish growth. But over the next -- for the next financial year, we have pressed up our capacities. So we recently completed a brownfield expansion in the Formulation segment, which has added about 30% additional capacities, for which revenues will start kicking in from Q1.

items.statement: Meaningful contribution from US FDA plant may not come in FY26, likely starting FY27 due to regulated market gestation period
items.quote: the meaningful contribution may not come from FY '26 itself. Probably it will start flowing-in in FY '27.

items.statement: Solar power SPV to generate 8.9 million renewable units per annum, commence operations by end of H1 FY26, saving INR 3.6 crores annually for Gujarat plant
items.quote: This solar plant will give us approximately 8.9 millio n renewable units per annum, and it is expected to commence the operation by end of H1 FY '26. This can result to a full year annual saving of around INR 3.6 crores for our Gujarat plant.

items.statement: Targeting 200-250 crore top line in FY26 from toys business at full utilization
items.quote: I think we should be expecting that, and that is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Phase-2 toys expansion planned for H2 FY26 with ~100 crore investment for injection moulded toys plant
items.quote: We anticipate an investment of about Rs. 100 crores for this phase, and we intend to leverage the benefits of the Production Link Incentive Scheme in addition to the newly introduced toy policy.

items.statement: Auto business has no fixed order book; POs come as replenishment schedules from CV OEMs
items.quote: In any automotive business, there is not an order book given for the entire upcoming month. There is always a schedule given, and the POs keep coming in, as in when the stock has to be replenished.

items.statement: Toys segment EBITDA margin expected at 22-24% at optimum capacity across toys, preschool furniture, outdoor play equipment
items.quote: It is about a 22% to 24% blended between toys, preschool furniture, outdoor play equipment. This should be the EBITDA that one should operate on, on optimum capacity.

items.statement: Budget reduced duty on electronic components for battery-operated toys; will benefit Phase-2 expansion
items.quote: Now, it has come down. If you are importing with the intent to add these components, say, in a particular toy. So, hence, this is, to us, personally, this will come up under our Phase-2 of the expansion plan.

items.statement: Toys demand strong; Q4 FY25 targeting 4x prior capacity utilization with 30 tons/day capacity yielding 60-70 lakh/day value
items.quote: We should be doing or closing this Quarter at about 4x of what our capacity used to be and we are on track to achieve those numbers.

items.statement: Phase-2 expansion to add injection moulded toys including battery-operated cars and role-play toys
items.quote: This phase will involve the production of injection moulded toys, including battery operated cars and role play toys.

items.statement: Auto business tied to CV market cycle; down 22-24% in 9M FY25, expects 4-6% CAGR long-term
items.quote: We are about 22% to 24% behind in terms of numbers if you take up a 9-month runaway.

items.statement: May raise more funds via preferential/warrants as opportunities arise; currently reducing debt
items.quote: See, all of this is very dynamic. It all depends on what opportunities come in. So, yes, we may be raising more funds, but as and when required.

items.statement: Air filtration subsidiary signed 10-year exclusive license with Mann+Hummel; pilots at IIT Delhi and GD Goenka showed >80% PM reduction
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that it has entered into a 10-year exclusive licensing agreement with Mann + Hummel for the manufacturing and distribution of air purifiers across India.

items.statement: Industry cement demand expected to grow 4-5% in FY25 with H2 much better than H1 supported by pro-infra and housing budget
items.quote: This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25, meaning H2 should be much better than H1, further supported by pro infra and housing budget in the 2025.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex target around INR9,000 crores with INR6,200 crores spent in 9 months and INR2,000-2,500 crores expected in Q4
items.quote: For the full year, it is closer to INR9,000 crores. And so, another INR2,200 crores will go for this quarter.

items.statement: Capex plan includes 40 new grinding units to reach 140-150 million tons capacity with progressive cost benefits each quarter
items.quote: Mind you, our number of locations, we'll add almost 40 new grinding units over Ambuja Cements Ltd., ACC Ltd. and the plan period when we hit 140 million, 150 million tons

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 18.4% in Q3 FY25 with EBITDA per ton of INR1,038
items.quote: With improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR1,712 crores at a margin of 18.4% and EBITDA per ton of INR1,038.

items.statement: Operational cost reduced to INR4,618 per ton in Q3 FY25 driven by 7% decline in energy cost and 6% decline in logistics cost
items.quote: Operational costs for the quarter is at INR 4,618 per ton. This is driven by a 7% decline in energy cost owing to better fuel management and strong focus on green power.

items.statement: Target to reduce total cost to INR3,650-3,700 per ton by FY28 from current INR4,600 through green power, waste heat recovery, captive coal mines and logistics optimization
items.quote: Our end-state target is to drop down the total cost to about INR3,700-3,800 over the next couple of years, that's the target.

items.statement: Green power share increased to 21.5% from 15.8% with target of 60% green power for 140 million tons capacity and 83% for clinkerisation by FY28
items.quote: Both WHRS and solar power would ensure that 60% of our power requirements are -- of the planned 140 million tons would be through green power. However, on clinkerisation, the share of green power will further rise to 83%.

items.statement: Logistics cost reduced 6% to INR1,239 per ton with lead distance down 4km to 285km and direct dispatch up 700bps to 57%
items.quote: Because of these initiatives, our logistics costs have been reduced by 6% to INR1,239 per ton in Q3 FY '25 from INR1,322 per ton in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: Ambuja Cements to grow faster than industry with traditional volumes growing 7% vs industry 5% and new capacity volumes growing 11%
items.quote: The traditional volume that we have, where there is no new capacity, it has grown at about 7%, which is slightly higher than the industry growth. And wherever we are having new capacity, we have grown much more at 11%.

items.statement: Blended cements at 82% and premium products as percentage of trade sales volume increased 400bps to 26%
items.quote: blended cements at 82%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales volume by 400 bps to 26 percentage.

items.statement: Sanghi and Penna acquired assets currently at sub-40% and sub-50% utilization with cost 10-15% higher than Ambuja; expected to reach 70%+ utilization next financial year
items.quote: So, I would say it's at least about 10% to 15% higher than Ambuja cost. Penna would be also the same. So, we expect 10% to 15% -- 15% maybe reduction in the cost of both the companies on a per ton basis.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition cash outflow ~INR4,000 crores in Q4 FY25 with open offer separate in mid next year
items.quote: In terms of the expected outgo for Orient, that is ballpark around INR4,000-odd crores, which will be there.

items.statement: Incentive income expected to rise from INR400-500 crores annually to INR600-650 crores prospectively with new capacities; INR4,500 crores total incentive bucket to be received over 7-9 years
items.quote: Historically, say, it was around, say, INR100-odd crores of incentive per quarter, almost INR400 crores for a year. But this will actually now start moving up to INR600 crores, INR650-odd crores prospectively with new capacities coming in and giving the benefit of incentives.

items.statement: Net worth increased to ~INR63,000 crores from INR51,000 crores in April with nil debt and AAA rating; tangible assets 75% of net worth and 15% cash equivalents
items.quote: I'm glad to share that we have achieved a net worth of almost INR63,000 crores, which was in April INR51,000 crores, so almost up by INR12,000 crores. And we remain nil debt and with the highest rating of AAA.

items.statement: Merger of Penna Cements, Adani Cementation and Sanghi announced and under regulatory approval; expected to consummate next financial year
items.quote: Already, we have announced one set of transactions to merge some entities, including Penna Cements, Adani Cementation and Sanghi. So, if you see out of all the entities, we've already announced 3 entities, which is currently under regulatory approval stage.

items.statement: Expect 12% revenue growth for FY25 while maintaining operating leverage
items.quote: Factoring in these challenges for FY25, we now expect 12% revenue growth while maintaining operating leverage.

items.statement: Aim for early teen revenue growth with operating leverage from FY26 onwards
items.quote: From FY26 onwards, we aim for an early teen revenue growth along with operating leverage.

items.statement: Expect gross margin around 62% in medium term
items.quote: From the gross margin point of view, we expect the gross margin to be in the region of around 62% in the medium term.

items.statement: Expect Germany to contribute to bottomline from FY26 onwards
items.quote: We further expect Germany to start contributing to our bottomline from FY26 onwards.

items.statement: Gross margin 61.3% in Q3 FY25, 110 bps lower YoY due to product mix
items.quote: Owing to a surge in demand of high-end jewelry, gross margin came in at 61.3%, which is 110 basis points lower YoY.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% in Q3 FY25, up 40 bps YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% this quarter, which is 40 basis points higher than last year.

items.statement: Expect gross margin to continue above 60% in upcoming quarters and years
items.quote: And we expect that our gross margin will continue to be above 60% in upcoming quarters and years.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds contribute 8.9% of quarterly sales vs 0.2% a year ago
items.quote: Owing to the consumer demand towards lab-grown diamonds, we have successfully scaled our offering, which contributes to 8.9% of quarterly sales versus 0.2% a year ago.

items.statement: Expect lab-grown diamond sales to be double digit around 10-12% for foreseeable future
items.quote: So, we expect it to be double digit for about 10%, 12% for foreseeable future.

items.statement: US revenue grew 3.6% YoY boosted by strong festive season and improving consumer confidence
items.quote: In the US, revenue grew by 3.6% Y oY, boosted by strong festive season and improving consumer confidence

items.statement: UK revenue up 6.5% with Ideal World making significant contribution
items.quote: In the UK, the revenue was up 6.5% with Ideal World making a significant contribution.

items.statement: Germany posted 30.7% YoY revenue growth with operations achieving breakeven
items.quote: Germany continued its robust performance, posting a 30.7% Yo Y revenue growth. With operations achieving breakeven this quarter, we are confident about maintaining this momentum in Q4 as

items.statement: TV revenue grew 6% YoY, digital revenue grew 12% YoY, digital contributes 40% of B2C revenue
items.quote: TV revenue grew by 6% year-over-year, and digital revenue grew by 12% year-over-year. Digital sales is contributing 40% of total B2C revenue.

items.statement: Mindful of macroeconomic trends, particularly muted consumer sentiments in UK and Europe
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain mindful of macroeconomic trends, particularly the muted consumer sentiments in UK and Europe.

items.statement: No major CAPEX for next two to three years
items.quote: And given now we don't have any major CAPEX for next two, three years, can we expect an increase in dividend in the years to come for next two, three years?

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of Rs. 1.5 per share representing 39% payout
items.quote: As we aim to balance growth, reinves tments and shareholder returns, the board has declared an interim dividend of Rs. 1.5 per share for this quarter representing 39% payout

items.statement: Credit growth expected at 13-14% for FY25
items.quote: I am expecting that my credit growth will flow in the range of 13 % to 14% in this particular year as a whole.

items.statement: Loan book growth guidance for FY25 is 12-13%
items.quote: Our guidance for this year is 11% to 12% of the loan book now and I am expecting that our growth will be in the range of 12% to 13% in the Financial Year '25.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY25 is 2.9% to 3% and will be exceeded
items.quote: As of now, the guidance which we have given for this financial year, that is 2.9% to 3%, that we are definitely we are going to achieve and we will cross that

items.statement: Targeting Rs 18,000 crore total recovery for FY25
items.quote: Yes, we are aiming for Rs. 18,000 crore, but with a conservative estimate, I can tell you that in this particular quarter, we should be in a position to mop up the recovery to the extent of around Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Expecting Q4 FY25 TWO recovery of Rs 1,500-1,600 crore
items.quote: definitely in the upcoming quarter, we should have a TWO recovery of around minimum 1,500 to 1,600.

items.statement: Expecting Q4 FY25 total recovery of Rs 5,000-6,000 crore
items.quote: we should be in a position to mop up the recovery to the extent of around Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Repricing corporate book to improve yield on advances
items.quote: One is we are repricing our corporate book. That is one strategy we have already initiated. And there are, I think, around Rs. 10,000 crore which renewals or repricing it came and we have gone for some modification in the prici ng and it has already

items.statement: Treasury income expected to improve in Q4 FY25 due to RBI OMO and liquidity measures
items.quote: I think I am expecting some rough calculation is there around Rs. 150 crore plus should happen on account of t his transaction. And liquidity front also, yes, liquidity front also. So, that will also ease my cost of deposit

items.statement: Deposit cost stable due to retail term deposit mobilization and CASA growth
items.quote: We are able to mobilize a sizable amount under the retail term deposit. And we have one special scheme of 7.25% for more than one year. And we are able to mobilize a good number of amount under that particular bucket.

items.statement: GNPA reduced to 4.09% and NNPA to 0.41% as of Dec 2024
items.quote: GNPA has reduced from 6.24% in December '23 to 4.09% in December '24. Similarly, the net NPA ratio, which was 0.96% in December '23, has improved to 0.41% in December '24.

items.statement: PCR improved to 96.77%, above FY25 guidance of >95%
items.quote: The PCR (incl. TWO) of 94.28% in December '23 has improved to 96.77% in December '24, which is well above our guidance of more than 95% for FY25.

items.statement: Slippages expected to remain in Rs 1,600-1,800 crore range
items.quote: So, 1,600-1,800 like that only the slippages are happening and we are very confident that we will be able to retain this slippage in the same range.

items.statement: Total SMA (0+1+2) at ~7% of loans; SMA-0 Rs 49,522 cr, SMA-1 Rs 15,000 cr, SMA-2 Rs 13,000 cr
items.quote: And if I can give you the number, Rs. 49,522 crore is SMA-0. And SMA-1 is Rs. 15,000 crore. And SMA 2 is 13,000 crore.

items.statement: Raised Rs 3,000 crore Tier-2 bonds in Q3 FY25
items.quote: During Q3 of FY2024-25, Bank raised Tier-2 bonds of Rs. 3,000 crore and CET-1, AT-1 and Tier-2 stands at 10.65%, 1.88% and 2.88% respectively.

items.statement: Planning to migrate to 25% tax regime in FY26
items.quote: We are estimating and we are planning now to decide in the 25, 26 at any quarter, depending upon our position. I think definitely we would like to move to the new regime.

items.statement: Digital transactions share increased to 91% in Q3 FY25 from 88% in Q3 FY24
items.quote: The share of digital transaction has increased to 91% for Q3 FY25 against the 88% in Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Launched cash-flow based digital lending journey for MSMEs up to Rs 25 lakh
items.quote: We are one of the few banks who have started cash flow based digital journey for MSME now. Even if the MSME, those who are not having any balance sheet or any documents based on their transactions happening in that account, their credit score model, the system is inbuilt and it is totally end to end up to 25 lakh.

items.statement: Expect Luxury & Semi-Luxury net sales to cross Rs. 500 crores in FY26
items.quote: Given the exceptional demand in the domestic as well as international market, we expect this to cross Rs. 500 crores net sales mark in FY26.

items.statement: Expect margins to grow 100-125 bps annually for next 3 years, reaching ~15% margin next year
items.quote: With the kind of product profiling and portfolio and the luxury growing much faster, we expect our margins to grow 100 to 125 basis points every year for the next 3 years, thereby growing on the 15% kind of margin in next year.

items.statement: Expect to become debt-free by middle of FY26 or FY27
items.quote: With the kind of cash flow coming from internal accrual, we are very confident of achieving the debt-free kind of situation by '26, '27.

items.statement: Capex run rate of Rs. 100-125 crores annually for next 2-3 years after major projects completed
items.quote: We have done with all our major CAPEXs and our CAPEX run rate will be Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 125 crores every year for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Anticipate strong IMFL volume growth momentum to continue in near term
items.quote: We anticipate this strong growth momentum to continue in the near term.

items.statement: Expect P&A volume growth of 15% plus to continue in times ahead
items.quote: We have great plans, marketing plans going ahead and other growth momentum of giving a P&A growth of 15% plus in the times ahead will continue.

items.statement: Regular segment growth to be maintained at mid-single-digit rate going forward
items.quote: And the growth will also be maintained in the mid-single-digit rate.

items.statement: Gross margin was 43% in Q3 FY25, up from 41.8% YoY but down 60 bps QoQ due to foodgrain inflation
items.quote: Gross margin during the quarter was 43% as compared to 41.8% in quarter 3 of FY24, and 43.6% in sequential quarter 2.

items.statement: Luxury & Semi-Luxury margin much higher than P&A category
items.quote: We do not quantify what margin is in the segments, but definitely, in the Luxury and Semi-Luxury segment, that's Royal Ranthambore and Above, the margin is much, much higher than the P&A category.

items.statement: Prestige & Above category now 51% of IMFL volume vs 50% YoY; Luxury & Semi-Luxury 12% of sales vs 9% YoY
items.quote: Prestige & Above category accounts for 51% of the IMFL volume, compared to 50% in Quarter 3 of last year.

items.statement: Luxury & Semi-Luxury volume grew 54% and value 45% in Q3; ratio increased to 12% from 9%
items.quote: As far as the ratio of sales of Luxury & Semi-Luxury brands are concerned, we have grown to a level of 12% in Q3 as against 9% in the previous year.

items.statement: Cautiously monitoring ENA and grain inflation trends; FCI rice at Rs. 22,500/tonne may ease raw material costs if policy continues
items.quote: Only now for the first time the government, which we were expecting long back, because huge pile of about 500 lakh tonnes of grains lying in the FCI godown, so they have just announced where ethanol can be produced from FCI. So, that [FCI Rice] is at Rs. 22500 / tonne.

items.statement: Royal Ranthambore to be introduced in CSD channel in Q4 FY25, expected to drive further growth
items.quote: We are very happy to report that in Q4 FY25, it will be introduced to the CSD channel, which is a very large market. We believe it will drive further growth.

items.statement: Malt availability expected to double in next 3 years; single malt industry overtaking international malts domestically
items.quote: The next 3 years, our malt availability should double in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Telangana dues to be cleared in Q4; current payments on 45-day cycle per policy
items.quote: But yes, the dues whatever our overdue will get cleared in Q4.

items.statement: Grain inventory built up seasonally will be liquidated by March end, reducing working capital and debt
items.quote: This is temporary phenomenon, and inventories will be liquidated by March end.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance for FY25 is 9-10% excluding Chromeni; EBITDA per ton guidance for FY25 is INR17,000 on stand-alone basis
items.quote: Stand-alone, when we talk stand-alone, Ritesh, and we're continuing with our guidance for this year. In terms of EBITDA per ton, we should do around INR17,000 crores for this fiscal year, and our volume guidance is around 10%.

items.statement: Volume guidance for FY26 targets double-digit growth including Chromeni volumes
items.quote: Correct. That is correct, absolutely.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA per ton guidance for FY25 is INR20,000-plus
items.quote: So what we have said is that we will try to maintain in this range itself because JUSL will continue to be the same level of EBITDA per ton. Volumes will increase. So that's why we are saying INR20,000-plus of EBITDA per ton, we'll be able to deliver on FY '25 on a consol basis.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of INR5,500 crores; INR2,700 crores spent on acquisitions and INR1,100 crores on other capex so far; some brownfield capex may defer to next year
items.quote: Out of INR5,500 crores capex, if you recall that the capex number for the year was INR5,500 crores.
