items.statement: Gross store additions target 170,000-180,000 sq ft for FY25; net additions lower due to closures
items.quote: So, at the gross level, we will be doing a decent amount of opening, close to about 1,70,000, 1,80,000 square feet, which is what we've been focusing on for the entire financial year. So, from a gross perspective, we are on track.

items.statement: FY26 store expansion depends on rental market stabilization; pipeline strong but signing delayed
items.quote: If things stable earlier than we anticipate, then we will definitely try to open more stores. However, if the rentals remain at similar levels, then it is difficult to comment on the scale at which we will be opening stores next year.

items.statement: Excluding AP & Telangana, SSSG was ~10% for Q2+Q3 combined; Q3 alone ~5% ex AP/Telangana
items.quote: Broadly what we saw is about 10% growth in L2L when we see the last 2 quarters, excluding of AP, Telangana. So our SSSG was about 10% in Q2 and Q3 combined when we exclude AP, Telangana.

items.statement: Tier 2/3 cities outperformed metros by ~5% delta; trend reversed positively from Q1
items.quote: Broadly, I think Tier 2, Tier 3 has a 5% delta over metros. So that's the sort of improvement we've seen. But the encouraging piece is that the trend was the other way around for many quarters up until Q1.

items.statement: Mohey productivity reached near Manyavar levels (25-30% area, 25-30% sales); Twamev growing strongly in metros
items.quote: Earlier, it used to achieve close to 70% of Manyavar's productivity within that area. But now what we are witnessing with all the new stores and even the older stores, we have reached almost Manyavar's productivity.

items.statement: ASP grew ~1-1.5% in Q3; premium and value ends growing, middle segment weak
items.quote: At a company level, our ASP has grown by about 1% or 1.5%. But if you see from a market angle, this has been quite varied. So we see both the premium end growing and the bottom end growing from our company's perspective.

items.statement: Middle-class discretionary spending weak; AP & Telangana macro headwinds persist
items.quote: We don't feel that competition per se has played a big role. But yes, we do feel at a macro level, there are some headwinds where the middle class is definitely sort of not back at the level of consumption when it comes to apparel as they used to be.

items.statement: Rental inflation in core markets delaying store signings; other brands signing at high rents
items.quote: The challenge lies in core markets where demand is already high, where the prices are becoming very difficult. So those are the kind of markets where the pain lies in terms of rental inflation.

items.statement: January trends similar to Q3; only 15 days of normal trading observed so far
items.quote: I think broadly, it's -- what we have seen is only 30 days, of which 15 days are always slower than normal period. So we have only seen about 15 days of January. But in the current 30 days, it's been similar to Q3.

items.statement: Online channel ~3-4% of sales; grew ~70% in Q3 driven by Diwas, quick commerce, manyavar.com
items.quote: It's about 3% to 4%, but our growth has been very strong in the online segment. We have been growing probably the fastest in that as a channel. And overall, about 70-odd percent growth is what we've seen in Q3 when it comes to online.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance raised to INR 510-520 crores from earlier INR 475-500 crores
items.quote: But definitely, we may cross INR 500 crores, we may reach somewhere between INR 510 crore, and INR 520 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 25-30% over FY25 with 15-20% organic and 10% acquisitive
items.quote: At least 25% to 30%. On which may be , because this year itself, if you see the 41% growth on that 25% is organic growth. So next year, if we say 25% to 30%, maybe 15%. Conservatively 15% to 20% can be organic growth balance 10% can be acquisitive growth.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance of 23% reported and 25% adjusted; PAT margin 15.5-16%
items.quote: Expected EBITDA margin we can see around same 24%, 25%. If you take all these adjustments, adjusted EBITDA definitely can be 25%. If non-adjusted EBITDA can be 23%. And then the PAT 15.5% to 16%.

items.statement: European acquisition target of EUR 10-12 million revenue size at 10x EBITDA or 1x revenue
items.quote: Size is, we are not looking at very big size because then it will be a very high share dilution and then the other thing will be otherwise, we have to again go to QIP and those kind of things or swap those kind of things. So we are looking at anywhere up to EUR 10 million - EUR 12 million size only, not beyond that.

items.statement: CCA guidelines force retail pricing with 40-50% commission, reducing gross margin percentage but not amount
items.quote: Nowadays, by the guideline we are forced to sell at the retail price and then pay a commission to the partner, so that way, and the commission varies from 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Digital signature volumes declined 40-50% due to income tax rule changes and 10-12 new competitors
items.quote: Volume declined, as I told last time, almost 40% to 50% volume decline is there, one, volume decline is due to the income tax.

items.statement: Cybersecurity now 75% of enterprise revenue vs 25% paperless; cybersecurity growing faster with less competition
items.quote: Today, that is maybe 25% only or 23%, balance 75% is the cybersecurity business.

items.statement: Stock repurchase of INR 2.5-3 crores per quarter to continue until September 2025
items.quote: It may go up to September of next year, because otherwise, if we commit to repurchase everything together, then suddenly, we have to sell out all the money and the partners also will not be focused on selling our stock there because today, too many competi tors some 13 - 14 people have

items.statement: US quarterly revenue INR 40-45 crores; CLM sold to large orgs like SBI, LIC, Qatar Commercial Bank
items.quote: US top line for the quarter maybe around between INR 40 crores to INR 45 crores.

items.statement: Cash balance stable at INR 166-167 crores end of Q3 FY25
items.quote: Cash balance, last quarter end was INR 167 crores. This quarter end also around INR 166 crores or INR 167 crores is there.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 7% (approx. Rs 305-310 crore) maintained; FY26 revenue growth expected at 30-35% with corresponding EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: For the 9 months FY '25, our EBITDA, operating EBITDA margin stands at 7.2% against a guidance of 7% given at the start of the year. For the quarter, notably, this stands at 9.1%. So, this gives us confidence that 7% achievement would be possible, and if any movement, it will be only north of 7% in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Open order book ~Rs 5,300 crore as of Dec 2024; execution over 9-15 months; auto ~30%, consumer ~38-40%, industrial ~20-22%, balance healthcare/IT/railways
items.quote: Coming to our open order book visibility a s on date, as on December 2024, it is around 5,300 crores, which comprises almost 30% plus of contribution from auto segment, about 38 to 40% from consumer segment , approximately 20-22% from industrial segment and balance from healthcare plus IT and railway segment as well

items.statement: Q3 FY25 operating EBITDA margin 9.1% (up from 7.2% 9M); 9M gross margin 21.3%, Q3 gross margin 26.7% (+200bps QoQ); improvement driven by product mix shift and operating efficiencies
items.quote: This quarter, we had a strong rebound of the margins led by expansion in gross margins on the back of change in the business mix. The consumer sector business is slightly lower than other segments here. The gross margin for the 9 month is 21.3% and for the quarter it is with a very healthy gross margin of about 26.7%. Broadly 200 bps of expansion on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Consumer share down to 31% in Q3 (from 54% in Q1, ~40% 9M); target to reduce high-volume consumer to ~35% of revenue; auto 24% in Q3 (21% 9M), industrial 30% in Q3 (25% 9M)
items.quote: For example, in Q3, my consumer business is only 31%, high-volume consumer business, which is a tight-margin business, whereas my industrial business is 30% for three months against the average of 25% for 9 months. My automotive is 24% of my revenue for this quarter comes from automotive. For 9 months it is 21%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 capex ~Rs 180 crore (Pune campus, Germany facility, SMT lines); Q4 FY25 ~Rs 32 crore; FY25 total Rs 200-245 crore; FY26 Rs 100-150 crore
items.quote: Coming to my capex, for this 9 months we had spent approximately 180 crores of CAPEX and largely towards building up this new campus facility in Pune and a facility there in Germany. Some bit of additional capex towards some SMT lines and plant and machinery stuffing for new customers' onboarding.

items.statement: Exports at 20% of revenue (down from 25%) due to Germany slowdown; expect rebound in FY26 but gradual; target exports north of 25-30% long-term; MedTech delayed ~9 months, expected to rebound in FY26
items.quote: Exports stand at about 20%. Exports have had a subdued sort of muted scenario because our geographies which we are servicing are essentially America and Europe. And in Europe, it's primarily Germany. And Germany is today the sick baby of EU. It has the highest delinquencies per month. So, we have had muted growth, but the turnaround is visible from the orders and the indications which we have rece

items.statement: Germany export market weak (highest delinquencies in EU); US policy uncertainty under Trump; consumer price renegotiations ongoing; working capital at 64 days (target <60 days)
items.quote: Germany is today the sick baby of EU. It has the highest delinquencies per month. So, we have had muted growth, but the turnaround is visible from the orders and the indications which we have received for the next year, that is FY '25-'26, I think will rebound back though it will be a painful and a long journey.

items.statement: QIP approved but not initiated; only for future growth opportunities (inorganic/OSAT), not for existing business; sufficient internal accruals for current growth
items.quote: We have taken our QIP approv al just to be ready for any future growth. We have never contemplated any growth. J. S. Gujral: Inorganic. Bijay Agrawal: We have never contemplated QIP for our existing business related any kind of a working capital funding. That's very clear

items.statement: ROCE target 14.5-15% FY25, 18-20% by FY27; asset turn 5.5-5.6x currently, targeting 6-7x; tax rate ~23-25%; PLI accrual ~Rs 14 cr 9M FY25 (full year ~Rs 15-17 cr)
items.quote: That's right. That's what we are also targeting. My overhead costs are much more stable now and the expansions have largely been taken care of. So, with this, the way we are anticipating next quarter also, we are targeting like this year we should be closing around 14.5% to 15% of ROCE and gradually it should then move towards our targeted ROCE of 20% over the next two years.

items.statement: New automotive/industrial clients onboarded in Q3; expected sub-Rs 200 cr revenue in FY26, significant in FY27; Pune campus commissioned Oct 2024, ramping up; Germany facility nearing commissioning
items.value: Sub-Rs 200 cr FY26 from new clients
items.quote: We have onboarded some good automotive and industrial clients in the current quarter , and going forward, which will be '26-'27, we expect significant business from these clien ts. In '25- '26, these clients will be yielding sub-200 crores of revenues

items.statement: Railway revenue ~Rs 70 cr FY25, targeting Rs 100+ cr FY26; signaling equipment ~50%, locomotive/wagon ~50%; MedTech order book 7-7.5% of total, targeting Rs 150-200 cr FY26
items.quote: I think we have guided that this year we will be doing about 70 crores of revenue from the railways, and we are on track to achieve that revenue this year. New product approvals are in pipeline. So, till those product approvals by RDSO happen, because every product has to be approved by RDSO, it will be tough to give a figure, but I believe that next year, this figure should be higher than 70 cror

items.statement: Working capital 64 days (Dec 2024), target <60 days sustainable; gross debt Rs 685 cr, treasury Rs 412 cr, net debt Rs 273 cr; term loan only Rs 65 cr
items.quote: On the working capital side, currently, as on quarter end, we st ood at around 64 days of net working capital days investments. Again, it is slightly higher than the last quarter. We continue to make efforts to keep this net working capital below 60 days on a sustainable basis

items.statement: Merger with Syrma SGS Johari Digital MedTech Devices pending NCLT final order; expected completion in 3-6 months
items.quote: Slight a bit of update on the merger side. We are waiting for the final order from the NCLT, and we hope we should be able to complete this merger in another 3-6 months of time.

items.statement: Renewing consumer contracts to improve margins; deliberate strategy to keep consumer volume in check for PLI optimization and margin improvement
items.quote: What we have done in the last quarter is that we have started renegotiating prices for the high volume consumer business to see whether we can have a bump in some margins or not. And that is a long-term strategy of the company to move to the high-profit, high-margin business, low-medium-volume, high-margin business.

items.statement: Industrial segment driven by smart metering, power supplies for data centers, solar trackers/inverters, industrial cleaning, automation; new global client for interface cars in high volume
items.quote: Just to delve on the applications within the industrial segment, utility metering, including smart metering, whether for gas, electricity or water is one dominant component. Power supplies and power management units for data centers is another dominant segment. Industrial cleaning, wet dry steam is a decent-sized business. Then we have into the renewable like solar trackers or solar inverters, whi

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance revised down; large order conversion delayed to Q1-Q2 FY26, only run-rate business expected in Q4 FY25
items.quote: While I'm not able to give you a very specific number, but mostly the conversion that will happen in this year in the remaining quarter is going to be from the run-rate business that we get.

items.statement: Order book at INR 21 crores as of 31 Dec; L1 pipeline increased to INR 400+ crores from INR 300 crores, entirely international
items.quote: Our order book as of 31st December stood at approximately INR 21 crores, with an L1 opportunity pipeline of INR 400-plus crores now as compared to INR 300 crores earlier.

items.statement: Demand-to-order conversion below expectations in first 3 quarters due to elections and delayed government procurements; larger opportunities expected shortly
items.quote: The year so far has been a mixed bag for us and the drone industry. While a lot of development is happening on new use cases, products and technologies, the demand-to-order conversion in the first 3 quarters of the year has been below industry expectations.

items.statement: International L1 pipeline now INR 400+ crores, all from abroad; tracking 25+ international opportunities including 12+ in North America and 6 in Africa
items.quote: A lot of this L1 pipeline is actually emanating from our international efforts right now. So there, we don't have that immediate dependency from the Indian MOD right now in this L1 pipeline.

items.statement: R&D expenses to increase slightly in absolute terms from INR 53 crores in FY24
items.quote: Hardik, the percentage, of course, will be determined at the end of the year, but the R&D expenses will go up slightly from last year, for sure.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin 46% on INR 8.1 cr gross profit; 9M FY25 gross margin 32.6% on INR 45.9 cr gross profit; EBITDA and PAT negative
items.quote: For the quarter, gross profit stood at INR 8.1 crores, with a gross profit margin of 46%. For 9 months FY '25, gross profit stood at INR 45.9 crores, with a gross profit margin of 32.6%.

items.statement: Order conversion delays due to government dynamics in India and Africa; international deal cycles longer than expected with licensing hurdles
items.quote: Conversion is still taking more time because of several challenges in the, you can say, dynamics of those deals in terms of not the deal itself but, let's say, peripheral issues around governments, etcetera.

items.statement: Next-gen products NETRA 5 and SWITCH V2 ready for customer demos, unveiling at Aero India 2025; tactical UAV and 500kg logistics platform development on track
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you that two of our next-generation products, NETRA 5 and SWITCH V2 are now ready for customer demonstrations, and we'll be officially unveiling them at the global flagship event in the coming month, the Aero India 2025.

items.statement: Unit 2 Phase 1 added 120 KL capacity, Phase 2 added 37 KL capacity; both now on stream
items.quote: In Phase 1, we added 120 KL capacity. And in Phase 2, we added another 37 KL capacity. The capacity that we had added in Phase 1 is now on stream, producing the cardiovascular intermediate optimally. The capacity that we added in Phase 2 has also gone live, and we are happy to announce that the validation batches for the contrast media intermediate have been successfully completed, and the first q

items.statement: Capitalized INR 1,000 million in 9M FY25; spent INR 620 million; plan additional INR 1,500 million on existing projects mostly at Mahad; INR 400 million R&D capex slated for FY26
items.value: INR 1,500 million additional; INR 400 million R&D
items.quote: During the 9-month period, we have capitalized production capacities amounting to INR1,000 million. Apart from this, we have spent around INR620 million, and we hope to spend an additional INR1,500 million on the existing projects, mostly in Mahad. As Shiven mentioned, we will also be investing around INR400 million in R&D, which is slated in FY 26.

items.statement: Targeting loan book growth of 20% plus in FY25
items.quote: Going forward, we remain committed towards achieving our loan book growth of 20% plus in FY '25 by capitalizing on the growing MSME, mortgage segment coupled with expanding middle income group segment.

items.statement: Targeting annualized ROA of 1.4% plus for FY25
items.quote: Our focus on expansion of NIM, NII and increasing fee income will be the key drivers for our targeted ROA -- annualized ROA of 1.4% plus for FY '25.

items.statement: Intend to expand CD ratio to mid- to high 80s in FY26
items.quote: We intend to expand our CD ratios to mid- to the high 80s in FY '26.

items.statement: Aspirational ROE target of mid- to high teens
items.quote: Our endeavour is to be hit the next capital market when we have ROEs in the mid to the high teens.

items.statement: NIM increased to 4.3% in Q3 FY25 from 3.9% a year ago
items.quote: NIM has increased to 4.3% in Q3 FY '25 against 3.9% in the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Targeting NIM expansion via CD ratio increase; every 100 bps CD ratio rise adds 4-5 bps to NIM
items.quote: As per the back of envelope calculation, if all other factors remain constant, that is our interest spread between the cost of deposits and yield on advances remain constant, with every 100 basis point increase in the average CD ratio, so there is a benefi t in the NIM by around 0.04% to 0.05

items.statement: Cost of funds at 6% and cost of deposits at 5.9% in Q3 FY25, flat QoQ
items.quote: The cost of funds for Q3 FY '25 stood at 6% against 6% a quarter back and cost of deposit being also 5.9% as was during the last quarter.

items.statement: Q3 historically sees muted advance demand due to harvest season; reversed trend with 2% QoQ growth
items.quote: If I look historically,, in last year FY '24, we degrew in Q3 by 3%. And in FY '23, we de-grew by 2%. So we are able to reverse that particular trend.

items.statement: Opex to average assets at 3.05-3.2%; expected to remain flat for next 12 months, then improve
items.quote: The opex, which is presently, on the basis of the Opex to the average assets is typically in the range of 3.05% to 3.15%/ 3.2%. I believe for the next 1 year, it will remain in the similar range, plus/minus 5 basis to 10 basis points.

items.statement: Punjab concentration reduced from 82.68% (Mar'23) to 79.11% (Dec'24); targeting Haryana as next Punjab
items.quote: Statistically, if you look into this particular number, as on March 31, 2023, the Punjab advances constituting 82.68%, which presently as on December 31, 2024 end, it is 79.11%. So we are able to reduce it by around 3.5% to 4%.

items.statement: Fee income expected at 0.9-1% of assets in Q4 FY25 due to accounting timing and advance growth
items.quote: Going forward, in Q4, I'm anticipating our fee income to be in the range of 0.85% or rather 0.9% to 1% in the Q4.

items.statement: Company aims to continue 20-25% average annual growth with specialty wire vertical as additional driver
items.quote: So, sir as a company, even in the last 10 years we have grown at 20 % to25% on an average, which is what we want to continue going ahead . With this we are also adding specialty wire vertical which is a new vertical and which is also one of our main focus areas.

items.statement: Dadri expansion increased from 3.5 to 4.2 lakh tonnes with additional Rs 70-80 crore investment
items.period: first two quarters of next year
items.quote: Now we have increased that by about 20% to 4. 2 lakh tonnes. This is owning to some demand that we are looking at in different products from our customers. Therefore our investment will also increase by about ₹ 70 to 80 crores in total.

items.statement: Stainless steel rod backward integration land acquisition in Sanand Gujarat finalized, equipment orders within 2 months, production in FY27
items.quote: Within a week we should have the possession on the land. And apart from that, even the equipment's, we are in daily touch with our manufacturers and we should be able to finalize some orders within the next two months. After this, it will take us about 15 to 18 months to really establish them and start production.

items.statement: Specialty wire pilot project 20,000 tonnes capacity with Rs 150 crore invested for steel cord
items.quote: With a 150 crore CAPEX that we have almost already done is only for steel cord .

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical selling 100-120 tonnes in first month January with expedited approvals for hose wire and steel cord
items.quote: We have got very good response, and in fact as we speak, we are able to sell about 100 to120 tonnes within this first month January.

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical targets 20-25% EBITDA margin versus current lower margins
items.quote: The revenue potential of this product for us right now is about ₹300 crore, in which if you look at the current prices, or the prices that were prevailing in the market till now, it has been about 20% to25% kind of an EBITDA that we look at, which is fairly different from our current numbers.

items.statement: Strong demand across all sectors in Q4 with automotive gaining market share despite seasonal slowdown
items.quote: So right now, it is all about producing more, because sales is not a challenge. So even in Q4 we see a good demand from our customers coming across all products, not just one, all high carbon stainless steel as well as low carbon we see a good response.

items.statement: Consolidation of group companies drove 25-30% volume growth in Q3 with 10-15% organic volume increase
items.quote: So you will see about 25% to 30% kind of a growth here, in which I would say most of it has come because of consolidation. So about 10% to 15% is the volume increase that we have done quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Raw material price fluctuations and geopolitical risks persist as challenges
items.quote: While challenges like fluctuating raw material prices and geopolitical risk persist, we see immense opportunity in both domestic as well as the export market.

items.statement: Natural hedge model with 70-75% orders backed by inventory or supplier orders, cost-plus pricing passes raw material changes to customers
items.quote: So, sir what we try to do is we try to create a kind of a natural hedge in our business model, wherein whatever orders we have is we already have either inventory or pending orders from our raw material suppliers. So therefore we try to keep about a 70% to 75% of our pending orders and stock booked against firm orders.

items.statement: IHT wire investment expedited with orders placed, targeting Q1 commissioning
items.quote: We were supposed to start investment in IHT wire by mid of next year, but we have already placed some orders, and we will hopefully do something within the first quarter.

items.statement: Dadri facility at 30% utilization with 80% of 3.5 lakh tonne capacity commissioned, full commissioning in 2 months
items.quote: We have now touched about 30% kind of a utilization level in Dadri. Deepesh Kashyap: And sir capacity is how much right now? Pranav Bansal: Sir the capacity, I would say about 80% of our capacity has already been commissioned, and the balance is also being commissioning w ithin the next two months, we should be able to commission the complete 3.5 lakh

items.statement: Export revenue reached Rs 250 crore in 9M FY25 versus Rs 219 crore in corresponding period
items.quote: Our export also accounted to about 250 crores till the end of Q 3 as against 219 crores compared to the corresponding year underscoring strong international demand from our products and new product offering.

items.statement: Working capital optimization through bill discounting to start next quarter or Q1 next year after consolidation
items.period: next quarter or Q1 of next year
items.quote: But after the consolidation of Balaji and Bansal High Carbon within Bansal Wire, now we see that maybe next quarter, or from Q 1 of next year we will start utilization which will bring our debt level down as well.

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical includes steel cord (import substitute), hose wire, bead wire, and IHT wire for EVs
items.quote: the main product in specialty wire vertical is a product that we call steel cord. Now, steel cord is a product that, we will be the first and the only Indian company to make this product t ill now. This is used in tyres

items.statement: Revised full-year FY25 revenue growth guidance to 30% from 25%
items.quote: In the light of 33% year-on-year top-line growth reported for the first 9 -months of FY25, we are revising our full-year guidance to 30% growth from 25% for FY25.

items.statement: Pre-IND AS EBITDA guidance for FY25 is INR950-980 million
items.quote: We are on track to close the financial year with an EBITDA of around INR950-INR980 million.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance 7-8% and PAT margin 3-4% on pre-IND AS basis
items.quote: And on the guidance on the EBITDA margin, it will be between 7% to 8%. And on the PAT side, it will be between 3 to 4%.

items.statement: Targeting 25-30% revenue growth with 8-10% L2L growth as balanced strategy
items.quote: We would like to grow ourselves between 25%-30% in terms of revenue with an L2L growth of around 8 %-10%.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at INR60-65 crores for 40-50 stores plus INR15-20 crores for tech/infra
items.quote: So you can expect anything between INR60-65 crores on that side, and apart from that if there is any other capex expansion going in the warehouse or the infra side that will be the additional cost on that.

items.statement: Net store additions of 37 in 9M FY25; expect 45-50 net additions for full FY25
items.quote: We now expect to add between 45-50 stores by the end of this fiscal year, further strengthening our footprint and positioning us for continued growth.

items.statement: Store-level pre-IND AS EBITDA margin improved to 14.23% in 9M FY25 from 14.08%
items.quote: So for the first 9 months, it is around 14.23% against 14.08% last year , for the full 9 months , including new stores.

items.statement: Corporate overheads increased 0.85% of sales to INR60-65 crores in 9M FY25 from INR40-45 crores
items.quote: So, approximately around INR60 crores-INR65 crores has been the corporate overheads for the first 9 months, against which last year it was around INR40 crores-INR45 crores.

items.statement: Private label margin premium only 0.5% due to aggressive pricing for market share
items.quote: Against which, 0.5% has been the higher margin that we are earning on private labels. But as a strategy, because we want to expand our footprint in all the areas and expand our private label brands in all the areas. As a strategy, we are going for an aggressive pricing.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook for Q4 FY25 driven by wedding season and Eid
items.quote: With the wedding season and the Eid approaching, we expect a strong performance in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Private label contribution 44% in 9M FY25 vs 37% in 9M FY24; apparel 87%, general merchandise 13%
items.quote: Private label contribution was at 38% in Q3 FY25 vs 35% in Q3 FY24 and 44% in 9 -months FY25 vs 37% in 9-months FY24. Our inventory per square feet has reduced by INR200 sq. ft from last year.

items.statement: Insurance claim of INR48 crores pending from Q1 fire incident; expected by March end
items.quote: So, around INR48 crores is the expectation amount from the insurance company which is due as of now. So, that fund is also utilized in this limit.

items.statement: Net debt INR100 crores (bank borrowings) plus INR16 crores bill acceptance; cash INR14.63 crores
items.quote: So, net debt is INR100 crores -- bank borrowings is INR100 crores, and bill acceptance is INR16 crores, total debt in books is INR116 crores, and cash and bank balance is INR14.63 crores.

items.statement: Inventory reduced to INR2,100 per sq ft from INR2,300; inventory days 112; creditor days 72 vs 83 last year
items.quote: In terms of inventory, we have reduced our inventory by INR200 per square feet from last year. So we were at INR2300 per square feet inventory, 9 -months FY24, which is around INR2100 per square feet as on 9-months FY25.

items.statement: 90% full-price sales in 9M FY25; mature store sales INR9,000/sq ft annualized
items.quote: 90% is the full price sale through for the first 9 months.

items.statement: Order book at end of Q3 FY25 stood at INR19,971 crores; INR12,244 crores under execution, INR4,642 crores awaiting appointed dates, INR3,084 crores L1 status
items.quote: At the end of third quarter, the order book stood in INR19,971 crores. INR12,244 crores worth of the projects are under execution, INR4,642 crores awaiting appointed dates and the rest that is INR3,084 crores include one project each of roads and OFC that are having L1 status.

items.statement: Declared L1 for Maharashtra road project INR1,947 crores and Western Railway project INR222 crores in January; 13 projects worth INR13,992 crores submitted and expected to open soon
items.quote: On a separate note, I'm happy to share that we have been declared L1 for the road project in Maharashtra, amounting to INR1,947 crores and a Rail Project of Western Railways amounting INR222 crores for this month that is in January. As on date, the company has submitted 13 highway, railway and ropeway projects amounting to INR13,992 crores, which are expected to be opened soon.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow target revised to INR17,000 crores from INR20,000 crores; FY26 order inflow target INR20,000 crores
items.quote: Current year, we are targeting almost INR17,000 crores of the orders in flow, right? Yes. So next year -- I mean, this year, our target -- original target was INR20,000 crores, so we'll try to stick with that for next year as well.

items.statement: FY25 capex not more than INR125 crores (INR30-40 crores remaining in Q4); FY26 capex maximum INR150 crores
items.quote: The capex, we are not expecting more than -- for the full year not more than INR125 crores. So maybe another INR30 crores, INR40 crores for the current year or for next year, again, because capex, we are, I would say, fairly -- capex is already having we are in our balance sheet, so we don't expect much -- I mean, there is not significant difference from what we have been doing for last 2 years, s

items.statement: Awarding activity muted in first 3 quarters with underbidding up to 40%; expect decent flow of large projects in Q4 FY25 given budget allocation; targeting INR1,35,000 crores pipeline across highways, tunnels, metro, power transmission, rai
items.quote: This year, awarding activity is a little muted in the first 3 quarters, also the instance of underbidding up to 40% persist. Having said that, looking at the central government's budgetary allocation towards infrastructure, we expect a decent flow of awarding utilities, especially large projects coming in the last quarter. The company is targeting an order pipeline of approximately INR1,35,000 cro

items.statement: Diversifying beyond roads into transmission, ropeway, tunneling, metros, telecom; road share of new orders not more than 30-40%; will bid for BOT annuity and BOT toll projects
items.quote: we are not targeting 50%. I would say road would be not more than 30% or 40% because given the competition so far, it has not yet come to that level, right? So what we believe is that we'll be bidding into different, different sectors, maybe transmission, ropeway, then road also. And then, Tunneling is also there, right

items.statement: InvIT income INR178 crores YTD FY25, INR39-40 crores in Q3, expecting INR60 crores in Q4; FY26-27 run rate INR200-250 crores
items.quote: for last quarter -- I mean, the quarter ended December 2024, we have received that in -- around INR39 crores or INR40 crores from InvIT, right, for the -- so far -- I mean, for the year, it is INR178 crores, the income which we have received from the InvIT, right? For last quarter, it was INR39 crores or INR40-odd crores. On -- in current quarter -- I mean, in Q4 for the current fiscal, we are exp

items.statement: Phase-2 brownfield expansion capex of Rs. 700 crores; Rs. 480 crores spent till 31 Dec 2024; minor delay of 2-3 months due to manpower and equipment supply delays
items.quote: On the ongoing brownfield expansion to reach capacities of 1 million tons of DI pipes, out of our planned CAPEX of Rs. 700 crores for Phase-2, we have already spent Rs. 480 crores till 31st of December. There is a minor delay of around 2-3 months on account of manpower shortage and delays in supply of equipment, and we are hopeful to reach installed capacity of 9 lakh tons by the end of March 2025

items.statement: Order book of around 8.5 months, approximately 6 lakh tons of DI pipes
items.quote: So, we have around 8-1/2 months of order book at the moment, so around 6 lakh tons of DI pipes.

items.statement: Demand for DI pipes remains robust driven by River Linking, Viksit Bharat, Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0; momentary government spending pause expected to reverse post Budget
items.quote: The demand for DI pipes and fittings continues to be robust on account of initiatives like River Linking, Viksit Bharat Vision, Jal Jeevan Mission and AMRUT 2.0. Although there is a pause for some time from the government on spending, which has been seen across all sectors, we are optimistic the government will continue to push towards infrastructure spending from the upcoming Union Budget FY2025-

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to sustain at 16%-18% range; currently at 16.7% standalone
items.quote: I think historically, if you see these, we have always hit a margin of 15%-18%. At the moment, we are at 16.7%. I think these are pretty stable numbers which we should be able to carry on for the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Coking coal prices down $35-$40; iron ore prices up; net raw material cost impact neutralized
items.quote: Actually, in the raw material front, on the coke front, and coking coals and all that, there has been a downward trend. And the price correction to the tune of some $35-$40 has come down, but at the same time, as far as iron ore is concerned, there has been a upward trend, so practically on raw material front, they have neutralized each other, more or less.

items.statement: US export business hit due to market slowdown and tariff concerns; now only 1% of exports vs 5% earlier; no immediate local manufacturing solution
items.quote: So, there is an overall slowdown in the US market for our product as a whole. And secondly, because of the impending possibilities of tariffs that to come and Made in America programs that are there. The customers are a little apprehensive in buying non-American products right now.

items.statement: Fittings volume increased ~3,000 tons in 9M FY25 vs prior year; targeting 25,000 tons; expanding coatings/linings portfolio
items.quote: In fact, let me highlight the fittings numbers, we have already seen an increase of approximately 3000 tons this Financial Year, 9 months average as opposed to last year and this is all owing to the addition of new product lines. So as such, we are looking at going up to 25,000 odd tons over there.

items.statement: Anti-subsidy refund of Rs. 23 crores received from European Commission in Q3; ongoing annual process, amount varies
items.quote: So, Sir, this is on account of anti-subsidy refund that we have got from the European Commission. There is an anti-subsidy duty that they avail on us, but we keep applying for refunds and we have managed to get a refund of Rs. 23 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: JSW coal block asset valuation and categorization ongoing; mine handed over but underground infrastructure nil; claim of Rs. 1,200 crores, majority expected to be realized
items.quote: Our claim is of Rs. 1200 crores so the way it is going on we are optimistic that the majority of this will be realized.

items.statement: Odisha greenfield project ~4-5 lakh tons capacity; realistic timeline FY27-28
items.quote: I think somewhere between FY27-28 is a bit more realistic.

items.statement: No demand-supply mismatch expected for next 3 years; live orders indicate demand will surpass supply once fund flows restart
items.quote: I am not really concerned about demand supply mismatch whether supply is more at least for the next 3 years. There might be temporary blips like we have seen in the last quarter, but that is very momentary. The kind of live orders in the market, once the fund flow start we will go back to a situation where demand is surpassing supply.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 and FY26 EBITDA margin expected to hold at 16%-18% range; difficult to give per-ton rupee guidance
items.quote: Sir, I think it will be difficult for me to give you an exact number in terms of rupees per ton, but as a percentage, I think we will be able to hold on to the performance we had so far.

items.statement: Momentary slowdown in Jal Jeevan Mission and AMRUT 2.0 tender outflows in Q3-Q4 FY25; expect recovery post Budget and in new financial year
items.quote: Definitely, there was a bit of a slowdown in Q3 and even in Q4FY25. As of now, it is not at the same pace that it was at say last quarter 3 and quarter 4. But as with all other infrastructure spending such as railway and highways, we are pretty sure that come the new Financial Year and even the last one or two months of this quarter with the budget coming out tomorrow, there will be a good allocat

items.statement: Cement demand expected to grow 4-5% in FY25 with H2 much better than H1
items.quote: This demand is expected to grow by 4% to 5% in FY '25, meaning H2 should be much better than H1, further supported by pro infra and housing budget in the 2025.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex target around INR9,000 crores with INR6,200 crores spent in 9 months
items.quote: For the full year, it is closer to INR9,000 crores. And so, another INR2,200 crores will go for this quarter.

items.statement: Capacity expansion to 140 million tons by FY28 on track with Orient acquisition taking capacity to 97 million tons
items.quote: As we plan to expand our cement capacity to 140 million tons by FY '28, we are pacing well to achieve the stated target.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 18.4% in Q3 FY25 with EBITDA per ton of INR1,038
items.quote: With improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR1,712 crores at a margin of 18.4% and EBITDA per ton of INR1,038.

items.statement: Operational cost at INR4,618 per ton in Q3 FY25, targeting INR3,650-3,700 by FY28
items.quote: Operational costs for the quarter is at INR 4,618 per ton. This is driven by a 7% decline in energy cost owing to better fuel management and strong focus on green power.

items.statement: Power and fuel costs decreased 7% to INR1,262 per ton in Q3 FY25 from INR1,355 per ton in Q3 FY24
items.quote: Driven by better fuel management and structural initiatives, our power and fuel costs have decreased 7% to INR1,262 per ton in Q3 FY '25 from INR1,355 per ton in Q3 last year.

items.statement: Logistics costs reduced 6% to INR1,239 per ton in Q3 FY25 from INR1,322 per ton in Q3 FY24
items.quote: Because of these initiatives, our logistics costs have been reduced by 6% to INR1,239 per ton in Q3 FY '25 from INR1,322 per ton in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: Green power share increased to 21.5% from 15.8%, targeting 60% of power requirements through green power by FY28
items.quote: Both WHRS and solar power would ensure that 60% of our power requirements are -- of the planned 140 million tons would be through green power.

items.statement: Industry demand growth was tepid 1.5-2% in H1 FY25, expected to rebound to 4-5% in FY25
items.quote: The improved consumption demand in housing and infrastructure segments and increased government spendings are poised to reverse the tepid 1.5% to 2% cement demand growth during H1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Blended cements at 82%, premium products as percentage of trade sales volume increased 400 bps to 26%
items.quote: blended cements at 82%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales volume by 400 bps to 26 percentage.

items.statement: Sanghi and Penna assets currently at sub-40% and sub-50% utilization, expected to reach 70%+ in next financial year
items.quote: My estimate is in the next financial year, both the assets should go up, I think Sanghi earlier and Penna because it's also in the market where it takes time to ramp up. But both of them should hit 70% plus utilization levels in the next financial year.

items.statement: Net worth increased to almost INR63,000 crores from INR51,000 crores in April, company remains nil debt with AAA rating
items.quote: I'm glad to share that we have achieved a net worth of almost INR63,000 crores, which was in April INR51,000 crores, so almost up by INR12,000 crores. And we remain nil debt and with the highest rating of AAA.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition cash outflow around INR4,000 crores in Q4 FY25, open offer separate later
items.quote: in terms of the expected outgo for Orient, that is ballpark around INR4,000-odd crores, which will be there.

items.statement: Incentive income expected to increase from INR400-500 crores annually to INR600-650 crores prospectively with new capacities
items.quote: Historically, say, it was around, say, INR100-odd crores of incentive per quarter, almost INR400 crores for a year. But this will actually now start moving up to INR600 crores, INR650-odd crores prospectively with new capacities coming in and giving the benefit of incentives.

items.statement: 200 MW solar power project at Khavda, Gujarat commissioned in Q3 FY25, 1000 MW RE target by June 2026
items.quote: 200-megawatt solar power, the project in Gujarat, Khavda, has been commissioned in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: 631 million tons of new limestone reserves secured in Q3 FY25, one mine in MP and one in Karnataka
items.quote: To secure our limestone supplies in Q3 FY '25, we have won bids for another 2 mines having reserves of 631 million tons, one in MP and one in Karnataka.

items.statement: Expect to launch at least 1 million sq ft of retail GLA each year from FY27 onwards and deliver on pipeline by FY2030
items.quote: we expect to launch at least 1 million square feet each year from 2027 onwards as well. And we are well to deliver on that pipeline that we had anticipated by FY 2030.

items.statement: 9M FY25 capex was Rs 1,758 crores including Rs 965 crores for land acquisitions and Rs 793 crores construction cost
items.quote: Capital expenditure for 9MFY25 was at Rs. 1,758 crores which includes acquisition of three assets, mainly the Mittal land (in Bangalore), Coimbatore and Chandigarh, total amount is Rs. 965 crores and the total construction cost is around Rs. 793 crores.

items.statement: Palladium Mumbai expansion 250,000 sq ft is about 90% leased; rental impact expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: Yes, it's about 90% leased. We are holding onto some space, because as the retailers commence their operations there, there is the opportunity to extract premium rentals from the last remaining space.

items.statement: St Regis Mumbai Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin about 49%; Courtyard Agra EBITDA margin 37%
items.quote: Income for Q3 FY25 at The St. Regis, Mumbai, was Rs. 148 crores with an EBITDA of Rs. 72 crores, representing healthy EBITDA margins at about 49%.

items.statement: Residential pricing at Rs 26,100 per sq ft for 9M FY25; management will not drop pricing to accelerate sales
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier in my communication, we are currently at about Rs. 26,100 or thereabouts per square foot is the current pricing. And we have really inched it forward, we have set a new benchmark

items.statement: January consumption extraordinary across portfolio; confident of significant consumption growth ahead
items.quote: Well, i f we go by how January has panned out for us, it's been extraordinary across the portfolio. So I cannot crystal gaze, on how the consumption will be for the rest of the year. But we are very, very confident that we are going to continue to see a significant growth in consumption

items.statement: Retail strategy: premiumization, category upgradation, F&B densification, optimized store sizes, new brands like Bershka
items.quote: We are now again at that same point where all of these assets we need to be working on premiumization, category upgradation, and of course optimizing the store size, introducing newer brands.

items.statement: Unseasonal heavy rains in Bangalore and Chennai impacted Q3 consumption by ~1.5% (Rs 55-60 crores)
items.quote: It is our estimate that our overall consumption would have been higher by about 1 .5%, approximating about Rs. 55 to Rs. 60 crores in Q3 FY25 had we not seen this unusual weather change.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA at 1.1x; average cost of borrowing reduced to 8.64% (20 bps lower vs Mar 2024)
items.quote: We reduced our average cost of borrowing to 8.64%, which is around 20 bps reduction as compared to March 2024, and we remain committed to the future optimization of our debt cost

items.statement: Thane retail mall 1.3M sq ft GLA; hope to break ground in calendar 2025 after approvals
items.quote: We are currently in the state of approvals, etc. and we hope that during this calendar year we will be able to break ground once we get all our approvals in place.

items.statement: Kolkata residential project One Belvedere launch expected mid to end Q1 FY26; work already commenced
items.quote: So, One Belvedere is the product , that's the name of our product . W e expect to launch it towards the middle or end of Q1 of FY26. And work is commencing over there already.

items.statement: Office portfolio to reach nearly 5 million sq ft by 2025 across Pune, Bangalore, Chennai
items.quote: Our office developments in Pune, Bangalore and Chenn ai will take our total commercial office portfolio to nearly 5 million square feet, in 2025.

items.statement: Core business 9M FY25 operating revenue Rs 2,613 crores (+19% YoY), EBITDA Rs 1,601 crores (+21% YoY)
items.quote: For 9M FY25, operating revenue from our core businesses stood at Rs. 2,613 crores, up 19% versus 9M FY24. EBITDA for the nine months from our core businesses was at Rs. 1,601 crores, up 21% versus 9M FY24.

items.statement: Retail consumption 9M FY25 Rs 10,500 crores (+23% YoY); Q3 FY25 consumption Rs 4,000+ crores (+21% YoY)
items.quote: Consumption reached Rs. 10,500 crores during the first nine months of this fiscal year, up 23% year-on-year.

items.statement: Trading occupancy 91% in Dec 2024 (up from 87% in Mar); new malls ramping fast: Palladium Ahmedabad 97%, Phoenix Mall of Millennium Pune 91%, Phoenix Mall of Asia 81%
items.quote: Trading occupancy continues to build strong momentum reaching 91% in December 2024, up 87% from March. Our newly launched malls are ramping up at an impressive pace, contributing significantly to this growth.

items.statement: Targeting at least 12% EBITDA margin overall for next financial year FY26
items.quote: Going forward, for the next financial year, we are targeting at least an EBITDA level overall with both garment chipping in very well since the restructuring has been done, Fabric growing, we expect the EBITDA level overall, regardless of what happens to the Yarn market to be at least 12%.

items.statement: Expecting 20% year-on-year growth in garment business for next 2-3 years without adding capacity
items.quote: So we are now looking at, in fact, in our garment business, a 20% growth year-on-year going forward for the next 2, 3 years without adding any more capacity.

items.statement: Expecting 20% year-on-year growth in Fabric division going forward
items.quote: We are expecting growth within the Fabric division of 20% going forward year-on-year and about similar growth in the Garment business.

items.statement: Capex plan for next year is INR50 crores in plant and machinery, with INR45 crores for Fabric, INR3 crores for Yarn, INR2 crores for Garment
items.quote: Our capex plan for the next year is about INR50 crores. Kavita Gandhi: In plant and machinery. Ravindra Toshniwal: In plant and machinery alone, out of which we are expecting to invest about INR45 crores into Fabric business, INR3 crores or so in the Yarn balancing and modernization and about INR2 crores in Garment

items.statement: Overall capex including infrastructure, power, civil and environmental enhancements expected at INR80-100 crores for next year in phased manner
items.quote: So overall, if we look at in the next year, we are looking at a capex of around INR80 crores to INR100 crores, all put together, but it will get into the phase manner.

items.statement: Order book looks good with inquiries and orders flowing in for Garment division, confident of completing existing orders on time
items.quote: We have inquiries and orders flowing in for our Garment division. The order book looks good, and we are confident of completing existing orders on time and continuing to get new orders.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 10.7% year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: The EBITDA margin in quarter 3 FY '25 stood at 10.7%. This is an improvement over year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin expected to be more or less same as Q3 at around 11.7%
items.quote: We achieved an EBITDA level of, I think, 11.7% almost in quarter 3. And quarter 4, we expect to do more or less the same or we'll see what it comes to, but we are expecting it to be more or less the same.

items.statement: Domestic demand subdued during Diwali and wedding season but company grew by substituting Chinese imports
items.quote: If we speak about the domestic market, the demand has been subdued in general, even across the last Diwali and the whole wedding season, the last wedding season, it wasn't great at all. And still we did manage growth within that in our fabric business.

items.statement: Export demand strong with good tailwinds from Bangladesh challenges and China Plus One, but margin pressure limits order conversion
items.quote: As far as exports is concerned, we do have a good tailwind in terms of sentiment. In terms of the fact that we actually conclud e deals, it is about margin. Having to compete on the margin and get the business, that is the

items.statement: Fabric and Garment business expected to increase from ~65% to 70% of total turnover
items.quote: We do expect that we can increase the percentage of our Fabric and Garment business to be even 70% of our turnover.

items.statement: India lacks trade pacts with Europe, putting it at duty disadvantage vs Bangladesh and Sri Lanka for garment exports
items.quote: India does not have trade pacts with Europe. And therefore, we are at a disadvantage as compared both to Sri Lanka and Bangladesh in dealing with Europe in terms of the duties applicable to our garments entering their countries.

items.statement: Buyers want Bangladesh-level landed prices with duty advantages, forcing margin sacrifices to win orders
items.quote: There are buyers who are willing to commit, but they want to commit at the same price that they would be buying from Bangladesh. And they have duty advantages which are coming from Bangladesh, and they want all of those advantages to get the same landed duty paid price as they would get from India, as they would get from Bangladesh from India. That we are not able to match without sacrificing marg

items.statement: SEZ to DTA transition will lose capacity for about a quarter but improve utilization by averaging domestic and export demand
items.quote: So we will lose capacity for about a quarter or so, before the capacity is utilized in a DTA across both Daman and Surat. So whatever capacity we had last year will now be able to be used across either export or domestic wherever demand is greater.

items.statement: Yarn division modernization expected to complete by Q1 FY26, improving productivity and value-added yarns
items.quote: So we're expecting by quarter 1 of the next financial year, everything will be gung-ho and going well in the Yarn division. The modernization will help us not only to get increased productivity per employee, but also improve the value-added yarns we make, both for internal consumption and external sales.

items.statement: Simone brand did INR8-10 crores turnover so far, may close year at INR15 crores vs INR25 crores target, expects better next year
items.quote: We've only been able to do about INR8 crores to INR10 crores of turnover so far. Maybe we'll close the year at about INR15 crores. Our original target was INR25 crores.

items.statement: Reaffirmed Vision 2027 sales target of Rs 40-45 billion by FY28 despite demand challenges
items.quote: Now there is a range, we are still fairly committed to achieve that range.

items.statement: On track to achieve FY25 target of 45-50 new restaurant openings
items.quote: We are on track to achieving our FY '25 target of 45 to 50 new restaurants.

items.statement: Opened 15 new restaurants in Q3 FY25, total store count reached 421 across 67 cities
items.quote: We added 15 new restaurants in the quarter and close to bringing our total store count to 421 across 67 cities as of December 31st.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 40 bps sequentially to 70.1% despite commodity inflation, expects stability around 70% near term
items.quote: Our gross margin improved by almost 40 bps sequentially to 70.1%, despite heightened inflation in key commodities such as oil, coffee, cocoa, etc.

items.statement: Implemented 50 bps portfolio-level price increase in November to mitigate commodity inflation
items.quote: We mitigated these inflationary pressures through supply chain and cost initiatives and a 50-bps portfolio level price increase.

items.statement: Annual pricing strategy targets 2-4% price increases, taking at least 50% of inflation
items.quote: Typically 2% to 4% of price increase is what we have conventionally taken, not more than 1% or 2% at one go.

items.statement: Same store sales grew 3% YoY driven by guest count growth with stable average check
items.quote: Same store sales were up by 3% year-on-year m oving back in the positive territory. A key highlight here is that it is a guest count -led same store sales growth, while average check remains stable

items.statement: Dine-in trends not fully recovered, eating-out occasions remain muted and flattish
items.quote: The IEO growth remains pretty much muted for the entire year, which is the informal eating out sector. Luckily, western fast food is doing quite okay, which is also reflected in our 9% growth overall. But the eating-out occasions have not grown or have remained muted.

items.statement: McCrispy platform and McCafe driving premium segment, chicken portfolio expanded to 160 restaurants with stable ADS salience
items.quote: We have 160 restaurants, I can share that. In terms of ads, it's remained largely stable. It has not grown exponentially. But we have seen a stable base over the last six months.

items.statement: Digital sales account for almost 70% of top line with 3 million monthly active users
items.quote: Digital sales that now account for almost 70% of our top line.

items.statement: Operating environment remains challenging with no significant increase in dine-out trends yet
items.quote: We are yet to see a significant increase in dine-in out trends.

items.statement: Restaurant operating margin and EBITDA down ~200 bps YoY due to operating deleverage and higher A&P spends, but improved sequentially
items.quote: Restaurant operating margin and operating EBITDA were lower by approximately 200 bps Y-o-Y due to operating deleverage and higher A&P spends for new product launch.

items.statement: Cash profit after tax stood at Rs 520 million or 8% of sales
items.quote: The cash profit after tax stood at Rs. 520 million or 8% of sales.

items.statement: Breakeven sales improved 2-2.5% in past quarter due to systematic cost governance
items.quote: Our breakeven sales have improved by 2% to 2.5% in the past quarter due to systematic cost governance, thereby enhancing li ke-for-like profitability, sequentially.

items.statement: Royalty percentage appears low in Q3 due to annual reconciliation of incentives in December
items.quote: Last year December also we had told that that on an annual basis we reconcile all the incentives, etc., which comes from the McDonald's Corporation on store opening etc.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue guided at Rs 800-825 crores
items.quote: It would be around 800 to 825 nearly.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected in double digits
items.quote: It will be double digit.

items.statement: Export OEM automotive revenue expected at Rs 200-225 crores for FY25
items.quote: Yes, total automotive export will be at 200 plus , 200 to 225 nearly.

items.statement: Export OEM automotive revenue targeted at Rs 400 crores in coming years
items.quote: Rs. 400 crores will be achieved in coming years.

items.statement: Export OEM sales expected to grow minimum 15-20% annually
items.quote: I am 100% sure that export OEM will increase every year in a good way, a minimum of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Mexico plant plan on hold for one month due to tariff uncertainty
items.quote: The plan is held up for a month to see how it happens.

items.statement: New export OEM orders received from USA and South Africa for new models
items.quote: We have received some good export orders from USA and RSA for OEM supplies to new models.

items.statement: BMW South Africa supply at 50,000 meters per month
items.quote: BMW also they have started buying from us in South Africa this quarter now we are doing about 50,000.

items.statement: Export OEM volumes ramping to 2-2.25 lakh meters/month in Q4
items.quote: Earlier we used to do 150,000 meter, in December-January we did 2 lakh meters, February would also be 2 lakh meters, in March it will be 2.25 lakh to 2.5 meters.

items.statement: Footwear segment expected to reach Rs 50 crores in Q4
items.quote: So, in quarter four, you can expect say Rs. 50 crores, approximately.

items.statement: PU sales grew 27-28% QoQ but segment still PBT negative
items.quote: No, it's a pickup in last quarter around 27%, 28% we have increased in PU sales in last quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by productivity, export mix and raw material prices
items.quote: It is because of your good productivity, because of your good sales in exports you are doing good , the margin is good.

items.statement: Global tariff uncertainty makes future predictions difficult
items.quote: Today the world situation is very difficult, nobody is in a position to commit anything.

items.statement: Lithuania subsidiary for European furnishing sales operational from April
items.quote: The material will go from here, it will reach in one and a half 2 months to two months time. So, the result will start getting from April.

items.statement: European market sales expected to increase 10-15% minimum
items.quote: The European market, whatever you are doing today , with that it will definitely increase 10% to 15%, 15% minimum.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 70%, PU at 25-30%
items.quote: Yes, it's nearly 70% overall, and PU is 25%, 30%.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance of 12% to 14% for FY26
items.quote: 2, 3 years is quite long, but still we would be around 12% to 14% growth.

items.statement: Retail contribution to total advances expected at 2% to 2.5% for FY26
items.quote: 2% is the number one we are looking at, contribution.

items.statement: Retail contribution to reach 8% to 9% in next 3 to 4 years
items.quote: We will be at 8% to 9% as we mentioned earlier, in the next 3, 4 years.

items.statement: Net NPA target of 1% to 1.25% for FY25
items.quote: We would reach between 1% to 1.25% net NPA for the financial year 2025 and would explore the possibility of improving the coverage ratio.

items.statement: Slippages guidance of INR800 crores for FY25 and INR700 crores for FY26
items.quote: We will exit this year with INR800 crores of slippages. And next year, we should close at INR700 crores.

items.statement: NIM guidance of 3.60% plus or minus 10 bps for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: As discussed in earlier calls, the margin should be 3.60% with plus or minus 10 basis points. We hope to maintain the same trend.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guidance of 48% to 50% for FY25
items.quote: As said in earlier calls, the cost-to-income ratio will be in the range of 48% to 50% for FY '24/'25, and we hope it will start going down once the retail business start delivering results.

items.statement: Yield on advances expected to drop to 9.7% from 9.81% with rate cuts
items.quote: Our yield on 9.81% can drop down to 9.7%. This is what we have projected. We expect 0.10 to 0.12 bps. This is what the number which we are doing.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to remain flat at 60-65 bps
items.quote: Correct. And we should also note that it depends on the economic cycle and it depends on the slippage. We expect it to remain flat.

items.statement: Target PCR without technical write-off of 60%
items.quote: We are looking at 60.

items.statement: Next year capex expected to be lower than current year
items.quote: The next year, the capex looks -- it is going to be lower than whatever we have seen in the current year.

items.statement: RBI gold loan circular had no impact as bank was already compliant
items.quote: We have been following this process for a couple of years. So this circular really did not impact us because in terms of process, in terms of LTV, in terms of data capturing, we have been strictly following this for the last 24 months, I would say, we are totally complied.

items.statement: Expect coking coal prices to reduce by around $10 per tonne in Q4
items.quote: As we look ahead for Q4, we expect a reduction of around $10 per tonne in coking coal prices.

items.statement: Announced next round of capex of INR 15,000 crores over next 3 years focused on cost efficiency, sustainability, value-added products and supply chain
items.quote: As we enter the final phase of current round of expansion, we are really excited to announce that we're also embarking on the next round of capex, where we will focus on cost efficiency, sustainability, increasing share of value-added products and improving supply chain, which will finally result in unlocking higher shareholders value.

items.statement: Exports rebounded 44% QoQ to 1.8 million tonnes; imports dropped 13% QoQ to 2.8 million tonnes as import order bookings slowed after government investigation

items.quote: Notably amongst them has been the launch of our new 2 mm mechanical pencil r ange. It is a substantial substitute to the traditional wooden pencil and comes in a range of Pastel and Disney- branded pencils

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Maped for distribution of premium stationery in India
items.quote: We took another decisive step in the overall development of our creative brand by partnering up with Maped. Maped is a French brand that has been in existence for close to 8 decades. They manufacture quality and premium stationery products and with this partnership, we will leverage our extensive network of distributors and retail touch points to distri bute Maped's products in India

items.statement: Domestic OEM business discounted from future projections, focusing on own brands
items.quote: So going forward, we have not even -- we are concentrating on our own brands and in domestic market, and we have not even taken into future projections, have discounted the domestic OEM business.

items.statement: Expects to close large expansion pursuits with top 10-20 customers in next few quarters.
items.quote: Our pursuit for large scale expansion with few of our top 10 to 20 customers continue to make progress, though a bit slower than what we originally anticipated. But with the increased momentum in the industry as a whole and these customers in particular, we remain optimistic about closing these pursuits in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Won five key deals with ACV of $2-4 million each, going live in coming months.
items.quote: Other than the regular renewals and conversion of pipeline in the quarter gone by, I would also like to mention that we won five key deals on expansion into new regions, adjacent areas with existing and new customers with deal sizes of 2 million to 4 million ACV each, which will go live in the coming month or two and start contributing revenues in the upcomi ng quarters

items.statement: Productivity and automation offset wage bill hike; expects this to continue.
items.quote: Continued productivity improvement initiatives through better capacity management and automation helped absorb the impact of the wage bill hike which was effective July and which you saw reflected in our margins in the last quarter and that impact has been negated and we believe this will continue to play out as we continue these initiatives in the future.

items.statement: Industry outlook for calendar year 2025 is cautious recovery with momentum.
items.quote: Heading into calendar year ‘25, this seems to be a year of cautious recovery for the industry. Many of you would have tracked the narrative from the biopharma companies in the JPM Healthcare Conference which happens every year in the early part of Jan and this time happened in SFO in mid Jan.

items.statement: Expects continued downward pressure on drug pricing, benefiting efficiency providers.
items.quote: The continued push to cut drug prices will exert pressure on the biopharma business model and margins. Both in the US and the rest of the world , government policies, competitive dynamics and the very rapidly evolving technology landscape , we believe will force biopharma to reimagine how they do commercialization and R &D.

items.statement: Plans to build $100M, $75M, $50M+ accounts in top 20 pharma mid-to-long term.
items.value: $100 million, 75 million and 50 million plus accounts
items.quote: We believe in the mid-to-long term this is a place where we will continue to grow and we will build USD100 million, 75 million and 50 million plus accounts. Something which we again spoken about earlier in our calls .

items.statement: Sees immediate growth opportunities in 20 to 100 pharma clients with shorter decision cycles.
items.quote: On the other hand, we see immediate opportunities for growth in the second track. This is 20 to 100 and our efforts are delivering results here. Already there's a large section of the industry which needs to moder nize and drive more effectiveness and efficiency.

items.statement: Has over INR 1,500 crores in cash and cash equivalents; actively scouting M&A.
items.quote: Our cash position remains strong. We now have a tad above INR 1,500 crores in cash and cash equivalents. We continue to actively scout for M&A opportunities and have a good pipeline of M&A opportunities.

items.statement: Regulatory complexity increasing, driving outsourcing and technology adoption.
items.quote: The r egulatory complexity continues to increase across clinical trials, manufacturing and safety, putting increased pressure on in house regulatory teams and driving greater outsourcing as well as adoption of technology. This provides another opportunity for players like Indegene to support the medical and regulatory functions within our customer groups.

items.statement: All major client renewals due this quarter largely renewed with minor variance.
items.quote: All our major client engagements which were due to renew this quarter have been largely renewed with minor variance without anything being out of line and we enter the calendar year ‘25 with a net positive rate of renewal.

items.statement: Pipeline is stronger than last year, aligned with industry outlook.
items.quote: Outside of the renewals, if I look at a pipeline compared to last year, it is clearly stronger. Again, this is in line with the macro industry outlook and also the fact that I think now after having consolidated, companies are stepping back and trying to evolve to the next level of progre ssion on their commercial and R &D medical models .

items.statement: Sees net positive impact from Veeva-Salesforce competition due to platform changes.
items.quote: We agree with that thing there is a tug of war between Veeva and Salesforce and from our perspective, actually there could be a net positive, right given this development for us. Because the opportunities play out at two levels.

items.statement: New clients added are mid-tier pharma with $2-5 billion revenue, potential $25-50M accounts.
items.quote: So, you could classify them as mid-tier companies which would have revenues, I would say north of $2 billion to $4-$5 billion each. And from a potential perspective, while as things stand today, if we were to look at a top 20 globally ranked customer becoming a $75-$100 million account for us over period, I would say these kind of accounts for the same kind of nature of wo rk would have a potentia

items.statement: Omnichannel segment has higher non-recurring projects, but moving to longer terms.
items.quote: So, this is a segment which is growing, but as you would understand, this segment has a higher proportion of non-enterprise or you could say higher proportion of non-recurring kind of business as projects with a finite life, 6 months, 9 months, 12 months, and therefore quarter-on-quarter, you would see some variability.

items.statement: Opened new centers in Hyderabad and Spain, expanded London office.
items.quote: Having said that last quarter in November, I would say we have also increased our footprint. We opened a center in Hyderabad in India. We now have close to 200 people in Hyderabad and the vicinity. We registered a presence in Spain and we started the journey of recruiting people based in Spain.

items.statement: Subcontracting costs up slightly due to Spain setup, will regularize.
items.quote: The subcontracting cost has gone up a tad bit, but that is also reflective of the growth I mentioned. One of the contributing factors there is we registered our office in Spain, but people that we took on board have been taken on board ahead of when the registration could be concluded through a third-party service provider.

items.statement: Aspires to achieve normalized margins, sticking to 10% to 12% guidance.
items.quote: And hopefully, as we go and become more mature in all the products, we should see more normalized margins, but we will stick to the guidance of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Mahad plant is a single product plant producing a mid-value product.
items.quote: So, I think, if you look at Mahad, Mahad is a single product plant. So, it's a mid-value product.

items.statement: Hydrogenation facility has a mix of high-value and bulk commodity products.
items.quote: If you look at the hydrogenation facility it's again a multi -product plant, where you have certain products, which are relatively high value, I mean, close to $80, $100. And then you have certain products, which are bulk, bulk commodities, which are like $7 to $10.

items.statement: Expects volume growth in current and new products assuming stable global demand.
items.quote: So we are pretty confident assuming that the demand now is more or less stable globally, w e will have volume growth in our current set of products as well as the new products that are being launched in the recently commissioned plants.

items.quote: So, I think currently in the current situation, the powd ered camphor prices would range anywhere between Rs. 450 to Rs. 500.

items.statement: Net block is around Rs. 425 crores.
items.quote: So, net block is around Rs. 425 crores.

items.statement: Hydrogenation facility utilization is 60% to 70% by end of FY25.

items.statement: Mahad plant utilization is 40% to 50%.
items.quote: And Mahad is less , Mahad is anywhere between say 40% to 50%, because it's recently commissioned.

items.statement: Mahad plant expected to reach optimal capacity in four to six quarters.
items.quote: So, to answer your question, we probably are anywhere between four to six quarters, where we will be able to achieve optimal capacity.

items.statement: Mahad plant will break even at 60% utilization.
items.quote: Around at 60% or this plant will be at break-even in the plant perspective.

items.statement: Mahad plant revenue expected from June or September quarter.
items.quote: And we will see the revenue incomin g from the June quarter or September quarter, because September quarter will be the H2 for the MNCs.

items.statement: Mahad plant will have revenues in Q4, with significant contracts starting Q1 next financial year.
items.quote: So, in Q4 we will definitely have revenues. And the actual contracts, etc., will start happening in Q1 of next financial year.

items.statement: Camphor division is breaking even and contributes to overall performance.
items.quote: So, like I said that, we defi nitely are breaking -even in our Camphor division, point number one, okay. I don't know if we kind of share individually division-wise ROCE number. But I can assure you that we are not only breaking-even, camphor also contributes to the overall performance of the company.

items.statement: Export margins are in line with local margins for most products.
items.quote: I think we can very broadly say, that in most of the products, the export margins are in line with the local margins.

items.statement: Bromine project to generate Rs. 50-60 crores revenue per annum with 40-50% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: the Bromine will give us approximately around 40%-50% EBITDA margin in the revenue of the bromine. The revenue will be in the range of around Rs. 60 crores, broadly, I am just giving, Rs. 50-Rs. 60 crores kind of a number.

items.statement: Vacuum Salt project to generate Rs. 100-120 crores revenue with 30-40% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Vacuum Salt will give approximate around Rs. 100-Rs. 120 crores once the fully operations are being established, around Rs. 100-Rs. 120 crores and the EBITDA will be in the range of around 30%-40% on this volume.

items.quote: 80% will be coming from that number, but the number in the 25-26 will be in the range of around Rs. 300 crores.

items.quote: this is for the new salt field, which we have been allotted. This amount is only for that and that will get spent over a period of next 3 years.

items.statement: Vacuum Salt and Bromine projects to be commissioned in FY25-26, around July and September.
items.quote: No, both the projects will get commissioned in FY25-26. One will be approximately around July and the second one approximately around September.

items.statement: Domestic demand and pricing scenario expected to be at bottom and improve going forward.
items.quote: We expect the domestic demand and pricing scenario to be at bottom. And demand should improve going forward due to the combination of following factors; MIP, minimum import price on soda ash, which will provide price protection from unchecked cheaper import coming into India; the second, imposition of duty on import, price of solar glass boosting domestic production; and the third growing force fo

items.quote: I personally believe that improvement in the price may take little longer time, but the volume benefit should start accruing going forward, maybe in a month or two.

items.statement: Cost optimization efforts to continue and margins should improve in longer term.
items.quote: Margin can happen on a quarter-to-quarter basis, but in a longer term, if you look at definitely this margin should improve.

items.statement: Sodium bicarbonate volume expected around 100,000 tons this year.
items.quote: Like you rightly said, our number will be likely to be around 100,000 this year in terms of the volume.

items.statement: Chinese soda ash prices below cost of production, recovery expected but timing uncertain.
items.quote: today, the Chinese sodas ash prices are below the cost of production of China.

items.statement: MIP on soda ash up to June, extension to be applied for after 2-3 months.
items.quote: After maybe 2-3 months, because this period is up to June, so we have to apply maybe in
