items.quote: if you look at the salt it is around 30%, we have backward integrated and one, the new land which has been allotted that number will significantly go up.

items.statement: Limestone backward integration at 20-25%.
items.quote: In terms of the limestone, I would say it is probably around maybe 20% approximately around 20%-25%.

items.statement: New salt field to feed 30-35% of current soda ash capacity, balance for new plant.
items.quote: approximately another around 30%-35% of the current capacity will get feed up from the new salt field and the balance will go to the new soda ash plant which we are putting in the Kutch area.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on solar glass from China and Vietnam to boost domestic production and soda ash demand.
items.quote: there is anti-dumping duty on China and Vietnam and that is very significantly higher and that will definitely give a much better levy to the solar producers in India and that is the reason we see a good amount of growth in 25-26.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% growth in booking value year-on-year.
items.quote: We are focused on future expansion through a joint development route and targeting 20 to 25% growth in booking value year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Expects aerospace business to grow post resolution of production issue.
items.quote: Further, we expect our aerospace business to grow post resolution of the production issue faced by one of the largest aircraft manufacturers which get to delays in the orders.

items.statement: Expects better Q4 and next year for engineering business.
items.quote: So all trends point towards a much better Q4, but also a much better next year.

items.statement: Expects better exports in Q4 in some markets.
items.quote: We will see better exports in Q4 as well in some of the markets.

items.statement: Expects better numbers in Q4 for tools and hardware business.
items.quote: And therefore, we would see better numbers in Q4.

items.statement: On track to list real estate business in next 6 to 7 months.
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that we have received the creditors as well as shareholders ’ approval earlier this week and remain on track for listing this business as a separate entity in the next 6 to 7 months.

items.statement: Expects scheme of arrangement for engineering subsidiaries to complete in next three months.
items.quote: In order to get more efficient and benefit from synergies, we are consolidating auto components and engineering consumables into a new subsidiary, while the aerospace business will be another subsidiary via a scheme of arrangement which is expected to be c ompleted in the next three months.

items.statement: No slowdown seen in any projects; on target for 20% booking value growth.
items.quote: We had given a guidance of about 20% booking value growth for the current y ear over the last year. And so far we are on target on that and continuing to be even in January also.

items.statement: Recent softness in auto component sector may impact near-term growth.
items.quote: However, with the post-addressing concern, we have witnessed signs of recovery, additionally, recent softness in the auto component sector due to weaker market may impact the growth in the near term.

items.statement: Q4 showing signs of recovery in engineering market.
items.quote: But I think the Q4 is definitely showing signs of recovery in terms of the market.

items.statement: Hybrid market in Europe grown; ED markets dampened.
items.quote: We have in particular seen that the hybrid market in the European region has grown while the ED markets have slightly been dampened.

items.statement: Forecast numbers from April much higher; Boeing strike called off.
items.quote: Boeing strike is called off. So there are inventories which will be eaten away over the next two, three months and we are already seeing forecast numbers from April to be much higher.

items.statement: Market share on some products expected to increase from 30-35% to 60-65%.
items.quote: So let's say our market share was 30% or 35% on some products. We're already seeing that they will take us to 60 % or 65%.

items.statement: 30% of new tower E inventory sold on launch.
items.quote: And 30% of that inventory is approximately already sold on launch itself.

items.statement: Total potential revenue from real estate business approximately Rs. 32,000 crores plus.
items.quote: Total potential revenue from our current real estate business is approximately Rs. 32,000 crores plus, which includes Rs. 25,000 crores from Thane land parcel and Rs. 7,000 crores from the four JDAs which we have sent.

items.statement: Both Dahej and Gopalpur projects expected to start production in H2 of next year.
items.quote: Both projects in next 12 months or I'll say, H2 of coming year, we do expect both projects to go live and start adding to our capacities. Project execution is currently in line with plan and expected to start production, as we spoke earlier, somewhere sometime during H2 of next year.

items.statement: Total capex on Dahej and Gopalpur plants expected around INR4,500 crores; INR1,300 crores spent till now.
items.quote: The total c apex which, in fact, if I recollect , we spoke about total c apex on these plants are expected to be around INR4,500 crores. Spend till now is around INR 1,300 crores.

items.statement: Peak net debt expected around INR5,500 crores in H2 of next year.
items.quote: Since we are in a capacity expansion mode and next year when -- our peak debt will be sometime towards H2 of next year when our both projects gets completed, we will be in a range of -- I'll say we'll be around INR5,500 crores kind of a net debt, and that will be the peak that what we expect to touch.

items.statement: Equinor gas supply starts Q1 FY27, reducing gas cost by 20% plus.
items.quote: The supply starts from next year first quarter. And yes, no, I'm talking financial year. So, FY '27 first quarter of next year, the supply from Equinor will start. And once it starts, it will take care of entire requirement what we have.

items.statement: Q4 typically peak for mining and infrastructure; expects increased demand from coal, cement, steel sectors.
items.quote: Looking ahead, quarter 4, typically a peak production period for mining and infrastructure activities. We expect increased demand coming from coal, cement, steel sectors, which recorded roughly 6% to 8% Y-o-Y growth in quarter 3 FY '25.

items.statement: Nitric acid demand and margin expected to remain stable.
items.quote: Looking forward, nitric acid demand and margin is expected to remain stable.

items.statement: IPA margin likely to improve gradually aided by anti-dumping duty and narrowing Phenol-Benzene spread.
items.quote: Meanwhile, IPA margin, which has seen some pricing pressure likely to improve gradually, aided by anti -dumping duty on IPA and narrowing Phenol -Benzene spread, which should enhance profitability in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Specialty products currently about 20% of overall revenue; intent to grow share.
items.quote: what we sell out of the total, company-wide, we are almost at 20% share of specialty, in our overall revenue. On IC side, this is a place which is catching up. In the next few years, it will be much bigger.

items.statement: Crop nutrition business is single-digit margin; intent to expand margin through specialty shift.
items.quote: Normally, we don't talk about business -specific EBITDA numbers. But this business, if you see, yes, it's a single-digit margin business. items.statement: Asset turnover for new capex expected around 0.7-0.8.
items.quote: Typically, for this kind of a business and this size of a c apex, asset turn anything around 0.7, 0.8 seems to be a good asset turn.

items.statement: Ramp-up of new plants expected to be fast as same products as Taloja.
items.quote: Good thing for our capacity, what we have put in, these are the same product or same plant which we are running in Taloja. For us, it's not a learning period, which will make difference to us. It will be a ramp-up, and we expect ramp-up to be pretty fast.

items.statement: Too early to provide FY27 outlook.
items.quote: Too early to talk about FY '27.

items.statement: Current performance sustainable till capex comes online, with premiumization growth.
items.quote: Correct. Correct. Yes, that's what the plans are.

items.statement: Normal tax rate to continue; last quarter was normal.
items.quote: The last quarter was normal tax rate. So, if you compute, that's what the normal tax rate will be for us.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 22% to 25% for 2025.
items.quote: And for '25 as well, we will continue to maintain that margin of 22% to 25%.

items.quote: give and take, we will see the market will grow in the range of 4% to 5%, and we are committed to grow above the market.

items.quote: our assumption is that it will be in the range of $75 to $80.

items.statement: Forex rate expected around 86 in 2025.
items.quote: forex, which is averaged out about 83 in 2024 is expected to be in the range of 86 roughly, again, you know following the global events.

items.quote: a part of our portfolio, retail, we've taken some pricing intervention already in the month of January as well.

items.quote: we've taken our necessary pricing interventions to cover that, okay?

items.quote: almost 4% of the PAT is coming from the essential CV.

items.quote: the rural volume gr owth is much higher, in fact in double digit than what we have done compared to last year

items.quote: B2C, we grew single digits; and B2B, we grew double digit.

items.quote: So 45% will be the personal mobility, cars and bikes, and the remaining 65% is industrial.

items.quote: India market is expected to grow at about 20% on this cooling solutions.

items.quote: Our ongoing project at Kakinada for setting up 2 lakh tons of phosphoric acid and related sulfuric acid is progressing well and we expect the plant to be commissioned by Q4 of next year.

items.statement: Aim for 60% of SSP volume from urea SSP and Gro Plus, blended margin Rs. 2,500 per ton.
items.quote: From the value-added products, both urea SSP and Gro Plus when we reach scale, I expect 60% to come from these 2 products. And balance 20%, 25% will come from normal granulated SSP with zinc and balance can be powder SSP.

items.statement: Blended SSP margin expected to go to Rs. 2,500 per ton with increased value-added products.
items.quote: So blended margin with this sort of a combination of 60:40 should go to Rs. 2,500 per ton. Currently, base SSP is powder SSP and granulated SSP in the range of Rs. 1,500 to Rs. 1,800.

items.statement: Aim to reach 1 million ton SSP capacity in 2 years, with 8 lakh tons next year.

But going forward, our aim would be to reach 1 million ton capacity in 2 years' time, probably taking it to 8 lakh tons next year and thereafter 1 million ton, and that too with focus on these specialty grades, which are as good as any other NPK products.

items.statement: Q4 volumes to align with market demand, not double-digit growth.
items.quote: So it won't be a double-digit growth. It will be as per our plan. And as you know, fourth quarter, we generally take annual turnaround.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth from debottlenecking, Ennore, and imports; scale up in next 2 years.
items.quote: See, it will be a combination of both. Very difficult to put a number, but we have been carrying out some debottlenecking of our facilities at Kakinada as well as Vizag. And that will be really adding to the volume increase next year.

items.quote: The last time also, we spoke about doubling the centers from current levels, and we are on that path. We'll be adding significant number of stores in fourth quarter as well.

items.quote: And this financial year, we are hoping to add another 8 stores.

items.quote: 175 will be a definite possibility. And we are trying, in fact, so many stores are going under work in progress. So, 175, we are definitely going to achieve, and we are trying to, in fact, open more stores even more than 175 stores.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin around 8% to 10%.
items.quote: Sustainable margin will be around 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Expect to maintain gross margin in coming quarters.
items.quote: But we expect that we are going to again maintain this gross margin in coming quarters.

items.statement: Expecting growth in February to March.
items.quote: But we are expecting growth in coming February to March.

items.statement: Very bullish on upcoming season, building inventory for summer.
items.quote: We are very bullish on this aspect Devanshu. In fact, we have already started building up our inventory because, as you know, approaching the summer, of course, it becomes very difficult for you to build on the inventories for air condition, refrigerators and other cooling products.

items.statement: Expecting very good Q1 for company due to summer and Kumbh mela.
items.quote: So, the entire money, we are expecting that with this summer, it will be a very, very good Q1 for our company.

items.statement: January demand flattish, expecting growth in February to March.
items.quote: Generally, it has been flat flattish. So, it has been flattish. Of course, we are in growth, but I'll say, I'll put it as flattish only. But we are expecting growth in coming February to March.

items.statement: IT and mobility share increased due to sluggish demand.
items.quote: Yes. That has been because whenever there is a sluggish demand then the IT and mobility, they have their share of counters will get bigger.

items.statement: Sluggish demand due to high inflation and interest, expected to ease.
items.quote: In my opinion, in fact, there has been a sluggish demand. This is only because of the macroeconomic in nature. In the sense with high inflation and high interest, this is the main factor. And I think in coming months, I think it is going to ease off.

items.statement: Utilized INR282 crores from fund raise for inventory and capex.
items.quote: We have already utilized INR282 crores and we have already filed all the details, you can find it from there.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth for 9 months FY25 at 15%.
items.quote: The same-store sales growth for 9 months FY '25 stands at impressive 15%.

items.statement: SSG in Q3 was 13%.
items.quote: SSG in this quarter was 13%.

items.statement: Targets 0.8 million tonnes steel volume for FY25 and 1 million tonnes for FY26.
items.quote: We are fully geared to meet our annual target of 0.8 million tonnes for FY '25 and are setting our sights for 1 million tonnes in FY '26.

items.statement: Aims to sustain 20%+ top-line growth and 3%+ EBITDA margin in FY26.
items.quote: See, top-line, we would like to sustain the 20% plus. The EBITDA, we would definitely be 3% plus.

items.statement: Plans to increase non-steel share from 10% to 20-25% in next five years.
items.quote: Today, the non-steel is about 10%, but our target in the next five years is to take it up to 20%, 25%.

items.statement: Expects to return to 3%+ EBITDA margin this quarter if steel prices remain steady.
items.quote: And if this quarter is a fairly steady period, we are fairly confident we will be back in the 3% plus kind of EBITDA this quarter itself.

items.statement: Aims to improve retail EBITDA margin by at least 1% in a couple of years.
items.quote: In a couple of years, definitely we would like that to go by at least 1% at this point.

items.statement: Anticipates completing demerger process by H1 FY26.
items.quote: Subject to the results of this meeting and subsequent regulatory processes, we anticipate completing the entire demerger process by H1 FY '26.

items.statement: Steel prices declined ~10% year-to-date, causing inventory losses of Rs. 22 crores in 9M FY25.
items.quote: We experienced a blended 6% decrease in realizations in Q2, followed by a further 3% reduction in Q3, resulting in an approximate total decline of approximately 10% in steel prices year-to-date.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin was 2.84%, down from 3.42% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: Despite our best efforts to operate efficiently in the face of such headwinds, our EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 2.84%, lower compared to 3.42% in Q3 FY '24 and relatively flat compared to Q2 of FY '25.

items.statement: Non-steel segment achieved record sales of Rs. 154 crores in Q3, up 19% YoY.
items.quote: This quarter, we achieved record sales of Rs. 154 crores in this segment, reflecting a 19% year-on-year growth in Q3, and even higher 29% growth in nine months FY '25.

items.statement: Steel prices are flattening out; some price increases from JSW etc. are talked about for this month.
items.quote: As of now, there is some talk of some increases from the JSW, etc., for this month. And it all depends on the global steel cycle, etc.

items.statement: Steel EBITDA margin was around 2.5% and non-steel around 5.5%.
items.quote: Yes, 2.5%, steel was around 2.5% and non-steel was around 5.5%.

items.statement: Steel price fluctuations are a risk; diversification into non-steel will mitigate it.
items.quote: I think what really will help us as we diversify more and more into the non-steel, I mean, this steel price fluctuation will get mitigated to a certain extent.

items.statement: Group level debt as of Q3 end is around Rs. 500 crores.
items.quote: Our group level debt as on quarter end Q3, it is around Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced from 36 to 33, target to bring down to 30.
items.quote: See, if you look at the number of days of working capital despite the last year, we started at about 36 days, which has come down to around 33. Our target is to bring it down to 30, number one.

items.statement: Cost of debt is approximately 9%-9.5%.
items.quote: Approximately around 9%-9.5% is our present cost of debt.

items.statement: Expects some debt reduction this quarter and tangible results from Q1 next year.
items.quote: We could see some reduction hopefully in this quarter itself and definitely tangible results from Q1 next year.

items.statement: Board approved asset-light built-to-suit 500-bed hospital in Thane, to be commissioned in 2028.
items.quote: Our Board has accorded its approval to enter into an asset -light ‘built-to-suit’ agreement for a 500 -bed hospital at a prime location in Thane , to be set up by the partner as per our specifications on a built -up area of appr oximately 6 lakh square feet. The hospital is expected to be commissioned in 2028.

items.statement: Board approved increasing capacity of Mohali (Zirakpur) hospital to 400 beds from 250 beds.
items.quote: The Board has also provided its approval for enhancing the capacity of our upcoming asset-light ‘built-to-suit’ hospital in Mohali (Zirakpur) to 400 beds from 250 beds planned previously.

items.statement: 128 beds at Max Lucknow: 64 beds commissioned in January 2025, balance 64 beds to be added in February 2025.
items.quote: 128 beds at Max Lucknow – 64 beds have been commissioned in January 2025, and the balance 64 beds will be added in February 2025.

items.statement: 127 beds at Max Nagpur: 12 beds added in October 2024; environmental clearance expected by March 2025; project completion in 24 months thereafter.
items.quote: 127 beds at Max Nagpur – 12 beds have been added in October 2024. For the balance beds on additional floors, we are expecting the environmental clearance (EC) to come by March 2025. Project completion should take another 24 months thereafter.

items.statement: 268 beds at Nanavati Phase 1: interior fit-out in progress; completion expected within next 3 to 4 months.
items.quote: 268 beds at Nanavati in Phase 1 – Interior fit -out work s are in progress currently. The project continues to be on schedule and we expect completion within the next 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: 400 beds at Max Smart (Saket Complex): majority structural work complete; completion expected within Q1 FY'26.
items.quote: 400 beds at Max Smart (Saket Complex) – Majority of the structural work is complete. The project is on track and we expect its completion within Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: 155 beds at Mohali: interior work in progress; completion expected by Q1 FY'26.
items.quote: 155 beds at Moha li – Interior work is in progress and we expect its completion again by Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: 500 beds at Sector-56 Gurgaon: structural work in progress; first phase of 300 beds expected by end of Q3 FY'26.
items.quote: 500 beds at Sector-56 Gurgaon – Structural work is in progress. We expect completion of the first phase of 300 beds by the end of Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: 367 beds at Patparganj: post environmental clearance, tendering in progress; project largely on schedule.
items.quote: Thereafter, 367 beds at Patparganj – Post receipt of environmental clearance (EC), tendering work is in progress currently. This project is largely on schedule.

items.statement: 550 beds at Max Vikrant (Saket Complex): forest approval delayed due to Supreme Court proceedings; all other statutory approvals in place.
items.quote: 550 beds at Max Vikrant (Saket Complex) – Forest approval is delayed due to Supreme Court proceedings in relation to tree felling involving DD A and the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi for the past 6 months. They have not permitted anybody to remove any trees in Delhi, but we think that this should get fairly resolved soon. All other statutory approvals are in place.

items.statement: 400 beds at Zirakpur, Mohali: fire department NOC received; project expected to be completed within 30 months.
items.quote: 400 beds at Zirakpur, M ohali – No objection certificate (NOC) from fire department has been received. Project is expected to be completed within 30 months.

items.statement: Upper limit for net debt-to-EBITDA is 2.5x; currently at 0.65x after Jaypee acquisition.
items.quote: So, our upper limit is 2.5 x net debt-to-EBITDA, but we are far from that. The new ones that we have announced such as Mohali (Zirakpur) as well as Thane, they are both asset-light models.

items.statement: Looking at Rs. 500-600 crore CAPEX over next 3-4 months towards brownfields.
items.quote: Now other than that, we are looking at Rs. 500-600 crore over the next 3-4 months of CAPEX towards the brownfields and then thereafter.

items.statement: Expecting price increase on institutional side, long overdue, should come within a month or two.
items.quote: We are not expecting a price increase on the insurance side , we were looking at a price increase on the institutional side. We are still expecting that as it is long overdue. Our belief is that it should come within a month or two.

items.statement: Expecting revisions in CGHS rates that will impact other PSU business; hope it comes this quarter.
items.quote: That's right. We are expecting some revisions to come up in CGHS rates that will also impact the other PSU business. The gap earlier used to be 44% betw een our cash rates and our institutional , and now it has come down to 36%.

items.statement: For asset-light model, EBITDA margin should be lesser by 5-6% on pre Ind AS basis.
items.quote: It should depend on what the maturity of the hospital is, but I think it should be lesser by 5-6%.

items.statement: Expects total net store additions of 300 in current financial year.
items.quote: We expect a total of 300 net store additions in the current financial year.

items.statement: Plans at least 600 store additions next year.
items.quote: No, I think it will be at least 600 stores for -- I don't think it will be less than 600 stores.

items.statement: Private label to increase by ~1% per quarter on MRP basis.
items.quote: So think about the private label as going up by roughly around 1% every quarter on the volume basis, which is on MRP basis, which means additional margin of roughly around 15 to 20 basis points maximum per quarter.

items.statement: Every 1% increase in private label MRP adds ~20 bps to gross margin.
items.quote: And that would mean possibly -- and if nothing else changed, I would say 1% growth in gross margin because every 1% in MRP, I think, increases our margin by around 20 basis points.

items.statement: Current margin level is sustainable; no significant dip expected from store additions.
items.quote: No, I think we are at a fairly sustainable kind of margin level for the company out there. Now the only reason which can change it is if we add a ton of stores -- new stores.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth expected at 4-5% steady state.
items.quote: 4% to 5% is what we are looking at, actually. That is a number at least we can be at a steady state as far as the profitability is concerned.

items.statement: Private label discount average ~50-51%, no plan to reduce significantly.
items.quote: About our private label discount itself, we advertise a 50% to 80% discount based on the molecule. And I think the average discount tough comes out to around 50%, 51%, that's all, because most of the higher selling drugs are all around the 50% discount.

items.statement: Adding 10 smaller warehouses of 30,000-50,000 sq ft.
items.quote: I think a total of 10 smaller warehouses, anywhere between 30,000 to 50,000 square foot kind of leases. That includes the ones I've already talked about.

items.statement: Muted growth partly due to seasonality and holidays; expects recovery.
items.quote: But yes, outside of that and a little bit of seasonal, I would say, effect having plenty of holiday season and all, especially in January and all, we did see a slightly, I would say, lesser sale than expected, but I expect that to get back.

items.statement: Cannibalization from new stores accepted; focus on store-level EBITDA.
items.quote: Some amount of cannibalization is always going to be there when we do this when we set up so many stores. But I'm fairly comfortable in saying that we should growth on the 2-plus year stores also at; inflation and slightly above that.

items.statement: Private label pharma share at 17.6% of GMV; non-pharma ~8%.
items.quote: Yes. So the private level itself on a GMV basis is around 17.6% right now on the Pharma side. If you look at the net sales side, I think it's around 1.6%.

items.statement: Private label share varies by region: metros ~7-8%, smaller towns ~20%.
items.quote: To give you an idea, I think Maharashtra, which is as urban as you can get, it's probably at around 7% or 8%. I think Bombay and all are at 7% or 8% for us on the Pharma side private label or maybe slightly less.

items.statement: Private label share in chronic and acute segments similar to regular brands.
items.quote: But to give you an idea, the number of -- I would say, the private label share of chronic versus acute is exactly the same as it is for the regular brands. So I think 60% to 70% of our sales are private label comes from the chronic segment.

items.statement: No drag from quick commerce if customers pay delivery fee; monitoring situation.
items.quote: As long as the customer is willing to pay the delivery fee, I don't think there will be a drag at all. If the delivery were to be 100% free, today we charge around INR 20.

items.statement: Will open close to 70-80 branches in full year.
items.quote: the guidance remains the same, we will be opening close to 70, 80 branches in a full year.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for the year is 0.75% to 1%.
items.quote: the credit cost as we guided was 0.75% to 1%, our credit cost for this quarter is 0.69%.

items.statement: Will maintain cost-to-income around 35% to 36% including credit cost.
items.quote: we are maintaining our numbers and we will continue to operate at around the 35% to 36% kind of cost -to-income. And when we mean cost -to-income, we include the credit cost as well.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 75 to 100 basis points for the business model.
items.quote: our guidance to you on the credi t cost is typically that the business model of Five Star can take a credit cost or will have to operate at a credit cost of around 75 to 100 basis points and I think we continue to maintain that same view

items.statement: No change in growth guidance for Q4 or next financial year.
items.quote: I think our guidance stands. So, we are not changing our guidance at this point of time, be it for Q4 or be it for the next financial year.

items.statement: Will revisit business outlook at end of March quarter.
items.quote: we will revisit our business outlook at the end of March quarter. So, I'll come out with the outlook in the April earnings call more clearly.

items.statement: Expect Q4 to be better than Q3.
items.quote: we are very confident that Q4 will be better than Q3.

items.statement: Expect to be back to business as usual in Q4.
items.quote: given that Q4 typically tends to be the best quarter for any financial institution, so we expect to be back to business as usual in Q4.

items.statement: No significant increase in credit cost in Q4.
items.quote: I don't think you will see any kind of significant increase in the credit cost in Q4.

items.statement: 30+ DPD to be at similar levels in Q4.
items.quote: I think it could be in similar levels is what we feel at this point of time.

items.statement: Will maintain appropriate level of provisions in coming quarters.
items.quote: we will continue to keep maintaini ng the appropriate level of provisions in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Eventual credit losses should not exceed 25 to 50 basis points.
items.quote: eventual credit losses… and th is is something that we have been guiding for the last many years since our DRHP was there, it should not be more than 25 to 50 basis points.

items.statement: No guidance for growth acceleration; existing guidance stands for next year.
items.quote: at this point of time, we are not guiding you for any acceleration. We will have to wait and see what are the focus areas both for the government as well as how does it gets translated into actions from an RBI perspective.

items.statement: Will come back on growth guidance in April earnings call.
items.quote: we will come back after the March quarter depending upon the environment around us and the regulatory thought process we will take appropriate steps is what we said in the last quarter, that remains the same. So, we will come back on the April earning call.

items.statement: No change in credit cost guidance of 75 to 100 basis points.
items.quote: even then we are not changing the guidance at this point of time. How you will see it, moving in a trajectory is something that we will also have to see when it will probably touch a 75 or 100.

items.statement: Will take technical write-offs as appropriate in consultation with board and auditors.
items.quote: We will continue to keep taking this depending on what we believe is the appropriate number for the Company both in consultation with the board and as well as the auditors.

items.statement: Targets 10 GW O&M portfolio in 3-4 years, with 7 GW organic and 3 GW inorganic.
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our target of 10 gigawatts in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Aims to double portfolio to 6 GW in a couple of years.
items.quote: in a couple of years, our target is to double it to 6 gigawatt.

items.statement: Maintains full-year EBITDA margin guidance of 50%.
items.quote: But on a full year basis, 50% guidance remains.

items.statement: Expects to commission 300-400 MW in Q4 FY25, reaching ~4 GW portfolio.
items.quote: we will commission near to about 300-400 megawatt in quarter 4. So broadly by FY '25, and we will be 4 gigawatt portfolio plus minus 100 megawatt, 200 megawatt here and there

items.statement: Plans to commission 1,200 MW in FY26 and 2,000 MW in FY27, reaching 7.2 GW organically.
items.quote: then we will get commissioned 1200 megawatts in subsequent year and then 2 gigawatts. So organically, our portfolio will increase to somewhere around 7.2 gigawatts.

items.statement: Hopes to acquire 2-3 GW inorganically in next 12-18 months.
items.quote: we are very hopeful that around 2 to 3 gigawatts when we acquire in next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Utilized ~INR300 crores of fundraise, plans to use another INR200-250 crores in 2-3 months.
items.quote: We intend to utilize another INR200, INR250 over the period of next 2 to 3 months.

items.statement: Demerger expected to complete within this calendar year, making balance sheet asset-light.
items.quote: We are hopeful that within this calendar year we will have the demerger of the business.

items.statement: Inox Green shareholders will receive 10% of Resco, with total 20% owned by Inox Green shareholders.
items.quote: the minority shareholder of Inox Green will get 10% in the consolidated entity. So currently, 50% is owned by the minority shareholders in Inox Green, so if we take our math accordingly, then the 20% shares of the Resco will be owned by the Inox Green shareholders

items.statement: Company has accumulated tax losses of INR700 crores.
items.quote: INR700 odd crores is the tax losses, which the company carries.

items.statement: Solar O&M to start contributing from next FY, with margins lower than wind but higher than industry due to synergies.
items.quote: Basically, the execution on solar is expected in the next FY. So as soon as the time line of 8 to 9 months, the project commissioning, so it will be taken over by Inox Green.

items.statement: NCLT acquisitions are lengthy but yield clean companies without hidden liabilities.
items.quote: the NCLT process, the bankruptcy route, is something that takes time. It is a little lengthy process. But then also the advantages that we get the company clean without any hidden liabilities

items.statement: Total fundraise was INR1,050 crores, with INR550 crores received and balance callable.
items.quote: the total was INR1,050 crores, as you would remember. And that’s obviously, we have received. Manish, correct me if I'm wrong. INR550-odd crores already in the company.

items.statement: Committed investment over INR1,000 crores; INR350 crores already deployed.
items.quote: We are committed to investment of over INR1,000 crores, of which INR350 crores have already been deployed.

items.statement: 25,000 new spindles to commence operations by June 2025.
items.quote: The addition of 25,000 new spindles is progressing as per schedule with operations expected to commence by June 2025.

items.statement: New project for 40 knitting machines at capex of INR38 crores.
items.quote: We have undertaken a new project to set up 40 knitting machines in our existing location at a capex of INR38 crores.

items.statement: By 2029-30, 30-35% of revenues from value-added segment.
items.quote: So the idea is by 2029, '30, we have almost 30% to 35% of our revenues coming from the value-added segment.

items.statement: After INR1,000 crores capex, 70% revenue from spinning, 30% from fabric and value-added.
items.quote: See, as I said earlier, overall, still, I would say, 70% of the revenue will come from spinning and around 30% of the revenue will come from the fabric and the value-added segment.

items.statement: Incremental capital in knitted fabric to give 13% to 14% ROCEs.
items.quote: So basis our estimates, probably the incremental capital will give us almost 13% to 14% ROCEs on going into the knitted fabric.

items.statement: New knitting investment ROCE around 13.5%, margins 3% to 4% extra.
items.quote: Our ROCE on the new investment, which we have just got approval will be around 13.5%. And our margins should be in the range of around 3% to 4% extra margin will get generated out of this number of these new investments.

items.statement: Incremental value addition INR14 crores, EBIT INR7 crores on INR38 crores investment.
items.quote: So it will be approximately in terms of the value, almost INR14 crores will be the incremental value addition that we'll get. On an EBIT level, approximately INR7 crores will be the value that we get on the incremental basis on this INR38 crores investment.

items.statement: Expect to operate at same levels as current 9 months.
items.quote: As of now, we believe that we'll operate more or less at the same levels where we are -- we have closed this current 9 months.

items.statement: Seeing export inquiries, waiting for conversion into orders.
items.quote: We have started getting those inquiries, and we are waiting for it to get converted into orders.

items.statement: Cotton prices expected to remain stable, supporting domestic textile industry.
items.quote: Yarn prices have mostly remained range bound, and it is expected that the cotton prices will remain stable, which shall support the domestic textile industry.

items.statement: Demand remains sluggish, longest period of sluggishness in yarn market.
items.quote: See, the demand still remains sluggish. So -- and this is probably the longest period of sluggishness in yarn market that we are seeing, almost now 2 years.

items.statement: Capex to be financed by internal accruals and bank finance, debt equity within 0.5:1.
items.quote: So both from the internal accruals plus bank finance, we'll be able to finance this capex. But we'll remain very much within those declared boundaries of debt equity of not more than 1:1, rather we'll maintain within 0.5:1 kind of numbers.

items.statement: No plans to monetize noncore assets as internal accruals sufficient.
items.quote: As and when if we feel there is any need, we'll look at that. But as of now, there are no plans to monetize as of now.

items.statement: Aiming for mid-teens revenue growth for the next couple of years.
items.quote: Going ahead, our company is aiming for mid-teens revenue growth for the next couple of years, driven by the expansion of new store locations across both new and established markets, depending upon a rebound in the industry demand for premium and mid-premium brands.

items.statement: Expects high single-digit growth for the full year FY25.
items.quote: We already mentioned that we would grow in high single-digit growth.

items.statement: Aspiring for mid-teens growth in the next financial year.
items.quote: Depending on market conditions again, but we are aspiring for mid-teens growth in the next financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected in the range of 27% to 30%.
items.quote: EBITDA should be in the range of 27% to 30%, Ruchita.

items.statement: Plans to open 20-25 stores in FY26, with potential for 40-50 depending on market.
items.quote: Ruchita, we intend to even now this year, open about 20, 25 stores, and we will be ready to open even 40 or 50 depending on how the market pans out.

items.statement: Expects to open 18-20 net stores by end of FY25.
items.quote: By the end of the year, I think we are confident that we should be able to open between -- at a gross level -- I mean, net level, sorry, about 18 to 20 stores.

items.statement: No price hike in the last year; future hikes depend on raw material costs and inflation.
items.quote: There hasn't been any price hike in the last year. But depending on the raw material costs and inflation, et cetera, price hike is a function of that.

items.statement: Constant premiumization in product mix is ongoing.
items.quote: However, there is a constant premiumization that's happening in the brand in terms of the product mix, et cetera, which is a constant work in progress and -- something that keeps going on.

items.statement: Expects consumption to improve with recent tax reductions.
items.quote: Additionally, we expect consumption to improve with the recent boost given by tax reductions.

items.statement: Faced subdued demand for premium and mid-premium branded apparel due to reduced discretionary spending.
items.quote: Despite facing challenges such as subdued demand for premium and mid-premium branded apparel, primarily driven by reduced discretionary spending and weaker consumer sentiment, impacting overall industry consumption.

items.statement: Aims to double business in 5 years, possibly a year less or more.
items.quote: See internally double in the 5-year period. However, depending on market, it could take a year less or a year more to achieve that.

items.statement: No plans to launch value products; may consider other categories in 2-3 years.
items.quote: As of now, we don't intend to launch value products. The core competence and the strength of the brand is to provide fashion that is unique and different from other brands and what's available in the market.

items.statement: No buyback plans currently.
items.quote: We haven't thought about it for the moment, Jaimin.

items.statement: Will use cash flow for store expansion, working capital, and shareholder payouts.
items.quote: So it will be all the 3 basically. See, we will use the money for internal -- this expansion of the stores also from internal accrual of the funds as well as we -- there will be some payout to shareholders also.

items.statement: Expects to close large scale expansion pursuits with top 10-20 customers in next few quarters.
items.quote: Our pursuit for large scale expansion with few of our top 10 to 20 customers continue to make progress, though a bit slower than what we originally anticipated. But with the increased momentum in the industry as a whole and these customers in particular, we remain optimistic about closing these pursuits in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Won five key deals with ACV of $2-4 million each, going live in coming months.
items.quote: Other than the regular renewals and conversion of pipeline in the quarter gone by, I would also like to mention that we won five key deals on expansion into new regions, adjacent areas with existing and new customers with deal sizes of 2 million to 4 million ACV each, which will go live in the coming month or two and start contributing revenues in the upcomi ng quarters

items.statement: Productivity and automation initiatives to continue offsetting wage bill impact, net positive to margins.
items.quote: Continued productivity improvement initiatives through better capacity management and automation helped absorb the impact of the wage bill hike which was effective July and which you saw reflected in our margins in the last quarter and that impact has been negated and we believe this will continue to play out as we continue these initiatives in the future.

items.statement: Industry outlook for calendar year 2025 is cautious recovery with momentum.
items.quote: Heading into calendar year ‘25, this seems to be a year of cautious recovery for the industry. Many of you would have tracked the narrative from the biopharma companies in the JPM Healthcare Conference which happens every year in the early part of Jan and this time happened in SFO in mid Jan.

items.statement: Downward pressure on drug pricing to benefit Indegene as pharma seeks efficiency.
items.quote: The continued push to cut drug prices will exert pressure on the biopharma business model and margins. Both in the US and the rest of the world , government policies, competitive dynamics and the very rapidly evolving technology landscape , we believe will force biopharma to reimagine how they do commercialization and R &D.

items.statement: Clients moving from under $1M to $1M+ and $1-5M to $5-10M categories, driving near-term growth.
items.quote: On clients which are in the USD1 to 10 million category, we see more active clients , less than USD 1 million moving to the USD 1 million plus category. Clients in the 1 to 5 million category, moving into 5 to 10.

items.statement: Cash position strong at over INR 1,500 crores; actively scouting M&A opportunities.
items.quote: Our cash position remains strong. We now have a tad above INR 1,500 crores in cash and cash equivalents. We continue to actively scout for M&A opportunities and have a good pipeline of M&A opportunities.

items.statement: Omnichannel segment projects evolving to longer durations and potential enterprise agreements.
items.quote: Many of them are actually moving from a 6 month kind of life to a 12 month with the ability to get transformed over period into enterprise agreements which tend to be a lot more recurring and sticky going beyond one year , r ecurring year-on-year.

items.statement: Opened Hyderabad center with ~200 people and expanded London office.
items.quote: Having said that last quarter in November, I would say we have also increased our footprint. We opened a center in Hyderabad in India. We now have close to 200 people in Hyderabad and the vicinity.

items.statement: Acquisition pipeline includes sub-$50-60 million revenue companies, disciplined valuation.
items.quote: As far as size of these concerned. What we have right now in the pipeline are I would call all of them being sub-$50-$60 million revenue all the way from $2 to $50 million type of revenue range right now. And we will be always disciplined in what we pay for these kinds of companies.

items.statement: Subcontracting costs increased due to Spain office setup, to regularize.
items.quote: The subcontracting cost has gone up a tad bit, but that is also reflective of the growth I mentioned. One of the contributing factors there is we registered our office in Spain, but people that we took on board have been taken on board ahead of when the registration could be concluded through a third-party service provider.

items.statement: Offshore mix expected to increase as projects stabilize, benefiting margins.
items.quote: So, I would use that slide to s ay that it is changing over period. You will also see some of that shifting back to the offshore side. We are not looking at moving the work that Trilogy, small business getting offshore.

items.statement: Expects to continue market++ growth and expanding profitability.
items.quote: Having consistently achieved market++ (plus-plus) growth over the years, we expect to continue performing at the same level moving forward, along with demonstrating strong operating leverage, achieving expanding profitability.

items.statement: UniReco commercial launch expected by end of Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We remain on track for a commercial launch by the end of Quarter 1 FY26, and this will further enhance our position as a comprehensive e-commerce enablement platform.

items.statement: Steady-state price for Uniware is Rs. 1.2 to Rs. 1.3 per item.
items.quote: See, we mentioned in the earlier earnings call as well that our steady-state price continues to be in the range of Rs. 1.2 to Rs. 1.3 per item for Uniware, our flagship platform.

items.statement: Overall e-commerce market growing early to mid single digits this year.
items.quote: And this year, we see that the overall market is growing in early to mid single digits.

items.statement: NRR continues to be more than 100%.
items.quote: In spite of the overall muted growth in the e-commerce market, we still continue to demonstrate a 100% plus NRR.

items.statement: Overall e-commerce volumes remain muted.
items.quote: So, we continue to see the overall e-commerce volumes to be muted and that's why our endeavor is to have a one-stop shop for e-commerce businesses across three platforms which is Convertway, Uniware and Shipway so that increasingly more and more businesses can opt for services that are available under a single umbrella and we continue to drive adoption across the ecosystem.

items.statement: Shipway annual run rate ranges between INR 70 to 80 crore.
items.quote: Yes, that ranges between INR 70 to Rs. 80 crore of annual run rate.

items.statement: Aim to make Shipway PAT positive very soon.
items.quote: And our endeavor is to make the business PAT positive very soon.

items.statement: Shipway loss for 15 days was INR 0.9 million.
items.quote: From the revenue standpoint , we consolidated Shipway and Shipway contributed near about 32.7 million INR and from a PAT standpoint, Shipway delivered a loss of INR 0.9 million for this period.

items.statement: One-time bonus reversal of INR 22 million.
items.quote: Reversal INR 22 million is the number.

items.statement: Headcount about 350 employees at end of Q3 FY25.
items.quote: If you look at our headcount, it is largely in the similar ballpark but like the headcount today is about 350 employees in the Quarter 3 ending FY25, that helps answer your question.

items.statement: SMB clients on Uniware are 3000 plus.
items.quote: So, the SMB clients, we have invested in the short term to drive sales in our SMB business and while our overall base is 7000 plus clients, within that SM B clients on our flagship platform Uniware are 3000 plus.

items.statement: Amortization period approximately 3 to 5 years.
items.quote: So, that will be in accordance to the IND AS guidelines, will actually range between 3 to 5 years also.

items.statement: Average revenue per shipment INR 70 to 80.
items.quote: So, see as an example today that average revenue is about INR 70 to INR 80 per shipment.

items.statement: Absolute margin per shipment about INR 15.
items.quote: So, even if at an absolute margin of 20.4% that you mentioned, it comes to about INR 15 per shipment.

items.statement: 1 GW TOPCon cell and module line expected completed by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Our expansion plans include a 1 gigawatt TOPCon cell and module line expected to be completed by Q1 FY26, and a 4 gigawatt TOPCon cell and module line expected to be completed by Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Total capacity to reach 7 GW cells and 9.1 GW modules by June 2026.
items.value: 7 gigawatt per annum for solar cells and 9.1 gigawatt per annum for modules
items.quote: With these facilities, our total capacity would reach 7 gigawatt per annum for solar cells and 9.1 gigawatt per annum for modules by June 2026.

items.statement: 2 GW wafer facility targeted for commissioning by FY26.
items.quote: Simultaneously, we have planned further backward integration into wafers with a 2 gigawatt per annum facility which is coming up and also this is targeted to be commissioned by FY26.

items.statement: Aluminum frame facility of 36,000 metric tons per annum to meet captive needs.
items.quote: Our aluminum frame manufacturing business with a 36,000 metric ton per annum facility to meet our full captive needs and to increase our share of total value addition and profitable margin.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved to 29.97% in Q3 FY25 from 17.30% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margin improved from 17.30% in Q3 FY24 to 29.97% in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Quarterly margins have been in the range of 25 to 30, could be an indicator.
items.quote: As you see quarter-on-quarter we have been in the range of between 25 to 30 as what you have seen in today's results. That could be an indicator, we'll be in this range.

items.statement: Order book is firm with advances received, not framework contracts.
items.quote: The order book which you see in the presentation is firm with advances received. We have not taken any framework contract into our order book.

items.statement: Most orders have a cycle of not more than 12 to 15 months.
items.quote: So, most of the orders are having a cycle of not more than 12 months to 15 months.

items.statement: Order book composition: 36% cells, 1% EPC, 63% modules.
items.value: 36% is for cells, 1% for EPC and 63% for module
items.quote: I think about 30%-odd is for cells which is already shown in the order book. 36% is for cells, 1% for EPC and 63% for module.

items.statement: Prices are stable, no significant change quarter on quarter.
items.quote: Prices are quite stable and the demand also is very, very strong. So we are not seeing any significant change as such quarter on quarter.

items.statement: Slight increase in pricing due to glass duty pass-through.
items.quote: In fact, in the non-DCR segment, there is a slight increase in the pricing because of duty imposed on glass. So overall, the pricing has gone up a little bit.

items.statement: Rooftop market expected to touch 9 to 10 GW over next 1 to 2 years.
items.quote: So we do expect the rooftop market alone in India to touch about 9 to 10 gigawatts over the next 1 to 2 years.

items.statement: India module demand expected to grow 15-20% year-on-year over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: We expect that number to grow by about 15% to 20% year-on-year over the next three to five years.

items.statement: US cell line investment under review due to IRA pause.
items.quote: And this is the reason why we have kept our cell line investment in the US under review because we will wait for clarity before we spend any money on the cell line.

items.statement: Exports limited to below 3% of revenue, focus on Indian market.
items.quote: Our export percentage is going to be limited to 3% because as I told earlier, we are committed to Indian market. So we will be restricting our exports, even though there is a significant demand from the US, but the management by choice is very clear.

items.statement: Expects gradual demand recovery, positive start in textile and apparel bookings, and return to growth trajectory in FY26.
items.quote: We expect a gradual recovery in demand, as we have observed a positive start in both our textile and apparel bookings for next year. We will be back to the growth trajectory clearly in FY26 and we continue to build on our initiatives to deliver sustainable growth and value to our stakeholders.

items.statement: Sees sustainable EBITDA margin of around 15% once retail expansion stabilizes.
items.quote: we clearly see a sustainable EBITDA margin of around 15 % odd for us , once the whole retail expansion is Raymon~ stabilized and that we are pretty confident

items.statement: Expects full EBITDA margin recovery in FY26.
items.quote: we will start seeing a gradual recovery happening clearly on EBITDA margins and I think we will see the full recovery happening in FY26.

items.statement: Branded textile EBITDA margin to be 20-21% steady state.
items.quote: our branded textile business will drive the EBITDA margins which would be in the range of around 20% to 21% kind of margin which we had maintained till now, till a couple of quarter back .

items.statement: Apparel EBITDA margin to settle around 13-14% over time.
items.quote: we also see over a period of time apparel EBITDA margin to be also settling down in the range of around 13% to 14% over a period of time.

items.statement: Garmenting business to return to double-digit EBITDA margin.
items.quote: our garmenting business also because there is a strategy playing out will come back to a double -digit EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Consciously postponed 1-2% annual price increases in branded textiles due to weak market; may take next year if economy improves.
items.quote: We also have the ability to take and we do tend to take 1% to 2% price increases every year in a branded textile segment. This time because of the weak market we started a year back, we have taken a conscious choice not to do that price increase because the market sentiment has been tough.

items.statement: Retail expansion journey is 36 months; 12-13 months in, another 20-24 months to go.
items.quote: We'll take maybe it's another it's an overall 36-month journey for us. I would say we are maybe 12, 13 months into it. It would take another couple of years, I think really to get the journey get completed.

items.statement: Bookings for next year autumn winter season underway with positive trend across suiting, shirting, fabrics, and apparel.
items.quote: we are right now seeing bookings in all the three segments which is suiting, shirting and fabrics as well as our apparel booking for the next year autumn winter season which begins. And they are currently underway or kind of finishing. And there is a pretty positive trend that we are seeing among all these three bookings which will play out for us in FY26.

items.statement: Secondary sales in Q3 were healthy across segments, indicating positive consumer offtake.
items.quote: Our secondary numbers of this quarter were pretty healthy and that is something which has given us a lot of confidence.

items.statement: January demand similar to December; urban discretionary spend pressure persists.
items.quote: I would say more of the same. I don't think there's any fundamentally shifted between December and January. I think it's been a mixed bag.

items.statement: New customer acquisition in garmenting initially lower-mix, expected to move up to jackets and suits over 12 months.
items.quote: the entry point into new customer happens with a segment which are for example shirts and then over a period of maybe a 12-month period, as the confidence in the relationship gets built, as your benchmarks get set, you start moving up the assortment in the product ladder moving towards jackets and then suits.

items.statement: Weak consumer demand, scale deleverage, upfront investments, and adverse segment mix impacted EBITDA.
items.quote: Our EBITDA at INR221 crores with an EBITDA margin of 12.3% was lower as compared to the same quarter last year mainly due to weak consumer demand, scale deleverage, upfront investments in retail storage expansion and advertising and an adverse segment mix.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis led to higher freight costs and blue-collar training costs impacted garmenting EBITDA.
items.quote: The EBITDA performance in this quarter was impacted on account of product mix due to addition of over 15 new clients across key markets including the US, UK and Europe, some Raymon~ higher freight costs on account of the Red Sea crisis and the incremental cost of blue -collar manpower training as a result of capacity expansion

items.statement: Aspiration to reach INR2200 crores EBITDA by FY28 may be delayed by 12-18 months.
items.quote: our aspiration remains a course in that ballpark. I wouldn't say that it's exactly 28, but I think we definitely remain in t he aspiration of reaching there, b ut maybe this could happen 12 months to 18 months later

items.statement: 1.4 GW Mono PERC cell line commercial operations expected in 10-15 days.
items.quote: As far as 1.4 gigawatt cell line is concerned, it's a matter of days. I would say anywhere between the next 10 to 15 days or even earlier than that. We will have our COD declared.

items.statement: 4 GW TOPCon cell lines to start commercial operations by April-May.
items.quote: As far as 4 gigawatts of TopCON line is concerned, we will, like I said in my opening commentary, anywhere between April and March, we should be in a position to start commercial operations.

items.statement: 6 GW PLI project for ingots, cells, wafers remains on target for 2027.
items.quote: The Odisha facility, the PLI facility is very much on track. We have talked about 2027 of operation and we continue to be optimistic that we will start at that point in time.

items.statement: Order book stands at 26.5 GW, around INR50,000 crores, as of yesterday.
items.quote: As of yesterday, ou r order book stands at 26.5 gigawatts, and in rupee terms, this is around INR50,000 crores

items.statement: Order book is 54% overseas and 46% from India.
items.quote: This order book is well diversified between India and international markets, with 54% overseas and 46% from India.

items.statement: Order book includes orders from subsidiary WRTL.
items.quote: This also includes order from our subsidiary, WRTL, which is a separately listed entity under Waaree Energies Limited.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline up to two years.
items.quote: You're absolutely right. It has got orders, all the way from now to the gestation period of two years.

items.statement: Board approved investments in green hydrogen, battery, renewable power, and inverter businesses.
items.value: INR551 crores, INR2,073 crores, INR650 crores, INR130 crores
items.quote: Our Board has already approved green hydrogen and electrolyzer business with an investment of INR551 crores, battery business with an investment of INR2,073 crores, and the renewable power infrastructure business with an investment of INR650 crores. We are also making an investment of INR130 crores in our inverter business.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin was 22.84%.
items.quote: EBITDA for Q3 FY '25 stood at INR809 crores, a significant growth of 257 % year-on-year basis, and a margin of 22.84%.

items.statement: 9M EBITDA margin was 19.28%.
items.quote: EBITDA for nine months FY '25 was INR2,063, which is an increase of 56 % over the previous year and a margin of 19.28%.

items.statement: Cell price in India is around $0.4 plus duties; US higher.
items.quote: So currently, the cell price is anywhere between four, I would say, $0.4. That's the average which is currently running. That's for the India market. And of course, for the US market, it is higher.

items.statement: Module prices in India are 17-17.5 cents; US 27-30 cents.
items.quote: As far as the module prices which are concerned, currently in India, the average prices are anywhere between 17-17.5 cents and US, of course, is higher. There are orders which are at 30 cents, there are orders at 27 depending upon the scope that you cover.

items.statement: Input costs for most materials have come down substantially in last quarter.
items.quote: The input costs for most of our materials have actually come down quite substantially in this last quarter and th at has also given a flip overall to the profitability.

items.statement: US clients unphased by recent changes; order pipeline growing.
items.quote: Our US clients are actually quite unphased by the changes that have happened in the recent past. In fact, all of them, we have actually spoken to most of them, and our order books clearly stand strong.

items.statement: India solar market expected to grow to 40-50 GW annually by 2030.
items.quote: India, at this point in time, I think we were straddling around 18, 19, 20 gigawatts a year. Every year till 2030, we are actually going to see an exponential rise. And in the out years, I will not be surprised if you are in the region of around 40 gi gawatts to 50 gigawatts overall and each of the segments is growing within this.

items.statement: Domestic cell manufacturing to prioritize US market and local DCR market.
items.quote: So the way in which we are going to use the cells, our own manufactured cells, the priority is two -fold. One is for the US market and the other one is for the local DCR market.

items.statement: Expects disbursals to return to FY24 levels, leading to stronger margins and bottom line.
items.quote: we see green shoots and we expect that disbursals will come back to the same level as FY'24, which will result in stronger margins and bottom line performance in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Long-term take rate in financial services expected to be 5-6%.
items.quote: on a longer-term secular basis, the take rates that we are in this business can be the 5% to 6% ballpark, which is what we've guided to earlier in the past as well.

items.statement: MDR on PPI on UPI expected up to 1%, not finalized.
items.quote: it is expected to be somewhere in the range… we don't know where it will land, it is not finalized, but discussions are ongoing, I think it could be anywhere in the range of up to 1%.

items.statement: MDR on PPI via UPI: 1.1% for P2M transactions above ₹2,000, still under discussion.
items.quote: a broad parameter which has been agreed is about 2,000, there will be a charge of 1.1% for all P2M transactions. However, I think that is still in the final stages of agreement across the multiple stakeholders and we do expect that it will become real in a short period of time.

items.statement: Gross take rate on ZIP EMI ~11%, net 4-5% after costs including 5% FLDG.
items.quote: On the ZIP EMI product, our gross take rate is around 11%. And against that, we have credit cost, we have underwriting cost, we have collection cost, we have marketing cost. So, you add all these costs, so we make roughly 4% to 5% as a net.

items.statement: Net margin remains similar at 4-5% despite contract changes.
items.quote: even though the nature of the contracts are changing, but the net we make is similar on a net basis, which is roughly 4% to 5% on a larger tenure product, which is the EMI.

items.statement: Secured credit card product in beta, no credit cost, to offset ZIP scale down.
items.quote: the secured credit card product, which we were just speaking about, an additional point to mention is because it's a secured product, therefore, there will be no credit cost on that, because it's a fully secured FD-backed credit card.

items.statement: ZIP product scaling down due to lower lending partner appetite, not profitability.
items.quote: we don't believe that it is the profitability that is resulting in the scale down of this product, it is more that there is a lower appetite amongst lending partners to do such a small ticket product. So, that is why we are moving away to a co-branded RuPay Credit Card.

items.statement: Lending related expenses increased to 9% from 3-4%, includes credit cost and delinquency.
items.quote: if you look at a lending related expenses, which is something that we report. Then all through last year if you look at the numbers again, we've reported these numbers that expense tended to be in the 3% to 4% range. Now, if you see that expense is more in the 9% ballpark.

items.statement: IPO capital of ₹572 crores not yet deployed, will invest in areas per prospectus.
items.quote: the capital raise in the IPO is not yet deployed. In fact, the only thing that has been even withdrawn from the IPO account is just the (GCP) the General Corporate Purpose. I can tell you that we will start making investments in the areas that we have already mentioned in our prospectus and we hope that the outcome will start playing out in the upcoming quarters and years.

items.statement: Fixed costs to be optimized, not increased, operating leverage to kick in.
items.quote: going forward we will continue to synergize and optimize on cost, definitely not increase it, look at opportunities to optimize it further from here on.

items.statement: Long-term bullish on distribution of financial products, including savings and investment.
items.quote: if you think about distribution of financial products, we are extremely bullish long-term across not just lending but also savings and investment products

items.statement: Payments GMV mix: wallet, bill payments, UPI, and others.
items.quote: the payment GMV that we have comprises of… I mentioned in the beginning also that we are the largest player in the wallet business. So, of course, people are using the wallet on eCommerce merchants for their daily life use cases like food, grocery, travel, etc., and same thing in offline merchants also whether they are organized retail, petrol pumps or small mom and pop stores. But apart from wall

items.statement: Insurance distribution license to launch in 2025.
items.quote: we also have the “Insurance Distribution License,” which we are yet to launch, but in 2025 this calendar year, we expect to launch that also.

items.statement: Expects to start receiving UPI incentives in future.
items.quote: we do expect that whatever are the budgeted annual incentives available, we expect that in the future, we will also start getting our proportion.

items.statement: No significant impact expected from new wallet license entrants.
items.quote: we don't expect that there will be a significant impact for any new player joining the ecosystem, as you can see, many more people are applying now for wallet licenses.

items.statement: Expects annualized jewellery EBIT margin between 11% and 11.5%.
items.quote: But yes, therefore, long story short, I think we can expect to be anchored around the current levels of EBIT margins. And for an annualized basis between 11% to 11.5% is what I think we are likely to realistically achieve.

items.statement: Sees 11% as a threshold for annualized jewellery EBIT margin, not to go below.
items.quote: But by and large, not going below 11% on an annualized basis is for sure my threshold. I don't know how much leeway the Board or Venkat will give me.

items.statement: Jewellery EBIT margin guidance is on a standalone basis, not consolidated.
items.quote: Yes, margin is on a standalone basis what we gave, 11% to 11.5%. Consol I am not giving.

items.statement: Q4 started well but difficult to predict due to gold price volatility.
items.quote: So, we started very well in the first few weeks of January, first 2 to 3 weeks. And then suddenly after many exciting developments in the international, especially US, has created a lot of excitement on gold price again and dollars.

items.statement: Hopes to sustain growth rates seen in Q2 plus Q3, but difficult to predict.
items.quote: We hope that we are able to sustain some kind of growth rates that we have seen between -- cumulatively between all the quarters put together, or at least quarter 2 plus quarter 3, but slightly difficult to predict. But longer term, we are more confident.

items.statement: Gold on lease rates could increase; will manage with other levers.
items.quote: But definitely the initial indications are that the gold on lease rates could go up. It's just that we need to wait for a month or two to understand how the supply, and therefore the pricing, will play out.

items.statement: Gold price volatility may cause consumers to become cautious.
items.quote: And therefore, during a very volatile period, consumers also kind of become a little cautious. But other than getting caught in the noise -- see, this year, quarter 1 was subdued.

items.statement: Gold price rise may dilute studded gross contribution percentages.
items.quote: As a consequence, with spiralling gold prices, there is likely to be some impact on the line-item level GC studded. And therefore, that also shows up.

items.statement: Wearables strategy to show results in 6 to 18 months.
items.quote: We should be able to implement and see the results in the next, I'd say, 6 to 18 months.

items.statement: Wedding season correlates with watch sales, especially higher-priced watches.
items.quote: So, wedding season does have a good correlation, and I think that, along with a slew of very attractive new products, should work in our favour.

items.statement: Taneira retail growth 30%, buyer growth 38%, but sales flattish due to fewer store openings.
items.quote: But if you look at our retail growth, we grew by 30% and our buyer growth was 38%. The reason why it looks flattish is because last year we had opened seven L3 stores in quarter 3, and whereas this year we opened only one L3.

items.statement: CaratLane like-to-like store growth 16% in Q3, previous quarter 21%.
items.quote: And I can give you some indication of our like-to-like store growth which is also very good, the 16% in quarter Sensitivity: Internal 3 and previous quarter is 21% which is significantly higher than what happened in the previous four or five quarters

items.statement: New income tax changes expected to benefit consumption sector, including jewellery.
items.quote: I think it will benefit the whole consumption sector, not just the jewellery sector. Of course, we will get our due share of that. It is certainly a welcome move from multiple angles.

items.statement: Competitive intensity on pricing is ongoing, no stability expected.
items.quote: I think it is an ever-increasing spree, and therefore our efforts are also in that direction to see what we can do between product mix, between better sourcing, between working on minimising gold loss, GC max, a lot of execution, which kind of helps us stay afloat, including even good strategies on hedging and spot buying versus gold metal loans.

items.statement: New competitor stores near Titan stores can impact performance in some locations.
items.quote: But there are stores which might be, let's say, intrinsically needing a bigger location Sensitivity: Internal or, let's say, the operational effectiveness of the store has been a little question mark. In those markets, in that particular store, we do see an impact

items.statement: Focus on growth over margins due to market share opportunity.
items.quote: We think it would be appropriate to chase growth over margins. And in a way, that has been our enduring strategy.

items.statement: Spent INR12,000 crores in 9M FY25, plans INR10,000 crores in Q4, total FY25 capex INR22,000 crores.
items.quote: During the last 9 months, we have spent capex of nearly INR12,000 crores, which was the total capex that we spent in the previous financial year. And we have plans to spend another INR10,000 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Expects peak power demand of 265-270 GW this summer due to intense summer.
items.quote: Considering that, we do expect that there will be a peak demand of nearly 265 to 270 gigawatt. Already today, it was more than 230 gigawatt.

items.statement: Cell plant first 2 GW stabilized at 90% capacity; second 2 GW commissioned in January, to stabilize by February, full benefit in FY26.
items.quote: The second 2 gigawatt also has been commissioned in January and is under stabilization process. And we expect that within February, it will get stabilized and will be able to produce at full capacity during the next financial year.

items.statement: 1,100 MW wind turbines under implementation, to be commissioned in 3-12 months; another 1.6 GW to be ordered in next 60 days.
items.quote: So as we have shared with you, 1,000 megawatts, we had already, in fact, 1,100-odd megawatt, we have already done. Those wind turbines are already under implementation. And all of them will get commissioned in the next 3 months to 12 months. There's another 1.6 gigawatts that we will be ordering. All this ordering will happen in the next 60 days.

items.statement: Plans to install 2 to 2.5 GW of renewable projects annually in FY26 and FY27.
items.quote: And as Sanjeev mentioned, in FY '25 -- '26 and '27, about 2 to 2.5 gigawatt of renewable projects, which will be a mix of solar and wind that we will implement.

items.statement: EPC margin guidance is 5% to 7% on a year-to-date basis.
items.quote: The best way to look is at the year to date number, which reflects the right position, and they're kind of in the range of 5% to 7% on EPC margin, which has always been our guidance.

items.statement: Nuclear power details still unclear; expects more details in coming months before action plan.
items.quote: So many of these are still gr ey areas and we expect that in the coming months, more details will be shared at. At that stage, we will be able to come out with our action plan on it.

items.statement: Committed to achieve 70% clean energy by 2030, currently at 43%.
items.quote: As we move forward, we are committed to our overall goal that we will achieve 70% of clean energy by 2030. We are already at 43% and the various projects which are under implementation, we should be in a position to meet those targets.

items.statement: Net debt INR44,700 crores, debt to equity 1.1:1, net debt to EBITDA less than 3.
items.quote: Our debt today is -- our net debt is about INR 44,700 crores and our debt to equity is 1.1:1 and our debt -- net debt to underlying EBITDA is less than 3.

items.statement: Rooftop business crossed INR500 crores revenue in the quarter with healthy EBITDA and PAT.
items.quote: For the first time we crossed in the quarter, INR500 crores of revenue with a very healthy EBITDA and PAT.

items.statement: Transmission projects won four bids; all to be completed in FY26 except one, benefits from FY26.
items.quote: We won four bids and construction activity of all those four projects are going up -- going on. And we expect that in FY '26, all of them will be completed excepting one 15 months and the benefit of that in terms of revenue, EBITDA and PAT will start coming from FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Odisha operations stabilized; Q4 expected better than Q3 and last year.
items.quote: And also the fourth quarter will be, again, much better than the third quarter and second quarter and also compared to last year because many of these things, initiatives in terms of technology, in terms of our interventions which we have carried out, will start showing better results.

items.statement: PAT growth for 21st consecutive quarter; trend expected to continue.
items.quote: This is the 21st consecutive quarter in which we have shown the PAT growth. And this demonstrates the strong performance of each of our businesses. And each one of them are now getting consolidated and stabilized in terms of their performance.

items.statement: Renewable business EBITDA up 38% in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the renewable business itself has gone up by 38%. And also our PAT has gone up for renewable business in this quarter as well as for the full 9 months.

items.statement: Won 400 MW solar module supply order under ALMM; execution next quarter.
items.quote: As Dr. Sinha was speaking, you see already those coming in that Tata Power has won solar in the sake is option for supply in 400 megawatt of domestically manufactured solar modules. So very clearly, we already see that happening next quarter with the sale as well as in-house.

items.statement: Pump storage projects: civil work started, orders to be finalized this month, full work next month.

items.statement: Maintains outlook for transition to growth in second half of this year and into next fiscal.

items.statement: U.S. biotech market dynamics stabilizing, albeit slightly later than expected.

items.statement: Expects robust business performance in medium term, with visibility for coming couple of years.

items.quote: This money I will see that utilization will be completed in next 18 months' time and will start aiding for the business of the Company.

items.quote: On our own at least another 10 locations will get added in FY26. I am talking about FY26 because current years 4 remaining locations I have already explained which are going to be completed by March '25.

items.quote: So, if any import policy change and if any additional tariff is levied on those imported items which are mainly coming from China, Thailand, Indonesia, then that may impact to certain extent to the price and to the cost. items.statement: Gross margin, EBITDA margin and PAT margin expected to remain stable within +/-1-2%
items.quote: Hardly (+/-1%) or (+/-2%) will be there.

items.quote: Those varies with the quality. But for us it will be around 30% to 40% on the gross level.

items.quote: It is a finance cost includes that credit card commission and during festival season there is a mini debit and credit cards are coming in and larger the sale, larger the card usages. Those costs are going up. Those costs are not going up because we are borrowing or anything.

items.statement: Fashion jewellery industry growing at 25-30% CAGR, boosted by tax changes and 8th pay commission
items.quote: This industry that is a fashion jewellery industry is growing almost at 25% to 30% CAGR. And if you look our turnover right now, this year it has surpassed the thing. items.quote: Overall sale with studded to the silver jewellery, silver jewellery is 48% and 43% is diamond.
