items.quote: It has gone up from 2% to almost 4.25% that is doubled in last one year time. And I am expecting in percentage wise it should reach to 6% to 6.5%. Again and again, I am telling you this is with zero cash burn.

items.statement: No government approval yet for 9 carat gold hallmarking, still pending with BIS
items.quote: No. Still government has not ap proved that request from the industry for adding 9 carat in the list of the BIS approved Hallmark K aratage. As on date it is only 14, 18, 20, 22 and to some extent a 24 carat

items.quote: Lab grown diamond and the category where we are dealing like a small diamond studded in the gold which are ranging from 1 cent to 15 cent. Secondly, the cost of setting of this diamond irrespective whether it is a lab grown or the natural that is not differing.

items.quote: And this Dipanjan we are now taking a 3-year view. Now we are clear that in 3 years, Wealth will move from 65 to 60 %.

items.quote: And I think even if capital markets deteriorate by 20% from here, given how our business is proportioned, our cost income will remain at 54%.

items.quote: But with that allocated cost loading, I think by the time we crossed about INR 20,000 crores, so maybe another 12 to 15 months.

items.quote: So, I think out of the two-three factors, two are temporary, and we will see the margins come back in Q4 for this part of the business.

items.statement: AUM growth to be at least 25% in two to three years.

items.quote: In terms of overall activity, I think institutional equity volumes is the only place where we are seeing some impact. Other than that, largely things remain to be in place.

items.statement: Global situation and US tariffs could impact markets, need to be watchful.
items.quote: I mean there is a significant change in leadership in the US . items.statement: Managed products share in MPIS flows increased to 65-70%.
items.quote: Basically, out of the net new money that is coming in now Prayesh , about 65%-70% essentially pertains to PMS, AIF and MF in terms of MPIS flow.

items.statement: Targets FY25 revenue of INR 2,150 crores plus.

items.statement: Guides FY25 EBITDA margin at 7.25%-7.5%.
items.quote: And for this current fiscal year, we believe that our EBITDA margins would be around 7.25%-7.5% range which we ha ve been also guiding previously to the market. So, we will be targeting to keep the margins somewhere around 7.25%-7.5% and further normalization of Sri City would definitely help us drive margins better in the coming years.

items.statement: Plans INR 220-240 crores capex over next 2 years; INR 55-60 crores already invested in 9M FY25.
items.quote: As we mentioned last time that there will be around INR 220-INR 240 crores investment in next 2 years, the company has already invested around INR 55-INR 60 crores in first 9 months.

items.statement: Expects AC dependence to reduce to 60-65% in 2-3 years from 80%.
items.quote: Despite growing at let us say, above the market growth of 20% in AC, we believe that our overall dependence on AC on an annualized basis will come down from 80% to somewhere around 60%-65% in next 2-3 years, which essentially means that our small appliances, the new segment of larger appliances like washing machines and coolers as well as component business is deemed to grow at a much faster rate.

items.statement: Targets component revenue to reach 12-15% of total in 2-3 years.
items.quote: So, the component definitely from 4% in the last year currently at almost 6% and then up to 12%-15% is definitely one number we are looking at in the medium term in next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Targets ROE/ROCE of 15%-16% in next 2-3 years, FY27-28 onwards.
items.quote: In terms of RO E/ROCE, we are looking at anywhere around 15%-16% in next 2-3 years, so FY27-28 onwards, we definitely will be able to improve the ROE to 15% plus level.

items.statement: Strong AC demand continues; order book for season extremely good.
items.quote: The order book for the sea son is extremely good and with this additional impetus given by the Government of India in terms of additional discretionary income, we believe that AC is definitely one segment which we will see a lot of better traction.

items.statement: Copper supply chain disrupted due to lack of BIS approvals; some relief now.
items.quote: Q3, we had a lot of disruptions in the critical raw material copper which kind of disrupted the industr y. There was no local supply available, and the BIS approval was not given to the Chinese manufacturers, so that definitely impacted the industry.

items.quote: Compressor is something which is not directly or currently impacting the industry, but definitely June onwards when a few suppliers lose their BIS certificate unless a renewal is done, that will definitely lead to certain disruption.

items.quote: So, definitely, Q1 of next financial year should be the period from where our real mass production to start for washing machine. items.quote: So, towards mid of March, we should be starting our production for air fryers and then more categories are in their addition and we will see lot of newer products coming in Q2 of next financial year.

items.quote: So, we are targeting to achieve revenue of almost Rs. 150 crores at the new facility for financial year 25-26.

items.quote: In terms of receivable, our last receivable of approx INR 30 crores is expected to be received before end of March. So, technically, last year also, we received it in the month of March. So, this year also, we are contemplating that March should be the time by when we should receive this Rs. 30 crores which has been included in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Working capital requirement maintained at INR 350-360 crores.
items.quote: And we will be maintaining this requirement around INR 350 - INR 360 crores.

items.quote: Our EBITDA margin, if you see, so we have already given the guidance that the pure EBITDA margin, that is from the construction of EPC, pure EBITDA margins would range from 12.5% to 13%.

items.statement: Aggregate EBITDA margin guidance 14.5% to 15.5%.
items.quote: Over and above that, including other income, bonus and royalty, we are targeting to achieve the aggregate margin of 14.5% to 15.5%.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth guidance 15% to 20%.
items.quote: So we have always guided our investors that we should always have organic growth of around 15%, 20%.

items.quote: The first HAM project is AAA rated, which is Malout Abohar Sadhuwali. And our equity IRR after the completion is almost 20%.

items.quote: As far as these Ayodhya, both the HAM projects are concerned s o we like we have to infuse INR350 crores. As well as Varanasi is concerned , we are supposed to invest INR 290 crores. Over a period of next 2.5 years.

items.quote: So if you talk about the fund-based limit, so we have a quantum of INR125 crores unutilized as we speak. You're talking about unutilized fund-based limit or unutilized non-fund-based limits?

items.statement: Expects export markets to recover to original levels in the medium term.
items.quote: However, notwithstanding the above, we expect these markets to recover and come back to their original levels in the medium term soon.

items.statement: Confident short-term domestic situation will correct in the near term.
items.quote: Even in the domestic market, we are positive of the long-term direction of the Indian industry and are confident that the short-term situation will correct in the near term given the push from the government as well as the major transition towards greener alternatives like the electric vehicles and alternate fuel solutions like hybrid, hydrogen, Compressed Natural Gas, HCNG applications, LNG appli

items.statement: Expects all powertrain technologies to coexist; IC engines in 2030 to exceed today's production.

items.statement: Coimbatore plant on track, starting by end of March.

items.statement: Will continue investing in legacy and new businesses; also looking for further M&A opportunities.

items.statement: U.S. annual contracts done with $0.50 to $1 reduction; India pricing steady.
items.quote: Yes, when I spoke about $0.50 to $1 reduction, that is mainly the U.S. market. It's a blended number. And in India, the pricing is more or less steady as we speak.

items.statement: China soda ash prices below cash cost; need at least $30 increase to be sustainable.
items.quote: But the real issue is that the synthetic Ash plants are selling below cash costs at the current price, $180, which is the current price. I think they need to sort of increase it by at least $30 more, in our view.

items.statement: UK Lostock soda ash plant ceased operations; unlikely to restart; other parts continue.
items.quote: The Lostock plant has ceased to operate, and it is unlikely that it is going to start. But other parts will continue. What I mentioned is the Bicarb at Winnington and salt at Middlewich which will continue.

items.statement: Took exceptional charge of Rs.70 crore for employee termination and decommissioning at Lostock.
items.quote: We also took an exceptional charges Rs.70 crore consisting of estimated expenses related to employee termination benefits, the decommissioning of the plant, as we cease the operation of Soda ash production at our Lostock site.

items.statement: 70,000 TPA Medi-Salt plant commissioned in UK.
items.quote: 70,000 TPA Medi-Salt plant has been commissioned in the UK.

items.statement: FOS plant on track for full capacity utilization.
items.quote: Our FOS plant is on track to go into full utilization of capacity.

items.statement: Imposition of MIP expected to be sentimentally positive, safeguarding domestic price volatility.
items.quote: Imposition of MIP is expected to be sentimentally positive as this will safeguard the domestic price volatility.

items.statement: U.S. exports to Southeast Asian countries increased significantly.
items.quote: U.S. exports to Southeast Asian countries , Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand increased significantly.

items.statement: India soda ash prices declined about 15% year-on-year due to lower-priced imports.
items.quote: In India, soda ash prices declined compared to last year's same quarter by about 15%, primarily driven by lower-priced imports.

items.statement: China soda ash prices sharply dropped 25% to 30%.
items.quote: In terms of pricing, China soda ash prices sharply dropped anywhere between 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Overall revenue down 4% versus Q3FY24 due to pricing pressure.
items.quote: Overall the revenue was down 4% against Q3FY24, largely due to pricing pressure.

items.statement: Expects current pricing levels to continue for at least three to six months.
items.quote: So , we had already highlighted that this level is likely to continue for three to six months at least.

items.statement: Expects M&HCV market to be down about 5% for the full year ending March.
items.quote: This year, that is ending March as a full year, we do expect the M&HCV market to be down by about 5% compared to last year.

items.statement: Expects Q4 M&HCV volume around 110,000 units, similar to last year.
items.quote: So, we are expecting the Q4 to be in the vicinity of last year's overall volume, which is around 110,000.

items.statement: Expects M&HCV market to be flat next year.
items.quote: So -- and coming to next year forecast, which we are working through, we expect the market to be flat again.

items.statement: Aims to double revenue by 2029-2030.
items.quote: So, in a long-term perspective, '29-2030, with the projected market volume, we are expecting a doubling of our revenue.

items.statement: Expects to grow better than the market, with 14-16% CAGR needed to double.
items.quote: On an average, we need to do a CAGR of about anywhere between 14% to 16% if we have to double the growth, right?

items.statement: Plans INR300 crores capex over next 3 years, with INR72 crores already approved.
items.quote: So, we are looking at initially next 3 years, as I mentioned, INR300 crores and of which about INR72 crores is already approved.

items.statement: Aims to maintain current margins and improve by 1-2% with investments.
items.quote: So, even with the increased revenues, we'll be able to maintain and then slightly improve upon like what Ranga mentioned, probably another 1% to 2% upside is available there.

items.statement: Aspires to improve EBITDA margin to 13-13.5% with volume support.
items.quote: So, even the current volumes, the volumes bless us, we will be definitely able to take it up even beyond 13%, 13.5%.

items.statement: Plans to launch bus axles by end of Q1 next year for MIDV segment.
items.quote: So, it will be ready by first -- end of first quarter next year for the MIDV bus segment.

items.statement: Trials for 13.5 and 15-meter bus axles to start in 2026, with SOP by end of 2025 or early 2026.
items.quote: So, the trials will begin in 2026 and a lot of external factors depend on the trials, readiness of the OEM.

items.statement: Bus market expected to be similar next year with replacement demand.
items.quote: And next year, it could be similar numbers because there's a lot of replacement going on with some of the state-run transportation units.

items.statement: Expects moderate CAGR of 10-11% to reach 500,000 M&HCV by 2029.
items.quote: So that is where we are expecting a moderate CAGR of 10%, 11%, taking us to 500,000 vehicles by 2029 time frame.

items.statement: Sees no major risk from geopolitical tensions or tariffs currently.
items.quote: At this moment of time, the answer is no. Even the global team will be discussing, we're not seeing anything.

items.statement: Working on model to make related party transactions operational from April 1.
items.quote: We will be concluding this somewhere in the first, second week of March to make these things operational and keep running from 1st of April.

items.statement: Maintains INR1,350 crores presales guidance for FY25.
items.quote: So given all this, you maintain the INR1,350 crores presales guideline for FY 257 Yes.

items.statement: Plans to launch six projects in next two quarters with 1.7 million sq ft and GDV INR4,300 crores.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are well prepared with the launch of our six projects in the next 2 quasters, collectively giving us about 1.7 million square feet with a GDV of INR 4,300 crores.

items.statement: Two projects to launch in Q4 FY25, four in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Sowe have given the quarter of the guidance kind of a thing, quarter 4 FY 25, which is the 2 projects and happy to bring the fact that Lakeside Paradise being thenew entrant in this particular launch list and for which we have already received the RERA certificate and which is going to be the event of this current quarter, March '25. And Wadala, we are very aggressively working to bring it within

items.statement: Police housing construction cost estimated INR50-80 crores.
items.quote: And that project, overall, our estimation is about INRS0 crores to INRG0 crores on construction and ofher approval processes.

items.statement: Added projects with total GDV INR2,450 crores in last 9 months.
items.quote: As a result of which we have added about a few projects, which is giving a total GDV of INR2,450 crores with an expected sales velocity of one million.

items.statement: Expects 33-34% EBITDA margins sustainable going forward.
items.quote: Yes, because like we have been having the good sales run-up kind of a thing, faster exceution of the projects, plus the recent equity, which is raised kind of a thing on which we have delevered our balance sheet kind of a thing. Those factors are like helping us to go further more cfficient. And we expect that on a going forward basis also, margin is sustainable.

items.statement: NGT order stayed environmental clearances, hindering approvals.
items.quote: But there were certain hindrances in the approvals related to the authority like the recent - there was, if you know, the NGT order, which had stayed the approvals related to the environment clcarances.

items.statement: Revenue visibility from ongoing projects INR1,700+ crores, launch pipeline INR4,300 crores, total INR6,000+ crores.
items.value: INR1,700-plus crores, INR4,300 crores, INR6,000-plus crores
items.quote: With the OC reccived and ongoing project ~ ongoing portfolio, we have now revenue visibility of INR1,700-plus crores, Additionally, our projects in launch pipeline are estimated to contribute about INR4,300 crores. So as a result, the total revenue visibility stands stronger than ever at about INR6,000-plus crores,

items.statement: Estimated net cash flow pre-tax post debt from OC received and ongoing projects about INR714 crores.
items.quote: The estimated net cash flow pretax post debt from OC received and ongoing projects is expected about INR7 14 crores.

items.statement: Reduced debt by 14% in last 9 months, improving debt-equity ratio to 0.57x:1.
items.quote: I'm also pleased to inform you that following our equity raise, the company has successfully reduced its debt by about 14% in the last 9 months, amounting to INR107 crores, thercby improving the debt-equity ratio to 0.57x:1.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of debt stable at about 12.22%.
items.quote: The weighted average cost of the debt remains stable at about 12.22%.

items.statement: Kanjurmarg project expected 35% project-level return.
items.quote: And overall, like we arc looking at a project level retum kind of a thing, almost on the upwards of 35%.

items.statement: Wadala project launch targeted in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Well, our endeavor is definitely to launch in Q4, and thatis what we are pushing to, just crossing fingers that approvals don't take a litfle further away, but we should be able to launch. Right now, our all endeavor is to launch this in Q4.

items.statement: Rustomjee redevelopment project launch targeted in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Yes. We are underway of the basic approval for the project. Partly, we've already got, part is under progress right now and our endeavour is to launch this by the first quarter of next financial year, that is FY '26. So between, let's say, April to June is what we endeavour to launch this project.

items.statement: Expects next financial year revenue around INR1,800 crores to INR1,900 crores.
items.quote: Next financial year, we are looking at around INR1,800 crores to INR1,900 crores revenue.

items.statement: Revised capital outlay for Odisha rPET expansion to 67,500 tons per annum is around INR600 crores.
items.quote: With regards to our expansion plans of 45,000 tons per annum of rPET granules in Odisha, we have decided to increase its size to 67,500 tons per annum and the revised capital outlay for the same will be estimated to around INR600 crores.

items.statement: Total capex for 90,000 tons capacity addition is about INR700 crores.
items.quote: About INR700 crores. Earlier, we were -- for the two lands, we had a capex of INR 450 crores, but now it is 90,000 tons, it has been now INR700 crores.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins of 22% to 25% in rPET granule business.
items.quote: So Prakash ji, if you are talking about the rPET granule, so the asset turn is about 1.25 to 1.5. Asset turn is lower because the capex is higher in this business, but of course as per the capital deployment, margins are also higher. So we are looking for EBITDA margins in the range of 22% to 25% in this business.

items.statement: With 90,000 tons capacity addition, about 65% revenue will come from value-added products.
items.quote: So with this capacity addition of 90,000 tons, we are looking for about 65% revenue will come from the value-added products.

items.statement: Good demand visibility for rPET granules next financial year; no difficulty from demand side.
items.quote: Our products has been well stabilized in the market already, and we have a good demand visibility for the next financial year and do not forsee any difficulty from demand side.

items.statement: Recycled filament yarn demand yet to pick up; noticeable ramp-up expected by Q2 FY26.
items.quote: In the recycled filament yarn segment, we are still exploring the market development and demand is yet to pick up. Noticeable ramp-up, we are expecting to pick up by Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Anticipates persistence of current adverse situation for some more quarters.
items.quote: Going forward, we are anticipating the persistence of the situation for some more quarters, it will get reversed if either the demand matches the supply or some kind of consolidation happens in the industry.

items.statement: For rPET granules, raw material price increase is not borne by company; margins protected.
items.quote: So for the rPET granules unit we are not putting up the raw material increase in our account. So our margins are protected in that business as of now.

items.statement: Raised INR500 crores via QIP and promoter warrants for expansion; funding capex through internal accrual and equity.
items.quote: So the capex is around INR700 crores, and we have raised the funds through QIP of INR350 crores and the promoter’s preferential warrants is also there for INR150 crores. So in all, we raised INR500 crores of funds.

items.statement: Warangal brownfield expansion expected operational by end of this calendar year.
items.quote: Yes, of course, we are looking for operationalizing this plant -- this expansion by the end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Expects other products from Warangal to take off by September 2025.
items.quote: As of now, we are expecting it will take another 2 to 3 quarters and we are expecting it will take off by September '25.

items.statement: Total debt may go up to INR700 crores to INR750 crores when working capital facilities are drawn.
items.quote: Yes. So presently, our total debt position is about INR500 crores. So going forward, when we draw down our working capital facilities, the debt may go up to INR700 crores, INR750 crores.

items.statement: Standalone capacity utilization about 106%.
items.quote: So the standalone capacity utilization is about 106%.

items.statement: Warangal plant capacity utilization about 65%.
items.quote: So sorry, it is about the Warangal plant -- it is not a consolidated one. Warangal is 65%.

items.statement: Robust positive demand and sentiment across trade channel ahead of Summer '25; confident about March '25 quarter performance.
items.quote: So ahead of Summer '25, very robust positive demand and sentiment across the trade channel, across the geographies and on top of it, as all of you are aware, considering the major income tax relief given which will be mainly availed by air cooler class of consumers that should further boost our business. And we are quite confident about performance of March '25 quarter.

items.statement: 17 new air cooler models received overwhelming response and will be margin accretive.
items.quote: There has been overwhelming response to 17 new range of air coolers, and they will be margin accretive.

items.statement: Record unbilled advances of about ₹150 crores for 17 new models; production started Dec-Jan, sales spill over to March quarter.
items.quote: As on 31st December, for Q3 end, there has been a record unbilled advances surpassing even domestic sales, which is about ₹150 crores. And primarily, they are meant for 17 new models.

items.statement: Temporary calibration in EBITDA and PAT due to low margin models, water heater launch expenses, and forex loss.
items.quote: There has been temporary calibration in EBITDA and business PAT, mainly because low margin models have been billed in December '24 quarter, and in addition to that, there has been water heater launch expenses and also forex loss of ₹3.8 crores on a stand-alone basis, while on a consolidated basis, there is a forex loss of almost ₹9 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Residual outstanding of ₹46 crores from Pathways provided as doubtful debt; stringent credit risk mitigation implemented.
items.quote: However, as per accounting standard, and also on a conservative basis, residual outstanding of ₹46 crores from Pathways has been provided for during the quarter as a doubtful debt. This is in addition to earlier provisions made.

items.statement: Interim dividend of ₹2 per share announced; total payout in 9M about ₹124 crores, 92% of consol profit.
items.quote: And during the quarter, interim dividend of ₹2 per share i.e. 100% has been announced. This is in addition to buyback of shares as well as earlier int erim dividends

items.statement: GSK China 9M turnover ₹75 crores vs ₹33 crores; PAT ₹10 crores vs ₹1 crore; repaid loan over ₹10 crores, remaining ₹50 crores.
items.quote: About GSK China, it has achieved a remarkable turnover and performance. For 9M, the turnover stands at ₹75 crores versus ₹33 crores, while PAT stands at ₹10 crores versus ₹1 crore.

items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia not performing well; CODB reduced from A$15 million to A$7.5 million; transformation Phase 2 almost done.
items.quote: So, Climate Technologies, Australia is not performing well. Its performance currently is in line with earlier years of IMPCO and GSK China. As conveyed earlier, its first phase of transformation i.e. CODB reduction from A$15 million to A$7.5 million has been already achieved.

items.statement: Stand-alone 9M top line up 49% at ₹814 crores; EBITDA ₹188 crores up 91%; PAT ₹132 crores.
items.quote: So 9M stand-alone performance as of 31st December, top line is up by 49% at ₹814 crores. EBITDA at ₹188 crores versus ₹98 crores, i.e. up by 91%, and PAT, after providing for exceptional item and December quarter specific expenses in all ₹54 crores, stands at ₹132 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated 9M revenue crossed ₹1,000 crores at ₹1,088 crores, up 32%; gross margin 50.50%, up 260 bps; EBITDA margin 19.40%, up 570 bps.
items.quote: For the first time in 9 months at a consol level, Symphony has crossed revenue of ₹1,000 crores and it stands at ₹1,088 crores, up by 32%. Its gross margin stands at 50.50%, Y-o-Y up by 260 bps.

items.statement: Subsidiaries 9M top line ₹327 crores up 10%; EBITDA ₹24 crores; ex-forex PAT ₹8 crores vs negative ₹5 crores.
items.quote: So subsidiary-wise financials for 9 months, all Subsidiaries put together in the 9 months have registered top line of ₹327 crores, up by 10% Y-o-Y. EBITDA is ₹24 crores, up from ₹15 crores, while ex-forex PAT is ₹8 crores versus negative ₹5 crores.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated top line ₹242 crores, PAT negative ₹10 crores, EBITDA positive ₹35 crores; EBITDA margin 14.7%.
items.quote: So at top line level, it stands at ₹242 crores. And at a PAT level, it is negative ₹10 crores, while EBITDA is positive ₹35 crores.

items.statement: Q3 stand-alone EBITDA ₹34 crores, PAT negative ₹4 crores; EBITDA margin 18.8%.
items.quote: So EBITDA otherwise stands at ₹34 crores, but after providing for all other expenses, etc, PAT is negative ₹4 crores. And about EBITDA margin movement, which stands at 18.8% for the quarter.

items.statement: Q3 December specific expenses stand-alone ₹53 crores including doubtful debt ₹46 crores, water heater launch ₹3.6 crores, forex loss ₹3.80 crores.
items.quote: For the quarter, overall, as I explained earlier, performance is subdued, but mainly spill over to March quarter and for the quarter, there are December quarter specific expenses in all ₹53 crores, which includes provisions for doubtful debt of ₹46 crores, water heater launch expenses of ₹3.6 crores and forex loss of ₹3.80 crores, in all ₹53 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated December specific expenses ₹59 crores including additional forex loss ₹5.6 crores.
items.quote: And on consol basis, December specific expenses stand at ₹59 crores, additional ₹5.6 crores on account of forex loss, which is mark to market as explained earlier for Brazil as well as Climate Technologies and partly IMPCO Mexico.

items.statement: Treasury as on 31st December ₹488 crores; capital employed negative ₹21 crores stand-alone; ROCE infinite; Return on Net Worth 24%.
items.quote: And treasury as on 31st December is ₹488 crores. For the quarter, overall, as I explained earlier, performance is subdued, but mainly spill over to March quarter and for the quarter, there are December quarter specific expenses in all ₹53 crores, which includes provisions for doubtful debt of ₹46 crores, water heater launch expenses of ₹3.6 crores and forex loss of ₹3.80 crores, in all ₹53 crores.

items.statement: Domestic business to end year at 430-440 crores, B2C at 300 crores.
items.quote: You are right, we had guided that this year we will end the total domestic business above 400 crores. We are likely to be there 430-440 crores, out of which the B2C will be 300 crores.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance for the year is 10-20%.
items.quote: So, you know, if you see while for the last three, four years, we have been guiding a 15% or so plus volume growth, at the start of the year, considering the volatility in the market, the high prices, we had indicated that this time our guidance will be between 10 to 20%.

items.statement: Long-term volume growth guidance of 15% is maintained.
items.quote: As long as the consumption is intact, I think things should settle down and probably should not impact our long-term growth guidance of 15%. So, that we are committed.

items.statement: EBITDA growth expected to be 15-20% until volume growth returns to 15-20%.
items.quote: So, we are very confident of maintaining this EBITDA growth of 15 to 20% till we are back into the volume growth of 15 to 20%, which then will again drive EBITDA at the same level.

items.statement: No CAPEX planned for next year; capacity building done for three years.
items.quote: I don't think so we will have any CAPEX in next year. We are done with our CAPEX for the next three years or so because most of our capacity building is over now.

items.statement: 7,000 metric ton capacity to be commissioned this quarter.
items.quote: This quarter we will commission that capacity.

items.statement: B2C segment expected to yield higher margins than B2B over long term.
items.quote: But having said so, we are confident that over a long period of time, definitely the B2C segment, the branded segment will help us gain more margins than the B2B setup.

items.statement: Taken 30-40% price increases in larger packs; another 10-15% lag remains.
items.quote: Having said so, in the larger packs, we already have taken almost 30 to 40% price increases in the last 1, 1.5 years, and I think another 10 to 15% lag is still left, but we will wait and watch for the leaders that how do they take this forward and accordingly we will formulate our price increases as strategy.

items.statement: 10-15% grammage cut in LUPs in last 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: There have been grammages cut over a period of time, not very much because, you know, there is a certain cup of coffee that you have to deliver with one LUP. So, we don't have a lot of leeway to cut grammages, but yes, there has been 10 to 15% grammage cut that has happened in LUPs in the last 1, 1.5 years.

items.statement: Coffee prices not expected to soften until Brazilian crop in May-June.
items.quote: So, probably we will have to wait for, you know, other crops to come in, which is Brazilian crop in May-June. That's the time we will see how the trend goes, but as of now the prices are not, you know, softening.

items.statement: Volume growth this quarter was 3-4%, YTD around 10%.
items.quote: So, volume growth, if you see this quarter has been marginal around 3 to 4% or so, and the YTD if you see the first quarter, we were around 13-14%, the second quarter was around 9-10%. So, we are on a YTD basis close to close to 10% of volume growth.

items.statement: 30-35% of sales from LUPs.
items.quote: The second question is as far as LUPs are concerned, almost today our 30 to 35% of our sales come from LUPs which is still reasonable considering that, you know, some of the leaders, their sales are almost 50 to 60% of their sales are LUPs.

items.statement: Working capital high at 1,200 crores due to high coffee prices.
items.quote: So, you know, working capital, yes, it remains high because of, it's almost 1,200 crores as we speak. It remains high because of the high coffee prices.

items.statement: Total debt around 2,000 crores; long-term debt 790-800 crores.
items.quote: And I told you the debt numbers, 1,200 crores of working capital. Long-term debt is around 790 to 800 crores as of now. Total is around 2,000 crores of debt.

items.statement: Peak debt not to exceed 2,200 crores in next two years; annual repayment 150-200 crores.
items.quote: I don't see the peak debt levels going beyond 2,200 crores in the next year or the year after that also. In fact, it should start reducing because we will be repaying it.

items.statement: Post-renovation, first full year revenues expected at INR170 crores with EBITDA north of INR60 crores.
items.value: INR170 crores, EBITDA north of INR60 crores
items.quote: So where potentially post-renovation, in the first full year, we're looking at revenues of about INR170 crores with an EBITDA north of INR60 crores.

items.statement: Post-renovation ADRs expected to improve to INR9,500 to INR10,500.
items.quote: Post-renovation, we expect our ADRs to significantly improve to INR9,500 to INR10,500 mark.

items.statement: Post-renovation ADR increase can lead to about 30% increase in revenues.
items.quote: But once we are finished, completed the renovation, we can look at the INR9,500 to INR10,500 mark, which can easily lead to about a 30% increase in our revenues.

items.statement: Courtyard by Marriott renovation: 56 new guest rooms on floors 6 and 7, gym/spa on 8, rooftop bar with pool on 9, operational by end of June.
items.quote: The interiors of the remaining four floors are being completed as we speak, and by the end of June, we expect 56 new guest rooms to be added to the sixth and seventh floor, and a brand new state-of-the-art gym and spa facility is on the eighth floor, and a rooftop bar with a pool on the ninth floor.

items.statement: Marriott convention center and select guest rooms renovation to begin April 2025, phase-wise over two years.
items.quote: In the Marriott property, the convention center and select guest rooms attached to the convention center will undergo renovation from April 2025. The Marriott property will undergo renovation in a phase-wise manner over two years, keeping in mind that it is a fully operational hotel.

items.statement: Entire renovation expected to be completed by 2027.
items.quote: And we're expecting the entire renovation to be completed by 2027.

items.statement: In metro cities supply growing 3-4% per year while demand growing 10-12% every year.
items.quote: Even in Hyderabad, there have been a lot of reports about how supply is only growing at about 3% to 4% per year, whereas the demand is growing at about 10%, 12% every year.

items.statement: Over next three to four years, great increase in demand expected.
items.quote: So that way, this is a great sign for us that over the next three to four years, we can see a great increase in demand.

items.statement: Evaluating another hotel in Hyderabad; expanding portfolio to three hotels very soon.
items.quote: So, currently as we speak, we are evaluating another hotel in Hyderabad. Once we have the definitive agreement signed, we will make that announcement. But we are looking at expanding our portfolio to three hotels very, very soon.

items.statement: Rights issue subscribed close to 112%, reflecting strong investor confidence.
items.quote: Also, we would like to state that the company's recent rights issue received an overwhelming response and was subscribed to close to 112%, reflecting strong investor confidence and demand.

items.statement: Flow-through profit from additional ADR jump is almost 95%.
items.quote: And majority of this is driven by the room business, which was typically the flow-through profit in this additional ADR jump is almost about 95%.

items.statement: Occupancy at about 70%, can improve a few percentage points post-renovation.
items.quote: While this is something that we've been able to beat and achieve in the current year in itself, we're almost at about a 70% occupancy mark. And we can see that going forward, once the product is also renovated, we can see a few percentage points improvement.

items.statement: Targeting roughly 20% to 25% CAGR EBITDA over 3 to 5 years.
items.quote: Our focus is on sustainable mid- to long-term growth targeting roughly 20% to 25% CAGR EBITDA over 3 to 5 year’s time frame.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance unchanged at INR1,300 to INR1,500 crore.
items.quote: Our projected capital expenditure for FY '25 remains unchanged as we have m entioned in the last quarter, INR1,300 to INR1,500 crore, with over INR380 crore spent in Q3 and about INR1,020 crore in the 9-month year -till-date time frame

items.statement: FY26 capex to be a bit lower than INR1,000 crore.
items.quote: As regards FY '26, the capex would be a number which will be a bit lower than INR1,000 crore.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA guidance based on 14% to 15% margin assumption.
items.quote: So that number of EBITDA is based on EBITDA assumption of 14% to 15%, right, so you can back calculate the revenue on the basis of that and Arun, as I had mentioned previously, we like to focus on absolute EBITDA and not necessarily give revenue guidance because bulk of our raw materials are linked to crude, right, benzene, aniline, which are 2 of our largest raw materials.

items.statement: Cost reduction plan 30-40% complete, to finish in 12-18 months.
items.quote: I think we are kind of 30% -40% there in terms of that journey. I think there still remains a lot of what's to be done, but we are confident of completing that exercise, as I mentioned in the last call, in the next sort of 12 to 18 months kind of time frame.

items.statement: Representative gross margin around 13%.
items.quote: I think more representative gross margin number is potentially in the range of, I think, 13% -odd kind of a range.

items.statement: Pricing pressure continues in agrochemical intermediates and other chains.
items.quote: However, pricing pressure continues across various product chains, especially in agrochemical intermediates.

items.statement: Non-energy volumes grew 14% Y-o-Y and 8% Q-o-Q.
items.quote: Volumes in the non-energy business grew by 14% Y -o-Y and 8% Q-o-Q, while the growth in the energy business came in at 10% quarter -on-quarter basis.

items.statement: MMA volumes ramp-up gradual but consistent.
items.quote: As indicated in previous communications, the ramp-up of MMA volumes will be gradual but consistent.

items.statement: Developing new products in ethylation value chain and backward integration.
items.quote: And further, in order to diversify our product base and to augment our utilization levels, we are engaged in the development of new products, especially within the ethylation value chain where we recently exp anded our capacity.

items.statement: Uncertainty in 2025 demand due to potential U.S. policy changes.
items.quote: Despite s ome uncertainty surrounding 2025 demand due to potential U.S. policy changes, we remain focused on increasing our market share in the global markets, especially in the U.S. and Japan, for polymer and additives segment.

items.statement: Committed INR100 crore to JV, INR50 crore each partner.
items.quote: So for the first year, both partners put toget her have committed INR100 crore, INR50 crore each, into the joint venture.

items.statement: Renewable share in power purchase to exceed 75% by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: With this, AIL's renewable share in total power purchase is expected to exceed 75% by Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Targeting 14% to 15% ROCE and ROIC in 3-year plan.
items.quote: And as we have indicated in our mid-term guidance, our objective is to hit 14%, 15% kind of ROCE and ROIC numbers. And I think we remain quite confident of hitting those numbers in our 3-year plan.

items.statement: NCB capacity utilization to ramp to 80%-plus next financial year.
items.quote: And in the coming financial year, we expect to ramp that up to 80%-plus kind of level.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY25 marginally negative or near zero; FY26 low single-digit.
items.value: marginally negative or about closer to 0; low single-digit
items.quote: The tax rate in this year, considering that a lot of projects are getting commercialized and there will be some IT depreciation benefits; will continue to remain the way it is currently. So it will be marginally negative and or about closer to 0. Next year, it should be in a more like a low single -digit kind of range, at least at this point of time.

items.statement: Anticipates high teens revenue CAGR over next 3-5 years, with EBITDA margins crossing 20%.
items.quote: I think we are anticipating a growth in the next 3 to 5 years of high teens per year-on-year CAGR if you were to project ourselves out and we were sitting together here in FY '28, 3-4 years from now, and we have to review where the business was in FY '24 and where we are stepwise, we'll get there.

items.statement: Aims to cross 20% EBITDA margin barrier and go beyond.
items.quote: Our aim is to cross the 20% barrier, which we were historically doing about 2, 3 years ago. So, our target is to cross that first and go beyond that also, yes.

items.statement: FY25 capex to be INR140-150 crores; FY26 plan INR150-200 crores annually.
items.quote: Absolutely. We are sticking to what we have said earlier. It will be INR140 crores to INR150 crores.

items.statement: 30-40% of capex for replacement, balance for debottleneck growth.
items.quote: See, 30% to 40% will be replacement capex. The balance will be the debottleneck growth capex.

items.statement: CDMO expected to overtake generics, moving towards 60-40 revenue split.
items.quote: But from a going forward, I think CDMO will overtake the generics business. So, it may be working towards a 60-40 type of split from a revenue perspective.

items.statement: Two NCE products close to launch by end FY26/early FY27; others in FY27 and beyond.
items.quote: Out of that, two products are very close to launch, which we expected to be launched in -- towards the end of financial year FY '26. And the others will get launched if everything goes well, in FY '27 and beyond.

items.statement: Animal Health validation to complete in next 2 quarters; commercial sales from FY26.
items.quote: We expect to complete the validation of the por tfolio in the upcoming 2 quarters, which will assist us in securing the product registration in various countries and ultimately enable the launch of these products across several global markets

items.statement: Animal Health business targeted to exceed INR400 crores over next 5 years.
items.quote: So, we really see a significant amount of growth in excess of INR400-plus crores of business over the next 5 years. So that's the long-term plan that we have and even grow it beyond that.

items.statement: Animal Health contribution margins expected 45% plus, with some products 55%.
items.quote: So, the margins will be -- on the contribution side, I would estimate the margins to be 45% plus, right? Because the portfolio in the Animal Health business is a mix.

items.statement: NCE or CDMO type products in Animal Health to have gross margins in excess of 50%.
items.quote: Yes, certainly. I mean, like I said, is that the NCE type or the CDMO type products will be in excess of 50% in terms of gross margins, right?

items.statement: Crop protection industry expected to stabilize in next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: Despite the ongoing challenges such as pricing pressure from competitors, especially from China, the global crop protection industry is expected to stabilize in the next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: API business recovery expected to remain steady in coming quarters.
items.quote: For our API business, we are witnessing recovery on the back of improved volume uptakes, which is expected to remain steady in the coming quarters.

items.statement: CDMO offtake improvements expected to persist and improve in upcoming quarters.
items.quote: On the CDMO front, we have seen consistently improvements in offtake from key innovators, a trend that is expected to persist and improve in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Intense pricing pressure and dumping from Chinese competitors for generics and commodities.
items.quote: Although China Plus One is expected to strengthen in the current operating environment, intense pricing pressure and dumping continues from the Chinese competitors for generics and commodity products.

items.statement: U.S. tariffs on Chinese chemicals create volatile situation; impact uncertain.
items.quote: So, look, of course, we've heard the news this morning about 10% tariffs on chemical companies in China. We're obviously looking at that. Those are in addition to supposedly 25% already existing tariffs that they have in place.

items.statement: R&D investment maintained at 4.5-5% of revenue.
items.quote: Additionally, we are consistently investing about 4.5% to 5% of our revenue into our R&D to drive innovation in products and services that meet the changing demands of all our customers.

items.statement: Reduced full-year MDF margin guidance to 13-14% from earlier 16% plus.
items.quote: As a result, we are reducing our full year margin guidance to 13 -14% as against earlier of 16% plus.

items.statement: Expects Q4 revenue substantially better and margins stronger.
items.quote: However, in the fourth quarter, we believe that the revenue will substantially be better and margins will be stronger.

items.statement: HDF flooring line delayed by 6 months; equipment to arrive March, fully functional May 2025.
items.quote: Construction of our HDF flooring line has been delayed by 6 months due to the late arrival of major equipment, which is likely to arrive in the month of March and will be fully functional in the month of May '25.

items.statement: Glue plant construction likely to be completed this quarter.
items.quote: Construction of our glue plant is also likely to be completed in this quarter.

items.statement: Aims to cross 10% margin in Q4 due to cost actions, price hike, and better volumes.
items.quote: With all these factors, I mean, definitely, we believe that we should be crossing 10% margin for quarter 4.

items.statement: Took 1.5% MDF price increase in Q3; no further MDF price hike as of now.
items.quote: MDF price increase is around 1.5% during the quarter. And on the plywood side -- plywood, you are saying in the last quarter?

items.statement: Took 1.5% plywood price increase in Q3; taking another 1.5% in Q4.
items.quote: Q3, the price increase was around 1.5%. And we are also taking another price increase during this quarter, which will also be in the range of 1.5%.

items.statement: Demand not picked up; liquidity bigger issue than demand.
items.quote: I think the demand scenario is that it has not really picked up. But added to that, the major problem, what we saw that, even if the demand was there in pockets, liquidity was a serious challenge.

items.statement: Expects positive outlook for panel and plywood business due to BIS regulations and organized shift.
items.quote: But for sure, I see now going forward, things will be very, very positive for panel business and for plywood business. A, because of the implementation of BIS regulations, which will definitely curb imports in the near term.

items.statement: Lost about 1.5% volume due to stringent receivables policy.
items.quote: So I could clearly see that we would have lost maybe easily 1.5% of volume just because we wanted to be controlling our receivables.

items.statement: Announced INR134 crores plywood capex adding 13.5 million sq meters capacity, 25% increase.
items.quote: It's already announced. I think INR134 crores, to be very precise is the number what we have declared. This will give us a new capacity of 13.5 million square meters, which is almost an addition of 25% capacity over our present manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Plywood volume growth target around 7% plus for FY25.
items.quote: So FY '25, the volume, I think we are at around 5.7% right now. And with quarter 4, we will try to be anywhere around 7% plus.

items.statement: MDF volume growth target around 50% for full year FY25.
items.quote: And for MDF, we had initially targeted almost a 50% growth over last year. We should be around that number for the full year.

items.statement: Adding flooring line to MDF to increase value-added sales and improve product mix.
items.quote: Number two, we are adding a flooring line to our existing MDF line. which will help us increase the value-added sales and help us improve the product mix further.

items.statement: Expects net debt around INR450 crores at year-end, net debt-to-equity around 0.55.
items.quote: At the year -end, our debt on a cautious approach would be around INR450 crores as guided earlier, which means our net debt -to-equity ratio at the year-end would be around 0.55 despite expansion and setting up of 2 new line of businesses.

items.statement: Samet JV expected to touch INR80-100 crores revenue in coming year.
items.quote: But just a ballpark number, I would say that definitely, we feel that touching anywhere around INR80 crores to INR100 crores in the coming year is a number which is doable.

items.statement: Expects to meet FY26 revenue target of INR600 crores based on seeding activities, new products, and JV benefits.
items.quote: Nevertheless, for FY '26, we are still expecting to meet what you mentioned, based on the seeding activities which I mentioned that we have done in recent quarters. So we have a good line-up of the products, which we have recently launched plus new products in pipeline. And the benefits from the joint ventures. So yes, so that looks more than achievable, I would say.

items.statement: Morris Co. JV benefits expected from Q2 or Q3 next financial year when new Kolkata facility operational.
items.quote: The JV with Morris Co. is advancing well, and we anticipate benefits to start accruing from Q2 or Q3 of next financial year, once our new manufacturing facility becomes operational, which is expected within the same timeframe in Kolkata.

items.statement: Aims to increase non-pen contribution from less than 10% to 30% in medium term.
items.quote: So, currently the contribution of non-pen would be less than 10%. So, which is quite, you know, lopsided I would say towards the core category. So, I think ideally, we are looking at least in the medium term 70-30 kind of a ratio.

items.statement: Non-pen categories margins expected to be lower due to outsourcing.
items.quote: Honestly, you know, it will be a little lower because these non-stationary and non-pen categories are mostly outsourced.

items.statement: Reintroduced three products at INR5 price point without new investment to counter competition.
items.quote: Absolutely. So, we have actually reintroduced three products, which we had in the past, not really, -- we had actually discontinued, but we did some cost engineering and then reintroduced three products at that price point without any new investment.

items.statement: Export realizations are 5-10% better than domestic.
items.quote: In the range of 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Pen category growth expected around 5-6%, driven by premiumization and market share gains.
items.quote: So, well, of course, the market estimates are that the category growth is -- of course, it is slightly stunted, but it is still more than 5%. So it could be around 5% to 6%. But definitely the growth will come mainly from the premiumization. And of course, we are also looking at gaining market share from the competition.

items.statement: Gross margin has room to increase; 50-50 in-house vs outsourced production model affects margins.
items.quote: So, if you compare to our peers, definitely the gross margin, we still have room in increasing our gross margin. But one significant difference is that the peers which you are mentioning, it's mostly their in-house production. Whereas in our case, it is a kind of a 50-50 model.

items.statement: Markers and mechanical pencils to launch in Q1 FY26; Linc calculators launched in Q4.
items.quote: Markers and mechanical pencils are set for launch in Q1 FY '26, further strengthening our presence in writing instruments. Lin c calculators launched in Q4 cater to the affordable segment, expanding our customer reach

items.statement: Active outlets currently about 100,000; trying to activate more from enrolled 250,000.
items.quote: So currently the active outlets are about 100,000 outlets. So as such there has been no increase if you say lately. It is just that we are trying to make these 250,000 outlets which are enrolled trying to make some of them active every month.

items.statement: Non-pen products reached about 15,000-20,000 outlets.
items.quote: I think about what? 15,000, 20,000 outlets.

items.statement: Pentonic average realization should increase with new products at INR20, INR30, INR40.
items.quote: So, the Pentonic average realization should increase because, as I mentioned in my opening remarks that, we have launched several new products in Pentonic portfolio at price range of INR20, INR30, INR40 and they are taking a little longer time to get the desired traction. So, we are heading for a better realization going forward in the Pentonic portfolio.

items.statement: Expects double-digit top line growth and EBITDA growth in sync or faster for FY26.
items.quote: Double-digit growth. I think we remain double-digit growth on our top line and EBITDA growth to be in sync or faster than our top line growth.

items.statement: Targets 17-18% EBITDA margin in next 6-8 quarters.
items.quote: So, in next, I think 6 to 8 quarters, we should see us touching a much higher level of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Gross margins have improved for 6-7 quarters and are expected to continue improving.
items.quote: So gross margins, we've been very, very focused on driving it back to the levels. And I think October, December numbers would reasonably matched October, December '21 kind of level.

items.statement: Price increases taken across multiple products due to commodity cost inflation.
items.quote: Yes. So there would be a price increase across multiple products wherever we are seeing the costs going up, largely commodity-led products, we are taking whatever required price increases.

items.statement: Urban demand setback seen as temporary; revival anticipated in coming quarters.
items.quote: We expect that the demand setback, especially in urban areas is temporary in nature and anticipate a revival in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Smaller packs growing faster, especially in Personal Care.
items.quote: It's small. We don't share those specifics, but it's building up much faster. In some of the categories like Personal Care, we've seen a very smart uptick of that, which is driven by, like I mentioned, small packs being low unit price, but also consumer behaviour, which is shifting to onetime use packs for freshness and experience.

items.statement: Naturell acquisition expected to be EPS accretive in FY26.
items.quote: And we believe FY '26, we could have an EPS accretive on this business.

items.statement: Online channels contribute 10-11% of revenue and growing faster.
items.quote: So first of all, from the online business perspective, about 10% to 11% of our revenue comes from selling in online platforms. And that's been growing at a much faster pace than the rest of the business, and we are quite conscious of the fact that since the consumers are shifting to this, we should be ahead of the curve.

items.statement: Food service (HoReCa) channel accounts for 8-10% of sales.
items.quote: So B2B, how would you define B2B? If you are saying food service -- if you're looking for food service, which is largely the HoReCa channel, that would be about 8% to 10% range.

items.statement: Working capital intensity expected to increase as e-commerce and modern trade share rises.
items.quote: Yes. Yes. Umesh Parikh: Yes, that's how we see it. That's right

items.statement: Deferred tax liability of INR3.5-4 crores to be recorded in Q4.
items.quote: And about INR3.5 crores to INR4 crores, you can assume as a deferred tax liability getting recorded in the Q4 as well.

items.statement: Company expects 20%+ growth as new normal, with 50-100 bps annual margin improvement over next 4-5 years.
items.quote: So, now we see that the new normal for this Company should be 20% plus growth. And today for us, maybe if you look at let us say predictability, let's say predictable growth for this Company, as we have seen already four year growth cycle now, from FY22 to 25 numbers which will be almost we are 9 months over.

items.statement: Nine-month capex Rs. 222 crores; full-year budget Rs. 300 crores; new plants to cost Rs. 400-500 crores over 18-20 months.
items.quote: So, this year we have done around close in 9 months Rs. 222 crores of CAPEX and budget of Rs. 300 crores. And probably another few more months of CAPEX and FY26 will then probably our CAPEX cycle for the old plants which were established between 23 and 24 will be over and then we will focus on the new plants which we are establishing , three new plants which were establishing.

items.statement: Dialysis machine run rate 40-50 per month; FY25 installations 300-350, next year to double.
items.quote: No, we will not be able to do 500 installations this year. This year we will be able to do between 300 and 350 installations. I don't have a real figure, but it should be around 350 plus. And then next year maybe we will double the installations.

items.statement: EBITDA margin projected at 27% for FY25, with 100-150 bps improvement over last year.
items.quote: And on the margin side, I think, we have already projected close to 27% EBITDA margin for this year. Last year, we were close to 26% this year, 100 bps improvement, 100-150 bps.

items.statement: Domestic price hikes typically 3-4% per year.
items.quote: It depends. So, sometimes the contracts are longer, you don't get a price hike. But typically, we can take between 3% to 4% price hike per year.

items.statement: Domestic business expected to end FY25 with over 20% overall growth.
items.quote: And hopefully, the current financial year, we should e nd up more than 20% overall growth rate in the domestic business.

items.statement: Exports growing at 28% in nine months, 30% in Q3; on track to deliver committed growth.
items.quote: Exports in the first nine months have shown a great growth. They have been growing at around 28% closely. And if you look at the quarter itself, it's grown by around 30%. So, overall, we are on track to deliver the committed growth.

items.statement: Europe expected to end FY25 with 27-28% growth.
items.quote: Europe has overall grown by around 30% in nine months. Last quarter growth was around 20%. And I think overall we should end up between 27 %-28% growth for Europe by the end of the year, which is a very healthy growth.

items.statement: Renal business targeting 20-25% market share by 2030.
items.quote: But our target is to maybe reach let's say, by 2030 around 20% to 25% of the market share.

items.statement: US business first stronger wave expected in FY27.
items.quote: We see the first stronger wave coming in FY27 because we have some more products to be included in the list, and they're undergoing some clinical trials and regulatory approval, and they will also start contributing to revenue maybe end of this year or early next year.

items.statement: US tariffs expected to be neutral for company as they apply equally to all countries.
items.quote: So, they don't impact India as such, but I think as these tariffs are also in China and maybe even if it comes on India, it will be neutral for us because it will be equally applicable to all the countries. So, we don't expect any impact of this tariffs.

items.statement: QIP proceeds: Rs. 500 crores for new capex, part designated for acquisition.
items.quote: Correct. There's a segmentation of QIP proceeds, so Rs. 500 crores is for new CAPEX, and that is where we will be using it.

items.statement: New plants to be commissioned in 18-21 months.
items.quote: And then all the QIP proceeds will be used for the three new plan ts, which are under construction right now , and will go live in 18 to 21 months.

items.statement: Solar power JV operational by September-October, aiming for green power.
items.quote: And hopefully this will be operational by end of September, October. And after that, most of the polymed manufacturing facility will be running on green power.

items.statement: Total EBITDA to be 1.5x FY25 in FY26, with at least 300 bps margin expansion.
items.quote: Let us say, the total EBITDA of the company is X as of FY '25. Then you can safely assume will be 1.5x by FY '26. And this entire 1.5x may come from the core domain.

items.statement: Core verticals to grow: defense 55-60%, ESAI 50-55%, aerospace 45-50%.
items.quote: see, the 3 verticals for when we say, we are at the core to grow at around 50% , then 55% to 60% at defence, 50% to 55% at ESAI and 45% to 50% at aerospace.

items.statement: Investments 1 and 2 to cost INR150-200 crores, pegged around INR180 crores.
items.quote: See, the 1 and 2 probably will take about INR150 crores to INR200 crores. We are -- probably peg it around INR180 crores, let us say.

items.statement: Order book as of Dec 31 was $83 million or about INR710 crores.
items.quote: The order book as on 31st December was at $83 million or about INR710 crores.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin was 18.7% excluding non-core; combined margin lower.
items.quote: if you remove the non-core from the equation, then you will see almost our EBITDA is 18.7%,

items.statement: Defense revenue for Q3 was INR92 crores, with prototype revenue around INR40 crores.
items.quote: The total defense revenues for Q3 was INR92 crores, of which the prototype revenues, which is what the forthcoming orders was around INR40-odd crores.

items.statement: Target to balance ESAI with aerospace and defense at 33% each in about 2 years.
items.quote: So, our immediate target is to bring ESAI in par with aerospace and defense. So almost like 2 years from now, we want to see that it is all 33%, 33%, 33%

items.statement: Non-core business to be recalibrated in next 6 to 9 months.
items.quote: As articulated by Dr. SRN, our endeavour is to recalibrate the low-margin non-core business in the next 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Vision for 2029: $1 billion revenue and at least 35% EBITDA.
items.quote: in 5 years from now or 2029, we should be -- at least we -- I want to be, I don't know whether it's appropriate to say, it should be $1 billion in revenue and it should have at least 35% EB ITDA.

items.statement: Planning to create a DeepTech fund to incubate companies for ESAI growth.
items.quote: We are trying to create a fund -- a DeepTech fund. And we are trying to sort of incubate several companies.

items.statement: New 180,000 sq ft facility to be operational by June 1.
items.quote: So, this will be ready by February end. So, we will do interiors, etc. We'll move into this facility by around end of May. That's the plan. So , by first of June, we'll be in this facility. It will be 180,000 square feet facility.

items.statement: No inorganic acquisitions planned for FY26 unless something exotic comes.
items.quote: And we are not looking at any inorganic acquisition unless something exotic comes in our way in FY '26.

items.statement: Defense order book visibility is 16x Q3 value, approximately INR800 crores.
items.quote: In other words, our Q3 value into you can safely multiply 16x, will be our order book.

items.statement: Counter drone systems: delivered 75 out of 100 systems; expecting repeat orders and upgrades.
items.quote: And also, as I mentioned to you, our antidrone systems, out of 100 systems, we have delivered 7 5. That also part of our Q3 program.

items.statement: Working with major chip manufacturers Texas Instruments, NVIDIA, NXP, Qualcomm.
items.quote: we are working with all the 4 at least major chip manufacturers, Texas Instruments, NVIDIA, NXP and Qualcomm, so we are working in partnership with them.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA for FY25 expected at approximately INR700 crores.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we reiterate that we will be closing F Y '25 with a consolidated EBITDA of approximately INR700 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated order book to close FY25 in range INR15,000-20,000 crores.
items.quote: The robust pipeline reinforces our projections and we are on track to close FY '25 with a consolidated order book of -- in the range of INR 15,000 crores to INR20,000 crores depending upon the timing of awards.

items.statement: Consolidated total income growth of 18-20% over next 3 years.
items.quote: With this consolidated foundation we anticipate a consolidated total income growth of anything between 18% to 20% in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands at INR14,500 crores with breakdown.
items.quote: Coming to the order book. I'm pleased to announce that our consolidated order book stands at INR14,500 crores, of which around INR9,300 crores comes from water, about INR1,950 crores from tunneling segment and remaining INR1,750 crores from transportation sector.

items.statement: WMEL order book as on Dec 31, 2024 is INR2,600 crores.
items.quote: On the financial front, our WMEL order book as on December 31, 2024, is INR2,600 crores.

items.statement: Expects FY26 order inflows of INR8,000-10,000 crores including spillover.
items.quote: We believe that we should be able to make up for this loss of about INR4,000 crores plus the additional INR6,000 crores in FY '26. So we should be garnering an inflowsomewhere between INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores order book in the FY '26.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expected around 19%.
items.quote: Margins in terms of the overall -- EBITDA margins should be at an overall level, be about -- will be about 19% or there around at a reported EBITDA level.

items.statement: WMEL EBITDA margin approximately 23% for 9M FY25.
items.quote: This performance has been consistent from a margin perspective. Our EBITDA margin works out to be approximately 23% for the 9 months FY '25.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue for FY25 expected close to INR3,700 crores total income.
items.quote: So we anticipate the consolidated revenue to be somewhere close to INR3,700 crores total income.

items.statement: Revenue and margins to grow 15-20% year-on-year.
items.quote: So we expect the -- our revenues and our margins to grow in the ranges of 15% to 20% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow mix: 35% transport, balance water.
items.quote: Yes. So we would -- we expect about 35% to 40%, 35% to be the transport vertical and the balance would come from the water vertical.

items.statement: SmartOps expected turnover INR150-200 crores in FY26.
items.quote: On a conservative level, I think we would do anywhere between INR150 crores to INR200 crores of turnover from SmartOps alone.

items.statement: SmartOps gross margin expected not less than 30%.
items.quote: Now the percentages that this brings to our EBITDA levels in terms of the earnings, we expect that we will not be earning less than 30% on the gross levels in terms of percentage profit margins.

items.statement: EDP approval for oil block delayed, expected in 3-6 months.
items.quote: So it will take at least 3 to 6 months still before the government approves this EDP.

items.statement: TBM for tunnel project ordered, delivery expected in 16 months.
items.quote: Our TBM has been finalized and an MoU and order has bee n placed. This delivery is expected in 16 months.

items.statement: Dharavi project completion targeted Q3 2026, ahead of schedule.
items.quote: This project aims for completion by the third quarter of 2026, ahead of its schedule.

items.statement: Full year volume guidance between 250,000 and 260,000 tons depending on invoicing.
items.quote: So with that, our full year volume, which is 187,000 tons for the 9 months, looks to be between 250,000 and 260,000 depending on invoicing, etcetera, is the guidance for the full year.

items.statement: Total capex for China and Ghana plants estimated at USD50 million.
items.quote: And the total capex for both plants is currently established at -- estimated at USD50 million.

items.statement: Next year capex up to INR50 crores in renewable power, INR50 crores maintenance, plus investment in two plants.
items.quote: So this year -- the next coming year, we'll do about -- up to INR50 crores in renewable power. And I think we'll be done with most of the strategy as far as optimizing power cost is concerned, up to INR50 crores in maintenance capex per year.

items.statement: Expect 25,000-30,000 ton annual addition on rolling basis in next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: But over next 2, 3 quarters, it looks like that we should be back on a 25,000, 30,000 ton annual addition on a rolling basis.

items.statement: Expect 30,000-40,000 tons incremental annual volume growth from new mine conversions.
items.quote: So we do expect on a rollover basis, at least 30,000 to 40,000 tons of incremental annual volume growth from conversion from new mines.

items.statement: China plant should start contributing in second half of next year.
items.quote: China should start contributing something in the second half of next year. That is what the target is, but let's see.

items.statement: Ghana plant should happen over next 18 months.
items.quote: Ghana should happen over next 18 months, that is how it looks like.

items.statement: Operating margins in range of 27-28% excluding treasury and other income.
items.quote: Even if you knock off my treasury and other income, we are talking of operating margins in the range of 27%, 28%.

items.statement: Believe should do better than 21-22% margins on medium- to long-term basis.
items.quote: I personally believe we should do definitely better than 21%, 22% on a medium- to long-term basis.

items.statement: Expect destocking customer volumes to return from June quarter, some in March.
items.quote: I think at least for one customer, we expect that to come back from the June quarter. Some in March, but mostly in June quarter.

items.statement: Expect order inflow from existing customers to regularize in next 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: And as Kunal explained, we do expect the order book or the order inflow from the existing customers to start coming at a regular level in next 1 or 2 quarters, primarily because of the fact that things look like stabilizing, even freight rates are normalizing.

items.statement: No major customer loss; destocking temporary, not structural.

items.statement: Expects FY25 revenue growth of 21.8% to 22.3% in constant currency.

items.statement: Signed three large deals in Q3, third consecutive quarter of at least three large deals.

items.statement: Macro environment remains uncertain, refi volumes unlikely to recover quickly.
items.quote: So, overall the macro environment conti nues to remain uncertain.

items.statement: Incremental capex of ₹60 crore for Power Transmission gears capacity.
