items.statement: Gears capacity to reach ₹700 crore by September 2026.
items.quote: This will take the gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026.

items.statement: Combined closing order book at ₹2,356 crore, up 52.4% YoY.
items.quote: The combined closing order book stands at ₹2,356 crore for the Engineering businesses, an increase of a handsome 52.4% on a year-on-year basis, signifying an all-time high for the Company.

items.statement: Power Transmission order book reached all-time high of ₹377 crore.
items.quote: The outstand ing order book reached an all -time high of ₹377 crore on the 31st of December, which included long duration orders of about ₹136 .6 crore

items.statement: Water business order booking stood at ₹1,979 crore.
items.quote: And as of the 31st of December 2024, the order booking for the Water business stood at a hand some ₹1,979 crore, which included ₹1,122 .6 crore towards O&M contracts, which are executed over a slightly longer period of time

items.statement: Sugar prices firmed up; blended realisation increased from December to January.
items.quote: For January, our blended realisation price was just a shade under ₹40 per kilo. And today, we are looking already at about 0.50 paisa higher than those levels on a blended basis.

items.statement: Expects sugar prices to remain at higher plateau, no significant decline.
items.quote: My personal view is that I think we've moved to a different plateau. So, I don't see prices coming down very substantially.

items.statement: Expects margin expansion in ethanol over next few quarters.
items.quote: But going forward, I certainly think over the next few quarters, you will see an expansion in margins.

items.statement: Ethanol blending percentage reached 16.4% as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: The achieved blending percentage for 2024-25 as of the 31st of December stood at 16.4%, while the blending percentage for the month of December was much higher, it was 18.2%.

items.statement: Plans to reduce sugarcane variety 0238 from 50-55% to 30-35% next season.
items.quote: However, we have intensified our efforts and plan to reduce the quantum of 0238 from about 50-55% this year to approximately 30-35% in the next year.

items.statement: Recovery gap at 0.6% and narrowing, but full catch-up unlikely.
items.quote: I would also like to point out that we have a negative 0.6% difference in recovery as of today. However, that difference is narrowing with the arrival of healthy plant ca ne across all the sugar factories

items.statement: Alcohol production in FY26 expected at 25 crore litres, with 22.5-23 crore litres ethanol.
items.quote: We would be going up to in terms of alcohol production in FY 26, close to about 25 crore litres of which 22.5-23 crore litres would be ethanol.

items.statement: Anticipates NCLT approval for Scheme of Arrangement by end of calendar year.
items.quote: As far as the Scheme of Arrangement is concerned, we anticipate approval from NCLT by the end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Defence facility projected to be operational during calendar year 2025.
items.quote: So, we're still projecting the facility to be up and running during calendar year 2025.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech expected to deliver revenues of approximately Rs. 360 crores in current fiscal and Rs.450–Rs.500 crore upon achieving optimal utilization at reasonable prices/margins during next fiscal.
items.quote: We expect the entity to deliver revenues of approximately Rs. 360 crores in current fiscal and Rs.450– Rs.500 crore upon achieving optimal utilization at reasonable prices / margins during next fiscal.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers top line target of Rs. 200 crore may be missed by 10-15%.
items.quote: But right now , given the way 3 quarters have shaped up, we believe that it's going to be quite tough for us to hit that Rs.200 crore top line. And we are looking to come close to it, but I believe that in the end we might end up being 10% to 15% short in the top line target of Rs. 200 crore.

items.statement: Expects double-digit volume growth in specialty polymers next financial year.
items.quote: So, of course, in terms of potential and pipelines, it's quite rich. How it materializes, we are quite sure that we will be looking at ,at least a double-digit growth in the next financial year across not only the existing products but the new products that we had started working on.

items.statement: Targets value-added product share at 30% plus-minus in current quarter.
items.quote: But right now, the focus for this quarter is to hold on to this Specialty Polymer , and make it in the range of, say, 30% plus-minus so that this trend of high profitability continues in this quarter at least.

items.statement: Expects to close near 5,000 tons including rPET for full year.
items.quote: We should be looking at, we should be closing near to 5,000 tons, including rPET.

items.statement: Expects rPET sales of 800 to 1,000 tons in Q4.
items.quote: In the fourth quarter, we are expecting rPET sales to be in the range of about 800 to 1,000 tons.

items.statement: Installing extruder in Ester Filmtech by June or July 2025.
items.quote: Ester Filmtech, there is an extruder to be commissioned, which is likely to be installed by June or July '25.

items.statement: Loop JV project cost $165 million, funded 40% equity and 60% debt; equity equally from Ester and Loop.
items.quote: It will be funded through debt and equity. Equity will be 40%. 60% will be debt. And the 40% equity is going to come equally in equal parts from Ester and Loop.

items.statement: Loop JV break-up: ~Rs. 90 crore land, ~Rs. 1,000 crore plant and machinery, balance GST and interest during construction.
items.quote: So, roughly around Rs. 90 crore is for the land part, and around Rs. 1,000 crore is for the plant and machinery which we are planning in this, and the balance part is your GST and interest during construction etc.

items.statement: Export business is recurring, not tender-driven; expects to hold 27% VAS volumes and at least same export sales as Q3.
items.quote: So, we have that proven pipeline, which we have executed in Quarter 3, and we expect that pipeline should continue to give us business in this quarter also, plus in some newly established businesses, we will try to see if our business can expand.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers EBITDA margins expected to remain stable around 30-33%.
items.quote: In terms of profitability, we think that the profits are going to remain stable around the EBITDA levels of 30%, 33%.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech EBITDA margins expected to be sustained at current prices and margins.
items.quote: And the EBITDA margins at the current prices and the margins that are prevailing, we should be able to sustain that because the fixed cost will remain the same.

items.statement: 12-micron commodity film value addition was about Rs. 43 per kg in December quarter, currently Rs. 40-42.
items.quote: So, the value addition, which is the difference between selling price and raw material cost, in the December quarter it stood at about Rs. 43 per kg. But the blended VA for the domestic or export market would be much higher for us , because we do various grades, various varieties of films, value-added and metalized, et cetera.

items.statement: Value-added products have incremental value addition of Rs. 45 to Rs. 65 per kg over 12 micron.
items.quote: So, in the VAS products, generally the value addition over and above the 12 micron is in the range of Rs. 45 to Rs. 65 a kg, depending on the product mix.

items.statement: Expects BOPET film demand growth of 9-10% in India from natural progression plus PWMR impact.
items.quote: So, that makes us very confident that if we take, say, a growth of 6.5% in the GDP, and multiply it by 1.5 x, so 9% to 10% of the growth in demand in India should come because of the natural progression plus whatever growth we get due to the implementation of PWMR would be on top of that.

items.statement: Expects improved demand-supply scenario and stable margins due to decelerated capacity addition and PWMR rules.
items.quote: So, this is making the market more balanced with respect to supply-demand, and therefore, we expect that this recovery should continue and the margins should stabilize, given that the supply and demand are now coming closer to each other.

items.statement: Expects 15% growth in demand in current quarter and better in Q1 next financial year.
items.quote: I believe this quarter would see some growth in demand, definitely, current quarter from the last quarter, I would say, roughly about 15% growth in demand would be there. Q1 of the next financial year would see even a better improved demand, particularly coming from data center areas and rural connectivity areas.

items.statement: Telecom product revenue expected to reach INR 350-400 crores in current quarter.
items.quote: In the current quarter, we expect roughly about reaching to INR 350 crores to INR 400 crores i n the particular quarter, something around that. I am not 100% sure, but INR 350 crores to INR 400 crores kind of we'll reach

items.statement: Aspires 20-25% growth, but may not achieve due to market conditions.
items.quote: Yes, this kind of growth should be there in the company, some 20%, 25% growth has to happen. But sometimes, despite of the best of the efforts, this, what we aspire, may not come through, particularly market situation, geopolitical situation , and those kind of things happen, whi ch results in the aspiration not reaching to the level we wanted it to be

items.statement: Poland OFC project on hold, saving INR 175 crores in capex.

items.statement: Fiber capacity expansion to complete by March 31, 2025.
items.quote: That capacity expansion of fiber would be completed by more or less by 31st March 2025. It is already happening in Hyderabad, so it should be completed by 31st March or so.

items.quote: Not always. average it should be sometimes something coming around 15% or so on an average.

items.statement: OFC demand picking up from data centers and rural connectivity.
items.quote: Particularly, demand is significantly growing from data centers because internationally, unlike India, data center, people are allowed to interconnect their data center across the cities where they require very high capacity cables. There also the demand is increasing.

items.statement: Target product mix 70% products, 30% EPC.
items.quote: Target is 70-30. 70 for Products, 30 for EPC. That is the target. Again, but let me qualify it a little bit. If I receive a profitable turnkey project, I am not going to deny it.

items.statement: Defense order delayed due to ammunition supply delay from government factories.

items.quote: We expect 2024-2025 would be more or less in line and we would more or less be doing possibly or hopefully close to 15 crore liters of sales for biofuels.

items.statement: Expects 20% ethanol blending target for next year to be on track.
items.quote: And we expect that the 20% target for next year would also therefore be, would be on track.

items.quote: Regarding the project completion, more or less all the projects whatever we have undertaken is complete except one grain distillery, which we are installing in Gorakhpur and hopefully that will also be completed by March 25.

items.quote: There is abundant stock with the government, and we expect that the grain prices will come down and this will positively impact the margins for on biofuels.

items.quote: So, the Potable Spirits business in India, which is expected to be about $56 billion in 2025, is expected to grow at 7.2%, going up to about 112 billion in 2034.

items.statement: Premium IMFL industry growing at over 20%.
items.quote: The premium industry is growing at more than 20%.

items.quote: Although we have more or less finalized depending upon the NWC for the working capital and term loan for the projects for which we have taken but we have yet to get the confirmation from SBI.

items.quote: Our glycol business, our sales are actually up by about 26% and our gross margin is up by about 83%.

items.quote: Hopefully, as we fix the product mix, we will come in the range that we typically like to be, which is around 25% or plus. As we have communicated in past, we would like to drive VNB growth and sales growth while being at around 25% margins.

items.statement: Net impact of surrender guidelines on margin is about 100 basis points, at the lower end of guidance.

items.statement: Q3 margin was 23.2%, lower than Q2, due to product mix and surrender impact.
items.quote: As a result, our margin for Quarter 3 stood at 23.2%, slightly lower than Quarter 2, despite the impact of the surrender guidelines.

items.statement: ULIP share increased to 44% in Q3 FY25 from 35% last year.
items.quote: As a result, the ULIP share in our product mix increased from 35% in last year, Quarter 3 to 44% in Quarter 3 of this year.

items.statement: Overall industry growth slowed to 5% in Q3, private sector to 13%.
items.quote: If I were to look at those numbers for Quarter 3, the overall industry is 5%. And overall private market is 13%.

items.statement: Targets 20% or above sales growth for the full year.
items.quote: I think 20% or above is the number that we are targeting. So, you know, 20% perhaps the lower end of where we should end up for the year.

items.statement: Guidance on margin between 23% and 24% for the year.
items.quote: Despite that trend, you know, the guidances on margin between 23 and 24, we will be able to meet.

items.statement: Aims to keep ULIP mix in the range of 35 to 40%.
items.quote: We will typically like to be in the range of 35 to 40%. There are efforts that we are making to ensure that ULIP remains range bound in the range of about 35 to 40%.

items.statement: Board approved listing roadmap; waiting for Section 35 amendment; process may take about one year.

items.quote: So, the Axis ownership in Axis Max Life Insurance stands at 19.02%. And there is a 0.98% option that exists. I think it's pending at Axis end.

items.statement: Rider attachment ratio reached 45%, up from 32% last year.
items.quote: Additionally, we also achieved our highest rider attachment ratio of 45%, up from 32% in the first nine months of last year, with rider APE growing at over 250%.

items.statement: Total APE expanded by 17% in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Additionally, our Total APE expanded by 17%, driven by an 11% increase in policy issues.

items.statement: Retained order inflow guidance of Rs. 20,000-22,000 crore.
items.quote: Earlier , we had shared with you an order inflow guidance of Rs. 20,000 -Rs. 22,000 crore which we decided to retain.

items.statement: Expects Q4 margin around 9.5%, which is sustainable.
items.quote: So, this margin, whatever we gave the guidance now revised to 9.25% as you said, we are expecting the margin should be around 9.5% in t his quarter 4, so that the reason we thought it will be around 9.25%. So, this at the moment it is sustainable.

items.statement: Expects Q4 revenue to be similar or slightly less year-on-year.
items.quote: It will be similar, or it will be little less.

items.quote: Now, the 4th Quarter , the execution would be on consol idated between Rs. 6,000-Rs. 6,400 crores, we are expecting.

items.quote: The L1 project in the pipeline is roughly about Rs. 9,000-Rs. 10,000 crores.

items.statement: Prospective project pipeline is about Rs. 2.45 lakh crore across verticals and states.
items.quote: I am happy to share with you this prospective pipeline of project the value is about Rs. 2.45 lakh crore. It is in all the verticals, all the seven verticals in which we operate and it is in almost all the states, large states at least.

items.quote: We have incurred a CAPEX of Rs. 253 crores in the current financial year as against the budgeted CAPEX of Rs. 250 crores for regular projects.

items.statement: Expects to spend up to Rs. 250 crores capex limit for the year.
items.quote: It was Rs. 250 crores and we have spent so far Rs. 223 crores. We expect that we will be spending up to that limit.

items.statement: Slow execution due to elections and elongated billing/payment cycles.
items.quote: We have witnessed the slow pace of execution due to general elections and elections in some of the states. Additionally, some of our projects have seen elongated billing and payment cycles, leading to a slowdown in execution.

items.statement: Debt increased due to payment slowdown and higher unbilled revenue.
items.quote: We have already explained you that there is a slowdown in the payment mechanism because of these elections and all that is the reason if you see the d ebt level has increased. At the same time, my unbilled revenue also got increased.

items.statement: Expects debt to decline from current Rs. 2,415 crores, possibly to Rs. 1,500 or 1,000 crores.
items.quote: So, at this moment, we cannot tell, but there will be some decline in the present level of debt we are expecting.

items.statement: Expects to receive Rs. 1,150 crores from AP capital city projects by end of March.
items.quote: So, AP exposure there are two parts, the first part about Capital City projects, we have pending of Rs. 1,150 crores that we expect to receive by end of March.

items.statement: Expects to realize Rs. 374 crores loan from Vizag deal in next couple of years.
items.quote: And as far as the loan is concerned about Rs. 374 is the loan amount and in the current year, we received about Rs. 15 crores against the interest amount and this Rs. 374 crores also, we are expecting to get realized in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Maintains H2 volume growth guidance of 7-8%.
items.quote: We are looking for the entire year, our volume growth of 7% to 8% in H2. We are looking at it over there.

items.quote: And we are also keeping our projection of what we said about H2 EBITDA increase, which we had indicated between first half to second half, H2 average would be about INR 150 increase in the EBITDA, and we are maintaining that and no change in that.

items.quote: Capex for the whole year, we are looking at a number of INR500 crores.

items.statement: 9-month capex around INR300 crores.
items.quote: 9 months, it is around INR300 crores.

items.quote: For this year, as guided earlier, we are expecting total incentive accrual to be around INR 100 crores.

items.statement: 9-month incentive accruals around INR60 crores.
items.quote: For 9 months, that accruals is around INR60 crores.

items.quote: Marki-Barka once that comes, it will be around 55% -- between 55% and 60% of our total requirements.

items.quote: So our aim is to reach to the level of 35%. But it will take -- as you rightly said, it will take another 1 year to 1.5 years.

items.quote: Our net debt as of the third quarter is around INR3,000 crores.

items.quote: As our closing balance is about INR435 crores as of 31 December '24, this is excluding the West Bengal incentive which is under litigation.

items.statement: Received INR187 crores cash subsidy this financial year.
items.quote: INR187 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: FY25 industry growth expected around 4-5%.
items.quote: Going forward, what we at JK Lakshmi see is that this year the growth is going to be around 4 % to 5%, somewhere around that, and next year FY26 may be around 6 % to 7%.

items.quote: I would say definitely about Rs.75 to Rs.100.

items.statement: Company expects to grow better than industry due to Udaipur and Surat.
items.quote: I think we are going to do better because I think we have now Udaipur and Surat also in place. So, our growth is going to be better than industry.

items.statement: Blended cement at 65%, trade proportion at 58% in Q3.
items.quote: Blended cement was at 65%, trade proportion was 58%.

items.statement: Premium sale at 11% of total volume in Q3.
items.quote: Premium sale on an overall volume basis, total trade, non-trade put together was at 11% and fuel was at 1.57 for 1,000 Kms.

items.statement: Renewable energy at 48% of energy requirements in last quarter.
items.quote: In the last quarter it was at 48%.

items.statement: Surat phase 1 commissioning by Feb end or March, phase 2 by June 2025.
items.quote: First phase is going to get commissioned in the month of March itself or February end, which is about half of the capacity about 0.8 million tons, and another rest of 0.6 million tons during around June 2025.

items.statement: Aims to achieve 5% EBIT margin by end of FY2026.
items.quote: Now the 5% margin is something that we hope to achieve by the end of FY 2026.

items.statement: Guides 12-15% growth for overall travel segment.
items.quote: We've said 12% to 15% growth is our guidance on the travel segment.

items.statement: Expects to close FY25 with healthy double-digit growth.
items.quote: On a look ahead, we expect to close FY '25 with a healthy double-digit growth and with continuing to build our base on business for FY '26.

items.statement: Expects 2025 to be a fairly strong year for DEI.
items.quote: With that forward-looking, we see 2025 to be a fairly strong year for us to get back to where we were -- where we have left it in the past.

items.statement: Bagged National Games Uttarakhand business of about INR 120 crores.
items.quote: We are actually doing the National Games in Uttarakhand, which the total size of that business is roughly about INR 120 crores, which will now reflect in the current operating quarter.

items.statement: Forward bookings show 20%+ volume growth and 35% value growth.
items.quote: But despite that, from a volume perspective, we are actually seeing close to about 20 -plus percent growth in terms of volumes. And in terms of value, we are saying close to about 35% growth.

items.statement: Expects 2,000 passengers for Kumbh Mela by season end.
items.quote: And we expect by the time this season ends or the Kumbh Mela ends, we would have roughly close to about 2,000 passengers who would have travelled through us.

items.statement: Japan bookings at 85-90% of last year's volumes; expects positive contribution.
items.quote: And as we speak, we are already close to about 85% to 90% of the volumes that we did last year. So I expect the Japan to contribute very positively in the quarter to come.

items.statement: Non-air business grew to 8% of portfolio in 2024 from 5% in 2023.
items.quote: In 2023, non -air business was about 5% of our portfolio. In 2024, we ended at about 8%.

items.statement: Travel vertical EBIT margin at 3.9% for 9 months; adjusted would be 4.1-4.2%.
items.quote: And if you look at our EBIT margin on the travel vertical, we are holding at 3.9%. Now if you look at FY '24 and compare that to FY '25 for the 9-month period, the 3.9% is despite the one -offs that we have seen in the curren t quarter. If I was to adjust for those, you will actually see the margins actually going closer to the 4.1%, 4.2%

items.statement: Sterling Q3 EBITDA margin exceeded threshold at 38.8%.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins for Q3 FY '25 has exceeded our intended threshold of 30% to 35% to close at 38.8%.

items.statement: Increased prices for Kumbh Mela due to demand outpacing supply.
items.quote: Just to give a case, I mean, look at kumbh, the kind of demand we have seen, where we see an opportunity to put the price up. We've actually done that because the demand was outpacing the supply in some form.

items.statement: Currency fluctuations impacted profitability by INR 60 million in Q3.
items.quote: So that impacted our business and the impact of that was roughly about INR 60 million on our profitability.

items.statement: East Africa sales dropped 30% due to customer bankruptcy.
items.quote: And therefore, their sales have dropped by about 30%.

items.statement: Expansion focus on asset-right model with limited or no capex.
items.quote: Our expansion focus shall continue to be on an asset -right model with limited or no capex investments only to sweat our existing assets for scale.

items.statement: Expects to be back to normal in the coming quarter.
items.quote: So, my expectation is that we will be back to normal in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Expects Q4 tractor industry growth over 15%, full year over 7%.
items.quote: We expect the industry in the Quarter 4 to grow by over 15%, which will take the full year growth to possibly over 7%.

items.statement: Initial EV SUV volume target about 5,000 units per month for both products together.
items.quote: it gives us confidence that irrespective of the price points that we are at, we should be able to do a starting initial volume of about 5,000 a month for both the products together.

items.statement: Will separately report EV contract manufacturing and born electric end-to-end margin from Q4.
items.quote: So, we're going to see two things and we'll start bringing this out from Quarter 4, which will be populated numbers. The Auto standalone number will have two components to it and we'll show them to you separately.

items.statement: EV percentage margin will be lower than ICE, but variable margin per unit similar over time.
items.quote: The percentage margin here is going to be lesser than ICE, which you know we've been repeating every time, because the denominator effect. Over a period of time we do expect the variable margin to be in absolute terms similar twice.

items.statement: EV pricing applicable at time of delivery, allowing flexibility to increase prices if costs rise.
items.quote: So, right now it's basically price applicable at the time of delivery, which means that we have the flexibility to take a price up literally when we want.

items.statement: Auto price hikes: 0.7% YTD December, additional 0.8% in January.
items.quote: Price hikes, basically, Auto YTD December, which was about 0.7, and then we have taken another 0.8 in January.

items.statement: 3XO capacity to increase by 1,500-2,000 units within 3-4 months.
items.quote: So, basically, we have a maximum upside of 1500 -2000 on each of these within the current infrastructure.

items.statement: Will not trade off quality for volume; may sell 3,000 instead of 5,000 if needed.
items.quote: So, if we have a doubt and if we don't sell 5000 and we sell 3000, that's fine. We will not trade off the number for the quality.

items.statement: Evaluating international farm operations, completion expected in Q4.
items.quote: We expect to complete that exercise in the 4th Quarter.

items.statement: PLI for MEAL to be booked in MEAL books, timeline depends on milestones.
items.quote: It will be booked finally in MEAL books.

items.statement: No firm timeline for MEAL PLI benefits due to audit and supplier certifications.
items.quote: So, there's no firm timeline because it will depend on us being able to. And most of just to be sure it's not very vague, there is a specific audit that needs to happen for us to be able to feel good that the PLI benefit is accruable.

items.statement: EV bookings open on 14th February at 250+ dealership outlets.
items.quote: So basically, bookings are opening up in 250 plus dealership outlets on 14th February.

items.statement: EVs and ICE to be sold from same showrooms to give customers choice.
items.quote: We want the customer to have a choice between whether they buy our ICE or our EV, which is why consciously we are keeping the showrooms, selling the EVs and the ICE the same.

items.statement: All critical integrating software including BMS owned by MEAL.
items.quote: No, all critical integrating software is owned by us. So, the BMS software is ours, all the zonal architecture, ECU software, all of that is owned by us.

items.statement: CAFE 3 norms may be delayed due to lack of consensus.
items.quote: Theoretically, yes, because there's so much discussion yet and there is no consensus on what exactly it should be.

items.statement: Total price increase taken is about INR100 crores in Q3, progressively going up to 4-4.5% by year-end.
items.quote: So our total price increase that we've taken currently is approximately about INR100 crores in quarter 3, so -- which would -- in percentage terms, Venkat, would be... N. Venkataraman: 2%. Varun Berry: It's about 2%, but it's progressively going up. By the end of the year, we will be at about 4%, 4.5% price increase

items.statement: Cumulative price increase of 6-6.5% planned: 2% in Q3, 2.5% in Q4, 1.5% in Q1 next year.
items.quote: No, there's no hesitation. It is a necessity today. And you're right, exactly right, there will be a 6% price increase. We've already taken in Q3 2%. In Q4, it's going to be another 2.5%. And then in Q1, which is going to be the Q1 of next year, it's going to be another 1.5%. So cumulatively, it's going to be 6%, 6.5% price increase.

items.statement: Cost savings target of 2.5% of revenue for next year, potentially more.
items.quote: We are also doubling down on our cost efficienc ies, as I said. We are planning to make sure, and as I keep repeating every time, these cost efficiencies and cost savings, they start with 0 on the 1st of April, and whatever has been achieved ends with the year, and there are new cost savings that come up every year. So we are again looking at 2.5% for next year, and hopefully even more than that

items.statement: Capex for next year expected at INR150-200 crores, lower than current year.
items.quote: are going to take the capex break, so to say. We have put up plants and we will try and keep it as low as possible. It will still be -- what, Venkat, about INR200 crores? N. Venkataraman: For the next year? Varun Berry: Yes. N. Venkataraman: Should be even lower. Varun Berry: Even lower. So INR150 crores to INR200 crores is what we'll keep it at, unless there is a volume increase

items.statement: Margins expected to stay in current range, no forward-looking forecast given.
items.quote: So we will stay in the current range, I would say. That would be the range that we would look at, although we don't give any forward-looking forecast, but I would say current range is what we would target.

items.statement: Commodity inflation at 11% requires 6.5% price increase to balance absolute profitability.
items.quote: And yes, the 11% inflation that we spoke about in commodities equates itself to 6.5%, it requires to be balanced, it requires 6.5% price increase.

items.statement: Volume growth may be impacted by price increases, but last quarter volume growth was 6.4%.
items.quote: Well, volumes do take a beating when there is a price increase. There is an arbitrage between volumes and revenues. So -- but we've been growing -- actually, if you look at last quarter, we grew at almost 6.4%, it's almost the same as our revenue growth. S o our volume growths were pretty good. Yes, there will be a little bit of arbitrage which will come through, but that's fine. You've got to do

items.statement: Croissant business to cross INR200 crores next year; milk shakes already crossed INR200 crores.
items.quote: I think it's important that we develop these categories and that's what we are seeing. So if you want to look at it, today, our croissant business is -- next year will cross INR200 crores, right. Our milk shakes business has already crossed INR200 crores, right.

items.statement: Employee cost growth to be 0.75 times top line growth.
items.quote: So we focus on making sure that our top line growths, which I must confess that we've not been able to do in the last 2 years, but we -- our principle is that our -- if our top line growth is X, our fixed cost growth or our people cost growth should be 0.75X. And that's what we will keep with, so that we are leveraging our top line growths.

items.statement: Other operating income from incentives expected to be similar to current year.
items.quote: So we estimate that for the coming years, the incentives that we should be able to get, subject to our fulfilling certain conditions that are prescribed under PLI for that, we expect it to be on similar lines as current year.

items.statement: No concern from new large players like Amul or Reliance in biscuits currently.
items.quote: Not really, Abneesh. We haven't seen any signs of worry at this point in time. And if we do see something, we will obviously react at that point in time. But no, at this time -- the brands are also very important, Abneesh. It's very difficult to just come in and work on one element, which is price and get away with it.

items.statement: Focus states contribute 15% of revenue and growing at 1.3-1.4x, driving rural growth.
items.quote: Yes, so Tejash, Vipin this side. So these states basically contributes about 15-odd percent to our overall revenue. And they have been growing at about 1.3 to 1.4x, which means that over a period of time from 12%, 13%, they've moved to 15%, 16%.

items.statement: E-commerce contribution: biscuits 4%, croissant 17%, cake 9%, dairy 11%.
items.quote: So for example, biscuits is 4% as far as e-com is concerned or slightly lower than 4%. But let's say, I'm just giving you 1 or 2 numbers so that you get an idea. For croissant, it's 17%; for cake, it's 9%, right; for dairy, it's 11%.

items.statement: Cost savings expected to beat full-year targets.
items.quote: No, cost savings are going very well for us. In fact, we probably will beat our targets that we've set for ourselves for the full year.

items.statement: Commodity inflation at 11%, would have been 2-4% higher without forward buying.
items.quote: Sugar is flat. Cocoa is at 103% inflation. Laminates is nominal at 3% and corrugated boxes are at 15%. So our inflation for our products that we buy is about 11%. This would have been at least 2% to 4% higher had we not done the forward buying, and we hadn't had that advantage of that forward buying.

items.statement: Capex benefits from new plants and PLI incentives to continue for longer period.
items.quote: No. So capex, most of the capex gains that we get or the benefits that we get are for a much longer period of time. Yes, there are some plants which exhaust their incentives, but there are other plants we've recently put up 3 large facilities, Ranjangaon, UP and in TN, also in Bihar, Bihta, and we've expanded our Orissa facility as well. So there are big incentives there as well.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to trend in the zone of 15.5% to 17.5% going forward.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect our EBITDA margins to remain strong and trend in the zone of 15.5% to 17.5% on the back of continued investments in A&SP.

items.statement: Guides EBITDA margin range of 15.5% to 17.5% with slight bias towards higher end.
items.quote: The guidance that we are giving is in the range of 15.5% to 17.5% with a slight bias towards the higher end of the range.

items.statement: Expects mid to high teens revenue growth.
items.quote: We are looking at mid to high teens kind of growth in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of Rs.15-20 crore; exploring Rs.35-50 crore for Andhra unit expansion.
items.value: Rs.15 to 20 crore; Rs.35 to 50 crore
items.quote: In terms of our CAPEX plans, while maintenance CAPEX will range between Rs.15 to 20 crore, we are exploring making an investment amounting to around Rs.35 to 50 crore for the expansion of our own unit in Andhra Pradesh, housed in our wholly-owned subsidiary, Prag Distillery Private Limited.

items.statement: Maintenance capex approximately Rs.20 crore next year; potential Rs.50 crore for Prag expansion.
items.quote: In terms of the maintenance CAPEX, I have already guided for a maintenance CAPEX for approximately Rs. 20 crore for the next year. There might be a potential investment which we are exploring of around Rs. 50 crore for the expansion of our own unit in Andhra Pradesh, which is Prag Distillery, which would entail expanding our capacity from 6 lakh cases to 36 lakh cases per annum.

items.statement: Took a price correction in Andhra Pradesh to maintain competitive position.
items.quote: On the NSR Front, we had to take a price correction in Andhra Pradesh in order to maintain our competitive position in the state.

items.statement: Blended price correction in Andhra Pradesh around Rs.200 reduction.
items.quote: The price correction in Andhra blended level on a state basis would be around Rs. 200, reduction.

items.statement: Primary volumes grew 14% in January 2025 YoY; expects to continue growth momentum.
items.quote: We believe that this period of transition in Andhra is over and is reflected by the fact that we have started Q4 on a very strong note, having grown primary volumes by 14% in January 2025 on a YoY basis. We now expect to continue this growth momentum going forward.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin stood at 17.7%.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for Q3 FY25 stood at 17.7%.

items.statement: Launched Monarch Legacy Edition luxury brandy; expanding to Goa, Karnataka, Puducherry.
items.quote: A key highlight of the quarter was the successful launch of Monarch Legacy Edition, our first luxury brandy. Monarch blends French grape spirits aged up to 8 years in French oak casks with premium Indian grape spirit from Maharasht ra’s Sahyadri region

items.statement: Expects to kick-start sales of Samsara Gin and Sitara Rum in Q4.
items.quote: We now also expect to kick-start sales of Samsara Gin and Sitara Rum in Q4 on the back of our usership agreement with Spaceman Spirits Lab.

items.statement: Remains vigilant about ENA price trends; overall cost environment favorable.
items.quote: With softening cost pressures on raw materials and packaging, our premiumization strategy is expected to continue to support margins. While we remain vigilant about ENA price trends, the overall cost environment has been favorable, strengthening our profitability outlook.

items.statement: Reduced gross debt by Rs.47 crore; gross debt now Rs.45 crore with net cash Rs.31 crore.
items.value: Rs.47 crore; Rs.45 crore; Rs.31 crore
items.quote: On the debt front, I am happy to share that in Q3, we have reduced our gross debt by Rs.47 crore. This reduction in gross debt was predominantly on account of full repayment of Kotak Bank term loan. Our aggregate gross debt now stands at Rs.45 crore with net cash balance of Rs.31 crore.

items.statement: Expects tax incidence from Q1 next year at normal rate of 25%.
items.quote: I think we had guided for that either, we may have tax incid ence from first quarter of next year which would be at a normal rate of 25

items.statement: Expects further subsidy in Q4; difficult to quantify amount.
items.quote: We do expect further subsidy to be received in Q4, but it will be difficult at this point to quantify the amount.

items.statement: A&SP reinvestment rates range 1% to 1.5-1.7% of net revenue; expects to increase.
items.quote: So, our A&SP reinvestment rates range anywhere between 1% to 1.5-1.7%, depending upon the quarter. We end up doing more A&SP spends during the peak seasons as such.

items.statement: Aims to deliver mid to high teens EBITDA margin.
items.quote: we have –communicated in the road shows which we have done, we aim to be deliver mid to high teens of EBITDA. That is what the team will keep on working to ensure this is what we want to deliver..

items.statement: Aims to maintain gross margin in 35% to 40% range.
items.quote: Our aim is to maintain a gross margin in the range of 35% to 40%. And blended, we are achieving 39.8% in the first 9 months, which is a good performance.

items.statement: Plans capex of INR800 million for FY25-26.
items.quote: I think in last call, Parikshit, we talked about $8 million to $10 million or about roughly INR800 million of capex that we plan.

items.statement: Order backlog of INR107.8 billion as of December 2024, up 72% from March.
items.quote: Our order backlog stood at INR107.8 billion as at December '24 versus INR62.7 billion as at March, up by 72%.

items.statement: Endeavors to maintain or grow quarterly order inflow run rate of INR17 billion.
items.quote: Excluding that, we have order book of about INR52 billion in the 9 months which gives almost INR17 billion as a run rate every quarter. So, our endeavour is to maintain that, and we are working towards that.

items.statement: Sees sustained project pipeline over next 12-18 months, including HVDC.
items.quote: We see a sustained pipeline of projects which will be coming during these times and 12 to 18 months should not be difficult, including the HVDC part of this.

items.statement: Pricing power expected to remain stable for next 12-18 months due to supply chain and raw material costs.
items.quote: But I don't see that at least in next 12, 18 months, there is any significant change happening. We have to also understand one thing is that this pricing power, which everybody is talking about, it is not only because of the OEMs.

items.statement: Supply chain challenges expected to persist as capacity increases lag demand.
items.quote: So, till the time the investments are not happening on an equal scale with the supply chain side, this challenge will remain as one of the biggest for the industry and the demand is not only growing in India, but growing globally.

items.statement: On 9-month basis, 25% revenue from projects and 75% from products.
items.quote: So, on a 9-month basis, roughly 25% of the revenue is from the projects and 75% revenue is from the products.

items.statement: Export margins are 3-5 percentage points higher than domestic, but difference is narrowing.
items.quote: Generally, the margin on export is better than the margin on the domestic side. There is 3 percentage point to 5 percentage point difference. But off late, we have seen that the margins in the domestic side is also picking up.

items.statement: Expects export revenues to pick up in coming quarters due to strong order backlog.
items.quote: So, we expect revenues to pick up from the export side in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Quarter-by-quarter revenue is going to grow based on order backlog.
items.quote: But looking into the order backlog which we have, definitely, the quarter-by-quarter revenue is going to grow.

items.statement: Targets 30% of order inflows from exports, including parent.
items.quote: Yes, the target will be to keep that 30% should come from exports.

items.statement: Majority of INR9 lakh crores investment from 2024 to 2032 is still to be awarded.
items.quote: No, no, no. Since the government is talking from like 2024 to 2032.

items.statement: STATCOM market size estimated at INR3,000-3,500 crores.
items.quote: So, we are looking at the market size, we are looking at about close to about INR3,000 crores to INR3,500 crores of market for STATCOM.

items.statement: Latching relay collaboration projected to generate INR200 crores plus revenue in FY30.
items.quote: This collaboration is projected to generate INR200 crores plus revenue in FY '30 and Sterling Tools will bring niche technology to manufacture and assemble latching relays locally at a new facility in Bangalore with an initial investment of around INR20 crores.

items.statement: HVDC contactors and relays production to commence in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Happy to share that our new manufacturing facility in Bangalore for HVDC contactors and relays has made good progress. We expect to commence production in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Full year margin structures expected around 15%.
items.quote: But basically, we are not worried on holding our guidance that we will -- our margin structures for the full year will be around 15%. So, we still hold that.

items.statement: FY26 marginal revenue from HVDC about INR30-odd crores.
items.quote: Yes. So I think on an FY '26 basis, we're looking at a marginal revenue of about INR30-odd crores only.

items.statement: HVDC business to have operating losses initially, then healthy double-digit margins in third/fourth year.
items.quote: Going on the margin structure, I think on a steady-state basis, we will probably -- because of low revenue in the first 24 months or so, we'll have some operating losses. But I think on a steady-state basis going third, fourth year, this business is going to have a healthy double-digit margin structure.

items.statement: HVDC business to be in profits by FY28.
items.quote: So, I would probably say more like FY '28 because we get operational in the second half of FY '26. So, on a full year basis, FY '27 will be the first full year. FY '28, second full year, we'll be in profits.

items.statement: Total capex for both product lines under STML about INR30 crores in next 18 months.
items.quote: But from a capex perspective, we are looking at a total capex for both the product lines coming under the same entity of Sterling Tech-Mobility, STML. We're looking at a INR30 crores-odd capex in the next 18 months.

items.statement: Current latching relay imports about INR200 crores, market growing dramatically.
items.quote: Yes. So, imports are about INR200 crores right now as of today. But understand the market is really growing both in terms of EVs, hybrids, smart metering, et cetera.

items.statement: Fastener business to grow 7-9% this year, faster than industry.
items.quote: So like I said, repeating what I said in my calls earlier, fastener is a very mature business with us. We'll be up 7%, 8%, 9% this year. Industry is only up 3%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue CAGR about 10% in short term.
items.quote: So Kush, our estimate is we are looking at -- we have a tough year coming up next year because we are bringing a lot more products into our portfolio. There has been a realignment of some customers or some product lines. It's a tough year. But I think if we are able to do a CAGR of about 10-odd percent in the short term, we'll be happy with that.

items.statement: Consolidated margins around 12.5% plus, aim to maintain or improve.
items.quote: So our margins are not 11%. Our margins are around 12.5% plus. And our effort is we want to stay there on a consolidated level or maybe even improve on that number.

items.statement: Integrated motor and controller units to be in production next financial year.
items.quote: So we are looking at the next financial year. I mean, I'm sorry, I'm already thinking about the next financial. Thank you for that clarification question.

items.statement: New verticals' losses are marginal, no large material impact.
items.quote: These are marginal numbers. The loss numbers are marginal numbers for the balance sheet size we have or the P&L we have. So, I don't think it's going to have any large material impact on our overall performance.

items.statement: On track to full year FY25 guidance for revenue and margins.
items.quote: We believe we've had a good quarter and last 9 months. We are on track to our guidance giving for the full year FY '25.

items.statement: Finalized greenfield alkaline battery plant in Jammu with Rs. 180 crore capital outlay, commercial production by end of this calendar year.
items.quote: We have finalized plans for a greenfield production facility for alkaline batteries with a capital outlay of Rs. 180 crore. This facility, located in Jammu, is expected to commence commercial production by the end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Expect 8% to 10% margin improvement on alkaline through domestic manufacturing.
items.quote: And we expect 8% to 10% margin improvement is possible on alkaline part of this operation through domestic manufacturing.

items.statement: Jammu plant first year revenue may start at Rs. 100 crore annualized, could go up to Rs. 400 crore.
items.quote: So, I am saying that first year, we may start with the Rs. 100 crore revenue from that plant on annualized basis, and which could go up to Rs. 400 crore.

items.statement: Jammu plant financing 75% debt, 25% internal.
items.quote: So, of course some part will be going internally if you have, I have already mentioned that like land we have internally paid money so maybe it's a 75-25 type of financing, 25% will be internal things and 75% probably will take from the banks and other financial institutions, so that is the point you are looking for and the revenue will be, so today if there will be some other things to enjoy the

items.statement: A&P expenditure expected 10% for next couple of quarters, may restrict to 8-9% as revenue scales.
items.quote: So, at this point of time, 10% is looking forward for the next couple of quarters at least, but once revenue becomes sizable, then at that point of time, we'll look for, because at that point of time, we may restrict to absolute value rather than talking about the percentage.

items.statement: Alkaline market share to remain around 11% in next 2-3 months, next step to 20%.
items.quote: So, we are currently at 11%. I would imagine to remain somewhere around this level by the next 2 to 3 months. But we would keep on this journey, whereby our next step would be to go to 20% kind of level.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin aspiration 39% to 40%.
items.quote: I guess we should look for 40%, it will be our inspiration to be there in a 39% to 40% but it all depends on that. So, as you know as of now, we have achieved 38% plus, so if you ask me, our aspiration will be towards 40%, but it's a highly commodity-driven business.

items.statement: Gross margin 45% plus or minus 1% could be good enough.
items.quote: So, in that case, if you ask me, we have 55% actually. 45% is a pretty good gross margin level we are looking for because as I said that material mix keeps changing time to time. Now zinc prices will be softened. So, 45%, 1% plus and minus could be the good enough.

items.statement: BIS certification for flashlights expected to weed out unorganized segment, immediate uptick possible.
items.quote: We believe that this will weed out bulk of the unorganized, so-called unethical segment. And that should turn more towards the organized part of the industry, which frankly speaking is basically us.

items.statement: Rechargeable flashlights to continue growth, battery-operated degrowth to continue gradually.
items.quote: The battery operated one has now come down to 30% of the overall flashlight market and we expect this degrowth to continue, but I would say gradually it's lower because there are some incumbent users who are not going to shift to rechargeable. However, rechargeable is the one which will continue to see growth and so we are sort of putting lot of focus and emphasis on bulking up on this segment.

items.statement: Jammu plant to add margin, not change market pricing structure.
items.quote: The Jammu plant is not going to change this market per se. The Jammu plant is going to add margin to our P&L.

items.statement: CCI penalty case next hearing deferred to May 5th, company to defend robustly.
items.quote: So, there was a hearing supposed to be on 28 th-29th of January, which has now been deferred to the 5th of May. So, basically not much movement has taken place on this case. We would of course robustly defend our position.

items.statement: Peak debt expected around Rs. 325 to Rs. 330 crore.
items.quote: So, maybe if I add that mathematically and Rs. 50 odd crore I will repay as a part of my, so maximum I think around Rs. 325 to Rs. 330 odd crore would be the peak, and we'll try to because we're in that limit.
