items.statement: No specific guidance on revenue or earnings will be provided.
items.quote: In line with our standard practice, we would not be providing specific guidance on revenue or earnings.

items.statement: Chairperson expects to sustain positive momentum and ensure smooth leadership transition in the medium term.
items.quote: Sustaining this positive momentum across our key business areas and ensuring smooth leadership transition will be our primary focus in the medium term while we remain steadfast in our commitment to delivering credible and trustworthy news and engaging ente rtainment content through our legacy platforms as well as new -age product

items.statement: AFE assets are not for long-term holding and most are for sale.
items.quote: These are not used for captive consumption, and we are not keeping this for a long-term. So, as you understand the AFE business, the generic characteristic of the business is that most of these assets are for sale.

items.statement: Print revenues have declined from 85% of total revenue 8-10 years ago to less than that today.
items.quote: But from, let's say, if I were to just broadly give you a perspective from about 8 -10 years ago, where Print revenues in the total revenue stream would constitute about 85% of the revenues. Today, they are less than that.

items.statement: Print will continue to be under pressure but remains core business.
items.quote: Print has been under pressure for the longest time. It will continue to be so. But at this point in time, it's still the main , the core of the business at this point in time.

items.statement: Company prefers to go deep rather than wide on investments, focusing on right to win and absorption capacity.
items.quote: Now beyond a certain point in time, I don't think we would like to just deploy investment for the heck of it because there's something called a right to win and something called the absorption capacity. So, at this point in time, I think we would like to focus on the things that we are doing, and we'd like to rather go deep than go wide on this.

items.statement: Company would like to simplify structure but currently continuing with two listed companies.
items.quote: Look, I mean, the simple answer is we'd like to simplify things as much as possible. But given the Indian environment, as you rightly alluded towards, there are a bit of challenges. But if we get, let's say, if we manage to bring all our creditors and shareholders together, we would definitely like to follow that stream. But at this point in time, we are continuing the way it is.

items.statement: Radio yields are still struggling versus pre-Covid levels; improvement is a marathon.
items.quote: The simple answer is no, they are still struggling versus the pre -Covid level. So, there are multiple things that we are trying in the marketplace. Of course, taking yield at this point in time where the digital music or the digital audio is gaining so much traction is not an easy journey, but we are on it for the longest time.

items.statement: Radio business is heavily regulated with royalty and license commitments; industry proposals pending with Government.
items.quote: Now, also the point to be understood is Radio is a very heavily regulated business, and there is a lot of royalty and license commitments and fees that you have to pay to the Government. So, there are various proposals that at an industry level are pending with the Government to give some ease to the sector.

items.statement: Print ad revenue growth driven by pricing and mix, not volume.
items.quote: The volume in the advertising market this quarter was not very robust. So, it is pricing and mix that has helped in the revenue growth as was articulated towards the first part of the conversation.

items.statement: Market volumes have not grown versus previous year; growth from pricing and mix.
items.quote: Market volumes have not grown versus previous year. However, we have been able to grow pricing, it's a combination of the absolute price increase as well as the categories because there is a difference in pricing between categories also.

items.statement: Circulation revenue down due to initial discounts to increase copies; cost is temporary.
items.quote: Well, not exactly. As I was explaining to another caller earlier, we are on a journey to increase our copies in the marketplace and for that, we are giving a certain amount of discount as a n initial discount for the copy so that's bringing down the circulation revenue.

items.statement: BSNL tie-up has sputtering start; full-fledged tie-up not yet in being.
items.quote: So, Mehul, first of all, that tie -up is having a sputtering start. I mean, BSNL being a Government organization is into various discussions with us . A full-fledged tie -up has still not come into the be ing.

items.statement: OTTplay expenses down 65% y-o-y; operating leverage in Print flowing to bottom line.
items.quote: But what vitiates the picture is because OTTplay expenses are sitting, which, by the way, themselves on a y-o-y basis are 65% lower than the same quarter last year, but there are still substantial expenses happening there.

items.statement: OTTplay addressable market more than 1% of 125 million paying viewers; ARPU and acquisition cost metrics need to improve.
items.quote: So, we are basically, definitely addressing more than 1%. But at this point in time, there is a certain ARPU and there is a certain acquisition cost that we are getting out of pocket on. And those are the metrics that have to go up.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 19%.
items.quote: So on the overall margins, I would say we are pretty much on track with the guidance that we gave earlier. Saion, as you know, Q4 is our lowest quarter, and we have a lot of filings that we are going to do in Q4, because of which our spending is also higher in Q4.

items.statement: India business expected to grow in line with market at around 7% for the full year.
items.quote: So, when it comes to the overall year-end, we sense that we should be broadly in line with the market as far as overall India growth is concerned. The market is growing at around 7%. We should be pretty much in line with that kind of growth as far as India is concerned.

items.statement: U.S. business expected to be flat in Q4 and better next year.
items.quote: So if you look at even for Q4, we are expecting it to be, say, flat because as we are moving ahead from a minus 22%, we are at minus 7%. My sense is that by Q4, we should be neutral as compared to last year.

items.statement: Non-U.S. markets expected to grow 13-14% going forward.
items.quote: And overall, I think for the non-U.S., I think we have given a guidance of 13% to 14% of growth going forward.

items.statement: R&D spend expected at 4.5% to 5% of sales.
items.quote: We're looking at around 4.5% to 5%, somewhere in that range.

items.statement: MedTech investment planned up to INR2,500 crores over 3-4 years.
items.value: INR2,000 crores to INR2,400 crores or INR2,500 crores
items.quote: See, on MedTech, maybe over the next 3 or 4 years, we may not go beyond INR2,000 crores to INR2,400 crores or INR2,500 crores of investment. That is what the plan is: a max of INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Enzene Pune expected to close FY25 at around INR300 crores sales, grow 15-20% next year.
items.quote: So Enzene -- means, including sales of products, we do from Alkem for products which are manufactured in Enzene, we have done a sales of around INR200 crores at YTD level, and our estimate is to clos e at around INR300 crores for FY '25. So we can assume growth of around 15% to 20% in next year from the Pune

items.statement: Trade generic margins now only slightly below consolidated margins.
items.quote: So, we are not going after a top line, but we want to have the right balance of our top-line growth as well as the margin. So earlier, the margins are very low. As far as this business is concerned, our margins are now only a shade less than our overall corporate margins.

items.statement: U.S. price erosion around 5%, or 2.5% on NRV basis.
items.quote: Yes, price erosion is to the tune of around 5%, though on the NRV basis, because we had some forex gains because of the dollar, it's 2.5%.

items.statement: PenG prices increased 20-25% in last two months.
items.quote: PenG, we see in the last 2 months, the price is going up. So there is around 20%, 30% -- 20% to 25% price increase from where it used to be a couple of months ago.

items.statement: Domestic growth expected stronger in Q4, around 9.5-10%.
items.quote: So, I think the calculations are fairly close. It comes to around 9.5% to 10% if on the overall domestic side. And we are pretty co nfident of delivering the same because of a lot of reasons, like I said, our secondary offtakes are good

items.statement: Semaglutide launch planned, among first wave in India.
items.quote: So, first, on the GLP-1, we should be amongst the first wave of players who would come in with GLP-1. We have already represented ourselves to the regulator in India. And I think we are pretty much on track to be amongst the first few players who will come up with semaglutide in India at the time of launch.

items.statement: Chile market degrew 30% due to tender exit and currency.
items.quote: It's largely from one of our large markets, which is Chile. In Chile, we have 2 issues: one is some tenders that we came out of, and the second is the exchange rate. So the currency actually played spoilsport over there. So because of that, Chile, which is our one of the largest non-U.S. markets that has shown alm ost 30% degrowth, which is where our overall non -U.S. growth is looking

items.statement: Net cash position around INR4,700 crores, no leverage.
items.quote: And also currently, we are in 0 leverage. So we don't have any loans in our books. The net cash position is around INR4,700 crores.

items.statement: Acquisitions: Adroit for INR140 crores, Bombay Ortho for INR147 crores.
items.quote: We have also announced 2 acquisitions, Adroit, the pharmaceutical health care company with a focus on dermato -cosmetology, at a cash consideration of INR140 crores. And second is Bombay Ortho, a manufacturer and supplier of automatic im plants such as hip and knee implants, which are extensively used in orthopaedic fields at a cash consideration of INR147 crores

items.statement: NSEIT DEX acquisition near completion; closing expected in next seven to ten days.
items.quote: The Share Purchase Agreement (‘SPA’) has been signed as you might have seen and which also was followed by the formal press releases from both sides. There are a couple of, absolute closure events that are pending, such as, taking over of the board, and such couple of stuff.

items.statement: NSEIT DEX has opening top line of Rs. 200 crores and 17% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: On day one, it starts with an opening balance of about a top line of Rs. 200 crores, and this gives us about 17% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Assessment TAM in India estimated at 9 crore people, poised to grow to 18 crore in next five to seven years.
items.quote: the TAM, the assessment opportunity in India, the total addressable market is estimated to be about nine crore people and, poised to grow to Rs. 18 crores in the next five to seven years.

items.statement: NSEIT DEX can conduct population scale exams of 5-25 lakh in over 700 districts.
items.quote: Today, NSEIT DEX has a capability to conduct a population scale examination between a five lakh or a 25 lakh, examination in over 700 districts across the country.

items.statement: NSEIT DEX can go international over next three to five years.
items.quote: the greater possibility that we do see over the next three to five years is where NSEIT DEX can go international.

items.statement: Plan to grow NSEIT DEX 3x to 5x over coming few years.
items.quote: our job is now to see how do we take it from where it is to a 3x and a 5x over the coming few years.

items.statement: NSEIT DEX to double over next three to four years.
items.quote: I think, for the next three years, three to four years, we should look at how d o we double this and give it a very, very impactful, profitable non -India presence while we go into penetration in India.

items.statement: NSEIT DEX will not enter test prep areas like MBA, law, IPM.
items.quote: the areas where CL has test prep interest, we will not venture DEX will not venture into those areas at all, which are, essentially the mandate MBA law, IPM.

items.statement: NSEIT DEX financials for first nine months not disclosed yet.
items.quote: Because the transaction is yet to get officially completed till we take over the Board, it's not a part of our business, so we can't declare those numbers yet.

items.statement: NSEIT DEX last financial year numbers Rs. 200 crore and 17%; this year could be better.
items.quote: The Rs. 200 crore mentioned, in the first slide and the 17% that Satya mentioned were numbers pertaining to the last financial year. This year's numbers could be better than that.

items.statement: UTSAV launched on January 12, 2025; targeting 1% of luxury weddings in 3-4 years.
items.quote: We had a very successful launch, officially on the January 12, 2025. These are the real pictures of an event that we conducted.

items.statement: UTSAV aims to do 400-500 weddings annually in year three or four.
items.quote: can we aim to do 1% of the luxury weddings in three to four years' time, which means can we build capacity and ability to do 400 to 500 weddings annually in year three or year four?

items.statement: UTSAV EBITDA expected 10-12% based on Kestone high value events.
items.quote: we are guided between, what is, high value events or conferences, EBITDA that we see in Kestone is what we are taking as the starting point, which is a 10 to 12% EBITDA is what we are thinking.

items.statement: UTSAV to focus on campus festivals in June-October to manage seasonality.
items.quote: in order to manage the seasonality, the other thing that we intend to do is look at the large format campus festivals and campus events in the June to October season.

items.statement: GST demand notice received; contesting based on prior Supreme Court win.
items.quote: We have now received a demand notice on the same. It pertains to a matter of composite supply. Books and coaching services should have the same, GST rate applicable.

items.statement: Funding NSEIT DEX acquisition with mix of debt and equity from Piramal Group consortium.
items.quote: we are using a mix of debt and equity. We will share more specific details on that when we do the, specific DEX session on, conclusion of the transaction.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected in the range of INR2,500 crores.
items.quote: Yes, it will be in the range of INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR4,000 crores.
items.quote: It should be in the range of INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow target of INR3,500 crores.
items.quote: This year, yes. You are right. INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow expected around INR5,000 crores.
items.quote: For the entire year FY '26 total order inflows will be around INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: Outstanding order book as of 9MFY25 was INR6,417 crore, a YoY growth of 44%.
items.quote: As on 9MFY25, the outstanding order book was to the extent of Rs.6,417 crore, a YoY growth of 44%.

items.statement: Expect to announce work orders from Adani Group within the range of INR2,000 crore.
items.quote: Currently, we are discussing with Adani Group on various orders and we shall announce work orders within the range of INR2,000 crore.

items.statement: In discussion with Adani Group for projects envisaging around INR5,000 crore for FY26.
items.quote: And for FY26, we are in discussion with Adani Group on various projects which we are envisaging for the next 1 year which will be in the range of Rs. 5000 crore.

items.statement: Capex for Q3 FY25 was INR16 crores.
items.quote: During Q3 FY 25, company has incurred capex of 16 crores.

items.statement: Next year capex expected to be 3% to 4% of expected turnover.
items.quote: Next year, see around 3% to 4% of our expected turnover will be spending on the capex.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected from Adani projects starting in May-June 2025.
items.quote: That is just because of the large order book to come from Adani, and most of the projects starting somewhere in the month of May-June 2025.

items.statement: UP project additional expenses expected to be within INR2 crores to INR3 crores maximum.
items.quote: But probably from now onward, I don't see any, but let's not consider that to be zero. So, it can be within the range of INR2 crores to INR3 crores maximum.

items.statement: Open offer expected to conclude before March 2025.
items.quote: But probably before March 2025 it should get concluded.

items.statement: Adani Infra to acquire up to 30.07% stake from founder promoter.
items.quote: As you all are aware during the quarter, the company entered into an arrangement with Adani Infra wherein Adani Infra to acquire up to 30.07% stake from the founder promoter.

items.statement: Company has filed Section 9 Petition in Commercial Court, Lucknow, regarding contract termination.
items.quote: With regards to the litigation, the Company has filed a Section 9 Petition before the Hon’ble Commercial Court, Lucknow, in which the Company has requested the Hon’ble Court to maintain the status quo of the contract terms and grant interim relief against the termination of the contract.

items.statement: Targets FY25 gross premium of INR 40,000-41,000 crores, 8-10% growth over previous year.
items.quote: If you remember, at the beginning of FY '25, we had given a guidance that compared to the previous year, we would grow about 8% to 10%, and we would be somewhere close to anywhere between INR 40,000 crores to INR 41,000 crores.

items.statement: Aims to reduce combined ratio by 2-2.5% annually over next 2-3 years to about 105%.
items.quote: So, over maybe next 2, 3 years, reduce it by 2% each, come to about 105%, and then start with struggle to really come further down, because that will mean really putting in place a lot of risk management features to ensure that our book is well balanced.

items.statement: Expects international combined ratio to improve and eventually be below 100%.
items.quote: We want to reach a situation where International Business ideally should be below 100%.

items.statement: Expects mid-teen growth in FY26 and double-digit growth in next few years.
items.quote: I would say so. I would say so. I think long term, that is what we would be looking for mid-term, that's what we will be looking for.

items.statement: Wrote about $80 million more business in Jan 1 renewals, with 15-16% signing rate.
items.quote: So, we finally got a signing of about 15%, 16%, which overall means that in 1st Jan, we have written about $80 million more, that works out to about INR 650 crores more.

items.statement: Fire pricing has hardened, returning to previous levels after 25% discounts.
items.quote: So, when you say the pricing holding up, has it gone back to the previous level, which means there is a 25% price increase to a large extent in the current environment? Ramaswamy Narayanan: Yes, I would say that. I would say

items.statement: Provided $25 million for LA fires in Q3, may revise next quarter.
items.quote: Currently, we have provided about $25 million in our provisions. Now you should realize this is basically an event, which has happened in the fourth qu arter in January. But prudently, we have already provided for it in our third quarter results

items.statement: Provided $7 million for US aviation event and small amount for South Korea aviation event.
items.quote: The U.S., we have already pro vided about $7 million for the U.S. event, slightly lower, but you can take it at about $7 million. Even on the South Korea, we have a very, very small share

items.statement: Sees growth opportunities in cyber and surety bonds due to regulatory push and market demand.
items.quote: Surety bonds is one where that business is slowly moving from banks, which used to traditionally do that to now the insurance market. Cyber, again, as an IT pr ogressive country, obviously, so when people adopt technology very well, cyber becomes a risk, which needs to be covered. We are seeing traction there

items.statement: Increased focus on health business to diversify away from catastrophe-exposed lines.
items.quote: So, I think Health, we kind of focused this year, because if you see typically, fire, the own damage part of Motor and agri are more or less climate change-related, which could get affected by catastrophe. So, that was the reason for us to also focus on Health as one of the areas where we would like to grow.

items.statement: Domestic combined ratio for Q3 was 102.76%, better than market's 118-120%.
items.quote: Currently, if you see for the quarter, the domestic combined is 102.76%, which is really good. Like I said, when the market is running at a combined close to 118% or 120%, for us to be doing 102% means that we have really managed our exposures well.

items.statement: International combined ratio improved to 122% in Q3 from 158% last year.
items.quote: Internationally, if you see the figures, typically for the quarter, that is 31/12/23, our combined was 158%, which has now come down to 122%.

items.statement: Expects combined ratio to reduce meaningfully in Q4 due to premium inflows and no major cats.
items.quote: So, going by what we have seen in the past, how we look at the results, I would expect a meaningful reduction. At this stage, I will not be able to tell you how much we will need to wait and watch there.

items.statement: Plans to increase employee strength to 568 with ongoing recruitment.
items.quote: We have also started another recruitment process in January, where people would hopefully join in the next financial year. That is another 110. So, we are actually ramping up our employee forces, because some of the elderly, older employees are retiring as well.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to be around 25% going forward.
items.quote: So, the normal tax rate will be continuing to be in the range of 25%.

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth in hospital business going forward.
items.quote: we continue to deliver the double-digit growth for our Hospital business. So, the trend will continue, because apart from that, there's a lot of activities which we have found that we are going to start in terms of the radiation and other things.

items.statement: Implant business to deliver multi-fold growth next financial year with CKS Gold approval.
items.quote: Implant, as you mentioned, we are good effort -- growing very fast. And with this approval of this CKS Gold, it is going to deliver the multi-fold growth in terms of the Implant business into the next financial year.

items.statement: Sanar to become EBITDA positive from Q4 or Q1 FY26.
items.quote: And going forward, we expect maybe from the fourth quarter onwards or maybe the first quarter of next financial year we should be EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Implant business to touch solid single to double-digit EBITDA by end of next year.
items.quote: I think we will touch end of next year close to solid single to double-digit EBITDA. And that's what I think. Next year, same time, I feel we should be in a good single to double-digit EBITDA.

items.statement: Minimal CAPEX of Rs. 50-100 crores to more than double top-line from existing beds.
items.quote: We have that kind of capacity within the existing facility with a very minimal CAPEX of between Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 100 crores. We will be able to generate this kind of revenue in the coming years.

items.statement: Taken line of credit of Rs. 40 crores for radiation, to come at end of Q1.
items.quote: For the radiation, we have already taken the line of credit of close to around Rs. 40 crores, which will come into the, at the end of the quarter one.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin to sustain at 21-22% and improve going forward.
items.quote: Yes. So, we are going to sustain the profitability. As I mentioned, there is one-off kind of OpEx has been there in terms of the orthotrends event. And apart from that, as an organization, we are always going at it with a lot of cost optimization process where we are optimizing in terms of the cost and other things. So, we are going to see the improvement going forward also.

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth in inpatient and outpatient counts long-term.
items.quote: Yes, the inpatient count and outpatient count you can expect double-digit growth on those numbers, yes.

items.statement: ARPOB growth typically 3-6% annually, volume growth 8-10%.
items.quote: See what happens is that ARPOB growth is usually on an annual basis, we are seeing that the ARPOB growth is between 3% to 6% and then the volume growth is another 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Oncology now highest revenue share after joint replacement, investing in LINACs.
items.quote: And essentially, from a lower single-digit kind of revenue share in terms of our total revenues, it is now, I would say, the highest after the joint replacement. So -- and we are continuously investing in this segment across the medical, the surgical, as well as the radiation oncology part.

items.statement: Tax rate on consolidated to remain elevated for next two to three quarters due to no deferred tax on loss-making entities.
items.quote: So, that is the reason you will see very abbreviated numbers in the tax that will continue for a couple of quarters. On the consolidated number, it will continue for the next two, three quarters at least.

items.statement: Evaluating shift to new tax rate next financial year, likely 25% on standalone.
items.quote: So, we are evaluating, currently we are under the MAT which is getting exhausted into the current financial year, and then after we are going to take a call into the next financial year.

items.statement: Debt to continue for implant working capital for one or two more quarters.
items.quote: Apart from that, for this implant, we keep investing in terms of the working capital. So that will continue on the trend what you have seen into the earlier quarter that will continue for the couple of one or two quarter more.

items.statement: EBITDA to improve in coming quarters and implant PBT losses to reduce next financial year.
items.period: coming quarters and next financial year
items.quote: So debt is not impacting the EBITDA also. So EBITDA will definitely improve into the coming quarters and we are going to see the growth in terms of the reduction of losses in terms of the PBT level for our Implant business into the next financial year.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 45% to 50% for next financial year.
items.quote: But as a guidance point of view, 45% to 50% is something that, we will continue to increase our revenue by 45% to 50%. That's the only guidance that I can give you at this point of time.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to reach 30% on balance sheet basis in next 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: So, the peak of 26%-27% whatever is there, that will continue to maintain. And it will go up to 30% on a balance sheet basis for the next 1-1.5 year.

items.statement: Production and development mix expected to be 60%-40% in FY26.
items.quote: I am unable to give the guidance for FY '27, how much the percentage would be. But for FY '26, it could be like 60%-40%.

items.statement: Unit 3 facility expected to be completed by Q2 FY26.
items.quote: And as a part of our forward integration focus for weapon integration, we commenced construction of our integrated plan for Ingenious Defense System IPiDS, which is Unit 3, and this is expected to be completed by Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Fund utilization: INR550 crores for working capital, INR66 crores for subsidiary, INR130-140 crores for general corporate purpose, balance for R&D.
items.value: INR550 crores, INR66 crores, INR130-INR140 crores
items.quote: So, we have given a clear breakup of the utilization of the funds where we are going to do actually. INR550 odd crores will be going for the working capital and INR66 crores we will be investing in our subsidiary for some acquisitions and other things like. And around INR130-INR140 odd crores for general corporate purpose and some of the -- the balance of the funds we will be investing in R&D.

items.statement: Next year R&D investment expected close to INR100 crores.
items.quote: Next year probably we may be investing close to INR100 crores on R&D in new product development actually.

items.statement: Naval defense expected to dominate order book increase for next 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: Naval defense is one area where we have developed the complete platforms, like a complete underwater mines we have developed, and where we are expecting a large ticket projects. So, naval defense will continue to dominate to certain extent for next 1-1.5 year in the increased order book.

items.statement: Expecting direct order from Indian Navy shortly.
items.quote: One is an order we are expecting from Indian Navy very shortly. That's a direct order from Indian Navy to us.

items.statement: Artillery and bomb programs expected to have large quantities in years to come.
items.quote: But broadly to tell you, the artillery and bomb programs are the ones which are going to have a very large quantity in the years to come. So, those are the programs which will have big numbers, coming.

items.statement: ATGMs like NAG, HELINA, MPATGM, AMOGHA-2 expected to get into large numbers in years to come.
items.quote: The ATGMs are the ones which you can keep a track on that, NAG, HELINA and MPATGM and AMOGHA-2. These are the ones which will also get into large numbers in the years to come.

items.statement: ALWT limited series production to start by Q3 or Q4 of next financial year.
items.period: Q3 or Q4 of next financial year
items.quote: ALWT, we will start getting some limited series production by Q3 or Q4 of next financial year.

items.statement: Varunastra repeat order expected shortly.
items.quote: Varunastra, the entire weapon is being done by BDL, sir, actually. I am restricted to comment on that, but yes, there will be a repeat order for Varunastra coming shortly.

items.statement: Promoter pledge to be reduced to 0% in next 1 year on phase by phase basis.
items.quote: In next 1 year, on a phase by phase basis. That's what we are working towards.

items.statement: Q4 expected to surpass Q3 performance.
items.quote: We are confident that upcoming quarters will also bring positive outcomes, with Q4 expected to surpass Q3 in performance, which has been a tradition earlier as well.

items.statement: Order execution lead time average 6 to 12-14 months.
items.quote: Average, you can take anywhere between 6 months to, 12 months to 14 months.

items.statement: Export orders expected in next financial year, execution may happen next after financial year.
items.quote: Presently, we are talking to a few countries, for -- we have given our proposals. We expect that, we will be able to back some orders in the next financial year, execution of which may happen maybe next after financial year.

items.statement: Expects 20% sales growth, citing strong order book and new facilities.
items.quote: By 20%, definitely. Because I have an order book of INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Already booked INR1,115 crores orders; expects additional INR550 crores, reaching INR1,700 crores for the year.
items.quote: We have already booked nearly INR1,115 crores worth of orders. We are expecting in these two to three months, we will ge t another INR550 crores. So, we will reach INR 1,700 crores worth of orders in this year.

items.statement: Current executable order book stands at INR1,906 crores.
items.quote: As of today, we have nearly INR1,906 crores executable orders are there.

items.statement: Plans to invest INR60 crores in capex this year; INR40 crores already spent, INR20 crores remaining.
items.quote: Still, we planned around INR60 crores to be invested in this year on capex . Already, INR 40 crores we completed. Balanced INR20 crores also we are going to invest now.

items.statement: Plans to invest INR100 crores in capex next year.
items.quote: And we are planning to invest further INR 100 crores in the next year.

items.statement: Can maintain 22% EBITDA margin, with potential for higher if yield improves.
items.quote: Definitely, 22% we can maintain.

items.statement: Saved INR29 crores from raw material price reduction and INR19 crores from increased plant revert usage.
items.quote: We could manage, we could save nearly INR29 crores on account of raw material price reduction, and INR 19 crores on account of conjunction.

items.statement: Increased usage of plant revert to 45% from 34%, reducing virgin material consumption.
items.quote: Last year, our conjunction of materials to scrap is around 66% virgin and 34% plant revert. Whereas, this time, it has come down to around 55% virgin and 45% is the scrap.

items.statement: Expects INR200 crores order from ISRO by year-end, executable within a year.
items.quote: This year -- at the end of the year, we are expecting to get another INR200 crores order we will get.

items.statement: Expects INR500 crores orders in Q4 from defence, aerospace, and other sectors.
items.quote: So, this year also we are expecting order worth of about INR 500 crores in this last quarter.

items.statement: NALCO JV not encouraging; consultant recommendation not positive, still under study.
items.quote: The benefits, again, the consultant has to firmly give recommendation. It is not some positive recommendation. Still we are studying.

items.statement: Titanium plant fully operational; expects 100% utilization with secured raw materials.
items.quote: There is no issue of utilization of titanium wire. It will be utilized 100%.

items.statement: Order book breakdown: aerospace 45%, naval 30%, army/space <10%, exports INR50 crores, energy INR30 crores.
items.quote: Today, I have INR1907 crores. In that, INR800 crores and odd is aero. Naval is INR500 crores. Army space INR150 crores, INR150 crores like that.

items.statement: Exports reached INR60 crores, highest ever; expects further growth with Boeing, Pratt & Whitney, Airbus, GE.
items.quote: Like that also, if you see this year, we have already touched INR60 crores exports. Ever in the history of MIDHANI, this much of export we have not done.

items.statement: Delayed order reduced from INR1000 crores to less than INR200 crores; expects no delayed orders next year.
items.quote: Now if you see our dela yed order, whatever it was, drastically it has come down. It used to be about 2 years back. It used to be about INR 1000 crores. Now it has come less than INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Confident to hit 20,000 rooms signed and operational in next 12-15 months.
items.quote: I had said we would be 20,000 rooms in our CY28 Vision, but we are already at over 16,000 and I am pretty confident we will hit 20,000 in the next 12 months to 15 months, signed and operational.

items.statement: Expects mid-teens RevPAR growth and lower cost growth, leading to operating leverage.
items.quote: I have always said we would like to grow at, depending on which combination of we follow, whether it's a focus on occupancy or average rate in which market? We would like to have mid-teens growth at the least.

items.statement: Renovation expenses to continue into FY26 and FY27, then normalize to 1.5-1.7% of revenue.
items.quote: Please note that the increased investment in renovation expenses will continue into FY26 and a little bit into FY27, until the entire portfolio of our own ed hotels of about 6,0 00 rooms has been fully renovated and refurbished. Post this, renovation expenses will close at 1.5 %-1.7% of revenue on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: Plans to list Fleur in next 1.5-2 years, which would make company debt free.
items.quote: That is very much on the plan, we are unable to right now brief the market in detail about it, but I can say with certainty it will happen in the next 1.5-2 years max. If that happens - automatically we go debt free.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA to be under 1.7x by end of next year.
items.quote: So, we think our EBITDA will increase significantly next year to this year, very significantly and our debt-to-EBITDA will be under 1.7x by the end of next year.

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai to stabilize in H2 FY26 at 85% occupancy and Rs. 11,000+ ARR.
items.quote: Stabilized to me would probably be H2 next year when on a sustained basis we will be north of 85% at Rs. 11,000 plus ARR.

items.statement: Shillong hotel to open in 2.5-3 years, 120 rooms, capex Rs. 120 crores, EBITDA Rs. 15 crores.
items.value: 120 rooms, Rs. 120 crores, Rs. 15 crores EBITDA
items.quote: We don't think we will invest more than Rs. 120 crores for 120 rooms because we get a 5% interest subvention, so instead of borrowing money at 8%-8.5%, we will effectively get debt at 3%-3 5%. Our estimate is this hotel will make about Rs. 15 crore EBITDA a year to begin with.

items.statement: Keys portfolio EBITDA target Rs. 60 crores, doubling from current Rs. 3.5 lakhs per year.
items.quote: I had said earlier that we will definitely target a Rs. 60 crore EBITDA from keys, which means really Rs. 6.5 lakhs a Key. Currently, if you look at our EBITDA for the Keys portfolio, it is Rs. 1 lakh, a quarter or I think Rs. 3.5 lakhs a year. We will double that.

items.statement: Management fee income expected to double in next 2 years.
items.quote: Then your management fee income we expect will double in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Renovation of 4,500 rooms: 2,600-2,700 done by end of FY25, high-value hotels by next year, few hundred into FY27.
items.quote: Now of these 4 ,500 rooms, this year I think we have renovated roughly 1,300 rooms. Last year we renovated about I think about 1,000. So, of these 2,300 rooms we have already renovated some are still going on, by the end of this financial year it will be probably 2 ,600-2,700. The high-value hotels will all be renovated by next year.

items.statement: Fleur listing to provide massive upside to Lemon Tree shareholders.
items.quote: But we would want the shareholders of Lemon Tree to get a massive upside. And I mean, I am using this word very clearly, massive upside when we list Fleur.

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai ARR target Rs. 11,500-12,000 at 85% occupancy.
items.quote: But for me that is still not stabilization because as I had mentioned, I think maybe a couple of concalls before, we would like this hotel to be at around Rs. 11,500 to Rs. 12,000 ARR, at about 85% occupancy.

items.statement: Shillong hotel equity payback within 1.5 years, EBITDA margin 65%.
items.quote: So, that means that if I add that to the EBITDA margin, the EBITDA margin will be about 65% and we think we will have our equity payback, for both partners within 1.5 year.

items.statement: Debt free in three years, or earlier upon Fleur listing.
items.quote: See, what I had said is that we will be debt free in three years. Now the point I am trying to make is that we will be probably debt free earlier the minute we list Fleur.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book is INR280 crores and total order book is around INR557 crores.
items.value: INR280 crores unexecuted, INR557 crores total
items.quote: Unexecuted order book is INR280 crores and total order book is around INR557 crores.

items.statement: Plan to double order book in coming months.
items.quote: So definitely, we plan to double this order book in the coming months. It's in due to elections this year, lot of orders were delayed.

items.statement: March 2025 looks quite good for us.
items.quote: But March '25 looks to be quite good with now new stable governments coming in the state, as well as center. So March '25 looks quite good for us.

items.statement: Expecting significant increase from FY24.
items.quote: So we are expecting a significant increase from FY '24. We are not allowed to divulge any numbers as such.

items.statement: Projects will help improve EBITDA margins going ahead.
items.quote: But going ahead, these projects are with good profit as usual. And going ahead, it will help us improve our EBITDA margins also.

items.statement: Focus on INR20 crores plus projects will see good improvement in EBITDA.
items.quote: So now instead of getting a INR5 crores or INR6 crores project, our team, our business development focus would be on INR20 crores plus projects, where we will see a good improvement in the EBITDA.

items.statement: Preferential money used to purchase two major equipment: falling weight deflectometer and mobile bridge inspection unit.
items.quote: So yes, capital allocation, as you can see in our quarter 3 also, our preferential money proceeds have been used to purchase two major equipment. One is the falling weight deflectometer which is the second one now and a mobile bridge inspection unit is also a second one.

items.statement: There will be non-fund-based requirement; banks happy to assist.
items.quote: And secondly, the fund requirement, yes, there will be a fund requirement -- there will be a non-fund-based requirement. As and when we are being received projects, bank guarantees would be required and our banks -- we are in talks with our bankers, our present bankers, who are happy to assist us for the same.

items.statement: Expecting major orders from international market in FY26.
items.quote: Now we are establishing ourselves in the highway sector in the international -- in the global market, where Mozambique has been our first achievement and many such orders we are expecting in this FY '26 major orders from the international market.

items.statement: FY25-26 looks dominated by international market with good success rate expected.
items.quote: So, FY '25 -- FY '25-'26 looks to be dominated by the international market for us and we are expecting a good success rate in these projects.

items.statement: Plan to replicate highway success in railways, metros, airports, public health engineering, energy and power.
items.quote: So we are going to identify five or -- we have identified five or six sectors, namely the railways, metros, airports, public health engineering, energy and power. So wherein we plan to replicate our success that we have in the past 20 years in highways in these sectors as well.

items.statement: Elections caused delay in orders and revenue dip in Q3.
items.quote: The major reason for a dip in the quarter-to-quarter revenue was the elections that were there in the state. So we were expecting a few orders in the Q3 FY '25, which will now be pushed to the Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR0.1 per share announced.
items.quote: We are pleased to announce our interim dividend of INR0.1 per share, reflecting our commitment to delivering shareholder value.

items.statement: Awarded LOA for authority engineer with Maps Global Tech, contract value INR23.46 crores.
items.quote: We were recently awarded with an LOA for authority engineer in association with Maps Global Tech with a total contract value of INR23.46 crores from Maharashtra State Industrial Development Corporation.

items.statement: Secured INR2.2 crores consultancy contract with NHAI and another from MoRTH Karnataka.
items.quote: Further strengthening our presence, we secured of INR2.2 crores consultancy contract with NHAI and another from Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in Karnataka.

items.statement: Received notice to proceed for Garkhal Bridge project, contract value INR11.05 crores over 24 months.
items.quote: We have received a notice to proceed for consultancy services on the Garkhal Bridge project in Himachal Pradesh, where we will observe the construction of cantilever bridge. The contract value is INR11.05 crores, which will be executed over a period of 24 months.

items.statement: On track to achieve approximately 13% revenue growth in Q4 and EBITDA margins in the range of 25% plus for Q4 FY25 and going forward.
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our guidance of approximately 13% revenue growth in Q4 and EBITDA margins in the range of 25% plus for Q4 '25 and going forward, reaffirming the strength of our strategy and execution.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics margin profile will be lower than Metropolis for first 12 months, diluting margins temporarily; will take 2-3 years to reach Metropolis margin profile.
items.quote: While we anticipate Core revenue growth to be strong and margins of Core to move up fairly in year 1 of acquisition, the margin profile will be lo wer than Metropolis for the first 12 months and will dilute the margin temporarily. It will take up to 2 to 3 years to reach the margin -- Metropolis margin profile.

items.statement: Synergies expected to drive expansion in Core's margin profile from Q1 FY26 itself.
items.quote: Once Core is fully integrated into Metropolis systems and processes, we anticipate a fair number of operational efficiencies with synergies driving an expansion in margin profile of Core from Q1 FY '26 itself.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics acquisition expected to be EPS accretive from year 1 and ROI should be strong.
items.quote: However, it will be EPS accretive from year 1 and the ROI on the Core acquisition should be strong considering the above numbers mentioned.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics expected to contribute to revenue starting in March of this financial year.
items.quote: We aim to finalize the acquisition by the end of this month with Core expected to c ontribute to MHL's revenue starting in March of this financial year.

items.statement: Net impact of market-specific pricing strategy expected to deliver a positive 2% increase in overall revenues starting quarter 4.
items.quote: The net impact of t his strategy is expected to deliver a positive 2% increase in overall revenues starting quarter 4, setting the stage for sustainable growth and market leadership.

items.statement: Market-specific pricing adjustments: net result upside of about 2% coming from this quarter.
items.quote: So I mean, the net results of this would be upside of about 2%, which is coming in from this quarter.

items.statement: Early indicators in Q4 suggest a rebound in volumes as seen in H1.
items.quote: However, we consider this a temporary seasonal fluctuation, and early indicators in Q4 suggest a rebound in volumes as we saw in H1.

items.statement: Expect 8% to 10% upside in B2C segment over next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: So we should definitely get into aro und 8% to 10% upside in the next 2 to 3 years' time on the B2C segment.

items.statement: Lab expansion phase from FY25, FY26 will end with final lap in Q4; focus will shift to accelerated collection centers and gradual EBITDA and margin accretion in FY26.
items.quote: With our final lap of lab expansion in quarter 4, it will end our lab expansion phase from financial year '25, '26. The focus w ill be more on accelerated collection centers and allowing gradual EBITDA and margin accretion in the year '26.

items.statement: Expect margin expansion to continue as lab expansion ends and normal expansion of few labs a year from FY26.
items.quote: And from '25, '26, it will be just a normal lab expansion, which will be few labs a year, probably 5 or 6, but not more significant than that. And that will allow us, therefore, our margin expansion to continue.

items.statement: Actively pursuing additional inorganic growth opportunities with several potential targets under consideration, especially in northern markets.
items.quote: We are actively pursuing additional inorganic growth opportunities with several potential targets currently under consideration, especially in northern markets. We are optimistic about achieving early closure on these opportunities.

items.statement: In advanced stages of evaluating a few acquisitions that have built strong B2C brands in North Indian cities.
items.quote: We are in advanced stages of evaluating a few such acquisitions that have successfully built strong B2C brands in North Indian cities.

items.statement: Using approximately INR 135 crores of internal cash for Core Diagnostics acquisition, balance will be stock swap.
items.quote: We will be using approximately INR 135 crores of internal cash for this acquisition, and the balance will be a stock swap.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics transaction expected to close by February end; MSL March consolidated numbers should include Core Diagnostics.
items.quote: We will be closing the Core Diagnostics transaction by February end and MSL March consolidated numbers should include Core Diagnostics if all goes according to the time line planned.

items.statement: Aims to close year with margins in guided range of 20% to 22%.
items.quote: Talking a little about the future, we aim to close the year with margins to be in our guided range of 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Attempt to come as close as possible to 30% growth in constant currency for the year.
items.quote: However, as you may have noticed, we have in subsequent quarters done a Q-o-Q growth of 27% and 28% and intend to do a similar if not better number in Q4, and our attempt will be to come as close as possible to the 30% growth number in constant currency that we had set for ourselves.

items.statement: Expects Q4 growth of about 27%-28% quarter-over-quarter.
items.quote: But the attempt will be to touch that 30% and as of now, it looks to be about 27%-28%.

items.statement: Long-term growth target of at least 1 to 1.5x market.
items.quote: We have said that we will be at least 1 to 1.5x market, which is what we have set as a long-term growth target.

items.statement: Would be disappointed if not moving into double-digit organic growth next year.
items.quote: We would be disappointed if we don't move into double-digit organic growth next year.

items.statement: Utilization target to improve to 78% to 80%.
items.quote: We must get the utilization numbers up and this is a lever available to us, and we are working to get these back to the 78% to 80% number that we earlier used to have.

items.statement: Investments in GenAI running at about US $3.5 million up to nine-month period.
items.quote: Investments into GenAI that would be number 1. It's about US $1.5 million for the first 6 months and now it's running at about US $3.5 million up to the nine-month period.

items.statement: Wage impact for senior profile in Q3 was about 0.9%.
items.quote: This quarter, we have for the senior profile, so it will be about 0.9%.

items.statement: Arttha banking license sales have positive impact on margin.
items.quote: The third is Arttha banking. What we have seen is it has got a very positive impact on margin because the moment a license is sold, almost all of it is to the bottom line.

items.statement: Bill rates on GenAI services are superior to traditional services.
items.quote: The bill rates on GenAI services is superior to even our traditional, but our PDES, Analytics, and related Digital services.

items.statement: Expects momentum in new logos to continue into Q4 and FY26.
items.quote: We had seven new logos cutting across various geos and verticals last quarter, and we expect this momentum to continue into Q4 and into FY 26.

items.statement: EduTech may stay in slow lane this year.
items.quote: Deborah Quazzo of GSV Ventures recently said that the EduTech may stay in the slow lane this year as companies grapple with artificial intelligence.

items.statement: Retail CPG vertical showed 3% to 4% quarter-on-quarter growth and expects it to continue.
items.quote: As you see for last quarter, we did have the retail CPG vertical showing pretty good growth of around 3% to 4% quarter-on-quarter, and we expect this to continue.

items.statement: Sees more propensity to spend in banking and financial services.
items.quote: So if you look at BFSI, I would say that the banking and financial services is an area that we are seeing more of a propensity to spend.

items.statement: About 15 GenAI projects in PoC stage, expected to convert to orders next fiscal.
items.quote: Apart from the projects we have already delivered in these few months, we have about fifteen projects in a proof-of-concept(PoC) stage, which will lead to significant orders and projects in the next fiscal.

items.statement: Expects 80% of GenAI PoCs to convert into orders.
items.quote: If you just take GenAI, we've reached a point where we are executing maybe about upwards of 10 or 15 proofs of concept. Maybe 80% of those will get converted into orders.

items.statement: Holding 15% revenue guidance for equipment business.
items.quote: And as mentioned earlier, we stand by our growth trajectory, what we have done in the past as well, and we are holding on to the 15% revenue guidance, which we gave earlier for equipment business.

items.statement: Chile project delayed by 6-8 months, expected completion in later part of FY26.
items.quote: You see we had earlier estimated the commercialization of the project by Q2 of FY '26, which is delayed by about 6 to 8 months, and we expect that the same shall be completed in the later part of FY '26.

items.statement: Order book of INR1,258 crores as of Dec 31, 2024, with executable orders within 1 year at INR758 crores.
items.quote: We have an order book of INR1,258 crores as 31st December '24, out of which executable orders within 1 year stands at INR758 crores.

items.statement: Blended gross margins for 9M FY25 at 57% vs 58% last year.
items.quote: The blended gross margins of the group for the 9 months ended December '24 is 57% vis-a-vis 58% during the same period last year.

items.statement: Robust demand for gold and copper expected to continue.
items.quote: A significant portion of our products, as you know, are customized for the gold and copper mines, and we believe robust demands for both the metals continue to prevail.

items.statement: DynaPrime liners sold at a premium over steel liners.
items.quote: And as far as the pricing is concerned, Harsh, we sell our DynaPrime liners at a premium over the steel liners.

items.statement: Logistics challenges like increased freight costs and container shortages persist.
items.quote: See, from a logistics point of view, increased freight costs, shortage of containers, congestion at ports and dependence on major shipping hubs still pose a serious challenge to the overall industry and is impacting the efficiency and reliability of supply chains for businesses.

items.statement: Ore grade decline increases consumption of consumables and services.
items.quote: So with higher ore quantity consumption, definitely, the consumables and the solutions which we give definitely increases by each ore grade actually.

items.statement: NMDC order execution started, with some portion booked in FY26 and small spillover to FY27.
items.quote: Some portion will be booked in FY '26 and a small portion may also spill over to FY '27.

items.statement: U.S. tariff impact uncertain, but manufacturing flexibility allows supply from multiple countries.
items.quote: But as you said, that depending on how the U.S. government reacts to tariffs across different jurisdictions, we are unable to assess the impact of that at this current time.

items.statement: FY26 guidance to be provided in Q4 earnings call.
items.quote: See, as I told earlier, we are firming our budgets for FY '26. And once that is firmed up in the Q4 earnings call, I'll give you the guidance for the future years.

items.statement: No significant cost overrun expected from Chile project delay.
items.quote: We don't expect any significant cost overrun at this juncture.

items.statement: Equipment business decline due to delays, but order book intact and expected to flow.
items.quote: You see, like I mentioned earlier, we are -- the decline what you are seeing is a very marginal decline. The percentage looks big, but the decline is not much. And the order book is intact, and we expect that all the orders should flow in.

items.statement: FY26 services revenue growth can ramp back up to 15% plus.
items.quote: This will, though ensure that FY '26 services revenue growth can ramp back up to 15% plus.

items.statement: Cash Logistics business can grow between 10% to 13% in the midterm.
items.quote: The Cash Logistics business can grow between 10% to 13% in the midterm.

items.statement: MS and Tech business should grow upwards of 15%.
items.quote: Our MS and Tech business should grow upwards of 15%, and our AIoT RMS business should compound at 15% to 20% growth rates over the medium term.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth opportunity is 13% to 15% CAGR.
items.quote: You combine these 3 on organic basis, our revenue growth opportunity is at 13% to 15% CAGR.

items.statement: CAPEX spend INR 50 crores in 9 months; expect INR 150 crores to INR 200 crore for full year.
items.quote: Our CAPEX spend has been INR 50 crores in 9 months of the year and we expect this to be INR 150 crores to INR 200 crore for the full year.

items.statement: Order book execution: 15% at H1, 30% at Q3, target 60% by Q4.
items.quote: We had completed 15% of this order book at end of H1, have ramped it up with 30% completion at the end of Q3 and our focus remains on getting 60% of this order book live by Q4.

items.statement: Over INR 700 crores of order wins this year, majority recurring services revenue.
items.quote: In our Managed Services and Technology business, we are continuing with a good order wins momentum and have over INR 700 crores of wins this year, majority being recurring services revenue in nature.

items.statement: PAT margin expanded by 140 basis points to 16%.
items.quote: Our PAT grew by 7% year-on-year to INR 93.2 crores. PAT margin has expanded by 140 basis points to 16%.

items.statement: Cash Logistics EBIT margin robust at 25.6%.
items.quote: Segment-wise, the Cash Logistic business with INR 404 crores recorded an 8% year-on-year revenue growth, while the EBIT grew by 6% to INR 103 crores, delivering a robust 25.6% margin.

items.statement: MS and Tech EBIT margin 17.9%.
items.quote: Our Managed Services and Technology Solution business revenue at INR 210 crores saw a decline of around 10% primarily due to lower banking automation revenue. Despite this, the business achieved an EBIT of INR 38 crores and the margin of 17.9%.

items.statement: Potential increase in ATM interchange rates would drive better economics and expand ATM TAM.
items.quote: The banking outsourcing opportunity is poised to grow with a potential increase in ATM interchange rates, which would drive better economics for the entire sector and also lead to an expansion in the ATM TAM.

items.statement: Highest ever cash volume handled in Q3 with 6% Y-o-Y growth and 10% business point addition.
items.quote: We have recorded our highest ever cash volume handled in Q3 with a 6% Y-o-Y growth and an overall business point addition of 10% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Recurring revenue should be almost 85% of MS and Tech segment in FY26.
items.quote: FY '26, we hope that recurring revenue should be almost 85% of this business segment.

items.statement: Risk cost reduced from 5% to 5.1% of revenues in FY24 to about 4% in H1 this year.
items.quote: So, what used to be about 5% to 5.1% of revenues FY'24 has reduced to about 4% in H1 of this year.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR 3.25 per share.
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that our Board has declared an interim dividend of INR 3.25 per share.

items.statement: May produce around 10,000 tons of additional sugar due to switching from syrup to B-heavy molasses.
items.quote: Due to this, definitely I would imagine anything around 10,000 tons of additional sugar produce. Definitely, I would imagine anything between 10,000 tons of additional sugar produce ho jani chahiye.

items.statement: Expects own cane crop to be 5-8% lower than last year.
items.quote: We expect, for us the cane crop to be probably anything between 5% to 8% lower than last year, which could be a little bit better than our peers, but there will be a reduction for sure.

items.statement: Expects 60-70% of area to be new varieties by next year, hoping for 100% replacement in plant cane.
items.quote: we do expect 60%-70% area hamara new varietys me to aa jaanaa chaahiye if not more by next year we hope 100% replacement ho jana chahiye plant cane me

items.statement: Sugar prices increased by INR1-1.50/kg after export policy; refined sugar now INR41.75-42, sulphitation INR41-41.25.
items.quote: So, after export policy around Rs. 1-1.50/kg was increase in sugar prices. So, we hope that prices should remain maintained going forward.

items.statement: May not divert sugarcane into syrup for next year if sugar and ethanol prices remain as is.
items.quote: I don't think we will be looking to divert sugarcane into syrup for next year if the sugar prices and everything remains as is where it is.

items.statement: Discontinued diverting sugarcane into ethanol; better off paying penalty and making B-heavy or C molasses.
items.quote: we have, in fact, discontinued the diverting any more sugarcane into ethanol. We are better off by paying the penalty and not diverting cane into ethanol and may be making B-heavy or C Molasses.

items.statement: Country Liquor business has 15-20% margin after duty; aims to grow and gain market share.
items.quote: If you take the duty element out and if you look at the raw material price, the levy molasses price, then there is some margin, maybe a 15%, 20% margin to be enjoyed in this business.

items.statement: Grain-based distillery to start operations in end April or early May after season.
items.quote: We should start its operation somewhere in end April, early

items.statement: Recovery is continuously improving for plant cane; hopes to reduce gap from first half.
items.quote: Recovery is continuously improving now for plant cane that the recoveries are continuing to go up. So we do hope that we will be able to reduce the gap that we had for the first half.

items.statement: Expects better performance in Q4 due to improving recovery and uptrend in sugar prices.
items.quote: We definitely believe so, Rajesh.

items.statement: Most capex cycle over in Sugar segment; small capex for C molasses capability and Country Liquor bottling capacity augmentation.
items.quote: most of our capex cycle seems to be over in the Sugar segment. The only difference is, as I was mentioning before, this year, we could not divert some of our capacity into C molasses. So some capex would probably go in small amounts into making us giving us the ability to make C molasses in all our units.

items.statement: No buyback planned; focusing on conservative capital management.
items.quote: No, I don't think we're looking at any buyback right now, Rajesh Ji, with the way this current year behaved. I think it is more prudent for us right now to be a little bit more conservative with capital.

items.statement: Sugarcane SAP fixed at INR370 per quintal, no linkage to recovery.
items.quote: So we continue to account for sugarcane prices at INR370, which was the last year SAP price for UP.

items.statement: Export quota of 12,489 tons sold due to better domestic prices.
items.quote: Yes, it's 12,489 tons.

items.statement: Levy molasses available at INR1,500 per ton, lower than own molasses realization of INR11,000 per ton.
items.quote: We will be able to buy levy molasses at the government sort of advised price of about INR150, a quintal or INR1,500 a ton.

items.statement: One PPA in a small unit expires next year; private power prices could be INR4.5-5 per unit.
items.quote: As of now, yes, I think one of our PPAs in a small unit is supposed to get over next year.

items.statement: Data production headcount may shrink more than 10% in the coming year due to GenAI.
items.quote: So potentially, there can be more than 10% shrinkage in the data production team size than what we saw in the previous year in the coming year.

items.statement: Company expects value growth from international segment, improving overall growth rate.

items.quote: We are on the verge of getting recombinant Asparaginase cleared by the office of DCGI. It should h appen in the next 6 months’ time because we have completed most of the

items.statement: Semaglutide to be vertically integrated, targeting first wave of launches in India.
items.quote: I am very confident that we will be in the first wave of semaglutide launches in India and the product will be vertically integrated.

items.statement: Cardio-diabetos restructuring impacted sales, improvement expected from Q4.
items.quote: I think we should start seeing some improvement from fourth quarter onwards. So it may not be fully getting normalized, but it should improve from what we have seen this current quarter.

items.statement: Acute segment growth muted, recovery expected next year.
items.quote: So I think acute this year has been a bit weaker. Our view is that we should see some pickup going forward next year

items.statement: Net debt INR 600 crores, targeting debt-free by Mar'26 from internal cash flows.
items.quote: So outside of any sort of M&A, we think that probably within the next couple of quarters, there should be enough free cash flow generation to pare down debt in next two to three quarters max.

items.statement: Sanand at ~60% utilization, Kadu near break-even, Mehsana injectables 12-18 months to optimal.
items.quote: is now closer to about 60 odd percent utilisation. Oncology is still in early stages because we are still ramping up -- the filings are still coming through. In terms of Kadu, that is now getting closer to break even

items.statement: R&D spend to be maintained at 4-5% of sales.
items.quote: So our R&D spend is around 4 %-5%. And I think even going forward that is what we look at.

items.statement: European CDMO contract worth EUR 200 million; commercial supply starts 2027 until 2032.
items.quote: The total agreement value is approximately EUR200 million over the length of the contract. This includes an upfront payment of EUR100 million. The approvals and product dossiers and manufacturing site approvals is expected by the end of 2026, hence the commercial supply will commence from 2027 and will continue until 2032.

items.statement: Capex of INR 32 crores over next 2 quarters for R&D upgrade.
items.quote: To further bolster our R&D capabilities, we will incur a capex of INR 32 crores over the next 2 quarters to improve and upgrade our R&D capabilities.

items.statement: Capex of INR 175-200 crores annually for next 2 years to commission new plants.
items.quote: And over the next 2 years, we will likely incur capex to commission new plants and production lines between INR 175 crores to INR200 crores annually.

items.statement: CDMO EBITDA margins to remain in current range.
items.quote: But I would still say that our overall EBITDA margins for the CDMO business should remain in the ZIP code we operate today.

items.statement: CDMO volume growth turned positive in Q3 vs Q2; Q4 looks good.
items.quote: So quarter 2, which had a sizable volume decline, we are seeing some green shoots, and we have already turned positive in Q3 compared to Q2. Q4 also looks good.

items.statement: Business should see similar revenue and EBITDA as past 3 quarters.
items.quote: So we sort of see that as we have guided earlier that for this period and the way we are guiding is that the business should see similar revenue and similar EBITDA.

items.statement: API business breakeven expected in 1 to 2 years.
items.quote: So we are progressing well. I think this is in a ZIP code of 1 to 2 years when we'll be in a breakeven.

items.statement: Focus on value products like small volume parenterals, large volume parenterals, bi-layered tablets, dry injectables.
items.quote: And if you really recollect what I said, the new dosage forms that we are adding, whether it is small volume parenterals, large volume parenterals, bi-layered tablets, dry injectables, the whole focus, if you really carefully think through is to drive value products rather than volume-based products.

items.statement: Cephalosporin API prices dropped 20-30%, leading to reduced sales.
items.quote: The challenge is not driving sales. You'll have to understand that number one is the market wherein the overall oral cephalosporin prices, which were almost 90% of our revenues, they dropped by 20% to 30%.

items.statement: European contract upfront payment of EUR 100 million received in NOSTRO account.
items.quote: So the money has been transferred from overseas, and we are still to receive it in our account. So it's in the NOSTRO account of the bank. So once we receive it, it will be an advance received against that contract.

items.statement: CDMO volume growth of 1.6% on trailing 12-month basis, industry flat.
items.quote: If I talk about complete 2024 to 2023 levels, on a trialling 12 month basis we have grown our volumes by 1.6%, where the industry was largely flat, right?

items.statement: Unosource and Akumentis EBITDA margins at 18-20%.
items.quote: But largely, the EBITDA margins for Unosource and Akumentis remain in 18% to 20% bracket.

items.statement: European contract and Triple Hair to contribute to P&L from 2027.
items.quote: So both the European contract as well as Triple Hair will kickstart contribution to the P&L in 2027.

items.statement: CDMO volume growth expected 4-5%.
items.quote: Yes. So 4% to 5% certainly, right.

items.statement: API capacity utilization at 30-odd percent.
items.quote: And on the API side, we are largely at a 30-odd percent utilization.

items.statement: Expects no exceptional items in coming quarters, including immediate quarter.
items.quote: we can probably give you a bit of guidance that we will probably not be having these exceptional items in the coming quarters, probably in the immediate quarter, we can expect none of these exceptional items to be repeating in the continued operations.

items.statement: Fuel sensor expected to stabilize in 18-24 months and deliver revenues equal to current overall telematics revenues.
items.quote: we have been able to unlock a category which basically will stabilize in the course of the next18-24 months, and we will be able to give rise to a new vertical which will deliver revenues equivalent to the current overall telematics revenues.

items.statement: Fuel sensor expected to start contributing materially to growth businesses in six to nine months.
items.quote: joining the party is basically now the fuel sensor model, where you will see probably in six to nine months down the line, you would see fuel sensor also starting to make material moves in the growth businesses, providing the much-needed lift in the revenues from the overall growth businesses.

items.statement: Fuel sensor expected to deliver 70% to 80% contribution margin on stabilized unit economics.
items.quote: And at the same time, we will be able to deliver a contribution margin profile of 70 % to 80% on the on the stabilized unit-economics perspective, right?

items.statement: Fuel sensor blended realization is about INR10,500 to INR11,000.
items.quote: So today in the market, we start selling the fuel sensor anywhere in the range of blended realization for us is roughly about INR10,500 to INR11,000 from the fuel sensor.

items.statement: Fuel sensor price was reduced from INR20,000 to INR15,000 and now to INR10,000 plus.
items.quote: We used to sell a fuel sensor at INR20,000 when we launched. We were able to bring some volumes and bring it down to INR15,000.

items.statement: PPI economics expected to improve by 15% to 20%.
items.quote: But the economics will probably not improve 25% to 30%, probably will improve in the range of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Load marketplace business expected to break even by December 25 to March 26.
items.quote: And we expect that business, we were expecting that business to break even probably by end of this year, as in December 25 to March 26, broadly.

items.statement: Load marketplace and vehicle finance businesses are growing close to doubling year-on-year.
items.quote: Both these businesses are probably close to doubling on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Program management fee is open-ended with no sunset date currently.
items.quote: As it currently stands out, it's an open -ended date given out saying that this is the MDR and this will remain as we keep moving forward because the minimum cost which any company incurs is a bare minimum cost in terms of running the entire issuance stack and that number for different banks and different players is a number where they just break even at that 1% scale because of the kind of market

items.statement: Tolling market share reached close to 43% by December.
items.quote: By December, and we already reached close to what 43%.

items.statement: Employee cost reduction included one-time leave encashment and gratuity reversals of INR1.5 crores to INR1.7 crores.
items.quote: I think the third point, just a one time, is that in December, some of our leave lapses, etc. happen. So, there are some reversals in leave encashment and gratuity. So, that is to the extent of INR1.5 crores to INR1.7 crores.

items.statement: Company continues to move towards variabilization of workforce.
items.quote: So, Gaurav, I think two things. One, as you have consistently said, we continue to move more towards the variabilization of the workforce , so that you would see that the other expenses has gone up.

items.statement: Expects current growth to continue in new segments.
items.quote: See, I can't like, I mean, we as we discussed last call, like we as a philosophy have taken not to provide guidance, b ut yes you can continue to expect the current growth coming through.

items.statement: Fuel vertical positioned for 20-25% YoY growth.
items.quote: we have been able to comfortably position a growth rate of 20%, 25% year-on-year in that vertical.

items.statement: Classified revenue projected max INR200 crores in 5-6 years.
items.quote: And the revenue projection of that vertical probably will be max INR200 crores in probably 5 -6 years down the line on an annualized revenue basis.

items.statement: Vehicle finance origination doubling every six months.
items.quote: That's a business vertical, which is growing, probably every six months it's doubling .

items.statement: Expects better disbursements as partners' measured approach eases.
items.quote: As we see into this quarter that measure d approach slowly is going away. So, we expect to see better disbursements, b ut yes Q3 was definitely measured by our partners.

items.statement: Brokerage business needs 6-8 quarters for understanding.
items.quote: But by when and how much, I think we need to wait for at least six to eight quarters to get some understanding in that business.

items.statement: Fuel sensor at INR10-11k profitable on first sale.
items.quote: Yes, at between INR10 to INR11,000, we will be in money in the first sale.

items.statement: May reduce fuel sensor price further at higher scale.
items.quote: Yes, I mean, because right now, we are only talking numbers like mere thousands. And as soon as we hit 10,000s, right, we can definitely get more.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost per vertical INR1300-1400 per truck.
items.quote: Like, the cost of acquisition of a customer on any one of the verticals for at a truck level, typically hovers in the range of like, INR1300, INR1400, like kind of number, right?

items.statement: Telematics growth trending as before.
items.quote: I think at this point in time, what you can infer is that broadly the growth is trending, how it was trending before in terms of telematics devices. Broadly, we are in the same course.

items.statement: Renewal rates early 70s first year, early 80s to late 80s thereafter.
items.quote: We typically have that the first year annual rate typically is roughly in the range of like early 70s in terms of annual rate. After that, typically, the renewal rates are in the early 80s to late 80s on a continual basis.

items.statement: Fuel sensor revenue model: upfront first year, then annual subscription.
items.quote: Yes, it's again – yes, it's the same model we charge upfront for the first year because that includes the device cost. And after that it's annual recurring subscription which again comes for annual and it's an annuity income again, nature of revenue again will be similar as the GPS revenue.

items.statement: Fuel vertical faces headwinds from OMC structure and cash usage.
items.quote: So Indian market structure, why is it different from those markets is that point number one, we have a oil marketing company structure, where there are largely four oil marketing companies, there's only one private and three government owned, right? So the real intensity to fight, for customers in terms of loyalty, etc., isn't that high, that's point number one.

items.statement: No material update on GNSS; backend work ongoing.
items.quote: So back end work is the toll charge of work, which will calculate the distance, which will map the toll plazas, do the lat longs, and like, send on a real time basis really how much money to be deducted, etc. So that work is on a priority happening , but materially, we don't have any updates on that.

items.statement: IMACID expansion CAPEX is $173 million.
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: $173 million.

items.statement: Current year CAPEX invested around Rs. 357 crore, of which TAN is around Rs. 250 crore.
items.quote: Anand Agarwal: Current year, we have actually invested around Rs. 357 crore of CAPEX, out of which, TAN is around Rs. 250 crore.

items.statement: TAN business will have positive contribution in FY27.
items.quote: Anand Agarwal: Yes, in FY '27 we will definitely have positive contribution. Currently we are not being too aggressive on our estimates, but hope it will get ramped up very soon.

items.statement: TAN commercial production date is January 26.
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: Yes, I will just make this point . January 26 is the date of commercial production delivery. That means it meets all parameters in terms of capacity , in terms of efficiency, in terms of quality. The trial will begin before January 26.

items.statement: Energy efficiency saving of 3% from Rs. 5,000 per Gcal.
items.quote: Abhay Baijal: See, I will just give you , this is a rough computation. 3% saving from Rs. 5,000 per Gcal.
