items.statement: Greenfield project at Atali, Gujarat for CDMO/CMO and Intermediate manufacturing progressing with minor delays; Phase-1 commissioning expected in Q1 with ramp up towards end of FY26.
items.quote: The greenfield project of Atali, Gujarat for CDMO/CMO and Intermediate manufacturing is progressing with minor delays, and we expect Phase-1 of this Atali to be commissioned in Q1 with a ramp up expected towards the end of FY26.

items.statement: Phase-1 will have about 450 KL reactor capacity.
items.quote: The Phase-1 will have about 450 KL reactor capacity, and has been specially designed to facilitate pilot to commercial scale up in the same block.

items.statement: Signed up with another captive solar energy project of nine megawatt DC for Gujarat units; likely to get commissioned in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Moreover, we have signed up with another captive solar energy project of nine megawatt DC for our units in Gujarat. The second project is likely to get commission in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Starting two solid multi fuel boilers capable of using bio briquettes at two Maharashtra plants in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Lastly, we will be starting to solid multi fuel boilers capable of using bio briquettes as possible fuel. At two of our plants in Maharashtra in Q4 FY25 in the current running quarters.

items.statement: Temporary shutdown of Vapi plant in January due to pollution control board notice; restarted in about two weeks; may push some CDMO/CMO sales from Q4 by one quarter.
items.quote: Let me also oppress you about the temporary shutdown of our Vapi plan t in first week of January. The unit had stopped operation because of the notice from the State Pollution Control Board, and the necessary steps were taken and unit was successfully restarted in about two weeks.

items.statement: Confident of delivering significant growth in CDMO business in medium to long term.
items.quote: Even our strong manufacturing capability and global tailwind in CDMO business, we are confident of delivering signific ant growth in medium to long term.

items.statement: Spot market prices for Xanthine declined by over $1 per kg; competition from China continues to be a headwind.
items.quote: The competition from China continues to be a headwind. In fact, the prices for the spot market have further declined by over $1 per kg .

items.statement: Xanthine derivative recorded highest ever quarterly volume sales and contributed 44% of turnover in Q3.
items.quote: The Xanthine derivative recorded highest ever quarterly volume sales and it contributed to 44% of the turnover in Q3.

items.statement: API and Intermediate business delivered best quarterly revenue performance and contributed 42% of turnover in Q3.
items.quote: The API and Intermediate business delivered the best quarterly revenue performance and contributed to 42% of the turnover in Q3.

items.statement: CDMO/CMO segment contributed 13% of turnover in Q3; working with 21 customers, 56 active projects of which 28 commercial.
items.quote: The third business segment CDMO/CMO has contributed 13% of the turnover in this quarter. We are presently working with 21 customers adding two customers in this quarter.

items.statement: CDMO sales for current year will exceed last year's number of 170 crores.
items.quote: So, that will happen in the current quarter, and we hope that next year, we will be able to do significantly better sales of CDMO products.

items.statement: Xanthine capacity expansion: first phase in first half, second phase in second half of next financial year, reaching 9000 metric tonne capacity; FY27 achieve 90% utilization.
items.quote: In the first half we will be able to do first phase of the Xanthine, and the second phase will happen in the second half of next financial year. Whereby we will reach this 9000 metric tonne capacity for Xanthine.

items.statement: CDMO/CMO margin profile is little bit higher than API intermediate, but not very different, about 5% point difference.
items.quote: And the profit margin profile of API intermediate , CDMO/CMO of course CDMO/CMO being little bit higher, but not very, very different 5% point difference between both, since we are doing multi stages in CDMO/CMO, as well as API intermediate so, that's how these percentage differences may not mean too much .

items.statement: Sizable order book in CDMO/CMO segment already for next financial year.
items.quote: Yes, we are in the process of making budget, and once we form it up and once we have the next concall with the complete set of PPCR, one by we will be able to but we see good, significant growth possibilities and good traction in this business segment, and we have also sizable order book on this business segment already for next financial year.

items.statement: Electrical business expected to grow 18-20% top line and 17-20% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Electrical business, we can expect a trajectory of 18% to 20% on the top line and EBITDA of 17% to 20% that band.

items.statement: Aluminium die casting revenues to remain flat for next couple of years.
items.quote: So I can say that you can expec t a flattish revenues in the next couple of years for alumin ium die casting

items.statement: Aluminium die casting EBITDA targeted to reach 15-17% after achieving single digit.
items.quote: In the next couple of years, we'll try to get our EBITDAs first to a single digit, then about 15% to 17% EBITDA, we will try to get on the die casting business.

items.statement: Alucast aims to achieve EBITDA breakeven in next one or two quarters.
items.quote: Our goal is to achieve breakeven at EBITDA level marking a critical milestone in our turnaround strategy in the next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Adding new SMT lines at Rishabh India and Lumel Poland by end of financial year.
items.quote: On capex front, we are further expanding our electronics manufacturing capacity by adding the state-of-the-art new SMT, Surface Mount Technology lines both at Rishabh, India and Lumel S.A. Poland by end of this financial year, which will support growth in our electronics products, EMS and solar production.

items.statement: Nashik facility construction on track, to double capacity, completion before end of next financial year.
items.period: before end of next financial year
items.quote: The construction work of our Nashik facility is shaping up very well and on time. This new 6-storeyed buildings, two of them will double our capacity across all core segments in the electronics and instrumentation business. This is expected to be completed before end of next financial year.

items.statement: Aluminium die casting share reduced from 40% to 35-36% as conscious shift away from automotive.
items.quote: So if you look at our whole -- in the group also, portfolio, we used to be close to 40% aluminium die casting business, which has dropped to about 35%, 36%. So that's a shift. That's a conscious shift, which we have made.

items.statement: Renegotiated contracts with automotive customers to get price increases this year and next.
items.quote: So effectively, with all the automotive customers with all this price increase, we have been effectively able to get some price increase in this year and also continuing in the next year.

items.statement: Revising pricing strategy in India to pass on rising commodity prices like copper and metals.
items.quote: And also in India, also, we are trying to revise our pricing strategy and pass on some of the commodity prices, which are increasing like copper and other things increase, which are used in current transformers and metal prices went up which are used in CTs and analog panel meters and all those -- some of the electromechanical products who we are trying to pass on those to the customers also throu

items.statement: Export business for electrical automation expected to increase with big project pipeline.
items.quote: This quarter from Rishabh exports, there is an uptrend. So that has some effect, I would say and the next quarter also, we are expecting the trend to be going. And we are also working on a big project pipeline from many customers in the export market, where we have to modify some of our products and develop some products for them.

items.statement: Electronics business growth of 17-20% sustainable with EBITDA 17-20%.
items.quote: And if we have to offset that, otherwise, we have this steady growth of anywhere between the 17% to 20% for electronics and with the EBITDA of anywhere between 17% to 20% based on different entities we have. That's very much sustainable, and our track record also shows that, and we have absolutely no doubts on that.

items.statement: European automotive industry turbulent; worst may be behind but geopolitical risks persist.
items.quote: The automotive industry in Europe is very turbulent with whatever we see now, and I can see for the next few quarters in one or two quarters, we should be good, sustainable and we can say worst is over. So that's what I strongly feel and want to believe on that. But if the things are like now with the Trump in place, so many different things are coming on a daily basis.

items.statement: R&D investment at 2% of revenues; target 10% incremental revenue from new products.
items.quote: We have about 15 products in pipeline to be added by financial year '26. We target to achieve about 10% incremental revenue from the new products launched in the last 2 years. We also actively invest about 2% of our revenues in our R&D facilities to innovate design and develop new products in-house.

items.statement: ESOP expenses of INR19 million expected in FY25.
items.quote: The ESOP expenses for 9 month FY '25 stood at INR96 million, and we expect another INR19 million to be booked in FY '25.

items.statement: Net debt-free with cash of INR776 million as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: On the consolidated level, we remain ne t debt-free with a strong balance sheet. Net cash and cash equivalents as on 31st December 2024 stand at INR776 million. The company remained net debt free as on 31st December 2024

items.statement: Full-year effective tax rate expected to bounce back to 18-19% by March 2025.
items.quote: We, however, believe that for the full year, it will bounce back to 18 to 19-odd percentage by March 2025.

items.statement: Adjusted quarterly margin is closer to 22% after discounting one-time expenses.
items.quote: If we adjust for the one-time adjustments and considering that during the last one year, we have gotten the benefits of the integration of the past acquisitions, we are heading in the right direction and on a quarterly basis, we are somewhere closer to 22%-odd as such once we discount the one-time aberration which we saw.

items.statement: One-time expenses in Q3 were approximately INR 1.822 crore, impacting margin by 1.2% for the quarter and 30 bps for 9 months.
items.quote: One-time quantum of spend will be in the range of roughly around 1.822 CR during the quarter, which is roughly around 1.2% for the quarter and approximately 30 odd bps for the 9 months.

items.statement: One-time expenses caused about 1.5% dilution in quarterly margin; excluding them, impact is 20 bps for 9 months and 1.3-1.4% for the quarter.
items.quote: The onetime expenses basically contributed to roughly around 1.5% dilution in the quarterly margin. In case if you were to remove that, it will have an impact of roughly around 20 bps for the 9-month period and approximately 1.3, 1.4% for the quarter.

items.statement: Contract liability as of December 31st was INR 227 crores.
items.quote: The contract liability is about 227 crores as of December 31st, and that continues to be healthy from an overall revenue growth perspective.

items.statement: Headcount as of December 31st was 6,250, with net increase mainly from government business contracts.
items.quote: And our head count ending December 31st is 6,250. Almost all of any net increase in the head count compared to March is only on account of the new contracts in the government business which are typically headcount-driven contracts.

items.statement: Medical inflation in portfolio has been sub 5% for the nine-month period.
items.quote: But from a loss ratio perspective, our average inflation or our medical inflation that we deliver in our portfolio has always been sub 5%. Even for the nine-month period, it is sub 5% in terms of an increase in average claims size.

items.statement: Network delivered over INR 700 crores in savings to insurance companies.
items.quote: Our network continues to deliver significant savings of over 700 crores delivered to insurance companies through pushing them into our cashless network.

items.statement: Fraud prevention savings to insurers increased by 2.5x year-on-year.
items.quote: We have delivered a 2.5x growth year-on-year on the value of savings delivered to insurance companies through fraud prevention.

items.statement: Raksha Prime enabled over 65,000 patients to avoid discharge waiting; crossed 10,000 discharges in December.
items.quote: Our Raksha Prime program enabled over 65,000 patients till December to walk out of the hospitals without waiting for discharge formalities. And this is powered by our proprietary AI technology for predicting out-of-pocket expenses. In fact, in the month of December, we crossed the milestone of 10,000 discharges a month, and it's improving month-on-month.

items.statement: Retention of Group accounts improved to 95% including acquisitions.
items.quote: Including all of our acquisitions on the combined base, we have improved our retention of Group accounts to 95%.

items.statement: Premium under management grew 16.6% year-on-year to INR 15,829 crores.
items.quote: Premium under management was 15,829 crores as on 31st of December. And as you will appreciate, this is a growth of 16.6% year-on-year on a base adjusted for premiums contributed by the acquired companies.

items.statement: Group premium under management grew about 14.7-15% year-on-year to INR 13,779 crores.
items.quote: This 16.5 odd percent growth when we share with you between Group and Retail PUMs or Premiums Under Management, you will appreciate that, the Group premium grew and was at 13,779 crores, which is a growth of about 14.7-15% year-on-year.

items.statement: Retail premium under management grew 31% year-on-year to INR 2,050 crores.
items.quote: And of course, as you have seen quarter-on-quarter, we continue to demonstrate improvements with a 31% year-on-year growth on the retail PUM, which is now touching 2,050 crores.

items.statement: Market share in health insurance premium administered increased to 19.8% from 19.2%.
items.quote: We are up from 19.2% as of December 23 market share to 19.8%, which is a 60 bps increase in the market share numbers for us.

items.statement: Operating revenue grew 40.2% year-on-year to INR 534.4 crore for 9 months.
items.quote: The revenue from contracts with customers excluding other income, which we call as operating revenue, was 534.4 crore, a growth of 40.2% again over the same period last year.

items.statement: Expansion at Athivaram Phase-2 and Kichha Line-3 to complete in Q1 FY26, adding 40,000 metric tons capacity.
items.quote: Once completed sometime in Q1 FY26, this expansion will add about 40,000 more metric tons to the installed capacity, bringing our total installed capacity to 200,000 metric tons per annum adjusted to about 80%-85% as utilizable capacity.

items.statement: Total order book stands at Rs. 1,305 crores.
items.quote: As of today, our total order book stands at Rs. 1,305 crores, which reflects a very strong pipeline and sustained demand.

items.statement: Order book to be executed in next 8-9 months.
items.quote: So, I think the Rs. 1,300 crores we have to finish in next 8-9 months.

items.statement: Expect to hold and increase margins going forward.
items.quote: A competitive environment is there, but certainly we will be able to hold and increase our margins going forward.

items.statement: See very good export opportunity, focusing on Western countries and neighboring countries.
items.quote: So, we see a very good opportunity and we feel that we are now in a good position to exploit it.

items.statement: Concentrating on renewable and new age sectors like semiconductors, which require larger buildings.
items.quote: So, the bigger orders are coming from this renewable line. Our normal orders of warehousing and from the manufacturing industry are continuing, but these renewable sectors and these new age sector like semiconductors and all, they require very large building.

items.statement: Competition is severe in large projects, but company's history and relationships help.
items.quote: So, competition is there. There is no doubt that competition is very severe, but I think the history that we have built up and the ability that we have shown in the past and the relationships we have built up.

items.statement: Gujarat plant planned to start after monsoon this year, depending on order intake.
items.quote: Depending on the order intake, if the order intake carries on as it is today and the pipeline looks good, our plan is to start it after the monsoon this year to go forward to the Gujarat plant

items.statement: Tied up with 2-3 companies for outsourcing production facilities.
items.quote: So, we have tied up with 2-3 of them to give us the production facilities of their which are world class to work according to our system.

items.statement: Expect to continue growing at the pace demonstrated.
items.quote: We expect to continue growing at the pace that we have demonstrated.

items.statement: Repeat order percentage remains more than 70%.
items.quote: And we take pride in our diverse customer base wherein our repeat order percentage remains more than 70%.

items.statement: Attrition rate for engineering is about 10%.
items.quote: I don't also have the exact figure, but I can say that for the recent period, it is about 10% for engineering in particular.

items.statement: Next year's objective is to increase sales by 20% and continue with 22% per year to double FY24 figures in 3 years.
items.quote: I think even our next year's objective is to increase the sales by 20% and continue with that 22% per year, so that in the next 3 years or now while 3 years left in the thing that we should achieve more or less the double the figure of our 24 figures.

items.statement: Two lines in Andhra Phase-2 and Kichha Phase-3 will be operational in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: This Capex will come into play by the 1st Quarter of FY26. It is already in production, the building is coming up, the machinery is ordered, so that the two lines coming up in Andhra Phase-2 and in Kichha Phase-3 will be operational in the 1st Quarter.

items.statement: Gujarat plant capex requirement is about Rs. 80-90 crores.
items.quote: I think similar, maybe about Rs. 80-Rs. 90 crores.

items.statement: Order book is Rs. 1,305 crores; pipeline is Rs. 4,000 crores with Rs. 2,500 crores confirmed bids and Rs. 1,500 crores under discussion.

Our pipeline overall is Rs. 4,000 crores, which is distributed into two facets. items.statement: Margins are sustainable for next 3-4 quarters; operational leverage can give better margins.
items.quote: The order book is good. The pipeline is good and so we do not see any problem right now at least for the next 3-4 quarters in margin sustainability.

items.statement: Operational leverage can give better margins, but difficult to quantify.
items.quote: Margin, yes, I think, operational leverage can give us better margins, but it is very difficult to say because at the same time you have to also prepare for higher turnovers and more sales going forward.

items.statement: Most prices are fixed; 30-40% of projects have variable pricing if stretched over 8-10 months.
items.quote: Yes, most of the prices are fixed. When there is a longer-term project, we do take variable pricing. So, I think today would be maybe 30%-40% of our projects would have variable pricing if the project stretches over 8-10 months

items.statement: Export margins slightly better than local, but freight costs high; looking at higher volume from exports for simpler buildings.
items.quote: So, we are looking at higher volume from there for simpler buildings and utilize more of our production capacity and execute those orders. But overall, I think the margin is only slightly better.

items.statement: Collaboration with JSPL for heavy structures and joint marketing of high-rise buildings, data centers, commercial buildings, malls.
items.quote: So, we are going to use them for the heavier structure production and joint marketing of other building like high rise buildings and data centers and commercial building, malls. items.statement: Land was a major issue for new plants; company now booking land earlier.
items.quote: And yes, we have found that land was a major issue, when we want to set up a new plant land was the biggest hurdle that took time. So, we have started booking the land earlier keeping it which we are not doing earlier.

items.statement: Working capital cycle to be held at 20-21 days; cash reserves nearly Rs. 300 crores.
items.quote: So, I think that we will be able to hold our working capital cycle to 20 -21 days and I don't think that working capital cycle if I am not mistaken doesn't include our cash reserve. I think it is debtor s, the customer, advances, suppliers and the stocks

items.statement: Top 10 customers can contribute 40%-50% of revenue.
items.quote: So, our top 10 customers would be very different in FY24 than in FY25 than in FY19, but if you were to ask me that whatever the top 10 customers will be, so top 10 customers could be, let us say, for FY25, it will be Reliance, Tata Projects, and let us say 4-5 more, next year it could be Aditya Birla and somebody else.

items.statement: Warehousing sector is about 23% of revenue.
items.quote: I think what we are showing is infrastructure is primarily that warehousing sector. So, about, say 23%, we have shown that as the warehousing, what we show as infrastructure is primarily the warehousing sector, “A” grade.

items.statement: Capacity utilization to reach about 90% of utilizable capacity in next one year.
items.quote: So, going forward, we do feel that we should be able to raise our capacity utilization of already utilizable capacity percentage by at least 3-4% and we should reach to about 90% of the utilizable capacity in next one year.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 15% with similar margins.
items.quote: I think Mr. Nanda had already mentioned about 15% during this call itself in the top line and margins being similar.

items.statement: After FY26, growth could be 20-25% to achieve doubling turnover in four years.
items.quote: All these capacities once they come on stream and we utilize them fully, our growth going forward in the years after FY26 could be greater than 15% to be able to achieve that doubling the turnover in four years as we had said, so it could also be 20-25% in those year.

items.statement: Gujarat plant capacity: 40,000 tons, Rs. 500 crores building sale.
items.quote: Gujarat will also be about Rs. 500 crores with 40,000 tons of buildings manufactured there.

items.statement: Gujarat plant production expected in Q1 FY27, 9 months after September start.
items.quote: Normally, it takes about 9 months. So, if you start in September, sometime by 1st Quarter, May-June next year, June-July, we should be able to have it in production.

items.statement: Upgradation at Pantnagar and Tamil Nadu to increase efficiency by 2-3%.
items.quote: I would say that they can increase 2-3% efficiency inside the plant.

items.statement: Average order value increased to Rs. 12 crores from Rs. 4 crores three years ago.
items.quote: The fact of the matter is that 3 years ago it used to be Rs. 4 crores. It moved up to Rs. 6.5 crores to Rs. 9 crores and now it is Rs. 12 crores.

items.statement: Order book may pick up from March with increased capacity in April and May.
items.quote: I don't see much change, maybe from March onwards it might start picking up, the order book because we will have increased capacity coming in place in April and May.

items.statement: Operational leverage expected to improve margins.
items.quote: I think operational leverage will kick in and make it better.

items.statement: Gross margins improved by 100 basis points sequentially and Y-o-Y.
items.quote: Gross margin have actually improved by 100 basis points sequentially as well as Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Small and medium orders are critical for pre-engineered building business.
items.quote: See in pre-engineered building, another thing I would like to point out is that the small and medium orders in numbers are very critical because they are the biggest beneficiaries of pre-engineered building.

items.statement: Skilled labor shortage may impact operations.
items.quote: But I think highly skilled people will always have a shortage going forward.

items.statement: Working capital requirement approximately 30 days of sales, Rs. 150 crores.
items.quote: So, right now, sir, we are operating at about 28 days and our requirement is going to be approximately 30 days of working capital, sir, 30 days of the sales will be our networking capital requirement.

items.statement: Fixed cost around 9.2% of sales, Rs. 12-13 crores per month.
items.quote: Right now, there are about 9.2%. Arvind Nanda: I think if we look at a figure I would probably about Rs. 12-13 crores a month

items.statement: Aims for revenue CAGR of around 15-20% over next four to five years.
items.quote: For the next four to five years, we aim for a revenue CAGR of around 15 to 20%.

items.statement: Aspires to reach EBITDA margin range of 28-30% in next 2-3 years.
items.quote: I think the 28-30% steady state that we are saying, we will get there in the next 2 to 3 years. That's our stated objective.

items.statement: Expects to add another 100 to 125 crores in current quarter.
items.quote: We probably expect to add another 100 to 125 crores in this current quarter.

items.statement: Added 100 KL manufacturing capacity in November; expects another 100 KL in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: The Company added 100 KL to its manufacturing capacity in November and expects to add another 100 KL in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Continues to grow pricing at 2-3% annually for most customers, not dropping pricing.
items.quote: In fact, we continue to grow at the 2-3% increase annually for most customers, and we are sticking to our pricing at this point.

items.statement: Sees strong demand across CDMO business due to cost efficiency and supply chain diversification.
items.quote: Additionally, we see strong demand across our CDMO business, as pharma and biotech companies seek cost-efficient, high-quality manufacturing solutions and supply chain diversification.

items.statement: Sees more Phase 1 to Phase 3 assets moving to India earlier than post-COVID.
items.quote: But what we are seeing is that now today we are seeing both late phase, which are coming from China, but we are seeing a lot more of the Phase 1 to Phase 3 assets coming in, which are moving much earlier than they did post-COVID.

items.statement: New company formation in biotech has slowed down; timing of recovery uncertain.
items.quote: But the new Company creation definitely has slowed down. Time frame is hard to judge. It's your guess as good as mine in terms of when new Company formation is going to start.

items.statement: Aims for ROCE of mid to high teens over 3-4 years.
items.quote: I think our aspiration on the ROCE side, I am looking at more return on capital employed, is probably a mid to high teens over a 3-4 year period. That's really what we aspire to get to.

items.statement: Expects Q4 to be strongest quarter, H2 stronger than H1.
items.quote: I think Quarter 4 has generally been the strongest quarter that we have had. And Quarter 3 and Quarter 4 relatively, H2 is generally stronger than H1, which is, you know, it's the case with most of the CDMO business across, and we also believe that it will be the same way.

items.statement: Expects reduction in interest cost in current quarter after debt repayment.
items.quote: The remaining debt was repaid in January and we expect a reduction in interest cost in the current quarter.

items.statement: Plans significant capacity increase across discovery, CMC, and development based on demand.
items.quote: We expect we will have significant investment, not investment, but increase in capacity across all three areas based on the demand we are seeing right now from our customers.

items.statement: Sees traction in peptides, amidites, ADCs, and conjugation technologies.
items.quote: One is peptides, which we are having reasonable traction with. Another one is Amidites, which we are part of several commercial products on Amidites. Another is ADCs, and the next one would be basically any kind of conjugation technologies going for peptide conjugation, prototype conjugation.

items.statement: Expects 3-4 molecules to commercialize over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: We have a few other molecules, Rahul, but I am saying, you know, from an overall perspective, there is at least three, four molecules that we are seeing that will get commercialized over the next 2-3 year period.

items.statement: Expects growth much faster than 12% TAM growth over next 10-15 years.
items.quote: So, I have maintained through the roadshows, and I will still maintain that the opportunity that we have created for ourselves is to execute far faster than the 12% TAM growth over the next 10, 15 years, not just over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Aims to reach steady-state EBITDA margin in mid-30s within a year.
items.quote: And I think as long as we stay on that path, maybe we get to the steady-state margins towards the mid-30s instead of the next two years within a year.

items.statement: Deals to ramp through Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26, full effect over next two quarters.
items.quote: As it relates to your specific question about when these deals will ramp, all of these three deals actually have gone live as we talk and they will ramp through Q4 of Fiscal ‘25 and Q1 of Fiscal ‘26.

items.statement: Expects to be debt free next fiscal if no other capital uses.
items.quote: So, all things remaining equal, we should be able to get debt free sometime next fiscal.

items.statement: Plans to reveal three to four new features over next 12-18 months.
