items.quote: There is no change in the tax rate. The tax rates are same, which have been prevailing for the past 2-3 years. So, there is no change in the tax rates.

items.statement: Targets 15% EBITDA in next 3 years.
items.quote: I have a very clear target of achieving 15% EBITDA in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Expects FY26 revenue of EUR210-220 million.
items.quote: we should be in the range of roughly EUR210 million, EUR215 million, EUR220 million, which is a realistic estimation that we have on our table.

items.statement: Plans to reach EUR350 million revenue in 5 years.
items.quote: we have a clear vision to reach that EUR350 million in 5 years.

items.quote: Quarter four should be better than quarter three, but nothing very dramatic, okay. So, which means that it will kind of take us to a closure of our EBITDA of 10% plus.

items.quote: It could grow to about EUR30 million business in the next 3, 3.5 years.

items.quote: We have already reached 76%. The target is to reach around 86%, 88% in the next 3 years, which will help us with that margin target of 15%.

items.quote: We are expecting at least six months wherein things should stabilize. It is an estimation. It is a judgment because the world or the feeling is the situation has bottomed out.

items.statement: Domestic market expected to grow stronger than exports next year.
items.quote: Probably domestic market will grow more stronger. But again, it's a matter of time. It's a cycle. And whenever exports pick up, it might even grow stronger.

items.statement: New high-tech products like Teleboom handlers to have above-average margins.
items.quote: whenever we launch these kinds of products, you can assume that they will come with a margin which is higher than average of our portfolio.

items.statement: Export business soft due to cyclical downturn in Europe and US, but no customer loss.
items.quote: business is soft for reasons which are outside the control of Carraro. We have to be very clear about it. Especially when we talk about export business, we are talking about mostly mature markets like Europe and the US, which in our industry are quite cyclical.

items.statement: Engineering services contract signed with leading Indian player, revenue stream with low cost.
items.quote: We already have got one engineering services contract for one of the leading players in India. We are seeing that engineering service outsourcing is also giving us a good revenue stream.

items.statement: Union agreement for 20% labor efficiency improvement.
items.quote: We have signed an agreement with the union where they have themse lves agreed for a 20 % improvement in our labor efficiency

items.statement: Zero-based merchandising rollout delayed by a quarter or few months; will focus on COCO stores in FY26, targeting top 50% turnover stores.
items.quote: I think the progress that we have seen between Jan and Feb also, I am pretty confident we should get back to the earlier plan, albeit with a lag of a quarter or a few months.

items.statement: Net store additions to return to earlier run rate of 30-40 stores per quarter after another quarter.
items.quote: So, my sense is it will be there for another quarter or so, but then the gross additions will keep happening. Eventually, net will start taking over.

items.quote: It's now become, in many stores, contributing to almost 8% to 10% of turnover, significantly accretive from a margin perspective.

items.quote: Our second largest brand, after Bata continues to grow faster, led by volume growth, almost close to double digits last quarter, and was backed by obviously new launches, Easy slide as well as Stamina.

items.quote: So, in terms of the margin, the overall gross margin has expanded by 17 bps. This has come on account of a couple of things. One is tightening of the way we source the product as well as in-house manufacturing.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded by 141 bps to 22.7%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin at 22.7%, which also expanded by 141 bps, and while the reported PAT is about Rs. 582 million, which is flat.

items.statement: Collapsed price points in ladies closed footwear from 11 to 3, leading to pairs growth and positive gross margin impact.

items.statement: Volume growth turned positive for the year and quarter, driven by all channels and better EOSS execution.
items.quote: We also saw volume growth after some time, even for the year, as well as for the three months of the quarter that went by, and we want to keep continuing that.

items.statement: One-time exceptional item of Rs. 11 crores for VRS at a south factory.
items.quote: This one was, partial VRS for a certain section of workers, which was amounting to about roughly Rs. 11 crores, yes. So, that we had taken incorporated.

items.statement: VRS impact on employee cost is about Rs. 2.5 crores per annum.
items.quote: So, it would be about Rs. 2.5 crores per annum.

items.statement: Availability increased by 20 percentage points, with potential for another 10 points.
items.quote: So, it's at 20 points extra than where we were earlier. And within that, the top articles are at 20 points extra. Overall availability keeps inching up further.

items.statement: Foods and FMCG to contribute nearly half of total turnover in next 4 years.

items.statement: Edible oil margin to return to 4-5% range.

items.statement: Food business margin to be 8-10%.
items.quote: We have consistently maintained that Food business overall will give between 8% to 10% margin in our business. And we still maintain that, and we are pretty much on course to achieve that.

items.statement: Biscuits yearly growth to be 6-7%.
items.quote: Second is that as a guidance perspective as to what we expect to end the year with, I would imagine that the yearly growth would be anywhere between 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Biscuits growth to return to 15% next fiscal.
items.quote: I think, we should get back to -- in the next fiscal, we should get back to the targeted range of 15%.

items.statement: Dental care category to grow 10-12%.
items.quote: Now having said that, the thing is that it has moved into a new entity, while we expect everything to stabilize in this quarter, but we are reasonably hopeful of maintaining 10% to 12% of growth in this category.

items.quote: But broadly, I would expect that this quarter 4 should be in a fully operational status.

items.statement: Plans to open 200-room Pune hotel in April 2027 and 100-room Vizag in October 2027.
items.quote: So, in FY27, the hotels will open, the first hotel Pune is going to open in April 27 followed by Vizag 100 rooms in October of ‘27.

items.statement: Plans to open 250-room Kolkata EM Bypass hotel in April 2028.

items.statement: Plans to open 400 keys in Navi Mumbai and Jaipur in FY29.
items.quote: And along with that, in ‘29, we will open about 400 keys, which is Navi Mumbai and our hotel in Jaipur.

items.statement: Plans to add 170 rooms in Navi Mumbai, total 250 keys.
items.quote: So, we plan to add another 170 rooms for which we have already completed the schematic design drawings. They are actually being completed and we are now going to be shortly going for the sanction of these drawings and for the additional approval of FSI .

items.statement: Expects 15% revenue CAGR over next 2-3 years including new hospitals and existing productivity.
items.quote: So for the revenue, we -- like we said earlier, we expect a 15% kind of CAGR growth over the next 2 to 3 years, which includes the new hospitals also coming and also existing hospitals productivity improving.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 22% to 23%.
items.quote: At the margin level, at EBITDA level, we would be around the 22% to 23% mark. Given the size of the existing hospitals and the improvement in productivity there, we should be able to absorb the initial losses from the new hospitals.

items.statement: Raipur hospital 152 beds, INR55 crore investment, asset-light rental model, commences early April.
items.quote: ILS Hospital Raipur, a 152-bed facility is expected to commence operations in early April. With a INR55 crore investment and an asset -light rental -based model, the hospital features ICUs, HDUs, OTs and specializes in oncology care as well.

items.statement: Signed MOU for third hospital in Jamshedpur, 150 beds, estimated outlay INR65 crores.
items.quote: Additionally, we have signed an MOU for our third hospital in Jamshedpur, which will have a capacity of 150 beds and an est imated outlay of approximately INR65 crores.

items.statement: Aims to become 1,000-bed hospital chain within next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: As previously announced, we are steadfast to become a 1,000 -bed hospital chain within the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Steadfast on 1,000 bed target by FY27; Raipur adds ~160 beds, Jamshedpur hopeful by Oct 2026.
items.quote: So we are still steadfast on the 1,000 bed challenge by FY '27, and we have taken significant steps to end up achieving that target. As disclosed earlier, the Raipur Hospital will be commencing, which will add around 160 -odd beds to our already 550 beds, taking a total almost 710 beds.

items.statement: Hopeful of commissioning Jamshedpur hospital by October 2026.
items.quote: We are hopeful of commissioning that hospital by October of 2026. Apart from that, we are also evaluating certain acquisition opportunities for ongoing hospitals, which when they click, will definitely add to the bed capacity much faster than that.

items.statement: Jamshedpur project should be operational by FY26 because it is under construction.
items.quote: But as a second safeguard, we have onboarded the Jamshedpur project in the state of Jharkhand, which should be operational by FY '26 because it is already an under construction building.

items.statement: Looking to stabilize ARPOB increase around 7%, 8% annually through newer treatments and insurance rate differentiation.
items.quote: The ARPOB has increased at a healthy rate across all our hospitals. We are looking at stabilizing the ARPOB increase in the next -- to around the 7%, 8% mark on a annual basis. This will be through newer treatments and through the rate differentiation of the insurance companies.

items.statement: No patients from Bangladesh now; last year 10% of Agartala volume.
items.quote: Last year around this time, almost 10% of our patient volume was from Bangladesh. At this point, we are not having any patients from Bangladesh. There has been a severe restriction on the number of medical tourism patients coming in.

items.statement: Ranchi project delayed awaiting government approvals; developer pursuing.
items.quote: So the Ranchi project is still something which is under - - we are still awaiting approvals from the government and the developer is following up. But as -- as we are still pursuing that project, it is not like we've given it up.

items.statement: No equity dilution planned; will take debt judiciously, net debt free.
items.quote: We're trying to take debt, right? No equity dilution.

items.statement: Radiation oncology components under installation, to be commissioned in Q4.
items.quote: As guided earlier, the radiation oncology components are under installation and will be commissioned in Q4.

items.statement: Focus on complex treatments like transplants, robotic knee surgeries, higher tertiary care impacting ARPOB.
items.quote: Across all our hospitals, we are focusing on more complex treatments, including transplants, including robotic knee surgeries and other higher tertiary care treatment. So that has definitely impacted the ARPOB.

items.statement: Inpatient volume 23,500 in 9M FY25 vs 23,100 last year, increase of ~400 patients.
items.quote: In terms of our inpatient volume, FY '25, we've had 23,500 patients compared to 23,100 patients in the last 9 months. There has been an increase of around 400-odd patients on a total basis.

items.statement: Evaluating acquisition opportunities in Guwahati, Bhubaneswar, Patna; will disclose later.
items.quote: We have been evaluating opportunities in Guwahati. There are a couple of opportunities at play even right now in a couple of cities like Bhubaneswar or even Patna, but we are evaluating them. We can disclose them later on once we are at a position of finalization.

items.statement: Anticipates gold demand to grow by 12%-15% and silver demand by 15%-18% by end of FY2025.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate gold demand to grow by 12% -15% and silver demand by 15% -18% by the end of FY2025.

items.statement: Targeting at least 20%-25% growth.
items.quote: Yes, we are definitely aiming to achieve the same growth. However, being conservative, we are targeting at least 20%-25% growth.

items.statement: Planning to raise up to ₹600 crores through QIP.
items.quote: To support our strategic expansion plans, we are planning to raise up to ₹600 crores through the QIP route.

items.statement: QIP proceeds to open company-owned stores.
items.quote: The proceeds from the QIP will be utilized to open company-owned stores.

items.statement: Majority of QIP funds for inventory, smaller portion for CAPEX including store development.
items.quote: Right, we are raising fund ₹600 crores. The majority of the funds will be allocated to inventory, with a smaller portion used for CAPEX, including store development.

items.statement: Aiming to double stores within next 2-3 years, opening 10 more stores.
items.quote: Right. We are undertaking a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) to significantly boost our store expansion, aiming to double them within the next 2-3 years. Additionally, we are planning to open a few franchises as part of our growth strategy, pursuing both avenues to achieve our goals.

items.statement: Plan to open 2-3 franchises within next 2 years.
items.quote: We plan to open 2 -3 franchises within the next 2 years, with further expansion to follow. Initially, our focus is on establishing these first few franchises.

items.statement: Aiming to improve current margins, targeting an increase of 20%-25% with focus on wedding, collection, diamond, studded, and Polki jewelry.
items.quote: We are definitely aiming to improve our current margins, targeting an increase of 20%-25% with continued focus on wedding jewelry, collection jewelry, diamond jewelry, studded jewelry, and Polki jewelry.

items.statement: 50%-55% of revenue from wedding jewelry.
items.quote: So, almost like the 50%-55% is coming from the wedding jewelry.

items.statement: White gold and rose gold jewelry contribution is 10% to 15%.
items.quote: So, the White Gold and Rose Gold jewelry contribution is nothing very much, but yeah, 10% to 15% is the total contribution.

items.statement: Inventory price is 8%-10% lower than market, naturally hedged if market falls.
items.quote: So, we are doing the weighted average method. So, our inventory price and market price is different. So, as of now our inventory price is lower than the market around like 8% -10% lower than the market. If market goes down so we are already hedged.

items.statement: Expect organized sector's market share to increase to 50% by FY29.
items.quote: Mandatory hallmarking and rising compliance costs are further steering consumers towards organized jewelry retailers, and we expect the organized sector’s market share to increase to 50% by FY29.

items.statement: New showroom in Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh, spans 7,700 sq. ft. with Ground+3 layout.
items.quote: As per the guidance for FY25 strategic expansion, we launched a new showroom in Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh, during Q3 FY25. items.statement: Second showroom in Ratlam to have carpet area of 12,000 sq. ft., expected launch by end of FY25.
items.quote: Additionally, the construction of our second showroom in Ratlam is progressing well. This showroom will have a carpet area of 12,000 sq. ft., with 8,000 sq. ft. dedicated to retail and the remainder for back-office operations. We expect to launch this showroom by the end of FY25.

items.statement: CAPEX for new stores approx ₹1-2.5 crores; inventory held ₹55-60 crores.
items.quote: This is approx. ₹ 1-2.5 crores capex and inventory which is held at the store is ₹55 cores- ₹60 crores.

items.statement: Stores expected to reach breakeven in around 6 to 9 months.
items.quote: Around 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Capex for current year will be lower than FY2024 and continue to unwind in FY2026.
items.quote: We believe that our capex for the current year will be lower than FY2024, and this will continue to unwind in FY2026.

items.statement: Capex moderation expected even in FY2026, with capex as percentage of revenues trending downwards.
items.quote: I would say at headline, you should see moderation of capex even in FY2026, and with the revenue growths that we are seeing, the capex as a percentage of revenues will continue to trend downwards and soon be at the levels of global peers.

items.statement: Transferring about 16,100 telecom towers to Indus Towers.
items.quote: we are planning to transfer about 16,100 telecom towers, approximately 12,700 from Bharti Airtel and about 3400 from Bharti Hexacom to Indus Towers.

items.statement: Launching comprehensive cloud solution in next few months.
items.quote: We will be launching a comprehensive cloud solution in the next few months.

items.quote: There is no reason why we should not get upwards of 50 million over the next few years on postpaid, because there is an 80 million base that is ready to actually get onto postpaid.

items.statement: FWA EBITDA margins similar to home services.
items.quote: Yeah, It will be in that same ballpark.

items.quote: In terms of addressable market, I would say this would be about 3 to 4 million.

items.quote: About 2 million home passes we have, currently at Bharti Hexacom

items.statement: Hexacom capex directionally same, could marginally increase due to FWA rollout.
items.quote: So, directionally same could be marginal increase, it all depends on FWA rollout.

items.statement: Hexacom dividend payout to be considered positively.
items.quote: Dividend payout is something which will be certainly looked at with a positive angle.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.4% in Q3 FY25 from 5.6% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: 5.6% improving to 6.4% in Q3 FY25, which is a jump of 30% year on year.

items.quote: We continue to improve our adjusted EBITDA from 10.7% in Q3 FY24, we have improved this by 50 bps to 11.2%, which is a n increase of 20% year on year for Q3

items.quote: And the 4% consol. EBITDA in nine months FY24 has increased to 5.1% for the nine months FY25, which is a n increase of 54% year on

items.quote: From 16% negative EBITDA in Q3’FY24, end of December, we have improved this to minus 15%.

items.quote: From 0.6% in Q3 FY24, we have improved this to 1.4% in Q3 FY25.

items.quote: EBITDA for the nine months is around 23% EBITDA, for Q3 is around 22%.

items.quote: Annual unique transacting customers in India and Middle East, 17% increase for the period ending Dec ’24 vis-a-vis period ending Dec’23, annual unique transacting customers.

items.quote: Likewise, our GMV grew for nine months over last nine months by 17% and the net revenue from operation s increased by 19% to INR 5,729 Cr

items.quote: So, next 3 years, we are looking at the growth rate of around 15% to 20%. Although, we will target to achieve more, but 15% to 20% definitely we will be able to achieve and EBITDA margins, we expect the EBITDA margins to be at the same, similar lines across the product.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain similar across products.
items.quote: and EBITDA margins, we expect the EBITDA margins to be at the same, similar lines across the product.

items.statement: Chennai plant phase 1 capacity ~55-60 crores, phase 2 total ~100-110 crores.

items.quote: We expect that this plant would be commissioned by Q1 of FY’25-26.

items.quote: So, we will be investing this CAPEX of 11 crore in different machines, in the Disc Spring, Coil Spring, and Fastener as well.

items.quote: We have a strong order book and pipeline, which gives us confidence of continuing our growth momentum.

items.quote: In fastener category in India, we are able to offer 3 to 4% saving because customers are looking more technical solutions, more customized suppliers rather than only price saving as compared to their local suppliers.

items.statement: Renewable and industrial to drive growth 30-40%, mobility 20-25%.
items.quote: I think, broadly, renewable and industrial will be the major drivers of the growth that will be about 30 to 40% and mobility will be about 20-25%.

items.quote: So, broadly the export and domestic mix will remain same which is about 35 to 40% exports and about 60% will be domestic even going forward.

items.statement: No major impact expected in next 1 year from US renewable uncertainty.
items.quote: But based on the discussion with customers of course in last couple of weeks we do not see any major impact in next 1 year because most of the projects are allotted.

items.statement: Wada plant max revenue potential 325-350 crore.
items.quote: Going forward with some incremental CAPEX we will be able to achieve around 325-350 crore from Wada itself.

items.statement: Fastener segment growth expected higher than other product groups.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to stabilize at 15-18%.
items.quote: Post COVID in fact year on year we are able to improve our EBITDA if you see our last 4 year performance and going forward we are thinking we should be stabilizing this EBITDA level 15-18-17 something and so there will be quarter-on-quarter there will be some plus and minus but because of the various reason or product mix or some one time cost and all.

items.statement: 68 crores of IPO funds unutilized, to be used for Chennai and Wada capex.
items.quote: Major portion of the 78 crores 68 crores is actually unutilized IPO funds which has been kept in fixed deposit which will get utilized for the Chennai and Wada CAPEX over the period of next 6 months to 1 year.

items.statement: Expects at least 15%-20% growth next year with new products.

items.statement: February order book approximately 4,000 axles.
items.quote: However, we've seen good growth in the month of January and our order book of February is approximately of 4,000 axles.

items.statement: Export business could run at 20% to 22% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: The margins, fortunately, are much better. I mean, if we are to draw our balance sheets only based on export business, we would be running with an EBITDA of 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Q4 demand from trailer business is good and strong.
items.quote: And more importantly, we see Q4, the demand from the trailer business is quite good, quite strong.

items.statement: Component business improving, OEM volumes getting better.
items.quote: The component business is getting better. Volumes at OEMs are getting better.

items.quote: This advanced technology will increase our capacity to 7,500 units per month, up from our current 5,000 trailer capacity for axles and suspension assemblies.

items.quote: But this is, you could say, it is a one-off case in this quarter. It's going to be back at our previous percentages from the coming quarters.

items.statement: Exports to reach 15% of revenue in next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: 15% of our revenue coming in from exports in the next 2 to 3 years. That's what I was explaining.

items.quote: So, we are looking at 5%, around INR25 crores-INR28 crores revenue coming in this year from the export front.

items.statement: Seamless tube investment of INR167 crores funded through debt and internal accruals.
items.quote: This will involve an investment of INR167 crores and this will be funded through a mixture of debt and our internal accruals.

items.statement: Anticipates double-digit growth in Q4 on a year-to-year basis.
items.quote: We feel that the situation has now improved quite a lot and we are anticipating double-digit growth in Q4 on a year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew 24%, offsetting 15% decline in EXIM container volumes for 9M FY25.
items.quote: The domestic volumes at the same time have shown a growth of 24% which has successfully offset this about 15% decline in EXIM container volumes for the first 9 months.

items.statement: Margin improvement too early to say, but should happen in the long term.
items.quote: So margin improvement it's too early to say, sir, because all of these new projects and work is in progress, but margin improvement should happen in the long term for sure, sir.

items.statement: International supply chain constraints caused dip in quarterly profits due to higher costs.
items.quote: So, that is the reason why we have seen a dip in our quarterly profits this time. It is really nothing to do with our own efficiencies, but more to do with the geopolitical situation.

items.quote: So, it is not a straight pass through Western Carriers ( to the customers. It depends on your order booking and the terms of your contract. So, not everything can be passed on to the customer

items.statement: Confident to give revenue growth this year.
items.quote: Yes, sir. I am very, very confident that we will be able to give revenue growth this year, sir.

items.quote: As on 31st December, the total outstanding debt is INR164 crores.

items.statement: Receivables slightly higher due to new orders; benefit of reduction visible from next year.
items.quote: So, since we've had a lot of new orders that have come in, the receivables are slightly higher. We are working very hard on actually reducing its quarter-on-quarter. And I think the benefit of that will be visible from next year more than this year, sir.

items.statement: Expects robust growth in Vedanta plant volumes in next three to four years.
items.quote: I would like to say that in the next three to four years, Vedanta expects very robust growth year on year in this plant.

items.statement: Third undisclosed project of 52 acres could add INR600-700 crores GDV if launched by Diwali FY26
items.quote: And this will be a big launch. So, if that comes, then the total number would be close to INR1,000 crores. But right now, we have visibility of INR360 crores. The big one, INR600-odd crores, we have not even applied for approval at the moment.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin 24.4% impacted by low-margin Imperia Phase 1; Imperia Phase 2 margin 45%-50%
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter was INR9.3 crores with an EBITDA margin of 24.4%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 average realizations at historical high of INR6,465 per sq ft driven by Eldeco Trinity
items.quote: During the 9MFY25 period, our average realizations were INR6,465 per square foot and are at the highest they have been historically, driven by steadily rising realizations in our luxury project, Eldeco Trinity.

items.statement: Lucknow market absorption 2,000-3,000 units annually but can absorb 8,000 units; supply constrained by land aggregation and approvals
items.quote: So, Lucknow, to my mind, can absorb 8,000 easily right now without any further big investment. 8,000 units annually should be a fair number, just to give you an idea of the demand supply gap in the market right now.

items.statement: Labour shortage emerging as industry-wide challenge due to government schemes in Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha
items.quote: Apart from a general comment that there is general labour shortage in the industry now because of all the schemes which are being rolled out in the hinterland in Bihar and Jharkhand and Orissa where labour usually comes from.

items.statement: Construction spend increased 68% YoY to INR105.1 crores in 9M FY25
items.quote: Our construction spend has increased by 68% compared to last year, amounting to INR105.1 crores.

items.statement: New launches Hanging Gardens and Skywalk at INR6,000 per sq ft; larger undisclosed project at INR5,000 per sq ft
items.quote: The one I'm alluding to later on in the year will be slightly lower, let's say, INR5,000. So weighted average should be around between INR5,000 to INR6,000 depending on the mix that we launch in the coming year.

items.statement: Added 7.3 acres to land bank in Q3 FY25; received map approvals for Hanging Gardens and Skywalk
items.quote: We have strengthened our land bank with additional acquisition of 7.3 acres during this quarter.

items.statement: INR120 crores debt facility deployed for new land acquisitions; no further debt plans currently
items.quote: Yes, that's where the new land acquisitions have happened from.

items.statement: Imperia Phase 2 revenue recognition possible in FY26 or FY27; Twin Tower CC received, revenue recognition in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, we may go for revenue recognition this year, but that will be touch and go. It will be either this financial year. And when I say this, I mean FY26, or it will be FY27.

items.statement: Open to JDA partnerships but Lucknow landlord ecosystem not mature for such structures
items.quote: We are 100% open, Manan, but the local market, the local landlord ecosystem does not seem to be that open, unfortunately.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth of 15% in FY26 and 20% in FY27
items.quote: For F '26, yes, about 15% and '27, about 20% consolidated.

items.statement: API segment revenue growth of 10-12% in FY26 and ~20% in FY27
items.quote: I see about -- I mean, first year growth of 10% to 12% and second year growth of about 20% in API segment.

items.statement: Revenue target of around INR1,200 crores in 3.5 years
items.quote: I would say, about INR1,200 around that.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 17-20% in 4 years
items.quote: It's difficult to predict, but definitely, it will be about 17% to 20%.

items.statement: Targeting >50% of business from CMO/CDMO in 2 years
items.quote: We see 2 years from now, more than 60% business should come from CMO and CDMO.

items.statement: 26 CMO/CDMO projects near completion; commercial supplies starting this quarter or Q1 FY26
items.quote: Commercial supplies are starting in this quarter or I mean all the projects, if I say, by first quarter of next year. We will be in commercial supply stage.

items.statement: 18 CMO/CDMO projects under implementation; commercialization in 12-24 months
items.quote: As far as projects which are under implementation, about 18 projects both put together, we say commercialization between 12 to 24 years -- months

items.statement: Formulations capex ~INR10 crores for 9 months FY25; no large capex expected for next 1-2 years
items.quote: In formulation, it's not very, very high. It's normal capex of about INR10 crores or so in formulations for 9 months.

items.statement: Panoli plant capex nearly complete; commercial production expected early Q1 FY26
items.quote: Panoli, almost all capex has been completed from last time we have given, barring some small here and there, and we are expecting commercial production to start in Q1, beginning of Q1 rather.

items.statement: Meropenem volumes increased to ~20 tons this year from 12-14 tons last year; market share increased
items.quote: We would be doing about 20 tons this year, as compared to many 12 or 13 tons last year, 14 tons.

items.statement: API price erosion from Chinese competition bottoming out; limited further downside of 3-5%
items.quote: These products -- I mean, these are almost at their bottom, I mean, barring another 3%, 4%, 5% one can say.

items.statement: China threat limited to fermentation-based antibiotics; synthesis-based KSMs becoming competitive in 3 years
items.quote: In the next 3 years, synthesis-based KSMs, you will see a lot from India. To that extent, Chinese will not be a threat.

items.statement: Government to protect domestic fermentation-based KSMs via minimum support price or anti-dumping
items.quote: The government has already assured that such basic KSMs, which will be made from fermentation in India to make us self dependent, the government will protect us.

items.statement: ESOP of 340,000-375,000 shares at INR179; 40% exercisable Sep'24-Aug'25, 30% Sep'25, 30% Sep'26
items.quote: We have given about 340,000 375,000 shares is ESOP at a rate of 179. And 40% of that is exercisable after 1 year, which is from September '24 till August '25.

items.statement: Forex policy: 98% USD exposure, ~60% hedged via forwards and banking credit
items.quote: As a policy, we keep certain percentage of dollar hedged by forward booking and some by foreign exchange banking credit. So about 60% is always hedged irrespective of where it is moving.

items.statement: Seamec Swordfish commenced a 50-day charter with Maritime Mermaid Subsea Services in Saudi Arabia with a firm order value of $3.46 million.
items.quote: key highlight this quarter is the successful commencement of a new charter for our vessels, Seamec Swordfish. The vessel began a 50-day charter with Maritime Mermaid Subsea Services ® SEAMEC LIMITED A Member of ~~~ in Saudi Arabia with a firm order value of $3.46 million

items.statement: Seamec Swordfish secured a 2-year charter at $78,000 per day expected to start between March 15-31, 2025.
items.quote: $78,000 per day for 2 years.

items.statement: Seeking Board approval for transfer of Seamec Anant from parent HAL Offshore at $70 million; acquisition expected to complete by Q2 FY26.
items.quote: However, we have secured a 2-year contract for Seamec Swordfish and seeking Board approval for transfer of Seamec Anant from the parent entity, HAL Offshore Limited at $70 million.

items.statement: NPP Nusantara acquisition agreement signed; delivery expected around July-August 2025 (Q2 FY26).
items.quote: So the tentative delivery, the delivery is going to be taken sometime around July or August, so we are also hopeful of completing that process of Nusantara acquisition sometime in Q2.

items.statement: Capex of roughly INR800 crores for two vessel acquisitions (INR600 crores + INR200 crores) plus dry dock expenses over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: So capex, as we already informed, there are 2 vessels. One is roughly INR600 crores and other is INR200 crores. So INR800 crores plus some dry dock expenses will be done.

items.statement: Peak debt should not exceed INR500 crores next year; confident of generating sufficient cash flows for FY26 and FY27 to repay debt.
items.quote: Debt profile, I would say that we are very much under control. Our debt, peak debt should not go more than INR500 crores next year, and that subsequent year will be repaid because we are confident to generate sufficient cash flows for FY '26 and FY '27.

items.statement: Seamec Anant expected to add INR135 crores revenue on full-year basis after acquisition.
items.quote: So we expect that around INR135 crores of revenue will be added on a full year basis after the acquisition.

items.statement: NPP Nusantara expected to add INR135 crores revenue on full-year basis after acquisition.
items.quote: Nusantara should give us around INR135 crore revenue on a full year basis.

items.statement: Demand for offshore oil and gas services remains substantial in India; government launched largest oil and gas bid round offering 25 offshore blocks covering 1.91 lakh sq km.
items.quote: In this context, we continue to see substantial opportunities ahead, particularly following India's recent launch of its largest oil and gas bid round. The government is now offering 25 offshore blocks, spending 1.91 lakh square kilometres, a move, which is aimed at boosting domestic production and improving energy security.

items.statement: Seamec Anant projected to deliver ~17% ROCE with ~14% IRR and ~6-year payback period.
items.quote: And with the remaining useful life of 23 years, this vessel is 2023 build and we are getting, we are projected to get a 17% odd of ROCE in years to come.

items.statement: MTM forex loss of ~INR13.5 crores in Q3 due to dollar moving from INR85.05 to INR87.1 and GBP from INR110.17 to INR104.44; GBP impact expected to reverse.
items.quote: So there is a difference of INR2.05, which give us an impact of INR4.5 crores. And similar to that, we have whatever loan we have extended to our subsidiary in UK. In that case, GBP had moved again from INR110.17 to INR104.44. There is a adverse movement of INR5.73 per GBP, so that again give us a hit of INR9.4 odd crores in Q3. So that was a major reason of MTM of around INR13.5 odd crores, which

items.statement: Seamec Paladin and Seamec II likely going for dry dock this year; dry docks planned and factored into contracts.
items.quote: So the Seamec Paladin and Seamec II will be likely going for the dry dock.

items.statement: Seamec Diamond resumed operations with ONGC on November 22, 2024 after repairs; deployed for ~42 days in Q3 with minimal revenue impact due to low day rate vs DSVs.
items.quote: And in this quarter, it has deployed for around 42 odd days. But around 50 days for which it could not be deployed, it has given us hardly any impact in terms of revenue generation. Reaso n being, it’s day rate is very minimal as compared to DSV, which we are running as a main fleet business for us

items.statement: All vessels on minimum 2-year contracts except Glorious Barge; most contracts full for coming year providing revenue visibility.
items.quote: And now there is a 2-year contact. So we are hopeful that such delay will not come in at least in most of our vessels. Only Glorious Barge will be renewing its contract next year. Otherwise, most of our contracts are full for the coming year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin contracted 309 bps QoQ to 9.1% due to sluggish OEM demand and higher natural rubber costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins during the quarter were recorded at 9.1% vis-à-vis 12.2% in the previous quarter, which has contracted by 309 basis points due to sluggish demand in OEM and the higher raw material costs, primarily driven by a significant rise in natural rubber prices.

items.statement: Prices increased 1% QoQ; 4-5% under-recovery remains to be passed on
items.quote: We have increased our pricing on a quarter-on-quarter basis to 1% and wherever price revision we could do, we have done that, and also we have improved our product mix. There is still some under recovery of 4%- 5% yet to be done.

items.statement: Ongoing Rs 1,400 crore capex (Rs 1,025 crore PCR, Rs 400 crore TBR/ASLTR); Rs 600 crore spent in 9M FY25
items.quote: We already have an ongoing capex program of Rs.1,400 crores, out of which Rs.1,000 crores plus is for the PCR expansion, which we've already shared and another Rs.400 odd crores is a combination of TBR and all steel light truck radial.

items.statement: Replacement demand promising; OEM recovery underway; PCR grew 24% YoY, replacement grew 16% YoY in Q3
items.quote: Just to tell you that replacement market in terms of the numbers from the previous corresponding quarter, we had grown at 16% and the passenger car radial had grown at 24%.

items.statement: Q4 margins expected to improve as high-cost inventory consumed, unless RM prices rise further
items.quote: the good thing is that most of the inventory has already been consumed in Q3, so in Q4, we can expect some improvement in margins unless there is again some increase in raw material prices going forward.

items.statement: RM basket up 2% QoQ; natural rubber volatility from seasonal and labor issues in Southeast Asia
items.quote: the average raw material prices have increased 2% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and here I would say that the natural rubber prices have actually played little havoc and the reason of which is actually because of the season changing and the climatic impact in this availability of natural rubber plus labor availability as well in the Southeast Asian belt.

items.statement: Year-to-date capex spend Rs 600 crore of Rs 800 crore planned for 9M FY25
items.quote: the outlay is about Rs.800 crores in these three quarters period. We have already spent about Rs.600 crores.

items.statement: Cavendish posted highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 1,025 crore with 9% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Cavendish posted a top line of Rs.1,025 crores, the highest ever for a quarter with EBITDA of Rs.92 crores, registering a margin of 9%.

items.statement: Focus on premiumization; new higher rim size products launched in Mexico for US and domestic markets
items.quote: we have launched new premium products in higher rim sizes, further strengthening our product portfolio, catering to the evolving needs of advanced markets like USA including domestic market.

items.statement: US 25% import duty on Mexican goods on hold for one month; negotiations ongoing
items.quote: this 25% duty on the imports from Mexico into America has been put on hold by the President of USA for about one month, during which time some negotiations are taking place.

items.statement: $100 million sustainability-linked loan from IFC for expansion and refinancing high-cost debt in Cavendish
items.quote: the $100 million loan which we have tied up with IFC is for the expansions which are under implementation at this point in time and partly this loan will be used for replacing the high-cost debt in Cavendish Industries Limited.

items.statement: Long-term industry EBITDA margin range 12-15%; FY26 target to be clarified next quarter
items.quote: generally, as we had earlier also said that in the longer term the industry is somewhere between that 12% to 15% range. So, let's see we will have to kind of keep it like that as of now, but maybe in the next quarter, we will be able to give you a sharper number on that.

items.statement: Radial capacity utilization over 80%; PCR near 90%; Bus 70%+; new expansions not yet commissioned
items.quote: terms of capacity utilization for radial, we are in excess of 80% , for Bus also, utilizations are at around 70 % plus, and this includes whatever capacities have already expanded that have been taken into consideration. Chirag Jain: And for PCR? Anuj Kathuria: PCR, as I said, it is close to 90

items.statement: Net debt Rs 4,319 crore (Dec'24); Net Debt/Equity 0.89x, Net Debt/EBITDA 2.4x; working capital borrowings to normalize in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Net debt stood at Rs.4,319 crores for the quarter ended December '24 as against Rs.4,340 crores in the previous quarter. Leverage ratios i.e. Net debt to Equity and Net debt to EBITDA were at 0.89x and 2.4x as on December '24, respectively.

name: Shri Keshav Cements And Infra Ltd

items.statement: New 1 million ton per annum kiln and infrastructure completed in Dec-Jan; switchover to new kiln planned for end of Feb or first week of March, taking 20-25 days
items.quote: We have just now completed the CAPEX in December- January and we are in a process to switch over to the new kiln. So, with the new kiln, what we are going to expect is the Shri Keshav Cement & power consumption will go down, the fuel consumption will go down and then we will have similar EBITDA margins like what we see in the industry level

items.statement: New power line received by end of January; kiln switchover delayed to March to avoid dispatch gap as utilization reached 90-95%
items.quote: finally, we received the new power line by end of January. Access the kiln and everything is ready right now. Now what has happened is suddenly there is a huge increase in dispatches from January. And once we start doing the switchover, it might take about 25 days Shri Keshav Cement & for us to shut down the kiln

items.statement: Q4 showing improved volumes and dispatches across all cement plants; capacity utilization expected to beat trends in Q4
items.quote: Q4 is already showing promises , so we would be able to beat the tr ends in Q4.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton currently below Rs. 50 vs South peers at Rs. 422 (9M FY25) and national average Rs. 719 (Q3 FY25); target to reach South peer levels plus solar benefit after new kiln
items.quote: So, what we will be targeting is to be as close as or equal to what we see in the South and even better. Plus, we also get a benefit of solar which I am not counting in these margins.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin 26.26% (Rs. 7.38 cr on Rs. 29.04 cr income); 9M FY25 EBITDA margin 24.29% (Rs. 20.17 cr on Rs. 85.64 cr income)
items.quote: From a financial standpoint, we recorded a total income of 29.04 crores, EBITDA of 7.38 crores, an EBITDA margin of 26.26% in Q3FY25.

items.statement: Naked cement price Q3 FY25 Rs. 3,302 vs Rs. 3,761 in Q3 FY24, down 8%; industry down 10-12%; Q3 vs Q2 down 1%
items.quote: So, in Q3 of FY24, what I generally use the word naked cement rate is because it excludes logistics, it excludes the tax, everything. So naked cement price of Q3FY24 is Rs. 3,761. Now it is Q3FY25 is Rs. 3,302. So, if you look at your realization standpoint, it has reduced by 8%.

items.statement: Cement prices expected to show upward trend in FY26 as consolidation completes and price discipline improves; government infrastructure spending to support
items.quote: And of course, cement prices are going to be showing an upward trend in FY26 because current prices are definitely not sustainable. Consolidation has almost is almost done. So, there is going to be a price discipline.

items.statement: Q1-Q2 FY25 weak due to elections and monsoons; Q3 volumes began improving; Q4 showing strong offtake and improved dispatches across industry
items.quote: Q1-Q2 was extremely bad mainly because of election and then the monsoons. The fag end of Q3 showed some kind of an improvement and Q4 has shown the very good offtake for all the cement plants in the country.

items.statement: New kiln switchover may face initial teething issues; 20-25 day shutdown required for changeover; delayed to March to avoid dispatch disruption
items.quote: So, let's say then we're talking about Q -on-Q FY26. So, we are going to see an improved margin storms currently other than the initially the teething issues what we might likely face like typically any new machinery will have some initial hiccups.

items.statement: No acquisition plans in cement; may consider renewable power acquisitions if opportunity arises but nothing currently
items.quote: No, currently we don't have any acquisition planned in the cement sectors. Not that we're looking at new renewable power either. But if there is some sc ope, if we see that there is someone who wants to sell in renewable sector, management will be keen to look at it.

items.statement: FY26 cement capacity utilization projected at 50% of 1 million ton (500k ton) conservatively; scope for improvement if demand increases
items.quote: So typically, any cement plants and basically what we have done is we have projected to begin with, we have projected 50 % utilization. But if the market demand increases , there's always a scope for improvement. But to be on the safer side, we have taken 50% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Industry EBITDA per ton: 9M FY24 national Rs. 1,064, South Rs. 750; 9M FY25 national ~Rs. 800, South Rs. 462; management expects recovery to Rs. 800-1,000 as consolidation ends
items.quote: So, 9 months FY24 industry generated Rs. 1,064 EBITDA per t on. And the same industries in 9 months F Y25, in ‘24 they generate d 1,065, in FY25 they generated around Rs. 800 per metric ton. This is the entire national level. But if you look at the South, EBITDA per ton generated by the South based leaders, they generated around Rs. 462 per metric ton for 9 months in FY25. So eventually this has t

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected to be lower single-digit, not high single-digit as previously projected
items.quote: No, we will not be ending FY25 with high single-digit growth. It will be more in the range of lower single-digit growth.

items.statement: Targeting Rs 2,900 crore revenue by March 2027, contingent on market recovery
items.quote: we are optimistic and committed in terms of meeting our projected target, what we have set i.e Rs. 2,900 crore by March 2027.

items.statement: EBITDA margin (ex-other income) at 13.2% in Q3 FY25, down 40 bps YoY; confident of returning to 16-17% range in next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: EBITDA margins excluding other income for the current quarter stood at 13.2 % as against 13.6% in Q3 FY24, registering a marginal decrease of 40 basis points.

items.statement: Management expects margins to recover to 16-17% in next one or two quarters as discounts have bottomed out
items.quote: we are quite confident that we are going to achieve this 16 % to 17% in the next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Planned capex for FY25 is Rs 25 crore, with Rs 15 crore deployed in 9M FY25
items.quote: Our planned CAPEX for FY25 stands at Rs . 25 crore, with Rs. 15 crore already deployed during 9 MFY25.

items.statement: Retail demand remains sluggish; B2B/project segment growing and now contributes 35-37% of revenue
items.quote: While demand in the B2C segment remains sluggish , the B2B segment continues to gain momentum, contributing 35% of the Q3 FY25 revenues.

items.statement: January and February 2025 better YoY but still not enough for high single-digit growth
items.quote: January and February so far have been better compared to last year on a year-on-year basis. But still, we do not anticipate achieving high single-digit growth as projected earlier.

items.statement: Price hikes taken: 6% in Faucetware, 1% in Sanitaryware; effective realization up ~2% in Q3
items.quote: Regarding the price hike, we have taken an average increase of 6% in Faucetware and 1% in Sanitaryware.

items.statement: Gas cost favorable: weighted average Rs 33.53/cu m in Q3 FY25, 1.56% of revenue; GAIL drawal at 81%
items.quote: The weighted average cost of gas in Q3 FY25 was Rs. 33.53 per cubic meter, which is notably below the industry average. Gas cost constitutes 1.56% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Luxe and Senator brands expected to contribute ~10% of revenue (Rs 290-300 crore) by March 2027
items.quote: Based on our Rs. 2,900 crore revenue target for March 2027, Luxe and Senator should generate Rs. 290-300 crore by then.

items.statement: Plan to open 20-25 exclusive Senator stores by end of FY25, scale to 75 by FY26; Luxe displays in 100+ stores by FY26
items.quote: By the end of FY25, we aim to establish 20 to 25 exclusive Senator stores and thereafter we will establish another 50 stores in the following year, enabling scaling up to 75 stores by FY 26.

items.statement: Greenfield expansion deferred; land acquired but project start delayed due to market uncertainty, will revisit at FY end
items.quote: given the market uncertainties, we do not expect expansion to begin in the current financial year. Looking to the market instability, we will revisit this decision at the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Working capital days increased from 60 to 76 in Q3 FY25 due to higher inventory (85 days) and receivables (33 days), lower payables (42 days)
items.quote: Consequently, the net working capital increased from 60 days to 76 days in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Retail network at 1,682 display centers as of Dec 2024; annual target to add 300-350 display centers
items.quote: As of December, we have around 1,682 display centers, categorized by store size.

items.statement: Faucetware capacity utilization at 91%, Sanitaryware at 90% in Q3 FY25; expansion to 4 lakh units/month yielding positive results
items.quote: Faucetware capacity utilization stood at 91% while Sanitaryware capacity utilization was 90% during the quarter.

items.statement: Aiming for 1% improvement in consolidated EBITDA margin over the next year and a half
items.quote: So keeping all of this in mind, we are still aiming for 1% improvement in EBITDA margin going forward at a consol level in the year and a half ahead.

items.statement: Three new facilities under construction adding ~1,100 machines in MP, ~750 machines in Karnataka, and a 200-machine leased unit in Ranchi (400 machines equivalent on 2 shifts), all expected to commence in FY26
items.quote: The first one is a new facility in This will increase the capacity by about 1,100 machines and is under construction. The second one is an additional unit in Karnataka, which will add about 750 machines, which is also under construction. The third incremental unit is expected in Ranchi leased premises. All these units are expected to commence operations at different points in FY '26

items.statement: Order book remains strong with good fall/winter placements and strong early indications for spring/summer
items.quote: The company's order book remain strong, securing robust near-term prospects. Fall/winter order placements have been good, the production for which happens in Q1 and Q2. Early indications for spring/summer is also strong.

items.statement: Matrix at ~14% EBITDA margin, Atraco at ~7%; targeting 10% for Atraco next year, Matrix at par or above Gokaldas standalone
items.quote: So I think Matrix is at about 14-odd percent and Atraco is proportionately, I think 7% or thereabouts.

items.statement: Raw material prices are a pass-through; cotton prices have dropped and should remain range-bound with no rapid spike expected
items.quote: Our business, if I look at only the garmenting business, which is bulk of our business, is really a conversion business. So we really do not -- our raw material prices are really a pass-through. So if there is a price increase or price decrease, we tend to pass it back through to our customers.

items.statement: U.S. retail apparel sales grew 3% in CY24; U.S. and EU imports picked up in H2 CY24 as retailer inventories normalized, supporting demand bounce-back
items.quote: U.S. retail apparel sales remained consistent, showing a 3% growth in calendar 2024. U.S. and EU apparel imports have picked up momentum since the second half of CY '24 on the strength of lower inventory with retailers.

items.statement: Outerwear ~30% of Gokaldas 9M revenue (~35% annualized); Matrix and Atraco low single digits; polyester/synthetic growing but fabric still sourced from Far East
items.quote: So outerwear on a 9-month basis for Gokaldas was about 30%.

items.statement: New capacity ramp-up depresses margins for 1-1.5 years; MP Phase 1 ramp-up added INR3-4 cr cost in Q3 without proportionate revenue; Kenya shilling appreciation pressuring Atraco margins
items.quote: So our incremental cost was about INR3 crores to INR4 crores on account of all of this, and it has not manifested in proportionate revenue. So that's -- that was the point I was referring to.

items.statement: Incremental revenue potential: MP Phase 2 ~INR175 cr, Karnataka ~INR125-130 cr, Ranchi ~INR55-60 cr, Atraco 500-machine expansion ~INR125-130 cr, knit fabric unit ~INR150-200 cr annually
items.quote: The incremental capacity in MP should net in about INR175 crores when it is fully ramped up. I'm talking of the incremental new capacity. One in Karnataka would yield about INR125 crores, INR130 crores. And the one in Ranchi would yield about INR55 crores, INR60 crores. So overall, I would say it's about INR300-odd

items.statement: Invested INR175 cr in BTPL via OCDs to date; further ~INR588 cr (adjusted for working capital) needed for 100% acquisition; merger process to initiate June 2025 via NCLT, taking 9-12 months
items.quote: So, till this quarter that is quarter ending December, we have invested INR110 crores in - BTPL and subsequently we have invested another INR65 crores. So, it amounts to about INR175 crores of investment till date.

items.statement: Top-end of 10-15% revenue CAGR over 2-3 years is a reasonable assumption; $1 billion revenue vision attainable in a few years
items.quote: I think it's a very decent assumption. I would say that top end of that range will be a more reasonable decent assumption.

items.statement: BTPL standalone peak revenue ~INR1,500+ cr at 12-14% EBITDA; consolidation not before FY27; will reduce fabric import dependence for synthetics but not eliminate it
items.quote: So the impact of BTPL, if I look at it on a st and-alone basis, its peak revenue could be about INR1,500-plus crores. But then again, a lot of it could be bought internally. So once it is merged, some of those revenues will get knocked off in consolidation

items.statement: No near-term M&A; focus on integrating acquisitions from last 9 months; multi-shift operations difficult in South due to women workforce transport constraints; INR depreciation hedged through Q1-Q2
items.quote: We want to consolidate what we have. Remember, we have only taken up some of these acquisitions 9 months ago, and there is tons of work required to be done to bring them to where we would like them -- like to see them.

items.statement: No significant preponement of orders due to tariff fears; buying is seasonal and India-sourced orders not seeing pull-forward; Africa may benefit if tariffs rise on other regions
items.quote: So I'm not seeing much of that happen out of here. And also the worry on tariff is more on the Far East. So there may have been some degree of expediting of deliveries from China, maybe even Vietnam and all of that. But then as far as the India denominated sourcing is concerned, we are not seeing so much of that.

items.statement: MP unit PLI not applicable due to product HS codes; DBT from MP government expected to start flowing next financial year, providing margin lever beyond 250 bps
