But lately, we have seen that the number of requests from the market is picking up, and that's a very good news because that means that we will be able sooner rather than later to book new projects and new customers for sure.

items.statement: Netherlands cholesterol orders coming in lately, likely to exceed target for that business unit
items.quote: And especially on cholesterol, we have seen a number of orders coming in lately, which are going in the right directions and probably we will be able to go beyond the target for that business unit.

items.statement: Interest cost to reduce by ~4% (2% from Jan, 2% from March) as financial covenants now met after Q2-Q3 improvement
items.quote: However, now with the improved performance of Q2 and Q3, we are now meeting the financial covenants and that should reduce the interest cost by almost about 4%. So, there would be a reduction of 2% that would be visible from January of this year and another 2% by March of this year.

items.statement: Commercial revenue ~60% of Q3 CRAMS vs usual 50-50 split; higher commercial share driving revenue growth
items.quote: So out of the total revenue in the quarter, roughly about -- so roughly about 60% of the revenue came from commercial and 40% came from development work. Usually, our split for the full year is roughly 50-50, but this year, the commercial revenue portion has been much higher as compared to development.

items.statement: FY25 operating income growth guidance of 12% to 13% with EBITDA around 11%
items.quote: So this fiscal, we have a guidance of 12% to 13% kind of revenue growth with an EBITDA level of approximately 11%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of INR 2,000 crores with EBITDA margin of 13% to 14%
items.quote: And next year, as we have already also mentioned in our presentation, we have taken a vision of achieving INR2,000 crores revenue in FY '26 with an EBITDA level of somewhere between 13.5%, like from 13% to 14% kind of an EBITDA level.

items.statement: Project Lakshya to contribute 65% to 70% of revenue by FY26
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect that by FY '26, 65% to 70% of our revenue will be contributed by distributors under Project Lakshya.

items.statement: Announced capex plan mostly completed; only 2-3 MW solar capacity pending over next 6-12 months
items.quote: Yes. Mostly our capex, which we announced earlier in '21-'22 with regard to our factory and the spinning plant, we already completed. And we also capitalized in the month of December only. So almost our announced capex plan is already almost completed. Now there is only a pending 2, 3 megawatt solar capacity we have to add in the coming 6 to 12 months.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin expanded 172 bps YoY to 35.6%; EBITDA margin expanded 109 bps YoY to 10.9%
items.quote: The gross profit margin for quarter three FY '25 stood at approximately 35.6% compared to 33.9% in quarter three FY '24, reflecting a 172 basis points expansion year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Nine months FY25 gross margin expanded 188 bps YoY to 34.8%; EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps YoY to 10.9%
items.quote: The gross profit margin for the first nine months of FY '25 stood at approximately 34.8% compared to 32.9% in the same period of FY '24, indicating a 188 basis points expansion year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Thermal segment grew 46% YoY in value and 41% in volume in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Thermal segment experienced remarkable year-on-year growth of 46% in value and 41% in volume.

items.statement: Force NXT brand grew 13.8% YoY in value and 23.3% in volume in Q3 FY25
items.quote: In Q3 FY '25, Force NXT brand saw a year-on-year increase of 13.8% in value and 23.3% year-on-year in volume.

items.statement: Modern trade and e-commerce share reached 11% of operating sales in Q3 FY25, exceeding FY26 target of 8-10% a year early
items.quote: In Q3 of FY '25, sales from modern trade and e-commerce channels accounted for approximately 11% of our total operating sales.

items.statement: South India contribution target raised to 13-15% in 2-3 years from current 8-9%
items.quote: So in two to three years' time period, we really want to see South India's contribution coming up from 8% to 9% to 13% to 15% kind of a contribution level.

items.statement: QIP fundraise deferred due to prevailing market conditions
items.quote: Now in view of the prevailing marketing condition, the company has decided to defer its plan to raise funds through the qualified QIP.

items.statement: Target to become debt-free by FY27 through internal accruals
items.quote: Mr. Shah, we have the target to debt-free the company by FY '27 as per our projection.

items.statement: Working capital cycle target of 140-145 days by FY26 and 135 days by FY27
items.quote: In terms of number of days, by FY '26, we really aspire to be somewhere at 140, 145 days. And by FY '27, I think we should come down to 135 days.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity reached 8 MW as of December 2024, up 2 MW in H1 FY25
items.quote: As of December '24, our total power generation capacity reached 8 megawatts, marking an increase of 2 megawatts in the first half of the fiscal year '24-'25.

items.statement: Quick commerce presence on Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, and nearing agreement with Blinkit
items.quote: Yes. So for quick commerce, we have already enrolled ourselves in Swiggy Instamart. We are present in Zepto also. And we are on the verge of completing our agreement with Blinkit.

items.statement: Pepe Innerfashion JV revenue doubled to INR 26 crores in nine months FY25 with INR 5 crores EBITDA
items.quote: Currently, we are standing at around INR26 crores. And for the first time, this is a first time -- first fiscal year where we are seeing good profitability also coming in with an overall EBITDA of around INR5 crores in INR26 crores sales.

items.statement: Adding 40 acres of vineyards by H2 FY25 and another 60 acres before Q2 FY26; commenced operations at new 50,000 sq. ft. winery building
items.quote: To strengthen our world -class wine making business, we are scaling up our production by adding 40 acres of vineyards by H2 FY25 with another 60 acres planned to be planted before Q2 FY26, ensuring the higher quality grape supply for our most premium wines. Additionally, we have commenced operations at our new 50,000 sq. ft. winery building.

items.statement: Gross margins are best in class at 77%-80% and have been very stable over many quarters
items.quote: I can tell you to the best of our knowledge, our gross margins are probably the best in class amongst the winemakers in the country and we are at around 77%-80% gross margin today and that has been very stable over the last many quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin dropped to 4.88% for 9M FY25 from 13.2% due to increased brand investments and new product launches
items.quote: On EBITDA, our EBITDA margin has dropped from about 13.2% to about 4.88% for the current 9 months and that is largely because the company has increased its brand investments and generally expenses in line with some new product launches, new initiatives, and many of those things will o nly begin to show its rewards in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin of 10%-12% in the near future
items.quote: We are aiming for around 10%-12% in the near future.

items.statement: Expecting normalized revenue growth of 10%-15% and aiming to do better than that
items.quote: But we expect to get back to some sort of normalized growth of between 10%-15%, and we expect to do better than that.

items.statement: New winery building and solar energy investments will save over Rs. 10 million annually
items.quote: The new winery building and the investments made in solar energy will result in savings of over Rs. 10 million in costs annually.

items.statement: Over 70% of sales come from premium and luxury wines
items.quote: Over 70% of our sales come from premium and luxury wines, and we remain geared to sustain our position here as the category further develops within AlcoBev.

items.statement: Canned wine portfolio grew 20% in FY24 and continues to be a focus area
items.quote: We have grown 20% in FY24, and it continues to be a good focus area.

items.statement: No drought concerns for vineyards in Maharashtra
items.quote: There is no such concern, just to clarify.

items.statement: Vineyard resort at Akluj expected to open in FY27
items.quote: The work on this is in advanced stages of planning and we expect to open in FY27, as a first of its kind property in India with multiple experiences besides vineyard tourism and luxury stays are being planned.

items.statement: Pour Room wine and coffee bar launched in Bangalore with plans to expand across major cities
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched 'Pour Room', which is our brand for wine and coffee bars in collaboration with Blue Tokai . The very first 'Pour Room' has opened at Koramangala in Bangalore to an encouraging response. This venture is set to expand across Bangalore and other major cities, offering consumers an experiential setting to enjoy our wines.

items.statement: RTD offering 'Shotgun' soft launched this quarter as category broadening initiative
items.quote: I am glad to share that our RTD offering, 'Shotgun', has been soft launched in the current quarter. 'Shotgun' is an accessible, all occasion wine-based drink and we see vast potential in it as category broadening initiative.

items.statement: Management indicates revenue growth guidance of around 60% for FY25, reconciling prior 60-70% and 50-60% ranges
items.quote: So, I said 60% to 70% in the last and Faruk sir said 50% to 60%. So, both have 60% common. You can take 60% as a common factor in both.

items.statement: Group order book stands at 3.8+ GW; standalone order book at 2.86 GW as of Jan 15, 2025
items.quote: As of today, if you look at our overall group level, we have a robust portfolio of 5.2 -plus gigawatts with 1.4 gigawatts already commissioned and a strong 3.8-plus gigawatts order book.

items.statement: IPP capex per MW ranges INR 3.25-3.95 crore for tracker-based plants excluding land (land taken on lease)
items.quote: you can say that depending upon the customization, depending upon the size of land and everything, the design, it might go from INR 3.25 crores to INR 3.95 crores depending upon how the land is.

items.statement: Strong demand pipeline from government institutions, private conglomerates, MSMEs; management sees potential to double or triple order book if bidding aggressively
items.quote: there are multiple tenders, multiple orders from the government institution from private conglomerates, from private players, individual MSMEs, mid-corporate kind of companies also. Everybody wants to go for renewable energy. So there are a lot of opportunities.

items.statement: No adverse government policy expected; all policies pro-renewable; green corridor development supports inter-state power transfer
items.quote: See at present, there is no such government policy. I think all the policies are pro renewable energy. In fact, in the latest budget also, they have shown in dication toward increasing the renewable energy

items.statement: Management expects to maintain PAT margins as IPP share grows from 13% to 21-22%
items.quote: PAT margin -- we'll be able to maintain the PAT margin because our business is a combination of CPP and IPP. I can tell you that going forward, our IPP component, which at present, I think, is 13% i.e. 13% is IPP this quarter and 87% is the CPP, which we plan to take it to the level of 22% to 21% kind of going forward.

items.statement: Order book stands at approximately 2.86 GW as of Jan 15
items.quote: At present, I have more than 2.86 gigawatt of order book, which is there as shown in the presentation.

items.statement: IPP capex: INR 6-8 crore/MW for wind portion, INR 3-3.85 crore/MW for solar portion
items.quote: See, hybrid, I mean, if I say, around INR 6 crores to INR 8 crores for the wind portion, you can say, INR 6 crores to INR 8 crores per megawatt for the wind portion. And when it comes to the solar portion, it ranges from INR 3 crores to INR 3.75 crores, INR 3.85 crores depending upon the land and everything.

items.statement: Demand for renewable energy is increasing due to government push and national targets
items.quote: No, I see the demand rather increasing in this space because a lot of players are entering into it. A lot of benefit. Government's push is more important. You see light of government has started on the renewable. They are also thinking of going into offshore windmill and everything.

items.statement: Module prices constitute around 60% of capex per MW
items.quote: It depends. I mean around 60%,would be the module price.

items.statement: O&M revenue charged at INR 4-5 lakh/MW/year with 2-3% escalation; land lease at INR 5 lakh/MW/year
items.quote: See, for what we say, C&I CPP, our revenue for O&M, I charge approximately INR 4 lakh to INR 5 lakh per megawatt per year with an escalation of 2% to 3% year -on-year. So at present, for example, if I have a CPP installed capacity of 362 MW, you can say that per year going forward, you'll see around, because a year or something we give free O&M. So from -- you can say once this all matures, you wi

items.statement: IPP share planned to increase from 13% to 21-22% going forward
items.quote: I can tell you that going forward, our IPP component, which at present, I think, is 13% i.e. 13% is IPP this quarter and 87% is the CPP, which we plan to take it to the level of 22% to 21% kind of going forward.

items.statement: No direct impact from US renewable policy as company is a developer with domestic contracts only
items.quote: See, you need to understand the U.S. market major decision will impact the manufacturers. We are not manufacturers. We are developers. We set up the entire plant and all my contracts at present are within our country, okay? So there is no direct or indirect link to the U.S. market or anything.

items.statement: Green hydrogen plans at nascent stage; will announce once finalized
items.quote: Yes, we are at nascent stage. We are looking to that. See, as I told you, if the technology needs to be supported, we will leverage on this technology. So we are in discussion. But at present, they are at a nascent stage, and we will shortly be coming in public domain once we finalize all those things.

items.statement: International opportunities being studied at nascent stage; will not disclose until constructive roadmap ready
items.quote: See, as I told you, international opportunities -- we are approached by international players. We are looking out for international. We are doing study on international markets also. But all these are at a nascent stage. We will not be coming out in public domain until unless we have some constructive road map for that.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to be minimum 60% and will surely surpass
items.quote: We will be minimum is 60%. We'll surely surpass.

items.statement: Reaffirm FY25 guidance with year-on-year growth on pro forma combined basis and accelerated growth trajectory in FY26
items.quote: We reaffirm our FY'25 guidance with year-on-year growth on a pro forma combined basis for the full year and with an accelerated growth trajectory in FY'26.

items.statement: Rs 2.3 billion capex invested in 9 months ending December 2024 for capacity expansion
items.quote: In the 9 months ending December '25, our CAPEX investment is Rs. 2.3 billion, which has been allocated to capacity expansion, ensuring that we stay ahead of the demand curve.

items.statement: RFQs increased 2x year-on-year in 9 months FY25 reflecting strong inbound inquiries
items.quote: We at Suven and Cohance continue to receive higher number of RFQs, it is about 2x in the 9 months versus last year, which is a reflection of the confidence that leading global pharma and select biotech comp anies have in our capabilities

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin at 38.7% in Q3 FY25 and 34.8% for 9 months FY25
items.quote: Revenue growth in Quarter 3 has been 40% year-on-year, driven by robust demand across all business units and our adjusted EBITDA margin is at 38.7%. For the 9 months of FY'25, our revenue growth is 5% year-on-year, reinforcing our resilience and long-term scalability with adjusted EBITDA margins at 34.8%.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals CDMO challenges bottomed out with early signs of demand stabilization and recovery trend
items.quote: In line with our communication in Q2, the challenges have bottomed out. And we have started seeing the recovery trend with early signs of demand stabilization.

items.statement: Phase-3 pipeline expanded to 15 projects with 9 active molecules, up from 12 projects and 7 molecules last quarter
items.quote: This brings us the Phase-3 projects to 15 with 9 active molecules, which was 12 at 7 molecules when we spoke last quarter.

items.statement: Acquired Sapala Organics for oligonucleotide chemistry and NJ Bio for end-to-end ADC CRDMO capabilities
items.quote: Sapala Organics, which establishes our expertise in oligonucleotide chemistry, allowing us to expand into high-growth nucleic acid therapeutic segments. NJ Bio, this establishes our end-to-end CRDMO leadership in antibody drug conjugates through our ability to support global pharma from early stage development to full-scale commercial manufacturing.

items.statement: Capacity constraints not expected for near-term needs; flexible capex approach for new commercial products
items.quote: Capacity side, as you understand when the cyclical nature was slightly hitting us, we don't have any capacity challenge right now and we have enough invested in the existing site and also in additional site of Suryapet.

items.statement: NJ Bio acquisition completely self-funded with no loans taken
items.quote: I think during the acquisition call, we had explained that it is completely self-funded. There is no loan that we have taken to fund the entire acquisition.

items.statement: Cohance merger shareholder approval received with 99.99% votes; NCLT meeting scheduled February 18, expected effective in 2-4 months
items.quote: With respect to Cohance merger – the shareholder approval was received with 99.99% votes in our favor. The final N CLT meeting is scheduled for February 18th. Subject to regulatory approvals, the merger is expected to be effective within the next 2 to 4 months

items.statement: Cash generation of Rs 3.2 billion in 9 months ending December 2024
items.quote: And cash generation remains good, with Rs. 3.2 billion being generated during the same period.

items.statement: Onboarded one of top 5 global pharma leaders for early to mid-phase projects
items.quote: We have onboarded one of the top 5 global pharma leaders for early to mid-phase projects, which solidifies our strategic value.

items.statement: Oligo GMP manufacturing facility for Amidites expected ready by end of calendar year 2025
items.quote: the first step is that we are getting ready for the GMP manufacturing of Amidites, which is the first step for O ligos. And that facility should be ready sometime towards the end of this calendar year

items.statement: Cross-pollination of ADC services (payload, linker, bioconjugation) takes 3-6 quarters for late-stage products
items.quote: If the product is of about 2A, 2B, and Phase-3 level, it's 3 to 6 quarters of a time where the qualification has to happen, samples have to be submitted, site has to be submitted.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR700 crores-plus with EBITDA margin 21% plus/minus 100 bps
items.quote: We anticipate to receive orders from Kaiga 5 & 6 reactor soon and also from the various refurbishment reactors almost close to 5 reactors, which we are looking forward. We're looking Building Nation with E:icceptlonal Engmteri ng forward for a very strong Q4 as well and falling in line with the guidance given by us with INR700 crores-plus revenues overall with EBITDA of 21% plus minus 100 basis po

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth 30% YoY with EBITDA margin 24%
items.quote: Based on the kind of work we have done over the last couple of years, looking at the future roadmap for the company, we predict a 30% revenue growth in FY '26 and similarly an equivalent kind of growth moving forward for the next 2 years as well with a progressive improvement in EBITDA starting with 24% for next year FY '26 and 2 percentage basis points -- like 200 basis points improvement each ye

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin 26%, FY28 EBITDA margin 28%
items.quote: And moving forward, FY '26 to FY '28, based on what I've explained earlier in the call, with the various projects and qualifications that we are going through, we are expecting a comfortable revenue growth of 30% year-on-year basis consistently for the next 3 years. And with improved margins of 24% in FY '26 and then moving on to 26% in FY '27 and stabilizing at 28% in FY '28.

items.statement: Expect INR1,000 crores nuclear orders (Kaiga 5&6 plus 5 refurbishment reactors) over next 3-6 months
items.quote: So overall, we're expecting close to 1000 Crs of orders, in history, it never happened, but finally, it's happening now. Close to about INR1,000 crores of orders, which can flow into MTAR over the next 6 months.

items.statement: Clean Energy fuel cells: expect >INR430 crores execution next year, majority orders already received
items.quote: We expect to execute more than INR430 crores in fuel cells moving forward for the next year, for which we have already received the majority of the orders, and there could be an upside to this based on the commencement of execution of AEP orders.

items.statement: MNC Aerospace: expect INR125 crores revenue in FY26 (first articles + batch production), major volume breakthrough in FY27
items.quote: For Aerospace and Defence, A&D. Srinivas Reddy: Yes. So Aerospace and Defence would really drastically improve. Like, for example, next year, we'll be doing around -- only in MNC aerospace itself, we'll be doing about INR125 crores next year, which is a phenomenal growth, right? And that's a combination of first articles and volume production and then FY '27 will be much larger than that

items.statement: Oil & Gas: first articles now, exclusive plant setup, volume production from FY27 targeting INR150-180 crores first year
items.quote: We already received the purchase orders for the first articles, which we are doing now. items.statement: Battery storage (Fluence Energy): proto units by June, volume production progressive from FY26, real ramp-up INR2-3 crores+ in FY27
items.quote: But we will see the real ramp up happening, which will be close to about INR2 crores, INR3 crores plus in FY '27, with respect to the battery storage systems as well.

items.statement: Plan INR60-80 crores debt-funded capex next year for oil & gas facility and bottleneck removal
items.quote: So next year, we are planning to take a debt of around INR60 crores to INR80 crores for the oil and gas and other areas and remaining we will spend from our internal accruals.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin target ~24% (+/-100 bps) to meet full-year 21% guidance
items.quote: And then the margins also, to maintain that margin, we'll be expecting close t o EBITDA margin of 24% for Q4 is what we're looking at is plus minus 100 basis points. So that's how we'll be able to achieve the overall annual margin guidance what we have given and the revenue guidance what we have

items.statement: EBITDA margins similar across divisions (~20%+), Bloom now in line with others due to operating leverage
items.quote: At the margins, across all divisions, we are pretty much having similar margins. Less than 20% margins we don't take normally. But in case of space, we have little bit more margins, say around 5% to 7% because of the free -issue raw material. Like some 4 -5 years, 3 years back, maybe Bloom is lower margin compared in. But today, with operating leverage, Bloom is also in line with the other margins

items.statement: Civil Nuclear: INR16 crores YTD, expect INR30 crores Q4, FY26 execution ~INR75 crores from WIP
items.quote: While we have executed INR16 crores of orders year-to-date for Civil Nuclear Power , we expect to execute around INR30 crores of orders in Q4. The execution of FY '26 is projected to be around INR75 crores as we have built a work -in-progress for existing orders, that can be dispatched in FY '26.

items.statement: Defence: INR12.2 crores YTD, FY25 annual ~INR30 crores, FY26 projection INR40 crores+ with exponential growth from FY26
items.quote: Moving on to Defence. The revenues stand at INR12.2 crores year-to-date and annual execution is estimated to be around INR30 crores. This year, we have witnessed an increase in inflow of orders and our Defence order book is expected to grow further over the coming quarters because of which we shall -- have an exponential growth in Defence starting from FY '26. We project around INR40 crores-plus o

items.statement: Target FY2026 revenue mix: 75% flights, 25% non-air (currently 86% flights)
items.quote: So, our target is that in FY2026, we should be able to say 75% of our business came from flight and 25% business came from all other sectors, which right now is at 86%.

items.statement: Middle East GBR grew 227% YoY to INR 170 crores in Q3 FY2025; growth seen as sustainable but lumpy
items.quote: Our Dubai operations have also shown remarkable progress, showing a year-on-year growth of 227% and the gross booking revenue stood at INR 170 crores in Q3 FY2025.

items.statement: Hotel nights booked grew 172% YoY to 2.5 lakh in Q3 FY2025, contributing 11.1% of GBR
items.quote: This quarter, total nights booked stood at 2.5 lakhs, reflecting a significant 172% year-on-year growth and contributing 11.1% to the gross booking revenue.

items.statement: Reduced discount rate from 3.8% to 3% QoQ while GBR still grew 7% YoY
items.quote: We took the call of reducing our discounts for this particular quarter and yet there was an increase in GBR, which we see as a positive sign.

items.statement: EV bus manufacturing initiative underway; will take a few more quarters to come to shape
items.quote: So, the EV buses, what we started off in the manufacturing mix, that is going to take more few quarters' time to completely come in shape.

items.statement: Promoter Nishant Pitti sold 1.4% stake; public commitment not to sell further shares this year
items.quote: Nishant has already taken a public stand saying that he has sold 1.4%, not 14%, which was incorrectly mentioned in the media. And yes, for this year, there will be no selling from the promoter side.

items.statement: Acquired Planet Education Australia to enter study tourism sector
items.quote: Furthering our expansion into specialized travel services, we have entered the study tourism sector with the acquisition of Planet Education Australia.

items.statement: Plant-6 brownfield project acquired last quarter will be built out to reach INR1,000 crores revenue capacity.
items.quote: along with Plant-6 which is the brownfield project that we acquired last quarter, we will build that out and then by finishing that we will reach INR1,000 crores

items.statement: Upcoming capex primarily for Plant-6 oral solid expansion; layout and machinery selection in progress.
items.quote: I think that one upcoming capex will be primarily for Plant-6 bringing up which is the oral solid expansion and we are in the layout and machinery identification selection process.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.3% for 9M FY25 and 12.6% for Q3 FY25 despite injectable facility depreciation increase.
items.quote: EBITDA surged by 22% Y-o-Y to INR68.6 crores, 12.3% margin for 9-month FY '25 and by 21% Y-o-Y to INR24.6 crores, 12.6% margin for Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Injectable facility expected to first cross breakeven then contribute to operating leverage over 3-4 years.
items.quote: as the injection facility starts to generate revenue and it will first crossover breakeven and afterwards start contributing to the margin so operating leverage will begin to come in the numbers

items.statement: Long-term ROCE target around 27%-28% despite ongoing capex for oral solids expansion.
items.quote: in long range we want to stay 27% - 28% likes of ROCE and more

items.statement: Trade Generics & Institutional vertical grew 44% Y-o-Y in 9M FY25 and 74% Y-o-Y in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: CDMO vertical grew 15% Y-o-Y in 9M FY25 and 8% Y-o-Y in Q3 FY25; volume growth historically flat to low single digits.

items.statement: Schedule M enforcement driving smaller competitor closures; compliant players like Windlas benefiting from customer shift.

items.statement: API price reductions passed through in cost-plus model; conversion impacted but neutral over long term.
