But having said that, there has also been increase in past and so API prices tend to have some impact because ours is a cost plus model. In the long run it gets pacified for plus as well as minus in API prices.

items.statement: Existing order book in place for injectable production; products ready for commercialization from stability batches.
items.quote: There is already some order book in place for our existing production happening and products getting ready for commercialization and out of stability batches.

items.statement: Sufficient oral solids/liquids capacity for ~INR800 crores revenue with Plant-2 expansion now online.
items.quote: So we have sufficient capacity for our oral solids and oral liquids business to reach across about INR800 crores. This is aside of injectables.

items.statement: Targeting KFC brand contribution margin of 19-20% at about 100,000 ADS over a few quarters
items.quote: we are targeting KFC to get to 19 to 20% margin at about 100,000 ADS , and we are tracking on that . It will take us a few quarters to be able to get there , but on an overall basis , we are confident that the kind of measures we have taken and once they start to kick in, we will be able to see the full results at about 100,000 KFC ADS with 19 to 20% brand contribution margins.

items.statement: Plan to add 20-25 KFC stores in Thailand (8-9% growth) and target 3-4% SSSG for ~11-12% revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: As far as the store growth is concerned, Thailand represents the largest opportunity. We plan to add about 20 to 25 stores, which is 8 to 9% of the stores that we have. And then on top , we are targeting a SSSG of about 3 to 4% which should give us about 11 to 12% revenue growth.

items.statement: Will moderate Pizza Hut expansion further; future expansion dependent on brand performance
items.quote: Going forward, as we have spoken in the past, we will be moderating Pizza Hut expansion, and you will see even further lower numbers versus what we have done so far. So, we continue to remain bullish on KFC . On the other hand, we have added new brands. We are monitoring Pizza Hut performance very closely. And therefore, depending on the brand performance, we will take a final call on the numbers.

items.statement: Focus on small format stores for capital efficiency and stronger payback potential
items.quote: A key driver of this has been our focus on small format stores over the past few years which are highly capital efficient and offer stronger payback potential.

items.statement: Consolidated brand contribution margin improved 70 bps QoQ to 14.3% due to sales leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: The brand contribution for Q3 FY25 stood at 14.3%, higher by 70 basis points versus the previous quarter. Improvement in brand contribution was mainly on account of sales leverage and fresh measures on cost optimization in the Indian and Nigerian operations.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution margin improved 60 bps QoQ to 17.2% due to sales leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: The brand contribution margin at 17.2% for the current quarter saw an improvement of 60 basis points because of better sales leverage and cost optimization measures.

items.statement: Pizza Hut brand contribution margin at 2.1% in Q3; margin improvement expected from next quarter via marketing cost optimization and fresh cost measures
items.quote: we will see margin improvement coming from next quarter because we are optimizing the marketing cost in Pizza Hut versus what we have done in the last 6 to 9 months. At the same time, we have taken some fresh cost optimization measures also in Pizza Hut as well as KFC, which will start to yield the results from January onwards.

items.statement: Costa Coffee brand contribution margin improved to 16.9% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Brand contribution in Q3 saw an improvement and stood at 16.9%.

items.statement: International brand contribution margin improved 60 bps QoQ to 16.6% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Brand contribution margin at 16.6% saw an improvement of 60 basis points versus Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Gross margin dropped 60 bps QoQ to 68.7% due to food inflation in oil, chicken, cheese, coffee beans
items.quote: The gross margin for the consolidated business was 68.7%, a drop of 60 basis points versus the previous quarter. The impact on gross margins was primarily due to food inflation that we have seen in core brands, driven by rising oil, chicken, cheese and coffee bean pricing.

items.statement: Seeing green shoots of recovery in metros and large cities during festive season; value menu items driving volumes
items.quote: While the overall consumer sentiment remained a little subdued , during the festive season our QSR in general and DIL witnessed some green shoots of recovery in the metro and large cities. For the budget conscious consumers, Value Menu Items such as KFC Roll Variants and Snackers were major attractions during the festive season.

items.statement: Three new QSR brands planned for launch from Q1 FY26 (April onwards)
items.quote: Yes, we are on track from Quarter 1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Opened first food court under JV with PVR INOX at Kota (51% economic interest); not fully consolidated per auditor opinion
items.quote: We opened our first food court under the strategic tie-up with PVR INOX at Kota. DIL has an economic interest of 51% in the new Company. Please note that this entity shall be consolidated in accordance with Accounting Standards 28.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 sales volume trimmed to 4.6-4.8 million sq ft and sales value to INR 2,400-2,700 crores
items.quote: Based on our sustainable sales expectation for Q4 and contribution from the 2 launches that are expected this quarter, we are constrained to trim our full year number to about 4.6 - 4.8 million square feet. Sales values go down to some extent.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 handover target of 1,500 units vs 1,300 units last year
items.quote: We are setting ourselves with a targeted Q4 handovers of about 1,500 units as compared to 1,300 units that we did last year.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin (excl. other income) guided at 22-25%, PBT margin 9-11%, PAT margin 8-10%
items.quote: We believe EBITDA without other income can reasonably stabilize between 22% - 25% at any point of time on an annual basis. Quarter-to-quarter fluctuations will always be there because of base effect.

items.statement: Medium-term target to nearly triple annual revenue by FY28 from ~INR 1,000 crores base
items.quote: On a medium-term basis, as we have said, we are looking at more than nearly tripling our revenues on an annual revenue recognition by FY '28, which is a 3 years plan that we have articulated publicly.

items.statement: Next year (FY26) top-line growth of at least 20% driven by 3-5 million sq ft handover momentum
items.quote: handover momentum of our -- completion and handover momentum of about 3 million to 5 million square f eet should give us at least a 20% growth on an annual basis in the top line. Can be higher, but for now, I will stay with 20

items.statement: New project investments of ~INR 40 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We made new project investments about INR ~40 crores. Therefore, we ended up consuming cash from closing cash and equivalents.

items.statement: Acquired 3 new projects with 1.1 million sq ft development potential and GDV of INR 850-1,000 crores
items.quote: Shriram Properties has acquired development rights for 3 new projects in Yelahanka, which is North Bangalore; Electronic City in South Bangalore; and Koyambedu in Chennai with a combined development potential of 1.1 million square feet and a gross development value of about INR 850 crores to INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Target to double launch pipeline from 17 million sq ft to 30-35 million sq ft over next 12-24 months
items.quote: As we have set out to achieve our medium-term aspiration, we need to nearly double our pipeline from 17 million square fee t launch pipeline to over 30 million square feet in the next 12 to 18 months, max 24 months

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin ~31%, EBITDA margin ~24% (incl. other operating revenue), PBT margin ~8%
items.quote: Overall, margins remained healthy, that clearly shows that the projects that are getting recognized have a healthy margin profile. Gross margins are about 31%. EBITDA margins were about 24%, 8% PBT margins.

items.statement: Portfolio price hikes ~5% in FY25 so far after ~20% growth in FY23-24; mid-market avg realization ~INR 6,700/sq ft
items.quote: Overall, price remains stable. Our portfolio price hike is in the range of about 5% during the year so far, appreciable modesty in price hikes because we have had very robust price hikes over the last 2 years, 20% growth in our portfolio price averages between FY '23 and '24.

items.statement: Customer activity revived strongly post festive season (late Oct 2024); no demand slowdown, only administrative delays
items.quote: Customer activities have revived post the beginning of festive season, midway through October-November 2024. We have seen a remarkable bounce back in customer activity; therefore, we remain positive about the underlying market conditions.

items.statement: Kolkata launch contingent on KMDA final approval (50% probability by mid-March); royalty dispute provisioning continues (INR 4 cr in Q3)
items.quote: The plan approval is received. But the KMDA last final approval is awaited still, and therefore, I'm not really raising hope on it, but it has a equal probability of coming through towards the second half of March.

items.statement: No definitive promoter buyback plans; index fund inclusion not yet eligible due to size
items.quote: On the question of promoter buying, there are no definitive plans right now. We'll come back to you if there any plans which is approved by the promoters as well as the shareholders.

items.statement: Land monetization in Chennai yielded INR 93 cr cash (mostly Q4); INR 5-6 cr capital gain recognized in Q3
items.quote: We have completed land monetization in Chennai and the cash flows of about INR 93 crores are received now, and that has augmented additional capital for growth for us.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced to INR 470 cr, net debt INR 400 cr; target net debt reduction but balanced with growth capital needs
items.value: Gross INR 470 cr, Net INR 400 cr
items.quote: Today, we've got a gross debt of INR 470 crores, net debt of INR 400 crores. So even on a net basis, we are down from INR 440 crores to INR 400 crores on a gross basis, reflecting these repayments, we have come down substantially from INR 631 crores to INR 470 crores.

items.statement: Current financial year topline will be more or less flat; bottom-line growth much higher, in line with current run rate
items.quote: So, to conclude, I wish to reiterate, while the current financial year topline will be more or less flat as indicated in the past, the bottom-line growth would be much higher, more or less in line with our current run rate we have achieved till now.

items.statement: 9-month bronze bushing sales around Rs. 60 crores, on track to cross Rs. 80 crores annual target
items.quote: Thus, the 9 months year-to-date sales for bronze bushing is around Rs. 60 crores plus, very much in line with our expectation of crossing Rs. 80 crores annual sales target of bushing this financial year.

items.statement: Major sourcing contract for cages with large global customer concluded; considerable additional business expected from second-half of FY26
items.quote: As informed to stock exchanges, we have concluded major sourcing contract for cages with a large global customer and we should start seeing considerable additional business coming to us in India from second-half of Financial Year 2026.

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 170 crores capex for FY25, primarily for new plant, building and equipment
items.quote: So, let me start with the second part, the CAPEX number, we are targeting for FY25, about Rs. 170 crores, somewhere in that range for FY25 and primarily attributable to the new plant and building and all equipment coming in.

items.statement: Greenfield site commissioning in phases; one subsection starting end of this quarter or early next quarter, all capacities online by end of Q1 next year
items.quote: So, this is going to be in a phase commissioning . One of the subsections will be starting pretty soon towards the end of this quarter or early next quarter and then most of the things will come online. All the capacities should come online by the end of 1st Quarter next year.

items.statement: India cage demand soft in Q3 due to year-end inventory reduction by MNC bearing companies; normal purchasing expected to resume in Q4
items.quote: If I talk of cages, this quarter was bit soft in India typically due to yearend inventory reduct ion pressure felt by our major MNC bearing companies operating in India. Since their overseas parent follow calendar year as their accounting year, I believe that normal purchasing will be resumed in quarter 4 and we look forward to a little bit improvement on demand from their side

items.statement: Domestic cage business expected to grow 8%-10% per annum in Q4; softness seen as cyclical, not structural
items.quote: We believe this quarter Q4 we should see India, the big business also again starting to grow 8%-10% per annum. That is what our assumption is. We don't see this as a structural issue. It is more like a cyclical issue.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 17%-18% long-term; currently 14%-15% range including Romania losses; India at 20% run rate
items.quote: But long term our target is the consolidated margin for 14% to 15% our target is to take it to 17% to 18% but it is very difficult for me to predict anything right now.

items.statement: Romania subsidiary unlikely to achieve operating breakeven in current financial year; losses to be reduced and capped at manageable level on combined basis with China
items.quote: However, Romania will not be in a position to achieve operating breakeven in the current financial year, given the fact that overall demand challenges continue. However, on a combined basis between our two key subsidiaries, I expect these losses to be reduced and capped at a manageable level in this current financial year.

items.statement: Focus on bronze bushing growth (70%-80% YoY) and stamping components for EV/battery vehicles as long-term growth drivers
items.quote: We will probably grow to the tune of almost 70 %-80% year-over-year on that segment last year to this year. And we expect that that will continue. That is not necessarily the market. The end market itself is growing, but application within end market is shifting from one product to another there we come in and we are able to grow and we think that that could be a continued additional growth opport

items.statement: Peak incremental opportunity from domestic customers' China Plus One CAPEX estimated around Rs. 200 crores for cage supply
items.quote: Our guesstimate is that this could be around Rs. 200 crores at the peak opportunity.

items.statement: Price reduction in India due to metal cost pass-through mechanism, mainly steel prices reduced
items.quote: With reference to the pricing change, there is a price change as we discussed in the last quarter also and as you know price through mechanism and hence the price has been reduced because of the metal has reduced on both front and majorly on the steel front.

items.statement: Japan-based customer revenue flat at ~Rs. 50 crores year-to-date; projects delayed but development progressing well
items.quote: I think a number for Japan based customer remains largely flat versus the previous year, I think about Rs. 50 crores is a year-to-date revenue from Japan based customer or not Japanese but Japanese customer, Japanese companies across the globe.

items.statement: No green shoots visible in Europe/US for FY26; high uncertainty due to trade war; unable to project clearly
items.quote: Having said that, right now we are not in position to really clearly project a lot of uncertainties in the US with this trade war, the things are still a developing situation. We have a very clear picture right now. Having said that, we are (Inaudible) unable to comment anything from here on in general.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance approximately Rs. 300 crores
items.quote: the cash and bank balance we have around Rs. 300 crores approximately.

items.statement: Incurred Rs. 70.8 crores capex in Q3 at consolidated level; continuing to spend on committed capex for future growth
items.quote: The company has incurred an overall CAPEX of Rs. 70.8 crore s in Quarter 3 at a consolidated level and continued to spend on the CAPEX size as committed for future growth.

items.statement: Expect to produce 20,000-25,000 tons of bromine in FY26 including captive consumption
items.quote: We expect to produce nearly 20,000 tons to 25,000 tons of bromine in FY ‘26, including captive consumption.

items.statement: Target 1 million to 1.2 million tons run rate for industrial salt in coming quarters
items.quote: We are optimistic about achieving 1 million to 1.2 million tons run rate in the coming quarters and constantly working on improving the supply chain as well on this front.

items.statement: Plan to invest Rs. 3,000 crores in compound semiconductor facility via subsidiary SiCSem Private Limited
items.quote: Through our subsidiary, SiCSem Private Limited, we will eventually invest about Rs. 3,000 crores in a compound semiconductor facility, the first of its kind in the country.

items.statement: Committed $12 million investment in Offgrid Energy Labs for zinc bromide battery technology
items.quote: Our Company has committed a total investment of $12 million in Offgrid Energy Labs Inc, Delaware, US, a Company specializing in zinc bromide battery technology.

items.statement: Order book healthy with bromine and salt volumes locked in for next 6-12 months
items.quote: Our order book continues to be healthy. And for the next six months to 12 months, both bromine and salt have locked in volumes.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 38% from previous quarter
items.quote: EBITDA for the Company stood at Rs. 963 million in Q3 FY ’25, with a margin of 38%, an improvement over last quarter.

items.statement: Bromine prices stable with slight improvements; salt pricing slightly below last year's contract levels but supported by freight savings
items.quote: Prices have remained stable, and in some cases we have seen slight improvements as well.

items.statement: Seeing demand recovery in bromine post Chinese New Year and China stimulus; agrochem revival expected in Q1 FY26
items.quote: While post to Chinese New Year, for our own business, we expect a partial recovery in both demand and pricing. And we are seeing this uptick happen as we speak.

items.statement: Captive bromine consumption for derivatives to grow from 5-7% currently to 20-25% in FY26
items.quote: So, currently this quarter our share for captive will be around 5% to 7%, which will obviously grow next year, next full year. And this can exceed about 20%, 25%, that's the kind of numbers we are looking at.

items.statement: Lease renewal approval from government still pending with no fresh update
items.quote: It's I think a work in progress. I do not have any fresh update as such. But I think we continue to await the approval.

items.statement: Semiconductor project financing mix includes Odisha state subsidy and pending ISM central government approval
items.quote: A good part of this CAPEX will be provided as a subsidy by the state government, which is approved by the Odisha State government under Odisha Semiconductor and Fabless Policy 2023. Our project is also pending under review with Indian Semiconductor Mission.

items.statement: Oren Hydrocarbon: plan to restart two units this quarter and two more in coming months; meaningful revenues expected soon
items.quote: We plan to restart two units this quarter with two more in the coming months. This business complements our CBF, which primarily caters to the oil and gas industry.

items.statement: SOP trials progressing well; pilot runs targeted pre-monsoon with ramp-up post-monsoon
items.quote: We are in the process of initiating the pilot runs and trials at site, basically moving it from lab where it's been tested, and the results are what we wanted. So, that should happen, we are aiming to do it pre-monsoon.

items.statement: Flame retardant technology transfer discussions restarted; prefer end-user contracts over buy-back arrangements
items.quote: We have restarted I think the dialogue on transfer of technology on flame retardant, given that I think we have always believed in that business being a natural extension of our derivatives business.

items.statement: Promoter pledge at ~3%, not expected to exceed 5% in near future; not linked to Archean business funding
items.quote: I think at the moment we are at about 3%, so I anticipate we should not be crossing more than 5% now or in the near future.

items.statement: Service revenue expected to reach INR 1,000 crores per annum soon
items.quote: It is also noteworthy to note that the service revenue for Landmark will soon touch INR1,000 crores per annum number, which is a big milestone in our journey.

items.statement: Personnel expenses reduced to 3.9% and other expenses to 3.5% of pro forma revenue by Q3 FY25, ahead of end-2025 target
items.quote: We had set a target to reduce personnel expenses and other expenses below 4% on pro forma revenue by end of 2025. Through the effective implementation of cost optimization initiatives, this objective was successfully achieved ahead of its schedule. As of quarter 3, the personnel expenses stood at 3.9%, while the other expenses were reduced to 3.5%.

items.statement: New car inventory reduced to near normal 35 days, among best in industry
items.quote: I'm happy to report that we have further reduced our inventory and now it stands at near normal 35 days. I have reason to believe that this is amongst the best in the industry.

items.statement: Capex for 23 new stores around INR 70 crores; total capex for 9 months around INR 125 crores
items.quote: So 23 store, the capex would be around INR70 crores. And then we have some other capex also for the existing store and the vehicle purchase. So total capex for the 9 months is around INR125 crores.

items.statement: Next year capex expected to be substantially lower than FY25's ~INR 75 crores for new stores
items.quote: But our historic numbers have not been at all anywhere near what we did last year, as far as the capex is concerned.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA INR 69.5 crores at 5.82% margin on reported revenue, highest in last 8 quarters
items.quote: The company has reported the EBITDA of INR69.5 crores at a 5.82% margin on reported revenue versus INR54.8 crores at 6.4% margin in Q2 FY '25 and INR67.1 crores at 6.99% margin in Q3 FY '24. In Q2 FY '25 (this was said erroneously. It should be read as “In Q3FY25”) the company recorded the highest quarterly EBITDA in the last 8 quarters.

items.statement: Gross margins pressured by new outlets where service contribution is half of mature outlets; expected to improve as workshops ramp up
items.quote: In the service business, new outlets are currently contributing half as much as existing one, impacting gross margin. However, service revenue is steady in new outlet increasing each month. And once these outlets reach their full potential, overall gross margins are expected to improve.

items.statement: Mercedes-Benz ultra-high-end models (>INR 1.5 cr) have similar margin percentage but higher absolute profit
items.quote: Arnav, the margin percentage is more or less similar. So in absolute terms, we make more money. But in percentage terms, it is same.

items.statement: Indian EV penetration expected to reach 7-8% of overall market this year from ~2% last year
items.quote: Now our view is that this number will go to maybe around 7%, 8% to begin with of the overall market and kind of stabilize there.

items.statement: Auto industry volume growth expected to be similar to last year's 4% in calendar year 2024
items.quote: As of now, the industry guys are talking about a similar growth. So it's not going to be a flying kind of a year.

items.statement: New Kia Syros expected to add ~15% to Kia volumes this year; MG Windsor largest selling EV in India
items.quote: The new Kia Syros, which was launched in January, has garnered a positive response, and we expect it to add around 15% to our Kia volumes this year.

items.statement: Global auto industry uncertainty due to US policy changes, tariff threats, and OEM alliance shifts (e.g., Honda-Nissan called off)
items.quote: The global auto industry is going through quite an uncertain time currently. The change in guard in USA has resulted in environmental goals of many countries being reset. The threat of tariff has also made the situation more complex.

items.statement: EV service revenue per car estimated 13-14% lower than ICE at 40% gross margin, ~5% impact on EV cars
items.quote: The global -- and we are not able to kind of give an exact number, but the global data and the news from China -- and all what we have is showing us that there is around 13%, 14% lesser revenue as far as the EV is concerned at a 40% gross margin, that will be around 5% kind of impact on the EV cars.

items.statement: Total debt INR 560 crores including INR 150 crores interest-free Mercedes demo car debt; reduced quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: overall debt is INR560 crores, Devesh. Out of that around INR150 crores debt is from the Mercedes-Benz demo car, which is the interest free. Sanjay Thakker: What has happened as far as the debt is concerned, Devesh, is that we have been able to reduce that quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Target of 65,000 POS machines for full year FY25
items.quote: We have installed over 52,000 POS machines in the first 3 quarters of the current financial year and well on course to achieve our target of 65,000 machines for the full year FY '25.

items.statement: DBJ segment expected to break even in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We expected to -- the DBJ segment to break even in the next 2 quarters or so, post which our numbers should improve.

items.statement: Investing in sales team and technological backbone for long-term growth
items.quote: Management has taken several initiatives, including strengthening the sales team and the technological backbone to grow this business at a brisk pace in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Added 51 new clients, 325 new end customers, and 6,744 new retail touch points in first 9 months
items.quote: During the first 9 months of this year, we added 51 new clients, 325 new end customers, and 6,744 new retail touch points in our retail cash management business.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 19.9% in Q3 FY25, up 221 bps YoY and 89 bps QoQ
items.quote: The consolidated margin for the quarter stood at 19.9%, an improvement of 221 basis points over t he same period of the previous year and 89 basis points over the previous

items.statement: Acemoney recorded EBITDA margin of close to 25% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: This quarter, we recorded a margin of close to about 25% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Management confident of further margin improvement in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The management is confident of further improvement in margins in the last quarter of the current year as well.

items.statement: Marginal degrowth in cash pickup revenue due to mix of points added
items.quote: The marginal degrowth is on account of, I would say, the mix of points that we have added in this period.

items.statement: Core retail cash management reported muted growth due to sluggish consumption sectors
items.quote: The sluggishness in the consumption sectors in the economy had its impact on the core business of retail cash management in the current quarter, which reported a muted growth in this quarter over the same period last year.

items.statement: Expect better core business growth depending on economic performance
items.quote: Depending on the economic performance, we are positive that it will exhibit better growth than what we witnessed in the current quarter.

items.statement: Direct clients now account for about 16% of standalone revenue
items.quote: We continued to report strong growth in our direct client segment, which now accounts for about 16% of our stand-alone revenues.

items.statement: Acemoney revenue INR112 million in Q3 FY25, 100% sequential growth
items.quote: Radiant Acemoney had an excellent quarter and has clocked INR112 million in revenues for this quarter, which is 100% sequential growth for the previous quarter.

items.statement: Cash losses remain lowest in industry by wide margin due to robust risk management
items.quote: Our cash losses continue to be the lowest in the industry by a wide margin, a result of a robust risk management framework.

items.statement: Net cash INR695 million as of December; debt increase temporary for month-end requirements
items.quote: INR695 million, that's the net cash available as of December.

items.statement: Dividend policy to remain on track
items.quote: Yes, we have a stated dividend policy and are likely to remain on track.

items.statement: Expect to cross FY24 numbers in FY26
items.quote: we expect this trend to continue and hopefully we w ill cross FY '23 numbers in '26 -- '24 numbers in '26

items.statement: Expect Q4 FY25 to be better than Q3 and FY26 revenue growth of 20-25% over FY25 with profitability back to FY24 levels
items.quote: We are expecting a revenue growth of about 20%, 25% in FY '26 over FY '25. In terms of profitability, we should be back on track of where we left over in FY '24.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 expected to be better than Q2 FY25 and Q3 FY25
items.quote: We are confident. We are hopeful that Q4 definitely would be better than Q2.

items.statement: JLR 3S facility in Nagpur to commence by September FY26 with existing facility refurbishment
items.quote: Operations are expected to commence by September FY '26.

items.statement: Four Ather Space 3.0 locations (3 Kerala, 1 Tamil Nadu) to commence in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Operations at all four locations are expected to commence in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margins dropped ~2.5% YoY due to higher discounts; EBITDA margin 2.5% in Q3 and 3.5% for 9M FY25
items.quote: Our gross margins Q3 to Q3 have dropped by about 2.5%.

items.statement: Maruti discounts doubled from ~INR6,500 to ~INR12,000 per vehicle in 9M FY25; expect Q4 discounts to return to FY24 levels
items.quote: On average per car, we were nearly double the discounts that we were giving to the customers, nearly from INR6,500 levels to nearly INR12,000 per car.

items.statement: Arena volumes declined 14% YoY in 9M FY25 but grew 3% in Jan FY25; Nexa grew 17% YoY in 9M and 48% in Jan
items.quote: In January, we found in the month of January, there was a growth of 3% in Arena. Whereas Nexa, we have more than 48% of growth in the Nexa.

items.statement: RBI rate cuts and income tax revisions expected to boost passenger vehicle sales in coming quarters
items.quote: Recent RBI rate cuts and the revision in IT rates announced in the union budget would result in higher passenger vehicle sales in the coming quarters.

items.statement: SUV/premium shift limited revenue decline to 2% despite 5% volume drop in 9M FY25; luxury segment grew 11% YoY
items.quote: Luxury segment grew by 11% for Y-o-Y for the 9 months FY '25.

items.statement: Divesting Piaggio EV 3-wheeler and Honda PV businesses; proceeds to fund luxury/EV expansion and debt reduction
items.quote: The Board of Directors has decided to disinvest from this venture, a process which is expected to take approximately 6 months.

items.statement: Received LOI for JLR 3S facility in Nagpur covering 11 districts; 4 LOIs for Ather Space 3.0
items.quote: Popular Autoworks Limited, the Jaguar Land Rover 100% step down subsidiary, has received a letter of intent to establish a state-of-the-art 3S facility for JLR vehicles in Nagpur, Maharashtra.

items.statement: Adding ~70 service bays by March 2025; total bay count ~1,316 currently
items.quote: By March 2025 we'll add another 70-odd bays to it.

items.statement: Service volume growth target of 8-10% in H2 FY25 will not be met; expect CAGR 20% growth in future years
items.quote: We're expecting next year and the year after to grow at the same rate.

items.statement: Maruti inventory days reduced from 75 in Sep to 43 in Dec; target 35 days by March 2025
items.quote: The endeavor is to bring it down to 35 days by March.

items.statement: Expect >INR5 crore quarterly interest cost savings in Q4 from inventory reduction
items.quote: More than INR5 crores of higher inventory costs we are incurring every quarter, which hopefully we should be saving in Q4.

items.statement: Inorganic acquisition expected to close in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26 in PV mass market or CV segments
items.quote: We definitely do hope to close out in Q4, might spill on to Q1, but we are hoping to close it out in Q4.

items.statement: Trending towards 25% increase in adjusted EBITDA for full year FY25
items.quote: But full year numbers are trending at the same pace and are trending towards a 25% increase in adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Targeting to maintain 19%+ adjusted EBITDA margin for full year FY25
items.quote: At YTD level if you look, we are trending towards 19% plus of EBITDA margin. So that's what we are targeting towards maintaining in the future as well.

items.statement: Expect full year effective tax rate of 16.5% to 17%
items.quote: But if you ask me, for the full year, it should be ranging in the range of around 16.5% to 17% on the overall effective tax rate for the full year.

items.statement: Guiding hotel take rates to remain range bound between 7.2% to 7.6%
items.quote: Our view remains that they'll remain fairly range bound, we have been guiding around between 7.2% to 7.6% because right now the company is not really focused on improving the take rate.

items.statement: Fast tracking planned investment and geographic expansion for next year
items.quote: we are fast tracking given the growth that we have seen in the first nine months of the year, and as we plan for next year, we are fast tracking our planned TBO Tek Limited Feb 12th, 2025 investment and geographic

items.statement: Expanded sales presence in 15 new countries and 40 new cities this year
items.quote: During this year, we have expanded our sales presence in 15 new countries and 40 new cities within those countries.

items.statement: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin at 17.77%, 9M margin at 19.34%
items.quote: For Q3, our adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 17.77% and PAT margin at 11.84%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA as percentage of GTV maintained at 1.05% QoQ
items.quote: But if we see adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of GTV, we have maintained a similar margin at 1.05% this quarter versus last quarter, same year.

items.statement: Voice bot operates at 50% cost and 5x faster than human callers
items.quote: The voice bot has similar or slightly better quality of outcome in comparison to a human caller, but it is 5x faster. On an average if you are taking five hours to close a ticket with a human caller, it takes only one hour to close the ticket; so it's 5x faster, and it operates at a 50% of the cost.

items.statement: International hotels GTV grew 52% YoY, Europe grew 90% YoY (60%+ organic)
items.quote: Overall, hotels' GTV has grown by a very impressive 48%. Revenue is growing at a more or less similar clip and gross profit has grown a little bit faster to grow by 52% compared to same period last year.

items.statement: India hotels and ancillary GTV grew 18% YoY in Q3, up from 9% in Q2
items.quote: If you see the headroom of growth in active buyers in India, we are still 3%. We have a very large active base, which is very high, but keeping that in mind, the market still remains beyond the whole outward story which all of us read in the press. But the fact is, this output story and the addition of new routes and airlifts being added will only help our story. So, 9% to 18% in India is a very s

items.statement: Hotels and ancillaries share of GTV rose from 51% to 60% YoY
items.quote: Gross profit as a percentage of GTV for Q3 improved from 3.89% to 4.14% on YoY basis. This enhancement was largely driven by an increased share of hotels and ancillary services within our GTV which rose from 51% to 60% YoY.

items.statement: Ramadan in March will impact Q4 growth, especially Middle East business
items.quote: Just a reminder, Ramadan is going to be in March this year and March is essentially Ramadan. Ramadan is traditionally a low season for the business because businesses essentially are closed in Middle East, Indonesia and in many of our key markets.

items.statement: Forex loss of Rs. 12.48 Cr in Q3 due to sharp USD movement post US elections
items.quote: Profit after tax came in at Rs. 50 Cr, showing a marginal drop of 1.6% over the previous year, largely due to Rs. 12.48 Cr forex loss triggered by sharp movement in USD against other major currencies.

items.statement: Three new legal entities incorporated in Indonesia, Greece, Israel in Q3
items.quote: Three new legal entities have been incorporated in the last quarter in Indonesia, Greece and Israel setting the base for significant ramp up in these source markets.

items.statement: AI email bot classifies supplier emails with 99.5% accuracy, auto-closes 45%
items.quote: Now this bot, with a very amazing accuracy of 99.5% is able to close 45% of those notifications automatically, which is a huge reduction in workload for our operations teams and the bot is already achieving that.

items.statement: Guidance for FY25 iGAAP EBITDA margin was 1.5%; currently tracking above that and will maintain for next quarter; FY26 guidance to be given in May
items.quote: So at the beginning of the year, we had given the guidance of 1.5%. What we have achieved right now, I think we'll continue to maintain that for at least next quarter. And we will, at the end of next quarter in May, give the guidance for FY '26.

items.statement: Target 135,000 operational seats by March 2025; currently at 120,000 operational seats with 40,000 more under fit-out or LOI
items.quote: Our guidance for this full year was 135,000 seats. So we already -- operational seats. So we have a clear visibility of another 25,000 seats on top.

items.statement: Blended capex per seat is around INR 54,000; lower for MA model, higher for straight lease; MA is 65% of portfolio
items.quote: So the capex cost what we are incurring at this point of time is in the range what we gave in the prospectus. It is in the range of around 54,000 per seat kind of a thing.

items.statement: Signed LOIs for 23 new centers adding 18,000 seats and ~0.8 million sq ft chargeable area
items.quote: We have a strong expansion pipeline with signed LOIs for 23 new centers, adding 18,000 seats and approximately 0.8 million square feet of chargeable area.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 iGAAP EBITDA margin at 14.7% vs 9.9% YoY (+480 bps); 9M FY25 at 13.8% vs 7.6% YoY (+615 bps)
items.quote: The margins stood at 14.7% as against 9.9% in Q3 of FY '24, which is a growth of 480 basis points.

items.statement: Seat pricing escalations: 5-8% for smaller cohorts, 4-6% for larger cohorts; new customers in up-rental cycle get higher realization reflecting current market rents
items.quote: In the existing client contracts for smaller cohorts, the general escalations, which we have tied in ranges from 5% to 8% in terms of the larger cohorts, the price escalations are usually between 4% to 6-odd percent.

items.statement: Signed demand contracts for 15,000 new seats in Q3 FY25 and 40,000 in 9M FY25; sales velocity up from 36,500 seats in full FY24
items.quote: On the demand side, we have signed demand contracts for 15,000 new seats in Q3 FY '25 and 40,000 new seats in 9 months of FY '25.

items.statement: Sector expected to grow 20-25% annually barring macro challenges; driven by hybrid work, remote work, satellite offices
items.quote: Barring any unexpected macroeconomic challenges, we foresee the sector growing at an annual rate of about 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Co-working & Allied Services 77% of revenue (INR 243 Cr, +52% YoY); Construction fit-out 23% (INR 73 Cr, +35% YoY); 50-50 split between landlord capex and third-party in fit-out
items.quote: During the quarter, our co-working and Allied Services segment grew by 52% to INR243 crores, contributing 77% to the total revenue. Meanwhile, the construction fit-out project, including our design and build business, experienced a robust growth of 35%, reaching INR73 crores and accounting for the remaining 23% of our revenue.

items.statement: Fit-out revenue split 50% landlord partners, 50% third-party; blended contribution margin 16-17%; third-party segment grew ~40% YoY
items.quote: in terms of the revenue, it's almost a 50 -50 split. 50% of the revenue comes from what the -- our landlord partners are giving to fit out the center and about 50% comes from third-party clients. At a contribution margin level, this business is some where in the -- about blended between 16% to 17% margin

items.statement: Managed aggregation model mitigates risk: 65% of portfolio in profit-share with landlords, minimum guarantee ~50% of market rent; landlord provides majority of capex
items.quote: In majority of our portfolios, almost 65% today, we are partnered with our landlord, which is in a profit share model and the minimum guarantee is typically about 50% of the market rental. Second, a majority of the capital in this situation comes from our landlord partner.

items.statement: No fund raise planned for Q4 FY25; FY26 funding needs to be commented on later; currently net debt-free with comfortable liquidity and strong internal accruals
items.quote: If you're talking Q4, obviously, no, we are not going anywhere for a fund raise. Next year, I'll not be able to comment at this point of time.

items.statement: Occupancy guidance: blended 70-73%, 12-month+ vintage 83-85%; expect blended occupancy to stay stable near term, rise gradually as portfolio matures
items.quote: At the beginning of the year, we gave the original guidance that the blended occupancy at the whole portfolio level was expected to be about 70% to 73%. The greater than 12-month center vintage occupancy is expected to be between 83% to 85%.

items.statement: Profit-share rental expense: INR 19.4 Cr in Q3 FY25, INR 59.4 Cr in 9M FY25; Ancillary services revenue INR 31.5 Cr in Q3 (+110% YoY)
items.quote: Profit share for 9 months is INR59.4 crores. 3 months is INR19.4 crores for the current quarter. And ASR revenue for Q3 is INR31.5 crores, which in last year was INR15 crores for the quarter 3 of last year, which is a growth of 110%.

items.statement: Target INR 1,000 crores revenue with 15% PAT margin in next 900-1,000 days
items.quote: And our target remains very clear that we would like to be a INR 1,000 crores company with a 15% PAT in the next 900 to 1,000 days. That's our target.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20-22% by mid next year as new stores mature
items.quote: I think the EBITDA margin of somewhere about 20% - 22% is what we should be aiming at. But because new stores are taking a little longer to breakeven and it takes a little longer gestation period, it's a little subdued now.

items.statement: Manufacturing capex INR 5-7 crores next year funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Say max INR 5 crores to INR 7 crores for next year, manufacturing capex.

items.statement: B2B order book flattish; Williams-Sonoma orders on hold pending US tariff clarity, expected by April
items.quote: So the B2B order book has remained flattish throughout the year. While we have ongoing discussions with Williams-Sonoma from America, nothing has materialized yet because they are waiting and watching the tariff issues that are happening in America currently.

items.statement: Expect inventory handovers to surge from Q1 FY26 driving demand recovery
items.quote: We are hoping starting from Q1, we are going to see a lot more inventory coming into the market. And of course, the sales have been very buoyant.

items.statement: Leather localization at 33%, targeting 35% this year and 45% by end of next year, long-term vision 80% in 24-36 months
items.quote: 35% was the target. We are on track. We are at about 33% right now. And my target is to get to about 45% end of next year.

items.statement: B2B2C segment de-grew 27% in Q3 due to shift from credit to cash-and-carry model, revenue loss ~INR 12 crores
items.quote: Because the third leg has de-grown by 30%, 27% to 30%.

items.statement: B2C (COCO) targeting 20% growth in coming year; B2B flattish; B2B2C recovery by Q2 FY26
items.quote: Whereas B2C is where we are expecting good growth because we have now signed up a lot more new stores that are coming up in areas we were not present. And we hope that we will definitely deliver 20% growth as explained in the past in the coming year too, quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Store expansion delayed due to Grade A property availability; 4 stores added in Q3 (2 Level Next, 2 Sofas & More), total 68 stores
items.quote: Continuing the expansion strategy, the company added 4 new stores in Q3 FY '25, 2 under the Stanley Level Next brand and 2 under Stanley Sofas & More brand. With this, our total store count is 68 stores.

items.statement: Cash balance INR 208 crores as of Dec 31, 2024; INR 150 crores from IPO proceeds for store expansion
items.quote: INR 208 crores bank balance. So this is like out of this INR 208 crores, INR 150 crores is like from IPO process, and this we are planning to use for this like store expansion

items.statement: Same-store sales growth negative in low single digits for Q3 due to store cannibalization; market share gained in expanded cities
items.quote: Our SSG is same-store sales growth is negative for the quarter. We have expanded the retail square feet. And quarter 2, quarter 3, we really saw subdued demand that led to my SSSG being negative.

items.statement: Marketing spend maintained at 7-9% of revenue; reduced spend this year due to store launch delays
items.quote: We have always ensured that our marketing spends are always within 8% to 9%, and that is the trend we will continue to follow.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty holding back B2B export discussions with Williams-Sonoma and other US buyers
items.quote: Because of the uncertainty today due to Trump and the tariff, it is on hold. Once we get some amount of clarity, we can restart that exercise.

items.statement: Case goods contribution increased from 11% to 16%; bedroom furniture new catalog expected to grow share
items.quote: Yes, that has significantly improved because we set up a new facility and started case goods, which are basically coffee tables, dining tables, dining chair. It has jumped from 11% to 16%.

items.statement: Expect top-line growth of 16% to 17% for FY25 with EBITDA margins in the range of 13% to 15%
items.quote: So, we expect to achieve a top-line growth of around 16% to 17% this year, with margins in the range of 13% to 15% as per our estimates currently.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for 9 months FY25 was 13.83%, down 289 basis points from 16.72% in 9 months FY24 due to pricing pressure and one-off expenses
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for 9 months FY25 stood at 13.83%, down by 289 basis points from 16.72% in the period of 9 months FY24.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from increased competition has reduced gross margins; management is re-strategizing to recover margins
items.quote: Yes, it is the last few months we have seen an increased competition which has put a pricing pressure which has also led to a decrease in our gross margins.

items.statement: Added over 130 new clients in 9 months FY25, including large IT MNCs, port logistics, management consultants, financial services, private equity, and consumer goods companies
items.quote: This year we have added over 130 clients, which we consider the clients are our strongest asset we believe.

items.statement: Revenue mix for Q3 FY25 was 43% CCR and 57% ETS; full year FY25 expected at 42% CCR and 58% ETS, similar for next year
items.quote: So, this last quarter, we did around 43% was CCR and 57% was ETS. And for the whole year, I think we will end up with around 42% for CCR and around 58% for ETS.

items.statement: Competition has intensified from both organized and unorganized players, partly due to IPO visibility; new entrants drop prices but lack delivery capability
items.quote: It is from both; it is a mix.

items.statement: International revenue crossed Rs. 8 crores in 9 months FY25 vs Rs. 5 crores full FY24; asset-light model, EBITDA positive, managed from India
items.quote: In this 9 months, we've already crossed around Rs. 8 crores of business for our international operations.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio is 0.04%; negligible debt, no plans to increase leverage; healthy cash position, evaluating acquisitions and dividend payout
items.quote: So, we are almost at a very negligible debt. If you see our debt ratio, it has consistently gone down and is now I think only 0.2% sorry 0.04% is our debt-to-equity ratio currently.

items.statement: Existing customers grew 23% year-on-year in 9 months FY25; new client revenue ramps up over subsequent quarters
items.quote: So, we have from the last financial year one number I do have handy is that in our existing customers, we saw growth of around 23%.

items.statement: Contract renewals mostly at financial year start (April-May); negotiations cover price, technical capabilities, and service value, not just price
items.quote: It's mostly at the beginning of the financial year.

items.statement: Working capital cycle unchanged despite pricing pressure
items.quote: It's the same. There's no change.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 expected to maintain momentum with strong wedding season and Gudi Padwa; no dip in footfall despite high gold prices
items.quote: Ongoing quarter, Q4 we do not see a dip in footfall primarily due to pricing, because prices it's somewhere with the consumer are some way accepted too. So I do not see that we'll have a major impact in terms of footfall.

items.statement: Target 53 stores by end of Q4 FY25 (March 2025)
items.quote: So we have already added two stores in January. So right now we are at 50 stores. And in the month of March, we will be adding three more stores. So we will be at 53 stores as of March end.

items.statement: Plan to add 25 stores in FY26: 8 COCO PNG stores, 7-8 franchisee PNG stores, ~10 litestyle stores (half COCO half FOCO), plus 1-2 US stores
items.quote: Next financial year, the plan is that considering a company-owned store and a franchisee store, along with our litestyle format what we have envisaged, the store with lighter weight jewellery, we would be adding 25 stores in the next financial year, which will be a mix of franchisee and company-owned stores.

items.statement: Litestyle stores require INR 5-7 crore stock investment and INR 7-8 crore capex for 1,000-1,500 sq ft
items.quote: The stock investment would be in the range of INR 5 to INR 7 crores. So our internal accruals are strong. And we will not be looking at raising heavy debt to fund the expansion.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement as studded ratio grows to 12-13% in 2-3 years and full hedging neutralizes gold price impact
items.quote: In the l ong run, the pricing in Maharashtra and other states is almost the same for jewellery. There isn't any much difference. So I think on the margin front, we would be looking at positive improvement because as the studded ratio goes further up, we would be se eing a benefit from that

items.statement: Nine Navaratri stores contributed INR 240 crores in Q3 FY25; at 24% of breakeven target of INR 1,010 crores
items.quote: So now, we have opened nine stores in nine days and the performance of these nine stores is that in Q3 they have contributed INR 240 crores in the top line. So, as per our plan, the breakeven is that once we reach INR 1,010 crores, then I think all my nine stores will be reached.

items.statement: Gold price at record INR ~80,000 vs INR 72,000 last year; still saw 5% demand increase
items.quote: Despite record high prices of almost INR 80,000 compared to INR 72,000 last year, we witnessed a 5% increase in demand.

items.statement: Q3 FY25: 21% transaction volume growth, 22% ATV growth to INR 86,000, 36% footfall increase, 93% conversion ratio
items.quote: Moreover, we recorded a 36% increase in footfalls and supported by a strong conversion ratio of 93%. This has helped us to really focus on the consumer demand and purchasing at all our stores in a most efficient way.

items.statement: Studded ratio rose 39% YoY to 7.4%; targeting 12-13% in 2-3 years via Polki, precious stones, natural diamonds
items.quote: Additionally, an important point we observed is a 39% year-over-year increase in our studded ratio, which now stands at 7.4% highlighting our evolving consumer preference towards more premium jewellery offerings.

items.statement: Fully hedged as of January 2025 (83.6% at Dec 2024); GML 558 kg, inventory INR 1,800 crores
items.quote: Lastly, the most important is the hedging, the met al loan which we avail for meeting our day-to-day gold requirement. This is based on daily sales criteria. In aggregate, the hedging is currently as on December is 83.6% and as on today that is January, we are fully hedged with respect to my total business in gold

items.statement: Debt-free post IPO (INR 50-60 cr term loan remaining); expansion funded via internal accruals, no heavy debt
items.quote: From the IPO proceeds, we have also repaid the entire bank debt. So if you have seen the IPO objectives, INR 300 crores was to repay the term loan, the bank debt and then the balance was primarily used for stock infusion.

items.statement: Marketing spend ~1% of turnover; FY25 expected INR 55-60 crores including new store launches
items.quote: So, Naveen, Kiran will give the numbers to you. But our total spend would be around 1% of our entire turnover. So, we are well in budget. This year, we should be closing at around INR 7,500 crores to INR 8,000 crores. So, marketing spend for the y ear would be in the range of INR 55 crores to INR 60 crores, including all the new store

items.statement: Litestyle stores target 15-20% margins, breakeven in 9-12 months, ATV lower than PNG stores
items.quote: And then there will be diamond jewel lery which is 18 carat gold and diamond. Again, designs which we don't keep in PNG. It may also have 14 carat gold, but the advantage of this is that the pricing here is a little premium. So margins here would range in the range of 15% to 20

items.statement: Old gold exchange 25-28%, scheme purchases 8-10%, balance spot purchases
items.quote: Our old gold which people exchanged for new jewellery would be in the range of 25% to 28%. Our scheme wherein people have what you call the future purchase plan, that would be in the range of 8% to 10%. And the balance is primarily on the spot fresh purchase.

items.statement: No plans for lab-grown diamonds under PNG; may consider for litestyle if trend catches on
items.quote: At PNG, there has been no demand from consumers asking for la b-grown diamonds. And the reason for that has been that we have been - most of the jewellery chain, diamond jewellery sales are in the size of minus 11 so 11 cents and

items.statement: E-commerce revenue doubled to INR 70 crores in Q3 FY25; operates via own website and marketplaces (Amazon, Flipkart, Tata CLiQ, AJIO)
items.quote: Our E-com revenue grows by almost 100% to INR 70 crores and the franchisee revenue rose by 87% to INR 226 crores in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: FY26 order flow guidance is INR25,000 crores.
items.quote: FY26 order flow guidance is INR25,000 crores.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected at 20%-25% in FY26, more towards 25%.
items.quote: And as we conveyed earlier, while the current year we expect ourselves to be the flat or marginally higher growth, next year we expect 20 % to 25% growth from that of current year, more towards 25%.

items.statement: Medium to long term CAGR target around 15% sustained over last 10 years.
items.quote: On a medium to long term horizon, we would like to sustain our CAGR which we have achieved over a longer period of time, say last 10 years. So we should be around those numbers which is around 15%.

items.statement: Pending order book INR38,000 crores as of 31st December, plus INR10,662 crores L1 and INR14,603 crores booked in 9M FY25.
items.quote: And as of 31st December, we have a INR38,000 crores of pending order and which excludes about INR10,662 crores of L1 and INR14,603 crores is the amount of order we have booked in the first nine months.

items.statement: Order book expected to reach INR45,000-50,000 crores by end of FY25, giving 3x revenue visibility.
items.quote: And at the end of the year, we will be somewhere between INR45,000 crores to 50,000 crores order book giving us more than 3 x visibility for the future period.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11%+; current year may cross 12% but guidance remains conservative.
items.quote: Our construction industry, as we keep always telling, has a lot of contingencies happening continuously. While our guidance will continue to be 11+. For the current year, it could be well crossing 12. And for the subsequent years or otherwise, we would say 11+.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected at INR450-500 crores; Q3 capex around INR125 crores; 9M capex around INR250 crores.
items.quote: For this financial year, we expect to close the full capex somewhere around say INR450 crores to INR500 crores. And this is much lesser than what we had budgeted for the year.

items.statement: Government capex allocation INR11.2 lakh crores, up 10.1% YoY; strong pipeline across roads, railways, metro, hydro, marine.
items.quote: In the recent budget, despite significant measures to boost consumption and the associated pressures on fiscal consolidation, which is an excellent step taken on the fiscal consolidation, the government has allocated INR11.2 lakh crore per capital expenditure, a 10.1% increase over the revised estimate of the last year.

items.statement: Overseas margins higher than domestic; targeting Eastern Europe, Saudi, Dubai, Africa; 30% of INR3.46 lakh crore pipeline is overseas.
items.quote: It includes both domestic and overseas. And close to 30% of this is overseas and 70% is domestic. Out of the INR3.46 lakh crores I have mentioned.

items.statement: Bangladesh project WP3 (INR600 crores) likely cancellation; other projects awaiting variation approvals and land handover.
items.quote: That project is probably going towards cancellation and that is something which will be about INR600 crores. About INR600 crores value. So that is likely to go out.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to AA- long-term and A1+ short-term by CRISIL; enables CP, NCD access and interest savings.
items.quote: We are very happy to inform you that we have got our credit rating upgraded to AA- for long term and A1+, which is the highest rating for short term from CRISIL.

items.statement: Debt target INR2,000 crores by end of FY25; net debt/equity 0.35x; debt/EBITDA to keep declining.
items.quote: In terms of absolute number, maybe it could be in the range what we have indicated for the year end, say around INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Bid success ratio 18-20%; rolling 2-year pipeline INR3.46 lakh crores across marine, transport, hydro, underground.
items.quote: So our bid success ratio is typically in the range of 18% to 20%. And the pipeline, as I have just mentioned, we have a very healthy pipeline. For around 2-year visibility, we have close to INR3.4 lakh crores of pipeline spread across segments.

items.statement: Interest-bearing advances now 70-75% of new projects vs historical 25%; mix shift offsets IPO debt repayment savings.
items.quote: But this time around the projects we have bagged we are seeing 70 %-75% projects are interest bearing. So that's where we have saved on the bank interest but interest from client advances have increased.

items.statement: PBT margins expected to improve gradually; 9M FY25 PBT margin up 80 bps YoY to 3.9%.
items.quote: What we have talked about that even going forward, we should see improvement in our PBT margin. Gradually, even our PBT margin should improve.

items.statement: TBM procurement delays due to India-China border issues; some project delays but resolution underway via indigenization and Germany JV.
items.quote: In general, the government had taken things seriously and had talked to the people and all the projects where TBMs are involved, there have been some delays. There is also fresh initiative from Government of India jointly with the Government of Germany to have a manufacturing base set up in India.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins in the region of 23-23.5% range in FY25
items.quote: Putting all of this together, we believe that we should be able to deliver EBITDA margins in the region of 23-23.5% range in FY25.

items.statement: Expect R&D to be around INR 1,750-1,800 crores for fiscal year 25 with significant increase in Q4
items.quote: For the full year, we expect R&D to be around INR 1,750 -1,800 crores with a significant increase in R&D in Q4.

items.statement: Anticipate US business to deliver double digit growth in full year FY25 ahead of earlier guidance of high single digit growth
items.quote: On a full year FY25 basis, we anticipate our US business to deliver double digit growth, ahead of our earlier guid ance of high single digit growth in the segment

items.statement: Expect margins in the range of 22%-23% in the current fiscal year
items.quote: We feel confident of maintaining our growth momentum going ahead with margins in the range of 22%-23% in the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Expect R&D spend to increase in absolute terms in FY26 but remain around same percentage of sales
items.quote: I would say, as an absolute there would be an increase but as a percentage of sales, it will perhaps be around the same levels.

items.statement: Expect US business to be at USD billion plus in fiscal year 26
items.quote: We expect in fiscal year '26, the US should be at a USD billion plus and then look at how we can sustain the growth from there.

items.statement: Expect overall margins between 22.5% to 23.5% for next fiscal year
items.quote: I think if you talk about overall margins, I did indicate the fact that between 22.5% to 23.5% would be a good range to aim for the next fiscal as well.

items.statement: Comfortable with bite-size acquisition of USD 200 million to USD 250 million
items.quote: But having said that, we would be comfortable with a bite-size acquisition, USD 200 million to USD 250 million should be easy enough for us.

items.statement: Plan to shift complex products to over 50% of portfolio over next couple of years
items.quote: We believe that our pipeline will enable us to continue to drive the shift to complex products to over 50% of our portfolio over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Plan to file more than 30 ANDAs in next 2 years with more than 50% complex products
items.quote: We have an exciting pipeline, with more than 20 respiratory products and 40 injectable products in development and plan to file more than 30 ANDAs in the next 2 years, of which more than 50 % will be complex products.

items.statement: India Formulation business recorded growth of 9.1% for 9M against IPM growth of 8.2%
items.quote: Our India Formulation business recorded growth of 9.1% for the 9M this fiscal year against an IPM growth of 8.2%.

items.statement: Respiratory market growth muted at 4% for nine months, company at 3%
items.quote: Even for nine months, the market was only at 4%. We were at 3% for nine months and I mean the quarter again has been disappointing.

items.statement: US business benefited from volume growth and new products but offset by low single digit price declines in base products
items.quote: As Vinita mention s, while we have benefited from volume growth in inline products and new product introductions, this has been offset by low single digit price declines in base products and anticipated new generic competition in products like Albuterol and Suprep

items.statement: Tariffs on pharmaceuticals would have significant impact on generic industry, 70% of generic drugs for US are imported, 50% from India
items.quote: So we are monitoring it very carefully and the industry has made a strong pitch, both from AAM standpoint as well as IPA, the tariffs will have a significant impact on the generic industry if it was implemented.

items.statement: Key products for next fiscal year are Tolvaptan, Glucagon, Risperdal Consta and potentially Liraglutide
items.quote: The major products are Tolvaptan and Glucagon, Risperdal Consta and potentially Liraglutide. So those will be the key products for next year.

items.statement: PLI benefit expected to decline next year, normal annual run rate around INR 200 crores
items.quote: So there would be a decline for sure next year. In the normal course, you would be expected to look at about INR 200 crores on an annual basis.

items.statement: Expects Q4 performance to be slightly better than Q3
items.quote: I expect performance to be slightly better than Q3 in Q4.

items.statement: Targets PAT positive in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, our target is to turn the PAT positive soon, at least for the coming quarter we are targeting that we will be PAT positive.

items.statement: Only normal maintenance capex, no major modernization due to negative PAT

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 4.8% in Q3 FY25 from 3.6% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The quarter was 4.8% compared to 2.3% i n Q3FY24 and 3.6% in Q2 FY 25

items.statement: Key EBITDA drivers are capacity utilization, product mix, and cost management
items.quote: The key drivers behind the increase in the EBITDA are primarily the capacity utilization, the better product mix, and management of our cost.

items.statement: Mélange yarn demand improved slightly in Q3; expects better capacity utilization in Q4
items.quote: In this quarter we saw this increase in capacity utilization being better on mélange. And as of today, if you look at the demand side, then India we are having some slight improvement trend whereas in export it is still having a lot of challenges in terms of pricing where we have to compete with other countries with more competition in terms of pricing. So, to sum up, it is slightly better and the

items.statement: Export revenue share is 30.5% of total; focusing on downstream denim and knitting plus value-added yarns
items.quote: Our current percentage of revenue which comes from exports is around 30.5% of the total revenue that comes from exports. Now coming to yarn, being at the lowest step of the value chain in textiles. And realizing that only as of today RSWM has two other businesses which are denim and knitting, which are downstream in terms of value addition.

items.statement: Indian cotton prices remain above international levels due to MSP and import duties, pressuring spinning margins
items.quote: Indian cotton prices as of today for the first time we have experienced this in the last couple of months now international prices of cotton are operating at the highest level of 67, 68. So there is a lot of overproduction in international cotton, especially in the US and Brazil, reflecting the cotton prices are a t the lower level internationally, whereas in India, because of MSP being a reality,

items.statement: No plans to raise funds; focusing on internal cash flows and working capital management
items.quote: No, we do not have any plans to raise the funds. We are channelizing our existing businesses, making them profitable and we are focusing on the very strin gent cash flows to maintain the working capital.

items.statement: Ginni knitting utilization at 70-75%; spinning utilization unchanged and variable based on profitability
items.quote: In terms of knitting, we have improved s o today we are having to the tune of 70 % - 75% utilization for knitting. Spinning varies whenever it makes sense in terms of running, considering the profitability and the cotton prices, spinning is something that you can improve or reduce depending on the count, depending upon the availability of orders, and making

items.statement: Targets capacity utilization above 90% as first step in annual business plan
items.quote: The first thing is to focus on our order book and ensure our capacity utilization percentage is more than 90% , which we are targeting as a first step.

items.statement: Debt at ₹1,600 crore as of Dec 2024; focusing on normal capex and leveraging past investments to control finance cost
items.quote: As of December 24, our balance sheet has a debt of around ₹ 1,600 crores. Out of which primarily ₹ 700 crores will be the term loan, and we have a repayment plan. So, what we are doing as a strategy is, we are not focusing on capital expenditure. We are doing only normal CAPEX and the CAPEX that has been done in the recent past. We are trying to leverage those, leverage the ROIs been related to th

items.statement: Bio-fuel boiler and solar investments yielding lower operational costs; 50% implementation in current quarter, full benefit from Q1 next year
items.quote: There are two main gains on this. One is in terms of lower operational costs and less team cost. That is one which we, where we have implemented this initiative that is already we are getting that benefit which you saw in this quarter results. Now, around 50% of that will be implemented in the current quarter and we will see that in the first quarter of next year.

items.statement: Power cost reduced substantially in Q3 vs Q2; employee cost controlled at inflation-level increments
items.quote: There has been the reduction in the power cost for quarter two numbers versus Quarter 3, there has been a substan tial reduction in the power cost and they have been able to drive savings as far as the employee cost, we have been working the employee cost aggressively , and the increments. Also, what we are doing is just equivalent to the normal inflation rate and not more than that.

items.statement: Sees export opportunity shift from Bangladesh to Indian apparel manufacturers
items.quote: Bangladesh is strong in those areas. So , I agree with you some amount of business definitely will be shifted to India. And as Indian textile, we expect better orders as a result of that.

items.statement: Quarterly copper EBITDA expected around Rs. 600 crores next year
items.quote: So our guidance would be that we expect next year the quarterly copper EBITDA to be around Rs. 600 crores, so that's how we would model it.

items.statement: India FY26 CAPEX around Rs. 8,000 crores; FY27 higher, peak FY27-28
items.quote: FY '26 CAPEX should be around Rs. 8,000 crores, FY '27 it will go higher, '27-'28 will probably be at the peak.

items.statement: Novelis cumulative CAPEX $6 billion over FY25-27 including Bay Minette, maintenance and debottlenecking
items.quote: So that's the answer to your specific CAPEX question. Can you just repeat exactly what was the second part of the question, so between Steve and I, we just want to be clear on that.

items.statement: Aditya alumina refinery 850 Kt at Rs. 7,500-8,000 crores and copper recycling 50 Kt at Rs. 2,700 crores broken ground; aluminum smelter 180 Kt and copper smelter 300 Kt filed for EC
items.quote: So the two projects that have already got EC and broken ground are the Aditya alumina refinery for 850 Kt in Odisha and the 50 Kt copper recycling plant in Gujarat. So the refinery is about Rs. 7,500 crores to Rs. 8,000 crores, the copper recycling plant is about Rs. 2,700 crores.

items.statement: Bay Minette 600 Kt: 420 Kt fully contracted to beverage packaging, 180 Kt primarily automotive with flexibility
items.quote: Of the 600 Kt, 420 Kt is now fully contracted to beverage packaging, and the balance 180 Kt is primarily allocated for automotive application with flexibility for other flat rolled products.

items.statement: Indian aluminum upstream Q3 EBITDA margin record 42%; EBITDA per ton $1,480 up 68% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins were also at a record high of 42% this quarter, and continued to be among the best in the global industry.

items.statement: Novelis Q3 EBITDA per ton $406 down 19% YoY due to high scrap prices and unfavorable mix
items.quote: Novelis delivered a quarterly EBITDA of $367 million, down 19% year-on-year due to high aluminum scrap prices and unfavorable product mix. The resultant EBITDA per ton stood at $406 dollars versus $499 in the previous year same quarter, down 19% year-on-year.

items.statement: Meenakshi coal mine expected to reduce coal costs by up to 30% from current levels when operational
items.quote: Meenakshi coming in would reduce those coal prices from current levels by up to 30%.

items.statement: Alumina index around $500 currently; traditional range $350-400; Q3 index ~$700 vs Q2 ~$375
items.quote: I think currently the indexes are around $500. So, I don't know, it's going to be in that. $400 Kt to $500 range. You have to remember the sort of more traditional pricing is more like between $350 and $400.

items.statement: Aditya FRP project on track for FY26 commissioning, raising downstream capacity to 600 Kt; 25 Kt copper inner grooved tube plant commissioning this month
items.quote: On our organic expansion projects in India, the Aditya FRP project remains on track for commissioning in FY '26, which will increase our total downstream capacity to 600 Kt per annum. We are also set to commission the 25 Kt copper inner grooved tube plant this month.

items.statement: TC/RC benchmark fell to 5.45 cents/lb for 2025 (73% YoY decline); full impact on copper EBITDA from Q1 FY26 as Q4 uses existing concentrate inventory
items.quote: Major Chinese smelters settled the 2025 annual TC/RC benchmark with large global miners at 5.45 cens per pound, representation a 73% year-on-year decline from 20.5 cents per pound in 2024. Uncertainty remains whether smelters outside China will adopt the same benchmark terms.

items.statement: US tariff exemption uncertainty for Novelis; scrap not subject to 232 tariffs but higher Midwest premium may offset; resolution expected in weeks
items.quote: We simply do not see a scenario where either between the countries; Canada, US, Mexico, Korea, we simply do not see a scenario that there will not be a settlement soon around reciprocal tariffs, because if you are following what's the latest discussion that is happening, it is about reciprocal tariffs.

items.statement: Indian aluminum cost of production Q4 flattish vs Q3, within 1-2%; coal may soften, caustic/furnace oil/CP coke up
items.quote: think Q4 will be more or less flattish, would not be more than 1% or 2% off from where we are

items.statement: Downstream aluminum EBITDA per ton approaching $200 in Q4 FY25; next year well into those numbers with FRP 2A and Silvassa ramp-up
items.quote: I think in Q4 we should be getting close to that number. And next year I am really bullish on the whole thing because the FRP 2A project will also commission, Silvassa will be ramping up quite well. So the $200 number we should be getting close to it in Q4, and next year we should be well into those numbers.

items.statement: Hindalco secured Meenakshi coal mine 12 Mtpa; Chakla box cut expected CY25 Q3-Q4, Meenakshi ~2 years for clearances
items.quote: Hindalco has successfully secured the Meenakshi coal mine with a capacity of 12 million tons per annum. This strategic move shall significantly improve our self-sufficiency, ensuring a stable and continuous supply of captive coal to our captive power plants.

items.statement: Novelis issued $750 million senior unsecured notes due 2030 in January 2025 to strengthen financial flexibility
items.quote: In January 2025, Nove lis successfully issued $750 million in senior unsecured notes due in 2030. This will help further strengthen our financial flexibility and support long-term growth

items.statement: Expect operating performance to improve on demand recovery, internal profitability initiatives, and reduced RM inflation
items.quote: We expect our operating performance to improve going forward on the back of , (a) recovery in the overall demand momentum , s econdly, initiatives being taken internally to significantly uplift profitability , a nd lastly, due to reduced RM inflation.

items.statement: Expect healthy replacement demand momentum to continue in Q4 with signs of further strong pickup beyond current levels
items.quote: In terms of the demand outlook, we expect the replacement demand momentum to continue to be healthy in Q4. And, in fact, we are seeing signs of a further strong pickup even beyond the current levels.

items.statement: RM cost expected to be range-bound in Q4 at similar levels to Q3, indicating plateauing
items.quote: Moving to the RM outlook, we expect the RM cost to be range bound in Q4, almost around similar levels as Q3, which indicates a certain plateauing out.

items.statement: No near-term price increases planned given market situation and competitive intensity
items.quote: Currently, given the market situation, etc., and the overall scenario, absolute near-term, no price increases planned. We'll continue to assess that situation and then take a call.

items.statement: FY25 capex likely INR 700-800 crore vs earlier INR 1,000 crore plan; FY26 capex to increase with growth capex for PCR capacity
items.quote: There would probably be some moderation. It is highly unlikely that we'll spend INR 500 crores in the last quarter.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at INR 1,500-1,550 crore (INR 700-750 crore maintenance + ~INR 800 crore growth) adding ~10% capacity
items.quote: So, if we take a normal maintenance Capex around INR 700 crores - INR 750 crores mark that we talked about earlier, on top of that , very much at the top of the numbers, maybe add around INR 800 crores more.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 13.7% in Q3 FY25, flat QoQ despite RM pressure; India margin 11.1% down from 12.1% QoQ
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 9.5 billion, a margin of 13.7% compared to 13.6% in the last quarter.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margin improved to 17.7% in Q3 FY25 from under 15% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at EUR 32 million, with an EBITDA margin of 17.7% compared to under 15% for the last quarter.

items.statement: Europe UUHP mix improved 400 bps to 48% of PCLT replacement volumes in Q3 FY25 from 43% earlier
items.quote: More importantly, w e registered more than 400 basis points improvement in our product mix with UUHP segment accounting for 48% of PCLT replacement volumes in the quarter. Earlier it was 43%.
