items.statement: BG limit to be increased from Rs. 200 crore to Rs. 400 crore (non-fund based, contingent liability); sufficient cash flows, no fund-based limit needed
items.quote: On the working capital, we have applied for certain BG limit. Whenever that BG comes, it will not come into the financial debt. It will be only the non-fund-based limit. We do not require any fund-based limit because we have sufficient cash flow in our book. Only the BG is required for bidding, and we are going to take that from Rs. 200 crore to Rs. 400 crore from the various banks. Whenever it co

items.statement: Order book target Rs. 5,000-7,000 crore per quarter; focus on profitable, executable orders; sustainable growth over next five years from water, irrigation, river linking, BESS
items.quote: As I told you earlier also, we have taken the target that we will not focus towards the top-line. We will be very focused in the bottom-line and we will target to have an order book which is good, profitable and which is easy to do, complete and which is meeting our target of taking the order. Our target is Rs. 5,000 crore to Rs. 7,000 crore every quarter, not that, whereas the opportunity is very

items.statement: Demand is strong and expected to continue growing in the coming future.
items.quote: The demand is pretty strong at this moment. And we foresee a good growth in the coming future.

items.statement: Management is confident of driving ADR growth and sees considerable upside in rates.
items.quote: We continue to drive ADR, and we're confident that we will be able to drive ADR like we've done in the past, and there's no reason for that to change.

items.statement: Hotels are underpriced relative to global peers, providing significant rate upside.
items.quote: We're still, in my view, underpriced for the quality of hotels that we offer, both in parts of Asia and in leisure and business, and also in Europe and North America.

items.statement: CapEx spent on London asset, Tirupati, Rajgarh, Gandikota, Hebbal, and renovations like Trident Nariman Point.
items.quote: We have invested roughly 241 crores in our London asset and also we have spent on CapEx. The few new hotels in the pipeline, which you see, we have spend around 200 crores.

items.statement: CapEx investments are happening in Tirupati, Rajgarh, and Gandikota projects.
items.quote: So, the spends are happening in Tirupati, Rajgarh and Gandikota projects. These 3 main places the investments are happening.

items.statement: Pipeline includes 19 properties: 13 hotels, 3 Trident hotels, 3 Luxury Boats & Nile Cruisers; 8 owned, 11 managed; 10 domestic, 9 international.
items.quote: Overall, if I look at the summary, we're going to add 13 hotels, 3 Trident hotels and will also add 3 Luxury Boats & Nile Cruiser. If we take the split, we are increasing in all geographies, including domestic and international - domestic growth of 10, and 9 international. Out of 19, owned are 8 and managed properties will be 11.

items.statement: Two new management contracts signed (one Oberoi, one Trident in India); press release next week.
items.quote: A press release will be coming out next week on two further management contracts that have been signed since our last presentation to you. Both of these hotels, one is a Oberoi, one is a Trident, and they both are in India.

items.statement: Oberoi Grand Kolkata expected to open in about 18 months.
items.quote: So, Oberoi Grand should open in about 18 months.

items.statement: Oberoi Rajgarh expected to start operations around August.
items.quote: So, hopefully in and around August.

items.statement: Flight services business saw significant margin improvement.
items.quote: It's been a significant improvement on margin as well.

items.statement: MICE and wedding segment remains very strong with high F&B spend and room rates.
items.quote: I continue to see the MICE being very strong for that segment, I continue to see parents are willing to make that event very special and memorable for their family.

items.statement: No correlation analysis done between stock market declines and hotel demand; recent market decline has not impacted RevPAR growth.
items.quote: We haven't done that analysis to correlate the stock market movements with our business. But what I can say which is reflected in the numbers is that we have strong RevPAR growth at high occupancy levels.

items.statement: Focus on driving ARR even at cost of occupancy to maximize RevPAR and bottom-line flow-through.
items.quote: Our focus will be to drive rates even at the cost of occupancy because you can by increasing rate the flow through to bottom line is 100% and that's going to continue to be our focus, to drive ARR.

items.statement: Company does not provide revenue guidance.
items.quote: We don't do guidance. Maybe we should but I don't know, Navin, and maybe we can have a chat separately but we've shied away from guidance.

items.statement: Actively seeking partner for an Oberoi hotel in Hyderabad.
items.quote: Absolutely, we'd love to have an Oberoi in Hyderabad. So, if anybody who's on the call is interested in partnering with us for a hotel in Hyderabad, we'd love that.

items.statement: Full year EBITDA fell 28% to INR1.5 billion and EBIT fell 36% to INR1.04 billion in CY24 due to raw material inflation, adverse mix, high freight costs and one-off items.
items.quote: Full year EBITDA stands at INR1.5 billion compared to INR2.1 billion in 2023, it reflects a decrease of almost 28%. And when we look at the EBIT for full year, it is INR1.04 billion versus INR1.6 billion we have in 2023, which also reflect a decrease of slightly higher than 28%, so that decrease is 36% in case of EBIT.

items.statement: Margin pressure stems from raw material inflation, unfavorable product mix, high freight costs from the Red Sea crisis, and one-off items including fair value impairment.
items.quote: The pressure on margin has arisen due to the cost inflation, which include raw material inflation, sales and unfavorable product mix, high freight costs due to Sea crisis and a couple of one-off items, one-off item we spoke in the first quarter in the March 2024 on fairly impairment and all.

items.statement: FMCG demand is under pressure from inflation across most segments, with heightened competition from small players impacting mix; rural demand shows improvement but urban recovery timing is uncertain.
items.quote: In the overall ecosystem FMCG sector from which HIL derives bulk of our demand, inflationary pressures are impacting demand across most of the segments, barring a few, and it's affecting consumer spending, and this is having a spiral impact.

items.statement: Rural economy shows promising improvement in consumption; urban demand is taking time to recover and timing is unknown.
items.quote: But other side, if you look at rural economy is showing some promising improvement. However, urban is taking time. So expectation is that when we read the articles and something is there really expected that urban is also going to come back. But when? We don't know yet.

items.statement: Blueloop sustainable packaging contribution rose from 25% to 27.5% of sales in CY24, but high-end complex structures that drive premium margins are still in early adoption.
items.quote: And as you rightly pointed out, we moved our blueloop contribution from -- sales contribution from 25% to 27% to 27.5% in last year.

items.statement: Blueloop contribution was around 22% in CY22 and 25% in CY23, rising a couple of percentage points each year; current structures are low-end with limited differentiation.
items.quote: So '23, it was around 25%. And '22, I think I remember around 22%. So it's like we have moved a couple of percent points every year.

items.statement: No major capex planned for CY25; only routine maintenance capex across 10 plants, unlike prior large investments for blueloop.
items.quote: But in 2025, we are not planning for any big capex per se. But obviously, when you have managing 10 plants and always there will be one another capex will be there. So we'll continue to focus on making sure that we are having our operations, which is running and we don't have any challenges.

items.statement: Capacity utilization has headroom of 15-20% more production with current capacity.
items.quote: But by and far, if you look at, I think we can do more production with the similar capacity. So we do have a room of somewhere between 15% to 20% more production.

items.statement: Geopolitical and tariff developments may create export opportunities for India, but also pose uncertainty; management sees India as a potential net gainer.
items.quote: But going forward, considering that what's happening as a tariff, I don't want to go any country-specific, but you know you are monitoring the market. There are definitely chances that India as a whole may emerge as a net gainer by whatever is tariff situation happening elsewhere in the globe.

items.statement: ECB debt of ~INR1 billion remains; no repayment scheduled in CY25, next repayment expected in CY27.
items.quote: On a 12 month on a full year basis, PBT for full year 2024 before exceptional items stands at INR860 million versus INR1.3 billion we have in 2023. Having said that, the EPS for the quarter after exceptional items at INR1.55 per share. And on a full year basis, it was INR11.65 per share. For full year 2024, the Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR2 per share, which is subject to a

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR2 per share for CY24, subject to AGM approval.
items.quote: For full year 2024, the Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR2 per share, which is subject to approval of the shareholders at the AGM of the company.

items.statement: Centralized services and IT charges from parent rose to ~55% of EBITDA in CY24; management says charges are at arm's length and benchmarked, but will review cost-benefit.
items.quote: Point noted. And definitely, we, as a management also and we make sure that whatever the cost we had, and we ensure that there are a consumer benefit for that. And yes, point well noted. Thank you.

items.statement: Price pass-through is limited in Indian flexible packaging due to commodity-like structures, competitive market, and customer agreements; recovery expected as demand shifts back to premium products.
items.quote: When it comes to flexibles packaging, what happens at a global level, we have certain agreements with our customers. And then also adaptation of a blueloop elsewhere has been better than what is happening in India. And third, the structures what we sell elsewhere, let's say, in Southeast Asia or in Europe are more complex, premium, and that's where the stickiness is with Huhtamaki. When it comes t

items.statement: No explicit forward guidance given; management expects gradual margin revival in future quarters as demand improves and blueloop adoption accelerates toward 2030 sustainability targets.
items.quote: But I can see that now the demand coming back strongly. Our end customers are also having some positive sentiment. So we shall see that in future quarters. We should see some revival.

items.statement: Revised FY25 consolidated EBITDA target to INR100 crores from earlier INR130 crores due to subsidiary underperformance
items.quote: So in the light of this, I would say that considering the good performance of standalone in Q4, we should be doing about INR100 crores of EBITDA for the full year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin target 13-14% for FY26; consolidated subsidiary EBITDA margin target 6-7% for FY26
items.quote: At a standalone level, we should be able to achieve around 13% to 14%. And at a subsidiary level, including Canada, we should be between 6% to 7% of EBITDA.

items.statement: Revised FY25 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 13% on gross accounting basis from earlier 18% due to Canadian subsidiary drag
items.quote: We expect to close the year with gross accounting 13% of revenue growth as against the 18%, and mainly because of the drop in the subsidiary.

items.statement: No FY26 consolidated guidance given pending Canadian subsidiary strategic decisions
items.quote: At this point of time, I wouldn't guide anything. Let us -- because we have certain actions to take in the Canadian subsidiary, perhaps we can see it in the next concall.

items.statement: Target to improve subsidiary margins to 7% in short term and 11-12% in subsequent years
items.quote: Our objective is to try to move that margin up to a 7% level or so in the short-term in the coming year, and then push it up further as growth comes in to 11% to 12% range in the subsequent years.

items.statement: Standalone BTS EBITDA margin 18-20%, EMS 11-13% on yearly basis; French engineering services at 4% but pulled down by Canadian losses
items.quote: BTS generally is about 18% to 20%, and EMS, it is between 11% to 13%. And that is what we are targeting and we are achieving on a yearly basis.

items.statement: Overall order book INR1,675 crores as of 31 Dec 2024; domestic BTS order book grew from INR376 crores (FY23) to INR427 crores (FY24) to INR563 crores (9M FY25)
items.quote: Our order book position stands at INR1,675 crores as on 31st December, 2024.

items.statement: Strong pipeline for Build to Spec and EMS in standalone business; expecting substantial Q4 orders in radar/naval and missile programs
items.quote: In Q4, we are also expecting some substantial orders, and we will receive them from the radar domain, and these are for naval programs.

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary losses dragging consolidated P&L; strategic decisions on Canadian operations expected in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We will be basically making some strategic decisions with regard to the Canadian operations in the next couple of quarters to ensure that it doesn't continue to drag the overall P&L.

items.statement: Worst case Canadian subsidiary drag to stop by September; variation orders and knowledge transfer to India underway
items.quote: The worst case before September we should be able to ensure that Canada is no longer a dragger.

items.statement: Board approved fundraising via QIP or other means for growth capital; timing to be decided
items.quote: We sought and got approval from our Board to be able to raise some funds through either a QIP or other means.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance provided; focus on fixing subsidiary margins rather than growth
items.quote: On the subsidiary front, obviously, it depends on what we will end up doing with the Canadian subsidiary and also in terms of the improvement on utilization in France, which we are doing.

items.statement: Domestic BTS business focused on defense/space (electronic warfare, space, radars, land systems); EMS adding strategic customers in ramp-up phase
items.quote: So with all of this, I think these are -- electronic warfare, space, radars and land systems are broadly areas that we have been building strong capabilities in.

items.statement: Negotiating variation orders with Canadian customers to cover engineering costs; shifting work from Canada to India for cost advantage
items.quote: First, in the short-term itself, we are -- we've been negotiating quite strongly with some of our customers to obtain additional purchase orders for -- or additional variation orders for the -- to support the engineering team in Canada.

items.statement: Exceptional loss provision for 30% stake in Ausar Energy (French associate) due to redressement judiciaire; four interested bidders for recovery
items.quote: As a matter of abundant caution and prudence, we have provided for the entire exposure. But as it evolves, perhaps in the next month or so, we should be able to get a better clarity.

items.statement: EBITDA margins should improve from next financial year as annual procurement contracts expire on 31st March 2025
items.quote: See, the EBITDA margins should certainly improve going forward from coming year because our procurement contracts are for -- on an annual basis, which will expire by 31st of March this year.

items.statement: Top line growth expected at 8% to 10% for the industry overall
items.quote: Top line growth, we are certainly looking, as I was telling earlier to replying to a question that we expect made me to grow much faster than what we have shown so far.

items.statement: Building Products segment will grow faster than current rates
items.quote: Building Products segment will grow faster than what we have grown so far. Thinking that the growth rates will be faster than what we have today.

items.statement: Agriculture segment to continue growing at 8% to 10% annual rate
items.quote: Agriculture will continue to grow as per the regular 8% to 10% annual growth rate.

items.statement: INR20 crores capex already spent in current year; expansion plans nearing finalization before end of financial year
items.quote: Already during this current year, INR20 crores capex has been -- payout has been already made, and we are further going ahead with our plans.

items.statement: Building Products segment EBITDA margins expected to gradually reach industry levels of 16% to 20%
items.quote: you will see generally industry is showing between 16% to 20% EBITDA margins. So we will try to catch up with the industry in EBITDA, but it takes -- it doesn't happen in steps.

items.statement: Raw material procurement contracts linked to Platt prices; local market prices 7-9% below contracted rates
items.quote: the difference between local market and the raw material manufacturers or landed prices were to the significant extent of 8%, 7%, 9% with month-to-month, they will be even higher than that.

items.statement: Building materials demand consistent across all regions; temporary rain impact of 10-15 days only
items.quote: as far as building materials are concerned, the demand is consistent and across all segments across India. It is not affected by sudden rains or short rain cycles.

items.statement: Government anti-dumping duty on PVC awaited; notification circulated but not yet announced
items.quote: Government has already issued and circulated country-wise manufacture-wise ADD, which they would like to apply. The only notification is awaited, which we are still not…

items.statement: Promoters converted INR17 crores warrants into equity; remaining 50% conversion in next financial year
items.quote: Only promoters have converted about 17 crores worth of warrants into equity. And the reason I always explain, you see in the current stock exchange rules, if you are having acquisition of more than 5% on a basis, it triggers certain other rules.

items.statement: Focus on Building Products and Agri segments; Industrial segment exposure to remain limited
items.quote: Our major focus will be BP, where we are growing well, and we are getting reasonably good response. And this is along with Agri that will be our major focus of business.

items.statement: Industrial segment sales down 73%; minimal outstanding receivables from institutional business
items.quote: we have come down from in institution by 73% sales are down. So you can understand hardly outstandings are there.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 may still be weak; significant improvement expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: I think the things have started getting on a correction side. I would say that this Q4 may be still not that great. But from Q1 next year, we hope to be doing much better.

items.statement: SCD achieved 11.8% EBITDA margin in Q3 FY25, first time crossing double digits
items.quote: Particularly Suprajit Controls division had a good turnaround in this quarter. For the first time, it has declared a double-digit EBITDA margin of 12%, 11.8%.

items.statement: SCD margin improvement driven by operational excellence across plants except Matamoros
items.quote: Except Matamoros, all other pieces of the puzzle have been performing well compared to last year. I think that is why the margins have improved for the quarter.

items.statement: Chairman believes SCD double-digit margin is sustainable going forward
items.quote: Is it sustainable? I would believe so that it is sustainable. I think the operations continues to be pretty good going forward.

items.statement: SED installed new SMT production line now fully operational
items.quote: To cater to the growing needs of our customers, we also inst alled a new SMT production line, which is now fully operational and will help us fill capacity and manage capacity going forward

items.statement: SED margins impacted by product mix changes in EV 2-wheeler segment
items.quote: As you know, the EV market in India last quarter is quite tumultuous and there were quite a few changes in the volumes of many players. This meant that revenue grew, but some of the margins were impacted by product mix changes.

items.statement: Indian automotive growth below expectations with flat PV and moderate 2-wheeler growth
items.quote: We all know that it was not up to the expectations and there was a flat passenger vehicles and moderate 2-wheeler growth. Industry grew by around 10% for the 9 months as of December 2024.

items.statement: US market sentiment flat due to tariff uncertainty and ICE vs EV questions
items.quote: So, these are some of the h aunting questions in the auto industry and that has led to a flat sentiment in the U.S. market and also kept the industry on wait and watch

items.statement: Europe continues to flounder with political indecisiveness and production cuts
items.quote: Europe continues to flounder. It continues its political indecisiveness and lack of economic stability. We have all been hearing about huge manpower cuts at OEMs, production cuts, Tier 1s, economic brinkmanship at the smaller niche vendors.

items.statement: SCD winning new contracts across plants including electronic products for EV division
items.quote: U.S. team also continues to win great business like Europe. But what is very important is in the last quarter, we saw them winning business for the electronic products, at least for our electric EV division, like various sensors, starters from 2 of the major off-highway OEMs.

items.statement: SAL Automotive won significant new contracts ramping up in coming quarters
items.quote: Suprajit Automotive has been winning some significant, significant large contracts, and you will see in the upcoming quarters, the growth of SAL Automotive will be even more exciting as we have won multiple new contracts, which will all go into production in the next few quarters starting now.

items.statement: Matamoros faces tariff and labor cost challenges; legal case progressing slowly
items.quote: Matamoros, Mexico, it still continues with the 2 challenges. One has been tariff, obviously, and the other one being the labor cost. On the tariff front, we have gone to the court, as you know, and like any courts in any part of the world, justice moves very slowly.

items.statement: In-sourcing electronics boards and motors from India to reduce Matamoros costs
items.quote: We are in the process of getting that particular product also in the process of being approved with customers. So once it is done, I think we will have a two-pronged cost reduction happening in that project, which would be a significant saving going forward.

items.statement: Morocco plant moving from 3-shift to 1-shift operation showing productivity gains
items.quote: We have, for example, moved from a 3-shift operation, we are moving to just about a 1-shift operation, which shows the kind of productivity improvements that we could have done on the same revenue and sales.

items.statement: SCS Europe turnaround expected in next few quarters; China/Canada profitable from April
items.quote: From 1st of April onwards, I think the numbers should look slightly better. And of course, the work in SCS Europe, it continues for at least 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: Indian cable exports grew 35% in 9 months ended Dec 2024
items.quote: Our Indian cable exports saw a fantastic 35% growth. This shows the underlying strength in our global strategy as to how we have moved literally almost, I would say, conquered the Western world.

items.statement: SMT line captive use expected to improve EBITDA by 1% to 2% over time
items.quote: But over a period of time, we expect at least 1% to 2% improvement in EBITDA through these initiatives for the internal consumption, captive consumption.

items.statement: IATF certification for automotive EMS expected in a couple of quarters max
items.quote: Work on that is going on, and we should be certified in a couple of quarters max because that needs some kind of preparation.

items.statement: Products and Solutions addressable market growing at 8% to 10%
items.quote: My understanding is the market is growing at about 8 to 10 percent.

items.statement: Solar O&M megawatts under management expected to reach 800 to 900 by year end
items.quote: I think we hope to end the year with about 800 to 900 megawatts under management, and it will consistently grow on that side.

items.statement: EMS expansion timeline depends on business growth and ODM partner investment decisions
items.quote: If the business grows really fast, those number of lines can come fast. If the business does not come in, those lines in 3 years also will not make any meaning.

items.statement: Mobile printers gaining traction in government and BFSI segments
items.quote: That is where the traction is, because if you notice the Department of Post was one big customer, a couple of others who are looking at taking the print or the business to the last mile into much more of the heart of India, that is where the mobile printers are being used and commissioned and that is where the use case has increased.

items.statement: Company investing 2% to 3% of revenue in EMS and R&D growth initiatives
items.quote: as explained in the earlier calls, we are continuing to invest 2% to 3% of our revenue in growth initiatives like EMS and R&D

items.statement: Retail sector growth has been very slow and a dampener
items.quote: the retail sector has been very, very, the growth has been very slow, and it has been quite a dampener as regards to that.

items.statement: Additional SMT lines will be added as EMS business grows
items.quote: as and when the growth happens, the additional lines will come. At this point of time, I think it is purely subject to the growth of the business and as the business grows, I think we should be in a position to add the lines as required.

items.statement: No specific timeline given for breaking even at EBT level
items.quote: However, we expect like in the future, this investment of 2% to 3% expected to contribute for growth much bigger than what we are growing 15% and expected to result in a positive margin at the bottom line.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM target 22,000-23,000 crore by FY25 end, yield normalization next financial year
items.quote: I think the year we should end at around 22, 23 and it will take maybe some more time to get to 25.

items.statement: Gold loan yield recovery of at least 1% in Q1 FY26, full normalization next financial year
items.quote: I expect at least 1% to be recovered in the first quarter of the new fiscal year itself. But it's very difficult to be precise on the forecast.

items.statement: MFI credit cost guidance 8-8.5% for current period
items.quote: On an average, we will be looking at a credit cost of around, for this, around 8% to 8.5% kind of a thing.

items.statement: MFI asset quality bottoming out now, worst quarter was Q3 FY25
items.quote: I think that we should be bottoming out now.

items.statement: Worst is behind us, things should improve from Q4 FY25
items.quote: I believe that we have taken, in case of MSME, our insurance cover starts from the loans, I think from September or October. In microfinance, I think some pain is still there, but it may not be as bad as the third quarter, which was the worst ever quarter.

items.statement: Raised INR 9,964 crore through term loans, bonds, CP and INR 1,477 crore from assignment in Q3 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, we raised INR 9,964 crores through term loans, bonds, and commercial paper and INR 1,477 crores was raised from assignment.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio yield down ~2% due to competitive customer acquisition
items.quote: Gold loan volume growth is there, but the portfolio yield is down by almost 2%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing increased 9 bps YoY and 1 bps QoQ to 9.16%
items.quote: Our quarterly average cost of borrowing increased 9 basis points year-on-year and 1 basis point quarter-on-quarter to hit 9.16%.

items.statement: Gold loan volume growing strongly, reached 15,000 crore from 10,000 at ban
items.quote: At the time of ban, we had 10,000, then we went up to 11,000 in the 10 days after the ban in September then 15,000.

items.statement: Karnataka MFI ordinance causing slight disturbances despite exemption for regulated entities
items.quote: We expect slight disturbances for a couple of months or so till people -- I mean, even now if you look at it on the ground, most of the stakeholders have understood that it is not for the regulated entities and things, but slight disturbances will affect K arnataka for slightly little thing

items.statement: Liquidity buffer INR 5,656 crore as of Dec 31, covers 6 months maturities of INR 5,297 crore
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalent and committed credit lines from banks and institutions stood at INR5,656 crores. This is adequate to meet near-term liabilities, but also fund growth.

items.statement: Dollar bond raised in Jan 2025 at near double-digit cost, will impact Q4 FY25 cost of funds
items.quote: The dollar bond that we have raised in the month of January with full hedging, the cost is significantly higher. It's almost kind of double digit, and that will impact the weighted average cost of fund going forward.

items.statement: Capital adequacy dipped to 22% from 26.3% QoQ due to loan growth and lower assignments, expected to recover as assignments pick up
items.quote: So the capital adequacy margin is down because the loan book has grown, Mr. Lee. And as I said that the assignments have been much lower because they require seasoning.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15-20% for FY26 and EBITDA margin guidance of 14.5-15% for FY26

items.quote: we should be looking – to similar a 9 -monthFY25 growth, anywhere between 20% to 25%, which should ideally get the total consolidated revenues closer to around INR 3,500 crores, and we should be able to sustain a similar EBITDA margin in quarter 4 as well.

items.statement: Capex guidance for full year FY25 remains INR 130-140 crores; INR 83 crores spent in 9 months
items.quote: The capex outlay during 9 months has been at INR83 crores, majorly on account of new products SOPs in IAC and Lumax Alps. The guidance for the full year remains at INR 130 crores to INR140 crores.

items.statement: Total order book INR 1,350 crores with 90% new business; 30% maturing in FY26, 40% in FY27, 30% in FY28; EV contribution ~40%
items.quote: The total order book, considering the value of all product categories, are INR 1,350 crores, out of which 90% is new business. 30% order book value will mature in FY '26, 40% in FY '27 and remaining 30% in FY '28. EV contribution is approximately 40% of the total order book.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14% for Q3 and 9M FY25; FY26 guidance 14.5-15%; levers are JV turnaround and Aftermarket recovery
items.quote: I think my margin guidance would be that anywhere close to 14.5% to 15% which we should be looking at perhaps in FY '26 at a consolidated level. items.statement: Raw material pricing showing signs of increase but recoverable from OEMs in 3-6 months
items.quote: There are certain signs of raw material pricing going up. But again, that is a lag. We should be able to recover them from the OEMs in 3 to 6 months' time frame.

items.statement: PV growth muted at 3-5% in FY26; 2W to surpass FY19 peak of 24.5M units with low double-digit growth; CV recovery expected in FY26 with govt/private capex uptick

items.quote: We are anticipating almost INR 60 crores to INR70 crores increase in our top line revenues with the implementation of the secondary oxygen sensor, which now becomes mandatory from 1st April 2025.

items.quote: I think overall, my commentary would be that we've seen a significant growth in the Mechatronics vertical. And for the next year onwards, we do expect to almost double our revenue within the Mechatronics vertical.

items.statement: IAC India 9M revenue INR 800 crores, up 20% YoY; order book INR 500-550 crores; FY26 manufacturing growth expected 15%+ on full year EV launch realization
items.quote: IAC total revenue for 9 months of this fiscal stood at INR 800 crores. And again, maybe I'll request Sunil Koparkar to just take the question on Tata Motors launch date and value of the business for IAC.

items.quote: for quarter 4 stand alone, we should be looking at a good double-digit growth rate, which is pretty similar to what the Aftermarket division used to do up until FY '24. Giving you a horizon, I think this growth momentum in FY '26 will continue very healthy into a double-digit territory. items.quote: as of now, in P&L, there is a content per vehicle of INR4,000 on account of CNG. But going forward in next year, we are seeing that content to increase to somewhere closer to INR 8,000 to INR 10,000 per vehicle.

items.statement: Lumax Cornaglia grew 5% in 9M despite anchor customer volumes down 5%; new SOPs for rooftops of E3-wheelers and body cabins in next 2 months
items.quote: Lumax Cornaglia, in spite of its anchor customer being down this year in production volumes by 5%, still reported about 5% kind of a top line increase.

items.quote: I think it would be in the range of 40 to 50 stores from the current level of about -- we end this year at about 70-odd stores, and we should be able to probably add closer to 50 stores next year.

items.quote: We will not be able to touch 2,000 crores, but yes, considering the profitability and all, cost margins and all those and working capital on, those parameters will be improving

items.statement: Grain processing revenue steady at ~₹900 crore; plants at ~80% utilization; no capacity expansion planned
items.quote: Yes, I think ₹900 crores is a steady revenue contribution from the grain processing segment. We have not taken any further capex in this segment until that happens, and the plants are already running at full capacity.

items.statement: Sorbitol exports stable at ~₹100 crore to 40+ countries; no significant deviation expected
items.quote: See, we export sorbitol to over 40 countries, and we have revenue of about ₹100 crore coming from it. So, the revenue from exports will remain stable, with not much deviation on either the upper or lower side.

items.statement: EU EV business recovery expected early CY26; no significant upswing for next 9-12 months
items.quote: And at this point of time, the best guess of recovery would be towards early part of next year. Until such time I think --

items.statement: India EV heavy vehicle electrification first vehicles on road in next two quarters
items.quote: And we expect that in the next two quarters or so we should have the first few vehicles on Indian road.

items.statement: India EV LCV demand pickup expected in next two to three quarters
items.quote: And so we definitely see that there will be more demand coming up in the next two to three quarters.

items.statement: New camshaft capacity to be fully utilized in next one and a half years
items.period: next one and a half year
items.quote: Yes, in the next one and a half year or so, because the capacity is not created yet, the plants are ready, the physical plans are ready.

items.statement: New plant capacity being created over next eight to 10 months; serial supplies after that
items.quote: The capacity will be built up in the next three to four quarters, like I said, eight to 10 months roughly. And then it will be the serial supplies after that.

items.statement: New camshaft projects awarded with SOPs in late 2025 or 2026; import substitution for running engines
items.quote: What we are doing is we are adding capacity for new projects that have been awarded to PCL which have SOPs or start of production in either late 2025 or 2026.

items.statement: Assembled camshaft capacity 50,000 to 70,000 parts per month; import substitution for known customer
items.quote: Right now we are looking at somewhere between 50,000 to 70,000 parts per month.

items.statement: India PV market flattish; Europe, Brazil, Mexico significantly reduced; US, Korea, Uzbekistan flat
items.quote: But if you ask me, in general, the Indian market has been flattish, Europe has significantly reduced. Brazil and Mexico have also slowed down significantly.

items.statement: India EV LCV commercial sales started August 2024; slower ramp-up than anticipated
items.quote: Commercial sales have started since August 2024. However, the ramp-up of volumes has been slower than anticipated in India due to various reasons.

items.statement: India EV heavy vehicle electrification: 3-4 customers willing to adopt; first revenues planned CY26
items.quote: And we are actually planning to start revenues of this project in calendar year '26 itself.

items.statement: EU subsidiaries facing severe headwinds; several competitors bankrupt; scaling operations to fit order book
items.quote: we are still staying afloat with the customer orders and some of the consistent revenue that we have. But we should not expect too much of an upswing from here , at least for the next nine to 12 months

items.statement: Subsidiaries self-sufficient, not leaning on PCL for financial support; scaling down operations
items.quote: our focus right now is to make sure that the organizations are self -sufficient, that they are not leaning on to PCL for any kind of financial support, which they are

items.statement: India EV LCV retrofitting in 7-8 cities; engaged with fleet owners across 20-30 cities
items.quote: So we have already started supplying vehicles in seven to eight cities across India, so whether that is a Calcutta, Delhi, Hyderabad, Solapur, Pune, Mumbai, etc.

items.statement: India EV LCV conversion cost Rs. 5-7 lakh per vehicle; revenues already in crores
items.quote: So the conversion cost is, let's say, Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 7 lakh. And our revenues are already in the crores of rupees for the small vehicle electrification pipeline that we have.

items.statement: Heavy vehicle electrification localizing content from first vehicle; 300 kWh battery pack vs 10-15 kWh for LCV
items.quote: Because instead of a 10 kilowatt hour to 15 kilowatt hour battery pack, we are talking about a 300 kilowatt hour battery pack on a truck like this.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 35-40% with EBITDA margin 12-14%
items.quote: In the coming year, we anticipated that the growth will be around 35% to 40% in the 25-26 and EBITDA margin will be in the range of around 12% to 14%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target Rs 1,850-1,950 crore
items.quote: The total turnover will be around 1850 to 1950 crores in the range.

items.statement: FY25 full-year EBITDA margin guided 10-12%
items.quote: This year we are guided around 10 % to 12%.

items.statement: H2 FY25 EBITDA margin expected 13-14%
items.quote: H2 EBITDA margins are around 13% to 14%.

items.statement: FY26 net profit margin expected 5-6%
items.quote: Net profit margin, should be around 5% to 6% in the next year considering an EBITDA of 12 % to 14%.

items.statement: Rs 425 crore deployed over last 2 years; additional Rs 50-100 crore planned
items.quote: See for the last 2 years we have deployed approximately Rs. 425 crores. May be another 75, 50 to 100 crores may be deployed further to separate the things in two sides.

items.statement: 9M FY25 EBITDA margin 11% due to lower realizations and new plant under-absorption
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 117 crores during the 9 months with EBITDA margin at 11%.

items.statement: Gross margin declined 200-300 bps in Q3 FY25 from lower technical realizations
items.quote: One is the reason is our gross margins has come down to around 2-3 basis also, so 200-300 basis points due to lower realization of some of our technical products also.

items.statement: New plant under-absorption cost Rs 15-20 crore in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Almost, you can say around Rs. 15 to Rs. 20 crore also in that.

items.statement: Export pricing bottomed out; some products up 7-10% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We have seen that in some products there has been a jump in price of around 7% to 10%, but for some it has been stable yet which may be once the season comes in, we will be able to see some price revision in those products as well.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 domestic and export demand improving; Q1 FY26 expected stronger
items.quote: Q4, we have already started seeing good demand coming in and because of demand we are also seeing price improvements in the product.

items.statement: Industry-wide pricing pressure from Indian and Chinese competition; peers' balance sheets in red
items.quote: If you see the balance sheet of all other companies, peers, it is all in red mark, negative. So definitely, there won't be any downward pricing now because all are suffering now.

items.statement: Registration pipeline for new products underway; some approvals expected FY25, more in FY26
items.quote: We have started doing the registration activities for the products that we were planning to come in. Since two years, so there'll be some registration that we will get in the current year, some registration that we will get in the next year.

items.statement: Total borrowings ~Rs 300 crore
items.quote: Total borrowing is around 300 Cr.

items.statement: Expect shrimp production in 2025 to be at same levels as last year and maybe slightly about 5% more
items.quote: So we expect that the production would be on the same levels as in the last year and maybe slightly about 5% more than w hat was in the last year

items.statement: Pet food plant land purchased for INR 36 crores; plant and machinery estimated around INR 60 crores
items.value: INR 36 crores land, INR 60 crores plant & machinery
items.quote: Capex, we have already incurred a land purchase about around INR 36 crores. Further, the plant and machinery will be around INR 60 crores.

items.statement: Pet food plant commercial production expected to start by December 2026
items.quote: We are expecting that by end of '26, we should be able to come out with our own production by end up December '26.

items.statement: Shrimp feed margins range 7% to 10% depending on raw material prices
items.quote: Maybe it is ranging from maybe 7% to 10% we keep our margins. It all depends on how the raw material prices are.

items.statement: Shrimp processing margins under pressure due to CVD duty; focusing on value-added products and cost optimization to mitigate
items.quote: There are two things that we're doing. First, we're reducing and trying to optimize our costs. That process has already started. Yes. That's point number one. Apart from our general cost optimization effort, like we're putting it as one of our main goals for this year. Second is concentrating on higher value products, which don't attract duty.

items.statement: Fish meal price expected to vary between INR 95 to INR 100 per kg
items.quote: So that is one of the reasons where the prices are looking more stable with maybe around INR 100, we are expecting that it should be varying between INR 95 to INR 100.

items.statement: Wheat flour price expected between INR 35 to INR 40 per kg; concern due to government procurement policy
items.quote: It should be around INR 36, INR 37. It should be INR 35 to INR 40. It should be between that. But it is really, bit of, concern.

items.statement: Soybean meal prices remain stable
items.quote: And as far as the soya is concerned, we are pretty stable, and we have been able to get the quantities.

items.statement: First aquaculture season 2025 started well with good farm gate prices and climatic conditions; farmers increasing cultivation area
items.quote: The season has started, the first season, which is the major aquaculture season for India that is started from most end of middle of January and it is progressing really very well. So the climatic conditions and other factors have helped to take off very smoothly, and with the good farm gate prices, the farmers are very much interested to increase the area cultivation.

items.statement: Expect feed consumption growth of 5% to 10% in next year due to good culture conditions and prices
items.quote: So, we normally expect see the next year we are expecting about a 5% or 10% increase. That's because this year the culture is good; the prices are good.

items.statement: Focusing on value-added shrimp products (ready-to-fry, breaded, tempura) which don't attract CVD duty
items.quote: Second is concentrating on higher value products, which don't attract duty. So those are the -- that is the second. We've always told in the past several quarters that value added products is what we're focusing on.

items.statement: Pet food brand 'Avant Furst' launched cat food in January 2025; dog food launch planned by July 2025
items.quote: The brand name is Avant Furst will be launched the cat food has already been launched and the dog will also be launched on the same name AVANT FRUST.

items.quote: However, the levy of CVD, which is at 5.77% now by U.S., is an additional burden to the export of shrimps to U.S., which is the largest export market for the company.

items.quote: The reduction of custom duty on feed import is actually a disadvantage for us, because if the 15% or 5% have reduced, so the imported feed competition will go up.

items.quote: So, we're talking raw material about 28,000 to 30,000 tons in the next 4 to 5 quarters?

items.statement: Government order book estimated at INR 25-28 crores for next financial year

items.quote: In terms of manpower, if I say, we have around 20-odd people. We are expecting that this 20-odd people will be multiplied 4x to 5x in next financial year.

items.statement: Expecting more than double growth in cybersecurity revenue next financial year
items.quote: And we are expecting really more than double growth in next financial year.

items.quote: As far as margins are concerned, as I told earlier that we are focusing more on those contracts where our margins are kept. So we keep at least 10% of profit margin in our every service contract from government.

items.quote: We are adding clients -- international clients, at least two to three clients every month. As a majority of clients, they are signing NDA and NCA with us, so we are not able to announce it to our shareholders.

items.quote: So this, as far as cybersecurity order is concerned, implementation stage is going on. So we'll get a portion of the income of that order in Q4 current year itself. As far as new two orders are concerned, again, that also will reflect in our Q4.

items.quote: In India, as you all know that, we are ve ry strong into e - governance market and now we have added that we'll be focusing more on manufacturing and engineering side, chemical and pharmaceutical side, retail and logistics side
